bg_1.speaker: Arjuna
bg_1.setting: Arjuna, seeing his own family in the enemy ranks, collapses in grief before the battle.
bg_1.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचकृपया परयाऽऽविष्टो विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत् । दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् ॥
bg_1.translation: Arjuna said: Krishna, when I see my own people standing here, eager to fight, I am overcome with pity and sorrow.
bg_1.line: Even Arjuna, the finest archer alive, froze when the fight was against his own people.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara treats Arjuna's pity as born of attachment and delusion, the grief the teaching will remove; Sanjaya's words frame it: overcome by deep compassion, despairing, he spoke.

prasang.title_en: Overcome by delusion, Arjuna speaks in fear, love and grief
prasang.summary: Seeing his kin ready to die, Arjuna trembles, his bow slips, and he argues that no victory is worth killing family. He sits down in the chariot and refuses to fight.
prasang.lesson: Even the strongest people freeze; the Gita begins with a breakdown, not a hero.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, who has collapsed in tears on the battlefield and refuses to fight.
bg_1.sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचकुतस्त्वा कश्मलमिदं विषमे समुपस्थितम् । अनार्यजुष्टमस्वर्ग्यमकीर्तिकरमर्जुन ॥
bg_1.translation: The Blessed Lord said: Where has this faintness of heart come upon you in this crisis, Arjuna? It is not fitting for the noble, it does not lead upward, and it brings disgrace.
bg_1.line: Where did this weakness come from, at the very moment it matters most?
bg_1.misuse: Not shaming fear; it's the opening of a long, patient answer.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: A rebuke meant to rouse Arjuna, before he has asked to be taught; Shankara begins his commentary only at 2.11. Plain sense as in Sridhara and Gita Press.

prasang.title_en: Krishna and Arjuna on Arjuna's faint-heartedness
prasang.summary: Krishna challenges Arjuna's despair. Arjuna admits he is confused about what is right, cannot tell which choice is better, and asks Krishna to teach him.
prasang.lesson: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, who has collapsed in tears on the battlefield and refuses to fight.
bg_1.sanskrit: क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते । क्षुद्रं हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्यक्त्वोत्तिष्ठ परन्तप ॥
bg_1.translation: Do not give in to this unmanliness, Partha; it does not become you. Throw off this petty weakness of heart and rise, scorcher of enemies.
bg_1.line: This smallness of heart isn't who you are. Shake it off and stand up.
bg_1.misuse: Not 'feelings are weakness' or 'man up'. It is a friend reminding you of your strength, said once, then explained for 700 verses.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Krishna's first words are a rebuke meant to rouse Arjuna; the teaching proper begins only at 2.11, after Arjuna surrenders as a student in 2.7. Shankara does not comment on the verses before 2.11.

prasang.title_en: Krishna and Arjuna on Arjuna's faint-heartedness
prasang.summary: Krishna challenges Arjuna's despair. Arjuna admits he is confused about what is right, cannot tell which choice is better, and asks Krishna to teach him.
prasang.lesson: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.

bg_1.speaker: Arjuna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, who has collapsed in tears on the battlefield and refuses to fight.
bg_1.sanskrit: न चैतद्विद्मः कतरन्नो गरीयोयद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः । यानेव हत्वा न जिजीविषामस्तेऽवस्थिताः प्रमुखे धार्तराष्ट्राः ॥
bg_1.translation: Nor do we know which is better for us, to fight or not, or whether we will win or they will. The very people after whose death we would not wish to live stand facing us.
bg_1.line: I can't tell which is better, or even what winning would look like.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Plain sense, as Sridhara and Gita Press give it: Arjuna cannot decide whether victory or defeat is better, since the kinsmen whose killing would make life unwanted stand facing him.

prasang.title_en: Krishna and Arjuna on Arjuna's faint-heartedness
prasang.summary: Krishna challenges Arjuna's despair. Arjuna admits he is confused about what is right, cannot tell which choice is better, and asks Krishna to teach him.
prasang.lesson: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.

bg_1.speaker: Arjuna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, who has collapsed in tears on the battlefield and refuses to fight.
bg_1.sanskrit: न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्याद्यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम् । अवाप्य भूमावसपत्नमृद्धम्राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम् ॥
bg_1.translation: I see nothing that could drive away this sorrow that is drying up my senses, not even an unrivalled, prosperous kingdom on earth or rule over the gods.
bg_1.line: Even winning everything wouldn't touch this grief that's drying me up inside.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Plain sense, as in Shankara's introduction: Arjuna's grief and delusion are such that no worldly or heavenly gain could remove them; hence only knowledge of the self can.

prasang.title_en: Krishna and Arjuna on Arjuna's faint-heartedness
prasang.summary: Krishna challenges Arjuna's despair. Arjuna admits he is confused about what is right, cannot tell which choice is better, and asks Krishna to teach him.
prasang.lesson: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
bg_1.sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचअशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे । गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः ॥
bg_1.translation: The Blessed Lord said: You grieve for those who should not be grieved for, and yet you speak words that sound wise. The wise grieve neither for the dead nor for the living.
bg_1.line: You grieve for what doesn't need your grief, while talking like you know better.
bg_1.misuse: Not 'don't cry' or 'your grief is wrong'. It opens a teaching on what in us does not die; grief still deserves time.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: this verse is the seed of the whole teaching; grief and delusion are the root of samsara and only knowledge of the self removes them. The 'wise' are those who know the self. Madhusudana notes the gentle irony in 'words of wisdom'.

prasang.title_en: The teaching of the deathless Self (Sankhya)
prasang.summary: Krishna begins his teaching: the self is eternal, bodies change like clothes, and pleasure and pain come and go. Grief for what must pass should not overwhelm us.
prasang.lesson: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
bg_1.sanskrit: न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः । न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम् ॥
bg_1.translation: Never was there a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor these kings; nor will there ever be a time when all of us cease to be.
bg_1.line: There was never a time when you, I, or anyone here did not exist, and never will be.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: in all three periods of time we are eternal as the self; the plural refers to the bodies, not to many selves. Ramanuja reads the plural as showing that selves are truly many and eternal.

prasang.title_en: The teaching of the deathless Self (Sankhya)
prasang.summary: Krishna begins his teaching: the self is eternal, bodies change like clothes, and pleasure and pain come and go. Grief for what must pass should not overwhelm us.
prasang.lesson: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
bg_1.sanskrit: यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ । समदुःखसुखं धीरं सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते ॥
bg_1.translation: The steady person whom these do not disturb, who stays the same in pain and pleasure, becomes fit for immortality.
bg_1.line: The one who stays the same in pain and pleasure, undisturbed by either, is ready for real freedom.
bg_1.misuse: Steadiness is not numbness or hiding what you feel.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: the one who sees the eternal self and is not shaken by pleasure and pain becomes fit for immortality, which is liberation.

prasang.title_en: The teaching of the deathless Self (Sankhya)
prasang.summary: Krishna begins his teaching: the self is eternal, bodies change like clothes, and pleasure and pain come and go. Grief for what must pass should not overwhelm us.
prasang.lesson: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
bg_1.sanskrit: नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः । उभयोरपि दृष्टोऽन्तस्त्वनयोस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः ॥
bg_1.translation: The unreal has no lasting being, and the real never ceases to be. Those who see the truth have seen the final word on both.
bg_1.line: What is unreal never truly lasts; what is real never stops being.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: The unreal, such as cold and heat with their causes, has no being; the real, the self, never ceases to be; the knowers of truth have ascertained both.

prasang.title_en: The teaching of the deathless Self (Sankhya)
prasang.summary: Krishna begins his teaching: the self is eternal, bodies change like clothes, and pleasure and pain come and go. Grief for what must pass should not overwhelm us.
prasang.lesson: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
bg_1.sanskrit: अव्यक्तोऽयमचिन्त्योऽयमविकार्योऽयमुच्यते । तस्मादेवं विदित्वैनं नानुशोचितुमर्हसि ॥
bg_1.translation: It is called unmanifest, unthinkable and unchanging. Knowing it to be so, you should not grieve.
bg_1.line: It is unseen, beyond thought, unchanging. Knowing this, ease your grief.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Not an object of any sense, it is unmanifest; not an object of thought, unthinkable; without parts, unchangeable; knowing it thus you ought not to grieve.

prasang.title_en: The teaching of the deathless Self (Sankhya)
prasang.summary: Krishna begins his teaching: the self is eternal, bodies change like clothes, and pleasure and pain come and go. Grief for what must pass should not overwhelm us.
prasang.lesson: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
bg_1.sanskrit: अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम् । तथापि त्वं महाबाहो नैवं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥
bg_1.translation: And even if you think of it as constantly being born and constantly dying, still, mighty-armed one, you should not grieve like this.
bg_1.line: Even if you believe life simply begins and ends, there's still no need to be crushed by grief.
bg_1.misuse: Grief is human; this asks you not to be destroyed by it, not to stop feeling it.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Granting, for argument, the common view that the self is born and dies with each body, even so grief is not fitting.

prasang.title_en: The teaching of the deathless Self (Sankhya)
prasang.summary: Krishna begins his teaching: the self is eternal, bodies change like clothes, and pleasure and pain come and go. Grief for what must pass should not overwhelm us.
prasang.lesson: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
bg_1.sanskrit: जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च । तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥
bg_1.translation: Death is certain for the one who is born, and birth is certain for the one who dies. So you should not grieve over what cannot be avoided.
bg_1.line: Whatever is born will die, and what dies is born again. Don't torment yourself over the unavoidable.
bg_1.misuse: Not a reason to stop caring for the sick or to rush someone's mourning.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: from 2.26 Krishna grants, for argument, the common view that the self is born and dies; even then grief is not fitting, because death and rebirth are unavoidable.

prasang.title_en: The teaching of the deathless Self (Sankhya)
prasang.summary: Krishna begins his teaching: the self is eternal, bodies change like clothes, and pleasure and pain come and go. Grief for what must pass should not overwhelm us.
prasang.lesson: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
bg_1.sanskrit: अव्यक्तादीनि भूतानि व्यक्तमध्यानि भारत । अव्यक्तनिधनान्येव तत्र का परिदेवना ॥
bg_1.translation: Beings are unseen in their beginning, seen in their middle, and unseen again in their end, Arjuna. What is there to lament in this?
bg_1.line: We come from the unseen and return to it; only the middle is visible. Why break over that?
bg_1.misuse: Grief is natural; the verse widens the frame, it doesn't forbid tears.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: bodies, the aggregates of cause and effect, are unseen before they arise and after they perish; what lament is fitting for what is seen only for a while, like an illusion?

prasang.title_en: The teaching of the deathless Self (Sankhya)
prasang.summary: Krishna begins his teaching: the self is eternal, bodies change like clothes, and pleasure and pain come and go. Grief for what must pass should not overwhelm us.
prasang.lesson: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
bg_1.sanskrit: देही नित्यमवध्योऽयं देहे सर्वस्य भारत । तस्मात्सर्वाणि भूतानि न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥
bg_1.translation: The self dwelling in the body of every being is eternal and can never be slain, Bharata. Therefore you should not grieve for any creature.
bg_1.line: The self within every body can never be destroyed. So don't grieve for any creature as lost.
bg_1.misuse: Not a reason to hurry anyone through mourning a person or a pet.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: The conclusion of the section: the embodied self in every body is eternally unslayable, so you ought not to grieve for any being, Bhishma and the rest.

prasang.title_en: The teaching of the deathless Self (Sankhya)
prasang.summary: Krishna begins his teaching: the self is eternal, bodies change like clothes, and pleasure and pain come and go. Grief for what must pass should not overwhelm us.
prasang.lesson: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
bg_1.sanskrit: भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां तयापहृतचेतसाम् । व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिः समाधौ न विधीयते ॥
bg_1.translation: For those attached to pleasure and power, whose minds are carried away by such talk, a resolute, settled understanding does not arise.
bg_1.line: Chasing comfort and power, the mind can never settle into a single purpose.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: For those who cling to enjoyment and lordship, whose discrimination is stolen by flowery promises of them, the resolute understanding does not arise in the mind.

prasang.title_en: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
bg_1.sanskrit: त्रैगुण्यविषया वेदा निस्त्रैगुण्यो भवार्जुन । निर्द्वन्द्वो नित्यसत्त्वस्थो निर्योगक्षेम आत्मवान् ॥
bg_1.translation: The Vedas deal with the three qualities; rise above them, Arjuna. Be free from the pairs of opposites, always steady in goodness, free from the urge to acquire and keep, and possessed of the self.
bg_1.line: Rise above the pull of opposites. Stay centred, not obsessed with getting and keeping.
bg_1.misuse: Not 'don't save or plan'; it's about not being consumed by getting and holding.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: The Vedas' ritual portion concerns samsara made of the three gunas; be without desire, free of the pairs, established in sattva, without concern for getting and keeping, and vigilant.

prasang.title_en: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
bg_1.sanskrit: दूरेण ह्यवरं कर्म बुद्धियोगाद्धनञ्जय । बुद्धौ शरणमन्विच्छ कृपणाः फलहेतवः ॥
bg_1.translation: Action done for its rewards is far inferior to action done with a steady mind. Seek refuge in that understanding; those who work only for the fruit are to be pitied.
bg_1.line: Working only for the payoff makes you poor inside. Take shelter in clear understanding.
bg_1.misuse: Not 'ambition is wrong'. It's about not letting rewards be the only reason you work.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: action done by one seeking results is far lower than action done with evenness of mind; kripana, the pitiable, are those who work for fruit, like the one who leaves the world without knowing the imperishable.

prasang.title_en: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
bg_1.sanskrit: यदा ते मोहकलिलं बुद्धिर्व्यतितरिष्यति । तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च ॥
bg_1.translation: When your understanding crosses the mire of delusion, you will grow indifferent to all that you have heard and all that is yet to be heard.
bg_1.line: When your mind clears the fog, you'll tire of all you've heard and all you're yet to hear.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: When your intellect passes beyond the turbidity of delusion that confuses self and not-self, you will reach dispassion about what is heard and to be heard, seeing it as fruitless.

prasang.title_en: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
bg_1.sanskrit: श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना ते यदा स्थास्यति निश्चला । समाधावचला बुद्धिस्तदा योगमवाप्स्यसि ॥
bg_1.translation: When your understanding, now confused by conflicting things you have heard, stands firm and unmoving in deep stillness, then you will attain yoga.
bg_1.line: Pulled by conflicting advice, the mind wobbles. When it settles and stays still, you've arrived.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: the intellect is distracted by hearing of many ends and means; when it stands without doubt, unmoving in samadhi, the self, then you gain the yoga of discriminating wisdom.

prasang.title_en: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
bg_1.sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचप्रजहाति यदा कामान् सर्वान् पार्थ मनोगतान् । आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्टः स्थितप्रज्ञस्तदोच्यते ॥
bg_1.translation: The Blessed Lord said: When a person gives up all the desires of the mind and is content in the self by the self, then he is called one of steady wisdom.
bg_1.line: When you stop chasing every desire and find contentment within yourself, your wisdom becomes steady.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: having given up all desires, satisfied in the inmost self alone with no need of outer gain, like one who has tasted nectar; such a knower is called steady in wisdom.

prasang.title_en: The person of steady wisdom
prasang.summary: Arjuna asks how a steady person speaks, sits and walks. Krishna describes someone content within, unshaken by sorrow, master of the senses, and traces how dwelling on things leads to anger and ruin.
prasang.lesson: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
bg_1.sanskrit: यः सर्वत्रानभिस्नेहस्तत्तत्प्राप्य शुभाशुभम् । नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
bg_1.translation: One who is without attachment anywhere, who neither rejoices on meeting good nor hates on meeting bad, has wisdom that is firmly set.
bg_1.line: Good news doesn't inflate them, bad news doesn't embitter them. That's steady wisdom.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: without affection even for body and life, he neither praises on gaining the pleasant nor hates on meeting the unpleasant; his discriminating wisdom is established.

prasang.title_en: The person of steady wisdom
prasang.summary: Arjuna asks how a steady person speaks, sits and walks. Krishna describes someone content within, unshaken by sorrow, master of the senses, and traces how dwelling on things leads to anger and ruin.
prasang.lesson: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
bg_1.sanskrit: विषया विनिवर्तन्ते निराहारस्य देहिनः । रसवर्जं रसोऽप्यस्य परं दृष्ट्वा निवर्तते ॥
bg_1.translation: Objects fall away from one who abstains from them, but the taste for them remains. Even the taste falls away once the Supreme is seen.
bg_1.line: Staying away from a craving dims it, but the taste lingers until something higher replaces it.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Even the ignorant ascetic's sense objects turn away, but not the relish for them; that subtle attachment ends only when the supreme reality, Brahman, is seen.

prasang.title_en: The person of steady wisdom
prasang.summary: Arjuna asks how a steady person speaks, sits and walks. Krishna describes someone content within, unshaken by sorrow, master of the senses, and traces how dwelling on things leads to anger and ruin.
prasang.lesson: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
bg_1.sanskrit: यततो ह्यपि कौन्तेय पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः । इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि हरन्ति प्रसभं मनः ॥
bg_1.translation: The turbulent senses forcibly carry away the mind even of a wise person who is striving, Arjuna.
bg_1.line: Even a wise, striving person can be dragged off by restless senses. Don't be surprised; be ready.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: the senses are turbulent and carry off by force the mind even of a discerning person who keeps trying; hence they must be restrained (2.61).

prasang.title_en: The person of steady wisdom
prasang.summary: Arjuna asks how a steady person speaks, sits and walks. Krishna describes someone content within, unshaken by sorrow, master of the senses, and traces how dwelling on things leads to anger and ruin.
prasang.lesson: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
bg_1.sanskrit: तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः । वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
bg_1.translation: Restraining them all, one should sit disciplined, intent on me. For one whose senses are under control, wisdom is firmly set.
bg_1.line: Gather the senses in, sit steady with your mind on what's highest. Mastery of the senses steadies wisdom.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: having restrained them, sit intent on the Lord, thinking 'I am no other than he'. Ramanuja: the senses cannot be conquered without fixing the mind on the Lord, so the two go together.

prasang.title_en: The person of steady wisdom
prasang.summary: Arjuna asks how a steady person speaks, sits and walks. Krishna describes someone content within, unshaken by sorrow, master of the senses, and traces how dwelling on things leads to anger and ruin.
prasang.lesson: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
bg_1.sanskrit: रागद्वेषवियुक्तैस्तु विषयानिन्द्रियैश्चरन् । आत्मवश्यैर्विधेयात्मा प्रसादमधिगच्छति ॥
bg_1.translation: But a disciplined person, moving among objects with senses under control, free from attraction and aversion, attains clarity and calm.
bg_1.line: Move through the world with your senses in hand, free of grabbing and pushing away, and you find calm.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: the answer to the chain of 2.62-63: one who uses the unavoidable objects with senses free from attraction and aversion, mind under control, attains serenity.

prasang.title_en: The person of steady wisdom
prasang.summary: Arjuna asks how a steady person speaks, sits and walks. Krishna describes someone content within, unshaken by sorrow, master of the senses, and traces how dwelling on things leads to anger and ruin.
prasang.lesson: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
bg_1.sanskrit: या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी । यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः ॥
bg_1.translation: What is night for all beings, in that the self-controlled one is awake; and where all beings are awake, that is night for the seeing sage.
bg_1.line: What the crowd sleeps through, the wise stay awake to. What the crowd chases, the wise see past.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: The supreme reality is like night to all beings and the sage is awake in it; the world of duality in which beings are awake is night to the sage who sees.

prasang.title_en: The person of steady wisdom
prasang.summary: Arjuna asks how a steady person speaks, sits and walks. Krishna describes someone content within, unshaken by sorrow, master of the senses, and traces how dwelling on things leads to anger and ruin.
prasang.lesson: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
bg_1.sanskrit: एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति । स्थित्वाऽस्यामन्तकालेऽपि ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृच्छति ॥
bg_1.translation: This is the state of Brahman, Partha. Having reached it, one is not deluded. Abiding in it even at the hour of death, one attains the peace of Brahman.
bg_1.line: Rooted in this steadiness, you aren't lost, even at the very end.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: This is the state of abiding in Brahman after renouncing all; staying in it even in the last period of life one attains liberation in Brahman, how much more one who stays in it from youth.

prasang.title_en: The person of steady wisdom
prasang.summary: Arjuna asks how a steady person speaks, sits and walks. Krishna describes someone content within, unshaken by sorrow, master of the senses, and traces how dwelling on things leads to anger and ruin.
prasang.lesson: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

bg_1.speaker: Arjuna
bg_1.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna, who asks why he must act at all if understanding is higher.
bg_1.sanskrit: व्यामिश्रेणेव वाक्येन बुद्धिं मोहयसीव मे । तदेकं वद निश्चित्य येन श्रेयोऽहमाप्नुयाम् ॥
bg_1.translation: With these seemingly mixed words you confuse my mind. Tell me decisively that one thing by which I may reach the highest good.
bg_1.line: Your advice sounds mixed and confuses me. Tell me the one thing I should do.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: Arjuna takes the praise of knowledge and the command to act as contradictory; 'as if' shows the Lord's words are not truly mixed, only seem so to him.

prasang.title_en: Why doing your duty without attachment is better
prasang.summary: Arjuna is confused and asks for one clear answer. Krishna says no one can stop acting, that repressing the body while the mind indulges is self-deception, and that action beats inaction.
prasang.lesson: Not acting is still a choice; do the work that is yours.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna, who asks why he must act at all if understanding is higher.
bg_1.sanskrit: न कर्मणामनारम्भान्नैष्कर्म्यं पुरुषोऽश्नुते । न च संन्यसनादेव सिद्धिं समधिगच्छति ॥
bg_1.translation: Not by refraining from action does a person reach freedom from action, nor by mere renunciation does one attain perfection.
bg_1.line: You don't get free by not starting, and you don't get perfect by just walking away.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: actionlessness, the state of abiding in knowledge, is not reached by not undertaking actions; action purifies the mind and is the means to it.

prasang.title_en: Why doing your duty without attachment is better
prasang.summary: Arjuna is confused and asks for one clear answer. Krishna says no one can stop acting, that repressing the body while the mind indulges is self-deception, and that action beats inaction.
prasang.lesson: Not acting is still a choice; do the work that is yours.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna, who asks why he must act at all if understanding is higher.
bg_1.sanskrit: न हि कश्चित्क्षणमपि जातु तिष्ठत्यकर्मकृत् । कार्यते ह्यवशः कर्म सर्वः प्रकृतिजैर्गुणैः ॥
bg_1.translation: No one can remain even for a moment without doing something; everyone is made to act, helplessly, by the qualities born of nature.
bg_1.line: No one can stay without acting, even for a moment. Your nature keeps moving you.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: this is said of the unknowing; all are driven to act by sattva, rajas and tamas. The knower, unmoved by the gunas, is a separate case.

prasang.title_en: Why doing your duty without attachment is better
prasang.summary: Arjuna is confused and asks for one clear answer. Krishna says no one can stop acting, that repressing the body while the mind indulges is self-deception, and that action beats inaction.
prasang.lesson: Not acting is still a choice; do the work that is yours.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna, who asks why he must act at all if understanding is higher.
bg_1.sanskrit: कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन् । इन्द्रियार्थान्विमूढात्मा मिथ्याचारः स उच्यते ॥
bg_1.translation: One who restrains the organs of action but sits dwelling in the mind on sense objects is deluded and is called a hypocrite.
bg_1.line: Holding back your hands while your mind keeps feasting on the craving is self-deception.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: one who holds back hands and feet but keeps thinking of objects is of deluded mind, a mithyachara, one of false conduct.

prasang.title_en: Why doing your duty without attachment is better
prasang.summary: Arjuna is confused and asks for one clear answer. Krishna says no one can stop acting, that repressing the body while the mind indulges is self-deception, and that action beats inaction.
prasang.lesson: Not acting is still a choice; do the work that is yours.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna, who asks why he must act at all if understanding is higher.
bg_1.sanskrit: यस्त्विन्द्रियाणि मनसा नियम्यारभतेऽर्जुन । कर्मेन्द्रियैः कर्मयोगमसक्तः स विशिष्यते ॥
bg_1.translation: But one who controls the senses by the mind, Arjuna, and without attachment engages the organs of action in the yoga of action, excels.
bg_1.line: Better: guide your senses with your mind and get to work, without being hooked.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: The unknowing one who restrains the senses by the mind and begins karma yoga with the organs of action, unattached, is better than the hypocrite of 3.6.

prasang.title_en: Why doing your duty without attachment is better
prasang.summary: Arjuna is confused and asks for one clear answer. Krishna says no one can stop acting, that repressing the body while the mind indulges is self-deception, and that action beats inaction.
prasang.lesson: Not acting is still a choice; do the work that is yours.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna on the cycle of offering that sustains the world.
bg_1.sanskrit: देवान्भावयतानेन ते देवा भावयन्तु वः । परस्परं भावयन्तः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ ॥
bg_1.translation: Nourish the gods with this, and may the gods nourish you. Nourishing one another, you will attain the highest good.
bg_1.line: Nourish one another, and together you'll reach the highest good.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: With sacrifice nourish the gods, Indra and the rest, and let them nourish you with rain and the like; thus sustaining each other you will reach the highest good.

prasang.title_en: Why action as offering is needed
prasang.summary: Krishna describes action as offering, the mutual nourishing of humans and gods, and the wrong of taking without giving back.
prasang.lesson: Life works by give and take; taking only for yourself breaks the cycle.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna on the cycle of offering that sustains the world.
bg_1.sanskrit: यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्वकिल्बिषैः । भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात् ॥
bg_1.translation: The good who eat what remains after the offering are freed from all faults. But the wicked who cook only for themselves eat sin.
bg_1.line: Those who share first are freed; those who cook only for themselves feed on wrong.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Those who eat what is left after offering to the gods and the rest are freed from sins, including those of the household's five places of harm; those who cook only for themselves eat sin.

prasang.title_en: Why action as offering is needed
prasang.summary: Krishna describes action as offering, the mutual nourishing of humans and gods, and the wrong of taking without giving back.
prasang.lesson: Life works by give and take; taking only for yourself breaks the cycle.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on why even the fulfilled keep working for the world.
bg_1.sanskrit: यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः । आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते ॥
bg_1.translation: But for the person who delights only in the self, is satisfied with the self, and content in the self alone, there is nothing that must be done.
bg_1.line: One who is content and delighted in their own self has nothing left to prove.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: For the knower of the self, the renunciate whose delight and satisfaction are in the self and not in objects, there is nothing to be done.

prasang.title_en: Even the wise, even God, act for the world's sake
prasang.summary: The one content in the self has nothing left to gain, yet the wise, like Janaka and Krishna himself, keep working because others follow their example.
prasang.lesson: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on why even the fulfilled keep working for the world.
bg_1.sanskrit: न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन । नानवाप्तमवाप्तव्यं वर्त एव च कर्मणि ॥
bg_1.translation: There is nothing in the three worlds, Partha, that I must do, nothing unattained that I need to attain, and yet I continue to act.
bg_1.line: I have nothing left to gain anywhere, Krishna says, and still I keep working.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: the Lord has nothing to do or gain in the three worlds, yet he acts, since people follow his path and would be ruined if he did not.

prasang.title_en: Even the wise, even God, act for the world's sake
prasang.summary: The one content in the self has nothing left to gain, yet the wise, like Janaka and Krishna himself, keep working because others follow their example.
prasang.lesson: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on acting free of ego, like and dislike, in your own way.
bg_1.sanskrit: सक्ताः कर्मण्यविद्वांसो यथा कुर्वन्ति भारत । कुर्याद्विद्वांस्तथासक्तश्चिकीर्षुर्लोकसंग्रहम् ॥
bg_1.translation: As the unwise act with attachment to their work, Bharata, so should the wise act without attachment, wishing to hold the world together.
bg_1.line: Work as hard as the ambitious do, but for everyone's good, not your own grip on results.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: As the unknowing act with attachment to the fruit, the knower should act with the same diligence but unattached, wishing to protect the world.

prasang.title_en: The ignorant and the wise; act free of like and dislike
prasang.summary: Krishna contrasts the attached and the wise, warns that ego claims credit for what nature does, and says to follow your own path rather than imitate another's.
prasang.lesson: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on acting free of ego, like and dislike, in your own way.
bg_1.sanskrit: न बुद्धिभेदं जनयेदज्ञानां कर्मसङ्गिनाम् । जोषयेत्सर्वकर्माणि विद्वान् युक्तः समाचरन् ॥
bg_1.translation: The wise should not unsettle the minds of the ignorant who are attached to action. Working steadily themselves, they should encourage others in all their work.
bg_1.line: Don't unsettle people who are still learning by doing. Do the work well alongside them and show them.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: the knower should not disturb the conviction of the unwise who are attached to action; doing the same work himself with a steady mind, he should lead them to do it.

prasang.title_en: The ignorant and the wise; act free of like and dislike
prasang.summary: Krishna contrasts the attached and the wise, warns that ego claims credit for what nature does, and says to follow your own path rather than imitate another's.
prasang.lesson: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on acting free of ego, like and dislike, in your own way.
bg_1.sanskrit: प्रकृतेः क्रियमाणानि गुणैः कर्माणि सर्वशः । अहङ्कारविमूढात्मा कर्ताऽहमिति मन्यते ॥
bg_1.translation: All actions are done by the qualities of nature, but the one deluded by ego thinks, 'I am the doer.'
bg_1.line: Countless forces do the work; the ego, fooled, says 'I did it all'.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: actions are done by the gunas, the modifications of nature in the form of body and senses; one whose mind is deluded by ego, identifying with them, thinks 'I am the doer'.

prasang.title_en: The ignorant and the wise; act free of like and dislike
prasang.summary: Krishna contrasts the attached and the wise, warns that ego claims credit for what nature does, and says to follow your own path rather than imitate another's.
prasang.lesson: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on acting free of ego, like and dislike, in your own way.
bg_1.sanskrit: सदृशं चेष्टते स्वस्याः प्रकृतेर्ज्ञानवानपि । प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति ॥
bg_1.translation: Even a wise person acts according to his own nature. Beings follow their nature; what will mere repression do?
bg_1.line: Even wise people move as their nature moves them. Brute suppression achieves little.
bg_1.misuse: Not 'I can't change, it's my nature'. The next verse says not to come under the sway of likes and dislikes.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: nature is the impressions of past deeds showing up in this life; everyone acts by it. He then raises the objection that effort is useless, and 3.34 answers: do not come under like and dislike.

prasang.title_en: The ignorant and the wise; act free of like and dislike
prasang.summary: Krishna contrasts the attached and the wise, warns that ego claims credit for what nature does, and says to follow your own path rather than imitate another's.
prasang.lesson: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on acting free of ego, like and dislike, in your own way.
bg_1.sanskrit: इन्द्रियस्येन्द्रियस्यार्थे रागद्वेषौ व्यवस्थितौ । तयोर्न वशमागच्छेत्तौ ह्यस्य परिपन्थिनौ ॥
bg_1.translation: Attraction and aversion to sense objects lie seated in every sense. Do not come under their power; they are your enemies on the way.
bg_1.line: Liking and disliking lie in wait behind every sense. Don't let either take the wheel.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: this is the scope of human effort: nature moves a person only through like and dislike, so one who checks these with their opposite is no longer under nature's rule.

prasang.title_en: The ignorant and the wise; act free of like and dislike
prasang.summary: Krishna contrasts the attached and the wise, warns that ego claims credit for what nature does, and says to follow your own path rather than imitate another's.
prasang.lesson: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Arjuna asks what drives people to do wrong against their will; Krishna answers.
bg_1.sanskrit: धूमेनाव्रियते वह्निर्यथाऽऽदर्शो मलेन च । यथोल्बेनावृतो गर्भस्तथा तेनेदमावृतम् ॥
bg_1.translation: As fire is covered by smoke, a mirror by dust, and an embryo by the womb, so is this wisdom covered by desire.
bg_1.line: Like smoke over fire, dust on a mirror, desire covers your clear sight.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: 'this' is knowledge, as 3.39 states; desire covers it. Later commentators such as Madhusudana read the three images as three depths of covering, light, middling and thick.

prasang.title_en: Restraining desire
prasang.summary: Arjuna asks why we do wrong as if forced. Krishna names desire, which turns into anger, as the enemy that clouds wisdom like smoke over fire, and tells him to master it.
prasang.lesson: Desire unmet becomes anger; see it clearly and you can master it.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Arjuna asks what drives people to do wrong against their will; Krishna answers.
bg_1.sanskrit: आवृतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनो नित्यवैरिणा । कामरूपेण कौन्तेय दुष्पूरेणानलेन च ॥
bg_1.translation: Knowledge is covered, Kaunteya, by this constant enemy of the wise in the form of desire, an insatiable fire.
bg_1.line: Desire is a fire that never gets enough. It quietly covers even the wise person's clarity.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: The wise know it as an enemy even while desiring, the ignorant only afterwards; hence it is the constant enemy of the wise, hard to fill, like fire.

prasang.title_en: Restraining desire
prasang.summary: Arjuna asks why we do wrong as if forced. Krishna names desire, which turns into anger, as the enemy that clouds wisdom like smoke over fire, and tells him to master it.
prasang.lesson: Desire unmet becomes anger; see it clearly and you can master it.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Arjuna asks what drives people to do wrong against their will; Krishna answers.
bg_1.sanskrit: तस्मात्त्वमिन्द्रियाण्यादौ नियम्य भरतर्षभ । पाप्मानं प्रजहि ह्येनं ज्ञानविज्ञाननाशनम् ॥
bg_1.translation: Therefore, best of the Bharatas, first control the senses, then cast off this wrongdoer that destroys knowledge and discernment.
bg_1.line: So start with the senses. Get them in hand, then let go of the desire that wrecks clear thinking.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Therefore first restrain the senses and abandon this sinful one, desire, which destroys knowledge from scripture and teacher and its direct realisation.

prasang.title_en: Restraining desire
prasang.summary: Arjuna asks why we do wrong as if forced. Krishna names desire, which turns into anger, as the enemy that clouds wisdom like smoke over fire, and tells him to master it.
prasang.lesson: Desire unmet becomes anger; see it clearly and you can master it.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Arjuna asks what drives people to do wrong against their will; Krishna answers.
bg_1.sanskrit: इन्द्रियाणि पराण्याहुरिन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः । मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः ॥
bg_1.translation: The senses are said to be higher than the body; higher than the senses is the mind; higher than the mind is the intellect; and higher than the intellect is the self.
bg_1.line: Senses are strong, the mind stronger, clear judgement stronger still, and your true self strongest of all.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: The senses are superior to the gross body, the mind to the senses, the intellect to the mind; and the one who is beyond the intellect, the witness, is the supreme self.

prasang.title_en: Restraining desire
prasang.summary: Arjuna asks why we do wrong as if forced. Krishna names desire, which turns into anger, as the enemy that clouds wisdom like smoke over fire, and tells him to master it.
prasang.lesson: Desire unmet becomes anger; see it clearly and you can master it.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Arjuna asks what drives people to do wrong against their will; Krishna answers.
bg_1.sanskrit: एवं बुद्धेः परं बुद्ध्वा संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना । जहि शत्रुं महाबाहो कामरूपं दुरासदम् ॥
bg_1.translation: Thus knowing that which is higher than the intellect, steadying the self by the self, slay, mighty-armed one, this enemy in the form of desire, so hard to overcome.
bg_1.line: Knowing what is higher in you, steady yourself with yourself and defeat the desire that's hard to beat.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: knowing the self as beyond the intellect and composing the mind by the purified mind, slay the enemy in the form of desire.

prasang.title_en: Restraining desire
prasang.summary: Arjuna asks why we do wrong as if forced. Krishna names desire, which turns into anger, as the enemy that clouds wisdom like smoke over fire, and tells him to master it.
prasang.lesson: Desire unmet becomes anger; see it clearly and you can master it.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna reveals the ancient lineage of this teaching and why he comes into the world.
bg_1.sanskrit: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत । अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदाऽऽत्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ॥
bg_1.translation: Whenever there is a decline of dharma and a rise of adharma, Bharata, then I bring myself forth.
bg_1.line: Whenever goodness declines and wrong rises up, I come forth, Krishna promises.
bg_1.misuse: Not 'wait for rescue'. Many read it as a call to be the force that restores what is right.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: when the dharma of the stations of life declines and adharma rises, the Lord manifests himself through his own maya.

prasang.title_en: The Lord's power and the yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna says he taught this yoga long ago, that he appears whenever goodness declines, and that he meets people on whatever path they come by. He calls the way of action deep.
prasang.lesson: Every path sincerely walked is met; goodness keeps finding a way back.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna reveals the ancient lineage of this teaching and why he comes into the world.
bg_1.sanskrit: परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् । धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय संभवामि युगे युगे ॥
bg_1.translation: To protect the good, to destroy wrongdoing, and to firmly establish dharma, I take birth age after age.
bg_1.line: To protect the good, end the harm, and set right what's broken, I appear age after age.
bg_1.misuse: Not a licence to punish people you judge wicked; the work of setting right belongs to the divine and to justice.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: for protecting those on the right path, destroying doers of evil and firmly setting up dharma, he comes into being in every age.

prasang.title_en: The Lord's power and the yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna says he taught this yoga long ago, that he appears whenever goodness declines, and that he meets people on whatever path they come by. He calls the way of action deep.
prasang.lesson: Every path sincerely walked is met; goodness keeps finding a way back.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna reveals the ancient lineage of this teaching and why he comes into the world.
bg_1.sanskrit: वीतरागभयक्रोधा मन्मया मामुपाश्रिताः । बहवो ज्ञानतपसा पूता मद्भावमागताः ॥
bg_1.translation: Freed from passion, fear and anger, absorbed in me and taking refuge in me, many, purified by the austerity of knowledge, have come to my being.
bg_1.line: Many have dropped craving, fear and anger, been refined by wisdom, and found their way home.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Many, free of attachment, fear and anger, seeing no difference from the Lord and relying on him alone, purified by the austerity that is knowledge, have attained liberation.

prasang.title_en: The Lord's power and the yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna says he taught this yoga long ago, that he appears whenever goodness declines, and that he meets people on whatever path they come by. He calls the way of action deep.
prasang.lesson: Every path sincerely walked is met; goodness keeps finding a way back.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna reveals the ancient lineage of this teaching and why he comes into the world.
bg_1.sanskrit: ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते तांस्तथैव भजाम्यहम् । मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः ॥
bg_1.translation: In whatever way people approach me, in that same way I receive them. People follow my path in every way, Partha.
bg_1.line: However people come to me, I meet them there. Every path, in its own way, leads to me.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: the Lord rewards each in the way they seek him, giving fruits to those who want fruits and liberation to those who seek it. Sridhara: even those who worship other gods follow his path. The line's 'every path leads to me' follows the Sridhara reading.

prasang.title_en: The Lord's power and the yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna says he taught this yoga long ago, that he appears whenever goodness declines, and that he meets people on whatever path they come by. He calls the way of action deep.
prasang.lesson: Every path sincerely walked is met; goodness keeps finding a way back.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna reveals the ancient lineage of this teaching and why he comes into the world.
bg_1.sanskrit: कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः । स बुद्धिमान् मनुष्येषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्मकृत् ॥
bg_1.translation: One who sees inaction in action and action in inaction is wise among people; he is disciplined and does all his work.
bg_1.line: See the stillness inside activity and the activity inside stillness, and you're truly wise.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Action belongs to body and senses and is wrongly placed on the actionless self; one who sees the self as non-acting amid action, and sees that sitting idle is also an act of the body, is wise.

prasang.title_en: The Lord's power and the yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna says he taught this yoga long ago, that he appears whenever goodness declines, and that he meets people on whatever path they come by. He calls the way of action deep.
prasang.lesson: Every path sincerely walked is met; goodness keeps finding a way back.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how the wise live and work.
bg_1.sanskrit: त्यक्त्वा कर्मफलासङ्गं नित्यतृप्तो निराश्रयः । कर्मण्यभिप्रवृत्तोऽपि नैव किञ्चित्करोति सः ॥
bg_1.translation: Having given up attachment to the fruit of action, ever content and dependent on nothing, though fully engaged in action, he does nothing at all.
bg_1.line: Content and leaning on no one's approval, fully busy, and yet inwardly at rest.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: nirashraya is without dependence on any means to a desired end; because he sees the actionless self, he does nothing at all even while engaged in action.

prasang.title_en: How the great yogis live
prasang.summary: The wise act without selfish motive, content and dependent on nothing, free from envy, steady in success and failure.
prasang.lesson: Contentment and freedom from envy let you work without being bound.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how the wise live and work.
bg_1.sanskrit: निराशीर्यतचित्तात्मा त्यक्तसर्वपरिग्रहः । शारीरं केवलं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
bg_1.translation: Without hope, with mind and self controlled, giving up all possessiveness, doing only bodily action, he incurs no fault.
bg_1.line: Expecting nothing, mind steady, letting go of possessiveness, you can work without being stained.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: The renunciate without desires, mind and body controlled, having given up all possessions, doing only what keeps the body alive, incurs no sin.

prasang.title_en: How the great yogis live
prasang.summary: The wise act without selfish motive, content and dependent on nothing, free from envy, steady in success and failure.
prasang.lesson: Contentment and freedom from envy let you work without being bound.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna lists the many forms of offering people make.
bg_1.sanskrit: ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्महविर्ब्रह्माग्नौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम् । ब्रह्मैव तेन गन्तव्यं ब्रह्मकर्मसमाधिना ॥
bg_1.translation: The act of offering is Brahman, the offering is Brahman, poured by Brahman into the fire of Brahman. Brahman is reached by one who sees Brahman in every action.
bg_1.line: The offering, the giver, the fire, the act: see the sacred in all of it, and you reach the sacred.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: for the knower every element of the sacrifice is nothing but Brahman, so his action is in truth no action; the verse is traditionally recited before meals.

prasang.title_en: The many kinds of offering and their fruits
prasang.summary: Krishna lists kinds of sacrifice: of senses, breath, wealth, study, and more, and says all are born of action.
prasang.lesson: Every act, even eating, can be done as an offering.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the power of understanding to end confusion and guilt.
bg_1.sanskrit: न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते । तत्स्वयं योगसंसिद्धः कालेनात्मनि विन्दति ॥
bg_1.translation: There is nothing in this world as purifying as knowledge. One perfected in yoga finds it in oneself in due time.
bg_1.line: Nothing here cleanses like understanding, and with steady practice you find it within, in time.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: There is no purifier equal to knowledge; one made fit through karma yoga and the yoga of concentration finds it in himself after long time.

prasang.title_en: The glory of knowledge
prasang.summary: Krishna praises knowledge: learn it humbly from those who know, it carries even the worst wrongdoer across, faith and self-control bring it, and doubt destroys. He ends: cut your doubt and stand up.
prasang.lesson: Learn humbly, trust the process, and cut through doubt to act.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the power of understanding to end confusion and guilt.
bg_1.sanskrit: श्रद्धावाँल्लभते ज्ञानं तत्परः संयतेन्द्रियः । ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा परां शान्तिमचिरेणाधिगच्छति ॥
bg_1.translation: The person of faith, devoted to it and with senses controlled, gains knowledge. Having gained knowledge, he soon reaches supreme peace.
bg_1.line: Trust, commitment and self-control bring understanding, and understanding soon brings peace.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: faith, devotion to the means and control of the senses together bring knowledge without fail, and knowledge quickly brings the supreme peace of liberation.

prasang.title_en: The glory of knowledge
prasang.summary: Krishna praises knowledge: learn it humbly from those who know, it carries even the worst wrongdoer across, faith and self-control bring it, and doubt destroys. He ends: cut your doubt and stand up.
prasang.lesson: Learn humbly, trust the process, and cut through doubt to act.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the power of understanding to end confusion and guilt.
bg_1.sanskrit: अज्ञश्चाश्रद्दधानश्च संशयात्मा विनश्यति । नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयात्मनः ॥
bg_1.translation: The ignorant, faithless person of doubting mind perishes. For the doubting self there is neither this world, nor the next, nor happiness.
bg_1.line: A mind that doubts everything finds no happiness here or anywhere.
bg_1.misuse: Questioning is welcome in the Gita; Arjuna asks constantly. This is about corrosive doubt that blocks every step.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: the ignorant and the faithless perish, but the doubting mind is the worst of the three, for it gains neither this world, nor the next, nor happiness.

prasang.title_en: The glory of knowledge
prasang.summary: Krishna praises knowledge: learn it humbly from those who know, it carries even the worst wrongdoer across, faith and self-control bring it, and doubt destroys. He ends: cut your doubt and stand up.
prasang.lesson: Learn humbly, trust the process, and cut through doubt to act.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the power of understanding to end confusion and guilt.
bg_1.sanskrit: योगसंन्यस्तकर्माणं ज्ञानसंछिन्नसंशयम् । आत्मवन्तं न कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय ॥
bg_1.translation: Actions do not bind one who has renounced action through yoga, whose doubts are cut away by knowledge, and who is self-possessed, Dhananjaya.
bg_1.line: Doubts cut away by understanding, steady within, your actions stop binding you.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: One who has given up actions through the yoga of seeing the supreme truth, whose doubt is cut by knowledge of the oneness of self and Lord, and who is vigilant, is not bound.

prasang.title_en: The glory of knowledge
prasang.summary: Krishna praises knowledge: learn it humbly from those who know, it carries even the worst wrongdoer across, faith and self-control bring it, and doubt destroys. He ends: cut your doubt and stand up.
prasang.lesson: Learn humbly, trust the process, and cut through doubt to act.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Arjuna asks whether giving up action or acting selflessly is better; Krishna answers.
bg_1.sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचसंन्यासः कर्मयोगश्च निःश्रेयसकरावुभौ । तयोस्तु कर्मसंन्यासात्कर्मयोगो विशिष्यते ॥
bg_1.translation: The Blessed Lord said: Renunciation and the yoga of action both lead to the highest good. But of the two, the yoga of action is better than renunciation of action.
bg_1.line: Stepping back and acting selflessly both lead to good, but of the two, acting is better.
bg_1.misuse: Not 'never rest or retire'; it prefers engaged, selfless work over withdrawal.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: karma yoga is better than mere renunciation without knowledge; renunciation with knowledge is a separate matter. Ramanuja: karma yoga is easier and safer and contains knowledge within it.

prasang.title_en: Knowledge or action: the verdict
prasang.summary: Arjuna wants one clear verdict. Krishna says both lead to the good, but selfless action is better, and the true renouncer is the one who neither hates nor craves.
prasang.lesson: Real letting go is inner: no grudges, no grasping.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Arjuna asks whether giving up action or acting selflessly is better; Krishna answers.
bg_1.sanskrit: ज्ञेयः स नित्यसंन्यासी यो न द्वेष्टि न काङ्क्षति । निर्द्वन्द्वो हि महाबाहो सुखं बन्धात्प्रमुच्यते ॥
bg_1.translation: Know him to be ever a renouncer who neither hates nor desires. Free from the pairs of opposites, mighty-armed one, he is easily released from bondage.
bg_1.line: The one who neither resents nor craves is the real renouncer, wherever they live.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: the karma yogi who neither hates pain nor longs for pleasure is to be known as always a renouncer, even while acting.

prasang.title_en: Knowledge or action: the verdict
prasang.summary: Arjuna wants one clear verdict. Krishna says both lead to the good, but selfless action is better, and the true renouncer is the one who neither hates nor craves.
prasang.lesson: Real letting go is inner: no grudges, no grasping.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on working in the world without being stained by it.
bg_1.sanskrit: कायेन मनसा बुद्ध्या केवलैरिन्द्रियैरपि । योगिनः कर्म कुर्वन्ति सङ्गं त्यक्त्वाऽऽत्मशुद्धये ॥
bg_1.translation: With body, mind, intellect and even the senses alone, the yogis act without attachment, for the purification of the self.
bg_1.line: Wise people work with body, mind and heart, not for gain, but to become clearer within.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: 'Alone' means without the sense of 'mine' in body, mind, intellect and senses; yogis act so, giving up attachment to results, for purity of mind.

prasang.title_en: Marks of the knower and the doer
prasang.summary: The disciplined person acts without attachment, like a lotus leaf untouched by water, and finds peace by letting go of the fruit.
prasang.lesson: Be in the mess without letting it soak in.

bg_1.speaker: Krishna
bg_1.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on working in the world without being stained by it.
bg_1.sanskrit: युक्तः कर्मफलं त्यक्त्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति नैष्ठिकीम् । अयुक्तः कामकारेण फले सक्तो निबध्यते ॥
bg_1.translation: The disciplined person, giving up the fruit of action, attains lasting peace. The undisciplined, attached to the fruit and driven by desire, is bound.
bg_1.line: Let go of the payoff and you find lasting peace. Chase it and it chains you.
bg_1.misuse: Letting go of the payoff isn't refusing fair pay or recognition; it's not being chained to it.
bg_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_1.our_note: Shankara: the one who acts for the Lord and gives up the fruit gains the peace that comes of steadfastness, by stages; the other, driven by desire, is bound.

prasang.title_en: Marks of the knower and the doer
prasang.summary: The disciplined person acts without attachment, like a lotus leaf untouched by water, and finds peace by letting go of the fruit.
prasang.lesson: Be in the mess without letting it soak in.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the inner happiness of one who sees clearly.
bg_2.sanskrit: इहैव तैर्जितः सर्गो येषां साम्ये स्थितं मनः । निर्दोषं हि समं ब्रह्म तस्माद्ब्रह्मणि ते स्थिताः ॥
bg_2.translation: Even here the world is conquered by those whose minds are established in evenness. Brahman is flawless and the same in all; so they are established in Brahman.
bg_2.line: Those whose minds rest in evenness have already won, right here in this life.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Even while living, birth is overcome by those whose mind stays in the sameness of Brahman in all beings; Brahman is untouched by the defects of bodies.

prasang.title_en: The yoga of knowledge
prasang.summary: Krishna describes the wise: equal-eyed towards all beings, not elated or crushed, finding joy within, seeing that sense pleasures end in sorrow, and able to withstand desire and anger.
prasang.lesson: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the inner happiness of one who sees clearly.
bg_2.sanskrit: न प्रहृष्येत्प्रियं प्राप्य नोद्विजेत्प्राप्य चाप्रियम् । स्थिरबुद्धिरसम्मूढो ब्रह्मविद्ब्रह्मणि स्थितः ॥
bg_2.translation: One should not rejoice on getting what is pleasant nor be troubled on getting what is unpleasant. Steady in understanding and undeluded, the knower of Brahman abides in Brahman.
bg_2.line: Don't get carried away by good news or crushed by bad. Keep your understanding steady.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Shankara: only those who take the body as the self are elated and dejected by the pleasant and unpleasant; the knower of Brahman, who sees the one faultless self, is not.

prasang.title_en: The yoga of knowledge
prasang.summary: Krishna describes the wise: equal-eyed towards all beings, not elated or crushed, finding joy within, seeing that sense pleasures end in sorrow, and able to withstand desire and anger.
prasang.lesson: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the inner happiness of one who sees clearly.
bg_2.sanskrit: ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते । आद्यन्तवन्तः कौन्तेय न तेषु रमते बुधः ॥
bg_2.translation: The enjoyments born of contact are wombs of sorrow; they have a beginning and an end, Kaunteya. The wise do not delight in them.
bg_2.line: Pleasures born of contact have a beginning and an end and breed sorrow. The wise don't stake their joy there.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Shankara: enjoyments born of the contact of senses and objects are sources of sorrow here and hereafter and have a beginning and an end; the one who sees the truth finds no delight in them.

prasang.title_en: The yoga of knowledge
prasang.summary: Krishna describes the wise: equal-eyed towards all beings, not elated or crushed, finding joy within, seeing that sense pleasures end in sorrow, and able to withstand desire and anger.
prasang.lesson: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the inner happiness of one who sees clearly.
bg_2.sanskrit: लभन्ते ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृषयः क्षीणकल्मषाः । छिन्नद्वैधा यतात्मानः सर्वभूतहिते रताः ॥
bg_2.translation: Seers whose faults are destroyed, whose doubts are cut away, who are self-controlled and delight in the welfare of all beings, attain the peace of Brahman.
bg_2.line: Doubts cut away, mind mastered, they give themselves to the good of all beings and find peace.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Seers of right vision, sins worn away, doubts cut, senses controlled, intent on the good of all and harming none, attain liberation.

prasang.title_en: The yoga of knowledge
prasang.summary: Krishna describes the wise: equal-eyed towards all beings, not elated or crushed, finding joy within, seeing that sense pleasures end in sorrow, and able to withstand desire and anger.
prasang.lesson: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, briefly describing meditation and the peace it brings.
bg_2.sanskrit: यतेन्द्रियमनोबुद्धिर्मुनिर्मोक्षपरायणः । विगतेच्छाभयक्रोधो यः सदा मुक्त एव सः ॥
bg_2.translation: The sage whose senses, mind and intellect are controlled, who is intent on freedom, and from whom desire, fear and anger have gone, is truly free forever.
bg_2.line: Senses, mind and judgement in hand, free of desire, fear and anger: that person is already free.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: The renunciate who shuts out outer contacts, controls senses, mind and intellect and is free of desire, fear and anger is always liberated; nothing further remains for him.

prasang.title_en: Meditation with devotion
prasang.summary: A short sketch of meditation: senses withdrawn, free of desire, fear and anger, knowing the divine as the friend of all beings.
prasang.lesson: You are not alone: the divine is the friend of every being.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on who is truly a renouncer.
bg_2.sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचअनाश्रितः कर्मफलं कार्यं कर्म करोति यः । स संन्यासी च योगी च न निरग्निर्न चाक्रियः ॥
bg_2.translation: The Blessed Lord said: One who does the work that ought to be done, without depending on its fruit, is the renouncer and the yogi; not the one who gives up the sacred fire or gives up action.
bg_2.line: The real renouncer does the work that's needed without leaning on its rewards, not the one who quits.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Shankara: this praises the karma yogi who gives up the fruit: he too is a renouncer and yogi in a secondary sense, not only the one who has given up the ritual fire and action.

prasang.title_en: Action, and the one established in yoga
prasang.summary: The true renouncer is the one who does the work that ought to be done without depending on its fruit, not the one who simply stops.
prasang.lesson: Quitting isn't renouncing; working without clinging is.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
bg_2.sanskrit: बन्धुरात्माऽऽत्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः । अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत् ॥
bg_2.translation: For one who has conquered himself, the self is the friend of the self. But for one who has not, the self acts with hostility, like an enemy.
bg_2.line: Master yourself and you become your own best friend. Don't, and your own mind works against you like an enemy.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Shankara: the self is a friend to one who has subdued the body, senses and mind; for one who has not, his own self acts against him like an outside enemy.

prasang.title_en: Lift yourself by yourself; marks of the realised
prasang.summary: Raise yourself by yourself; you are your own friend or enemy. The self-mastered person stays calm in heat and cold, praise and blame, and sees friend and foe alike.
prasang.lesson: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
bg_2.sanskrit: जितात्मनः प्रशान्तस्य परमात्मा समाहितः । शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु तथा मानापमानयोः ॥
bg_2.translation: For one who has conquered himself and is at peace, the higher self stays steady in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, honour and dishonour.
bg_2.line: Self-mastered and calm, you stay centred in heat and cold, pleasure and pain, praise and insult.
bg_2.misuse: Staying steady under insult is not accepting mistreatment; you can stay calm and still speak up.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Shankara: for the one who has mastered himself and is serene, the supreme Self becomes directly his own self, and he is even in cold and heat, honour and dishonour.

prasang.title_en: Lift yourself by yourself; marks of the realised
prasang.summary: Raise yourself by yourself; you are your own friend or enemy. The self-mastered person stays calm in heat and cold, praise and blame, and sees friend and foe alike.
prasang.lesson: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
bg_2.sanskrit: ज्ञानविज्ञानतृप्तात्मा कूटस्थो विजितेन्द्रियः । युक्त इत्युच्यते योगी समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः ॥
bg_2.translation: The yogi whose self is satisfied with knowledge and understanding, who is unshakeable, master of the senses, to whom a clod, a stone and gold are the same, is called steadfast.
bg_2.line: To the settled mind, a lump of earth, a stone and a bar of gold are worth the same.
bg_2.misuse: Not a reason to neglect money or family finances; it is about not being ruled by them.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Knowledge is understanding what scripture teaches and vijnana is making it one's own experience; satisfied by these, unshakeable, he is called established in yoga.

prasang.title_en: Lift yourself by yourself; marks of the realised
prasang.summary: Raise yourself by yourself; you are your own friend or enemy. The self-mastered person stays calm in heat and cold, praise and blame, and sees friend and foe alike.
prasang.lesson: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
bg_2.sanskrit: सुहृन्मित्रार्युदासीनमध्यस्थद्वेष्यबन्धुषु । साधुष्वपि च पापेषु समबुद्धिर्विशिष्यते ॥
bg_2.translation: One who is even-minded towards well-wishers, friends, enemies, the indifferent, the neutral, the hateful, relatives, the good and the wicked, excels.
bg_2.line: Friend, enemy, stranger, relative, saint or wrongdoer: the one who sees all with an even mind stands highest.
bg_2.misuse: Even-minded is not naive; you can treat someone fairly and still keep a boundary.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Shankara: the one who does not judge 'who is this, what has he done' toward any of these, good or sinful, is the best among those established in yoga.

prasang.title_en: Lift yourself by yourself; marks of the realised
prasang.summary: Raise yourself by yourself; you are your own friend or enemy. The self-mastered person stays calm in heat and cold, praise and blame, and sees friend and foe alike.
prasang.lesson: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
bg_2.sanskrit: नात्यश्नतस्तु योगोऽस्ति न चैकान्तमनश्नतः । न चातिस्वप्नशीलस्य जाग्रतो नैव चार्जुन ॥
