bg_2.translation: Yoga is not for one who eats too much, nor for one who does not eat at all; not for one who sleeps too much, nor for one who keeps awake too long, Arjuna.
bg_2.line: Balance isn't for those who eat too much or too little, or sleep too much or too little.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Shankara: yoga does not come to one who eats beyond his measure or not at all, nor to one who sleeps or wakes too much.

prasang.title_en: Meditation in detail
prasang.summary: Krishna describes meditation: moderation in food and sleep, the mind like a lamp in a windless place, bringing the wandering mind back, and feeling others' joy and pain as one's own.
prasang.lesson: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
bg_2.sanskrit: यत्रोपरमते चित्तं निरुद्धं योगसेवया । यत्र चैवात्मनाऽऽत्मानं पश्यन्नात्मनि तुष्यति ॥
bg_2.translation: When the mind, restrained by the practice of yoga, becomes still, and one sees the self by the self, one is content in the self.
bg_2.line: When the mind finally goes still, you see yourself as you are, and you're content.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: When the mind, restrained by practice of yoga, withdraws, and one sees the self, the supreme light, by the purified inner organ, one is satisfied in the self.

prasang.title_en: Meditation in detail
prasang.summary: Krishna describes meditation: moderation in food and sleep, the mind like a lamp in a windless place, bringing the wandering mind back, and feeling others' joy and pain as one's own.
prasang.lesson: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
bg_2.sanskrit: यं लब्ध्वा चापरं लाभं मन्यते नाधिकं ततः । यस्मिन्स्थितो न दुःखेन गुरुणापि विचाल्यते ॥
bg_2.translation: Having gained it, one thinks no other gain greater; established in it, one is not shaken even by heavy sorrow.
bg_2.line: Find the gain beyond all gains, and even heavy sorrow can't shake you.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Shankara: having gained the self, one thinks no other gain higher; established in the truth of the self, one is not moved even by great pain such as a sword stroke.

prasang.title_en: Meditation in detail
prasang.summary: Krishna describes meditation: moderation in food and sleep, the mind like a lamp in a windless place, bringing the wandering mind back, and feeling others' joy and pain as one's own.
prasang.lesson: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
bg_2.sanskrit: प्रशान्तमनसं ह्येनं योगिनं सुखमुत्तमम् । उपैति शान्तरजसं ब्रह्मभूतमकल्मषम् ॥
bg_2.translation: Supreme happiness comes to the yogi whose mind is calm, whose passions are stilled, who is free from wrong and one with Brahman.
bg_2.line: A calm mind, its turmoil settled, finds the highest happiness.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: The highest happiness comes to this yogi of tranquil mind, whose rajas, the afflictions such as delusion, has subsided, who is free of taint and has become Brahman.

prasang.title_en: Meditation in detail
prasang.summary: Krishna describes meditation: moderation in food and sleep, the mind like a lamp in a windless place, bringing the wandering mind back, and feeling others' joy and pain as one's own.
prasang.lesson: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
bg_2.sanskrit: सर्वभूतस्थमात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि । ईक्षते योगयुक्तात्मा सर्वत्र समदर्शनः ॥
bg_2.translation: One whose self is joined in yoga sees the self in all beings and all beings in the self; he sees the same everywhere.
bg_2.line: See yourself in every being and every being in yourself, and you see the same everywhere.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: One whose mind is absorbed in yoga sees his own self present in all beings from Brahma to a clump of grass, and all beings as one with the self.

prasang.title_en: Meditation in detail
prasang.summary: Krishna describes meditation: moderation in food and sleep, the mind like a lamp in a windless place, bringing the wandering mind back, and feeling others' joy and pain as one's own.
prasang.lesson: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

bg_2.speaker: Arjuna
bg_2.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
bg_2.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचयोऽयं योगस्त्वया प्रोक्तः साम्येन मधुसूदन । एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात् स्थितिं स्थिराम् ॥
bg_2.translation: Arjuna said: This yoga of evenness that you have taught, Madhusudana, I do not see how it can last, because of restlessness.
bg_2.line: This calm you describe, Krishna, I can't see it lasting. My mind is too restless.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Arjuna, seeing how hard the yoga of right vision is, says he does not see its steady continuance because the mind is fickle.

prasang.title_en: Mastering the mind
prasang.summary: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Krishna agrees, and says practice and letting go can train it.
prasang.lesson: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

bg_2.speaker: Arjuna
bg_2.setting: Arjuna asks what becomes of someone who tries and fails; Krishna reassures him.
bg_2.sanskrit: कच्चिन्नोभयविभ्रष्टश्छिन्नाभ्रमिव नश्यति । अप्रतिष्ठो महाबाहो विमूढो ब्रह्मणः पथि ॥
bg_2.translation: Fallen from both, does he not perish like a broken cloud, without support, mighty-armed one, bewildered on the path to Brahman?
bg_2.line: Fallen from both sides, does he scatter like a torn cloud, with nowhere to stand?
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Shankara: fallen from both the path of action and the path of yoga, does he perish like a cloud torn from one mass and not joined to another?

prasang.title_en: What becomes of one who falls from yoga
prasang.summary: Arjuna fears that one who falls short is lost like a torn cloud. Krishna promises that no one who does good comes to ruin; past effort carries forward and they strive again.
prasang.lesson: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.

bg_2.speaker: Arjuna
bg_2.setting: Arjuna, afraid of failing halfway on the inner path, turns to Krishna.
bg_2.sanskrit: एतन्मे संशयं कृष्ण छेत्तुमर्हस्यशेषतः । त्वदन्यः संशयस्यास्य छेत्ता न ह्युपपद्यते ॥
bg_2.translation: Krishna, please cut away this doubt of mine completely. No one but you can remove it.
bg_2.line: Only you can clear this doubt completely. There is no one else I can ask.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: No sage or god other than the Lord can destroy this doubt, so he alone should cut it.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Arjuna asks what becomes of someone who tries and fails; Krishna reassures him.
bg_2.sanskrit: तत्र तं बुद्धिसंयोगं लभते पौर्वदेहिकम् । यतते च ततो भूयः संसिद्धौ कुरुनन्दन ॥
bg_2.translation: There he regains the understanding of his former life, and from there strives again, more than before, for perfection, joy of the Kurus.
bg_2.line: What you learned before isn't lost. You pick it up again and push on harder.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: In that birth he regains the understanding acquired in the earlier body and strives more intensely than before for perfection.

prasang.title_en: What becomes of one who falls from yoga
prasang.summary: Arjuna fears that one who falls short is lost like a torn cloud. Krishna promises that no one who does good comes to ruin; past effort carries forward and they strive again.
prasang.lesson: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Arjuna asks what becomes of someone who tries and fails; Krishna reassures him.
bg_2.sanskrit: पूर्वाभ्यासेन तेनैव ह्रियते ह्यवशोऽपि सः । जिज्ञासुरपि योगस्य शब्दब्रह्मातिवर्तते ॥
bg_2.translation: By that former practice he is carried on, even against his will. Even one who merely wishes to know yoga goes beyond the ritual word.
bg_2.line: Past practice carries you forward, even when you don't feel like it.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: He is drawn on by the force of the earlier practice even against his will; even one who only wishes to know yoga rises above the fruit of Vedic ritual.

prasang.title_en: What becomes of one who falls from yoga
prasang.summary: Arjuna fears that one who falls short is lost like a torn cloud. Krishna promises that no one who does good comes to ruin; past effort carries forward and they strive again.
prasang.lesson: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Arjuna asks what becomes of someone who tries and fails; Krishna reassures him.
bg_2.sanskrit: प्रयत्नाद्यतमानस्तु योगी संशुद्धकिल्बिषः । अनेकजन्मसंसिद्धस्ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥
bg_2.translation: But the yogi who strives with diligence, cleansed of faults, perfected through many births, then reaches the highest goal.
bg_2.line: The one who keeps at it, steadily, over a long time, gets there.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Gathering a little merit in each of many births, the striving yogi becomes perfected and then, with right vision, reaches the highest goal.

prasang.title_en: What becomes of one who falls from yoga
prasang.summary: Arjuna fears that one who falls short is lost like a torn cloud. Krishna promises that no one who does good comes to ruin; past effort carries forward and they strive again.
prasang.lesson: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna opens the teaching on knowing him fully.
bg_2.sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचमय्यासक्तमनाः पार्थ योगं युञ्जन्मदाश्रयः । असंशयं समग्रं मां यथा ज्ञास्यसि तच्छृणु ॥
bg_2.translation: Hear, Partha, how with your mind attached to me, practising yoga and taking refuge in me, you will know me fully, without doubt.
bg_2.line: Keep your mind attached to me, lean on me, keep practising. You will come to know me fully.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: With mind fixed on the Lord, taking him alone as refuge and practising yoga, you will know him completely, with his powers and glory, without doubt.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna explains how everything holds together in him.
bg_2.sanskrit: मत्तः परतरं नान्यत्किञ्चिदस्ति धनञ्जय । मयि सर्वमिदं प्रोतं सूत्रे मणिगणा इव ॥
bg_2.translation: There is nothing higher than me, Dhananjaya. All this is strung on me like pearls on a thread.
bg_2.line: Everything is strung on me like pearls on a single thread.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: There is no other cause beyond the supreme Lord; all beings and the whole universe are woven on him like cloth on threads, like beads on a string.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the divine within all things.
bg_2.sanskrit: बलं बलवतामस्मि कामरागविवर्जितम् । धर्माविरुद्धो भूतेषु कामोऽस्मि भरतर्षभ ॥
bg_2.translation: Of the strong, I am the strength free from desire and passion. In beings, I am desire that is not contrary to dharma, best of the Bharatas.
bg_2.line: In the strong, I am strength without greed or grasping. In all, I am desire that stays within what's right.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Shankara: kama is thirst for what is not had and raga is attachment to what is had; strength free of both, needed only to keep the body, is the Lord; so is desire not against scripture, such as for food and drink.

prasang.title_en: The Lord as the cause within all things
prasang.summary: Krishna says he is the taste in water and the light in sun and moon, strength without greed, and desire that does not oppose what is right.
prasang.lesson: Strength and desire are good when free of greed and within what's right.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna admits the confusion of the world is hard to get through, and says who gets through it.
bg_2.sanskrit: दैवी ह्येषा गुणमयी मम माया दुरत्यया । मामेव ये प्रपद्यन्ते मायामेतां तरन्ति ते ॥
bg_2.translation: This divine power of mine, made of the three qualities, is very hard to get past. Those who take refuge in me alone cross beyond it.
bg_2.line: This tangle is hard to get through. Those who take shelter in me get through it.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Shankara: this maya, made of the gunas and belonging to the Lord, is hard to overcome; those who give up all else and take refuge in him alone, their own self, cross it. Ramanuja: surrender is the only means of crossing.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna has named four kinds of people who turn to him, including the distressed and the one in need.
bg_2.sanskrit: उदाराः सर्व एवैते ज्ञानी त्वात्मैव मे मतम् । आस्थितः स हि युक्तात्मा मामेवानुत्तमां गतिम् ॥
bg_2.translation: All of these are generous souls, but the wise one I regard as my very self, for with mind steadfast he has taken me as the highest goal.
bg_2.line: Everyone who turns to me, even in need, is noble. The one who loves me is my very self.
bg_2.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Shankara: all are noble, but the knower is the Lord's very self, not other than him. Ramanuja: the Lord cannot sustain himself without such a devotee, so he calls him his self.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna on worship of other deities.
bg_2.sanskrit: यो यो यां यां तनुं भक्तः श्रद्धयार्चितुमिच्छति । तस्य तस्याचलां श्रद्धां तामेव विदधाम्यहम् ॥
bg_2.translation: Whatever form any devotee wishes to worship with faith, I make that very faith of his unshakeable.
bg_2.line: Whatever form someone chooses to worship with faith, I make that faith steady.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Whatever divine form a desirous devotee wishes to worship with faith, the Lord makes firm that same faith; the fruit they get is finite (7.23).

prasang.title_en: Worship of other deities
prasang.summary: Those who worship other forms with faith have that faith made steady by Krishna, though their gains are limited.
prasang.lesson: Sincere faith, in whatever form, is strengthened.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna on those who miss him and those who know him.
bg_2.sanskrit: इच्छाद्वेषसमुत्थेन द्वन्द्वमोहेन भारत । सर्वभूतानि संमोहं सर्गे यान्ति परन्तप ॥
bg_2.translation: Through the delusion of the pairs of opposites, arising from desire and aversion, Bharata, all beings fall into confusion at birth, scorcher of enemies.
bg_2.line: From the pull of want and push of dislike comes the confusion that traps every being.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: By the delusion of the pairs, born of desire for the pleasant and aversion to the unpleasant, the intellect of all beings is overpowered from birth, so knowledge of the self does not arise.

prasang.title_en: Those who miss the Lord and those who know him
prasang.summary: The deluded see only the outer form; desire and aversion confuse all beings. Those freed from confusion come to know the divine fully.
prasang.lesson: Pull and push of like and dislike are what confuse us.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Arjuna asks seven questions about the self and death; Krishna answers.
bg_2.sanskrit: यं यं वापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम् । तं तमेवैति कौन्तेय सदा तद्भावभावितः ॥
bg_2.translation: Whatever state of being a person remembers when leaving the body at the end, to that he goes, Kaunteya, always shaped by that state.
bg_2.line: Whatever you keep thinking about shapes who you become, right to the end.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Shankara: whatever being one thinks of at the time of death one attains, because of lifelong dwelling on it; hence the instruction in 8.7 to remember the Lord always.

prasang.title_en: Arjuna's seven questions and their answers
prasang.summary: Krishna defines key terms and says that what one dwells on at death shapes where one goes, so remember the divine always and keep working.
prasang.lesson: What you dwell on shapes who you become.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Arjuna asks seven questions about the self and death; Krishna answers.
bg_2.sanskrit: तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु मामनुस्मर युध्य च । मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्मामेवैष्यस्यसंशयम् ॥
bg_2.translation: Therefore remember me at all times, and fight. With mind and understanding offered to me, you will surely come to me.
bg_2.line: So remember the divine at all times, and keep doing your work.
bg_2.misuse: 'Fight' here means do your rightful work; it is not a call to pick battles.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Shankara: remember the Lord at all times as scripture teaches and do your own duty of battle; with mind and intellect fixed on him you will reach him.

prasang.title_en: Arjuna's seven questions and their answers
prasang.summary: Krishna defines key terms and says that what one dwells on at death shapes where one goes, so remember the divine always and keep working.
prasang.lesson: What you dwell on shapes who you become.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna on steady remembrance and the cycles of creation.
bg_2.sanskrit: अभ्यासयोगयुक्तेन चेतसा नान्यगामिना । परमं पुरुषं दिव्यं याति पार्थानुचिन्तयन् ॥
bg_2.translation: With a mind disciplined by the practice of yoga and not straying to anything else, meditating constantly, one goes to the supreme divine Person, Partha.
bg_2.line: With a mind trained by practice and not wandering elsewhere, you reach what you meditate on.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Practice is the repetition of the same thought of the Lord, unbroken by other thoughts; with a mind so engaged, one reaches the supreme Person.

prasang.title_en: The yoga of devotion
prasang.summary: Krishna describes meditating at the time of death, the cosmic days and nights of Brahma, and the imperishable beyond them.
prasang.lesson: A mind trained by practice reaches what it rests on.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna tells Arjuna how near he is to those who keep him in mind.
bg_2.sanskrit: अनन्यचेताः सततं यो मां स्मरति नित्यशः । तस्याहं सुलभः पार्थ नित्ययुक्तस्य योगिनः ॥
bg_2.translation: O son of Pritha, whoever remembers me constantly, every day, with a mind turned to nothing else, for that steady seeker I am easy to reach.
bg_2.line: For the one who keeps remembering me, I am easy to reach.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: For the yogi who remembers the Lord without break, for as long as he lives, with mind on nothing else, the Lord is easily attained.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna explains how all beings rest in him without being cramped.
bg_2.sanskrit: यथाऽऽकाशस्थितो नित्यं वायुः सर्वत्रगो महान् । तथा सर्वाणि भूतानि मत्स्थानीत्युपधारय ॥
bg_2.translation: As the mighty wind, moving everywhere, always rests in space, know that all beings rest in me.
bg_2.line: As the wind, wherever it blows, always rests in the sky, all beings rest in me.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: As the great wind, going everywhere, stays always in space without touching it, so all beings stay in the Lord, who is all-pervading like space, without contact.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna describes his relationship to the world.
bg_2.sanskrit: पिताऽहमस्य जगतो माता धाता पितामहः । वेद्यं पवित्रमोंकार ऋक् साम यजुरेव च ॥
bg_2.translation: I am the father of this world, the mother, the one who holds it up, the grandfather; what is to be known, the purifier, the syllable Om, and the Rig, Sama and Yajur Vedas.
bg_2.line: I am the father of this world, and its mother, and the one who holds it all up.
bg_2.misuse: Not a replacement for a parent who is gone; a reassurance that care runs through everything.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: He is the father and mother of the world, the dispenser of the fruits of action, the grandfather, the thing to be known, the purifier and the syllable Om.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on simple, wholehearted devotion.
bg_2.sanskrit: मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु । मामेवैष्यसि युक्त्वैवमात्मानं मत्परायणः ॥
bg_2.translation: Fix your mind on me, be devoted to me, sacrifice to me, bow to me. Having joined yourself to me, with me as your goal, you will come to me.
bg_2.line: Fix your mind on me, love me, honour me, bow to me. Joined this way, you come to me.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Shankara: with mind on the Lord, devoted, worshipping and bowing to him, having steadied the mind, with him as the supreme goal, you will reach him, the self. Repeated at 18.65 with a promise.

prasang.title_en: The glory of selfless devotion
prasang.summary: A leaf, flower, fruit or water offered with love is accepted. Offer everything you do; the divine hates no one, and even a wrongdoer who turns wholeheartedly is counted good.
prasang.lesson: Small offerings given with love matter; no one is beyond turning around.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna begins chapter 10, speaking to Arjuna as to someone he loves.
bg_2.sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचभूय एव महाबाहो श्रृणु मे परमं वचः । यत्तेऽहं प्रीयमाणाय वक्ष्यामि हितकाम्यया ॥
bg_2.translation: Listen once more, mighty-armed, to my supreme word, which I will speak for your good, because you delight in it and are dear to me.
bg_2.line: Listen again. I am telling you this for your good, because you are dear to me.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: The Lord speaks again of his own accord, wishing Arjuna's good, because Arjuna is delighted by his words as by drinking nectar.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna on devotees who find joy together and the light he gives them.
bg_2.sanskrit: मच्चित्ता मद्गतप्राणा बोधयन्तः परस्परम् । कथयन्तश्च मां नित्यं तुष्यन्ति च रमन्ति च ॥
bg_2.translation: With minds fixed on me and lives given to me, enlightening one another and always speaking of me, they are content and delighted.
bg_2.line: Their minds on me, they talk of me with each other, and find joy and contentment in it.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Shankara: with minds on the Lord and lives given to him, teaching one another and speaking of him, they find contentment and delight as if meeting a beloved.

prasang.title_en: The yoga of devotion and its fruit
prasang.summary: Devotees talk of the divine with each other and find joy; out of compassion Krishna lights the lamp of knowledge in their hearts.
prasang.lesson: Good company and an inner lamp clear the dark.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna names the chief glories in which the divine shows itself.
bg_2.sanskrit: अहमात्मा गुडाकेश सर्वभूताशयस्थितः । अहमादिश्च मध्यं च भूतानामन्त एव च ॥
bg_2.translation: I am the self, Gudakesha, seated in the hearts of all beings. I am the beginning, the middle and the end of beings.
bg_2.line: I am the self seated in every heart: the beginning, middle and end of all beings.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Shankara: the Lord is the inner self to be meditated on always, dwelling in the heart of all beings; one unable to do that may meditate on him in the glories that follow.

prasang.title_en: Krishna describes his glories
prasang.summary: Krishna lists his manifestations: among lights the sun, among rivers the Ganga, and ends by saying any excellence is a spark of his splendour.
prasang.lesson: Whatever excellence you admire is a spark of the divine.

bg_2.speaker: Arjuna
bg_2.setting: Arjuna, shown Krishna's cosmic form, is overwhelmed by its scale.
bg_2.sanskrit: नभःस्पृशं दीप्तमनेकवर्णंव्यात्ताननं दीप्तविशालनेत्रम् । दृष्ट्वा हि त्वां प्रव्यथितान्तरात्माधृतिं न विन्दामि शमं च विष्णो ॥
bg_2.translation: Seeing you touching the sky, blazing with many colours, mouths wide open, with huge fiery eyes, my inner self trembles, Vishnu, and I find neither courage nor peace.
bg_2.line: Seeing something too big to take in, my heart trembles and I can't find steadiness or calm.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Plain sense: before the terrible cosmic form Arjuna's inner self is shaken and he finds neither firmness nor peace.

prasang.title_en: Arjuna sees the cosmic form and praises it
prasang.summary: Arjuna sees all beings, gods and worlds in Krishna, and warriors rushing into his mouths like moths into flame. Terrified, he asks who Krishna really is.
prasang.lesson: Facing something vast can shake you to the core, and that's human.

bg_2.speaker: Arjuna
bg_2.setting: Having seen Krishna's cosmic form, Arjuna realises how casually he treated his closest friend.
bg_2.sanskrit: सखेति मत्वा प्रसभं यदुक्तंहे कृष्ण हे यादव हे सखेति । अजानता महिमानं तवेदंमया प्रमादात्प्रणयेन वापि ॥ यच्चावहासार्थमसत्कृतोऽसिविहारशय्यासनभोजनेषु । एकोऽथवाप्यच्युत तत्समक्षंतत्क्षामये त्वामहमप्रमेयम् ॥
bg_2.translation: Whatever I said rashly, thinking of you as a friend, 'O Krishna, O Yadava, O friend', not knowing your greatness, out of carelessness or affection, and whatever disrespect I showed you in jest, while at play, resting, sitting or eating, alone or in company, I ask your forgiveness for it, immeasurable one.
bg_2.line: I treated you casually, as just a friend, never seeing how great you were.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Plain sense, shared by the commentators: seeing the cosmic form, Arjuna begs pardon for what he said out of carelessness or affection, treating the Lord as a companion.

prasang.title_en: Terrified, Arjuna prays to see the gentle four-armed form
prasang.summary: Trembling, Arjuna praises Krishna, asks pardon for having treated him as just a friend, begs him to bear with him as a father, friend or lover would, and asks to see his familiar form.
prasang.lesson: We take those closest to us for granted; it is never too late to say sorry.

bg_2.speaker: Arjuna
bg_2.setting: Having seen Krishna's greatness, Arjuna remembers years of casual friendship.
bg_2.sanskrit: यच्चावहासार्थमसत्कृतोऽसिविहारशय्यासनभोजनेषु । एकोऽथवाप्यच्युत तत्समक्षंतत्क्षामये त्वामहमप्रमेयम् ॥
bg_2.translation: Whatever disrespect I showed you in jest, while playing, resting, sitting or eating, alone or in front of others, Achyuta, I ask forgiveness of you, the immeasurable.
bg_2.line: For every careless joke, every time I took you for granted, alone or in company, forgive me.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Plain sense, shared by the commentators: Arjuna begs pardon for slights made in fun while walking, resting, sitting and eating. This record duplicates the second half of bg.11.41 in the library.

bg_2.speaker: Arjuna
bg_2.setting: Arjuna, shaken by the cosmic vision, asks Krishna to forgive his years of casual familiarity.
bg_2.sanskrit: तस्मात्प्रणम्य प्रणिधाय कायंप्रसादये त्वामहमीशमीड्यम् । पितेव पुत्रस्य सखेव सख्युःप्रियः प्रियायार्हसि देव सोढुम् ॥
bg_2.translation: So, bowing and prostrating my body, I ask your grace, adorable Lord. As a father with his son, a friend with his friend, a lover with the beloved, please bear with me.
bg_2.line: Bear with me as a father bears with a son, a friend with a friend, a lover with the beloved.
bg_2.misuse: Asking for forgiveness is not demanding it; the other person still decides.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Shankara: as a father forgives a son's fault, a friend a friend's, a lover the beloved's, so the Lord should forgive him.

prasang.title_en: Terrified, Arjuna prays to see the gentle four-armed form
prasang.summary: Trembling, Arjuna praises Krishna, asks pardon for having treated him as just a friend, begs him to bear with him as a father, friend or lover would, and asks to see his familiar form.
prasang.lesson: We take those closest to us for granted; it is never too late to say sorry.

bg_2.speaker: Arjuna
bg_2.setting: Overwhelmed by the cosmic vision, Arjuna asks to see Krishna's familiar form again.
bg_2.sanskrit: अदृष्टपूर्वं हृषितोऽस्मि दृष्ट्वाभयेन च प्रव्यथितं मनो मे । तदेव मे दर्शय देव रूपंप्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास ॥
bg_2.translation: I am thrilled to have seen what was never seen before, yet my mind is shaken with fear. Show me only that form of yours, God; be gracious, Lord of gods, refuge of the world.
bg_2.line: I'm thrilled and terrified at once. Show me the familiar face again.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Plain sense: glad at seeing what was never seen, and afraid, Arjuna asks to see the earlier gentle form.

prasang.title_en: Terrified, Arjuna prays to see the gentle four-armed form
prasang.summary: Trembling, Arjuna praises Krishna, asks pardon for having treated him as just a friend, begs him to bear with him as a father, friend or lover would, and asks to see his familiar form.
prasang.lesson: We take those closest to us for granted; it is never too late to say sorry.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna calms the frightened Arjuna and returns to his familiar form.
bg_2.sanskrit: मा ते व्यथा मा च विमूढभावोदृष्ट्वा रूपं घोरमीदृङ्ममेदम् । व्यपेतभीः प्रीतमनाः पुनस्त्वंतदेव मे रूपमिदं प्रपश्य ॥
bg_2.translation: Do not be afraid or bewildered at seeing this terrible form of mine. Free from fear and glad at heart, see again that same familiar form of mine.
bg_2.line: Don't be afraid or confused by what you've seen. Let the fear go and look again with a calm heart.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Plain sense: the Lord comforts Arjuna and shows again the gentle form; 11.50 says he consoled the frightened one.

prasang.title_en: Krishna returns to his gentle form
prasang.summary: Krishna tells Arjuna not to fear, and returns to his familiar form to reassure him.
prasang.lesson: After the storm, kindness and a familiar face restore us.

bg_2.speaker: Sanjaya
bg_2.setting: Terrified by the cosmic vision, Arjuna begs to see his friend again; Krishna returns to his familiar form.
bg_2.sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाचइत्यर्जुनं वासुदेवस्तथोक्त्वास्वकं रूपं दर्शयामास भूयः । आश्वासयामास च भीतमेनंभूत्वा पुनः सौम्यवपुर्महात्मा ॥
bg_2.translation: Having spoken so, Vasudeva showed Arjuna his own form once more; the great-souled one, becoming gentle in form again, comforted the frightened Arjuna.
bg_2.line: Seeing Arjuna frightened, Krishna took his gentle, familiar form again and comforted him.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Plain sense: Vasudeva showed again the form born in Vasudeva's house and, with a gentle body, consoled the terrified Arjuna.

bg_2.speaker: Arjuna
bg_2.setting: Arjuna sees Krishna's human face again after the overwhelming vision.
bg_2.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचदृष्ट्वेदं मानुषं रूपं तवसौम्यं जनार्दन । इदानीमस्मि संवृत्तः सचेताः प्रकृतिं गतः ॥
bg_2.translation: Seeing this gentle human form of yours, Janardana, I have now come to myself; my mind is steady and I am back to my natural state.
bg_2.line: Seeing your gentle human face again, I am calm. I feel like myself again.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Plain sense: seeing the gentle human form, Arjuna says his mind is collected and he has returned to his natural state.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: After the vision, Krishna says what alone makes it possible.
bg_2.sanskrit: भक्त्या त्वनन्यया शक्यमहमेवंविधोऽर्जुन । ज्ञातुं दृष्टुं च तत्त्वेन प्रवेष्टुं च परंतप ॥
bg_2.translation: But by undivided devotion, Arjuna, I can be known like this, seen in truth, and entered into, scorcher of foes.
bg_2.line: By a love that looks nowhere else, I can truly be known, seen, and entered.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Not by Vedas, austerity, gifts or sacrifice, but by devotion that turns to nothing other than the Lord, he can be known from scripture, seen directly and entered, which is liberation.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna tells Arjuna that only undivided devotion sees him.
bg_2.sanskrit: मत्कर्मकृन्मत्परमो मद्भक्तः सङ्गवर्जितः । निर्वैरः सर्वभूतेषु यः स मामेति पाण्डव ॥
bg_2.translation: One who works for me, holds me as the highest, is devoted to me, free from attachment and without enmity towards any being, comes to me, Pandava.
bg_2.line: Work for the divine, love it, drop clinging, and hold no hatred towards any being.
bg_2.misuse: No hatred doesn't mean no boundaries; you can wish someone no harm and still keep away.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Shankara calls this verse the essence of the whole Gita teaching, gathered up for practice. Without enmity even toward those who do one great harm.

prasang.title_en: Only undivided devotion sees him
prasang.summary: Arjuna is calm again. Krishna says no ritual or study reveals this form, only devotion, and the one free of attachment and enmity towards all reaches him.
prasang.lesson: Hold no enmity towards any being.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Arjuna has asked which devotee is best: lover of the personal God or seeker of the formless.
bg_2.sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचमय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते । श्रद्धया परयोपेतास्ते मे युक्ततमा मताः ॥
bg_2.translation: Those who fix their minds on me and worship me, ever united, with supreme faith, I consider the most united with me.
bg_2.line: Those who rest their mind in me, always, with deep trust, I count as closest to me.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Answering 12.1: those who worship the Lord in his form with mind fixed and highest faith are the best yogis. Shankara notes the worshippers of the imperishable also reach him (12.3-4); Ramanuja takes devotion to the personal Lord as plainly superior.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Arjuna asks which devotee is best; Krishna offers a ladder of practices.
bg_2.sanskrit: संनियम्येन्द्रियग्रामं सर्वत्र समबुद्धयः । ते प्राप्नुवन्ति मामेव सर्वभूतहिते रताः ॥
bg_2.translation: Restraining all the senses, even-minded everywhere, rejoicing in the welfare of all beings, they too reach me.
bg_2.line: Senses in hand, even-minded everywhere, glad in the good of all beings: they reach me too.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Shankara: those who meditate on the imperishable, with senses restrained and equal vision, intent on the good of all, reach the Lord; 12.5 adds that their path is harder for the embodied.

prasang.title_en: Form or formless: which devotee is best, and the ways to reach him
prasang.summary: Krishna says devotion to a personal form is easier, then offers a ladder: fix your mind; if not, practise; if not, work for me; if not, let go of results. Letting go brings peace at once.
prasang.lesson: If the ideal is too hard, take the next step down, and keep going.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna describes those whom he lifts out of the sea of mortality (12.7).
bg_2.sanskrit: ये तु सर्वाणि कर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्पराः । अनन्येनैव योगेन मां ध्यायन्त उपासते ॥ तेषामहं समुद्धर्ता मृत्युसंसारसागरात् । भवामि नचिरात्पार्थ मय्यावेशितचेतसाम् ॥
bg_2.translation: But those who lay all their actions in me, intent on me, and worship me meditating with single-minded yoga — for them, whose minds are set on me, I soon become the one who lifts them out of the ocean of death and rebirth, Partha.
bg_2.line: Lay your work in me and keep your mind on me; I soon lift you out of the drowning sea.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Shankara: for those who offer all actions to the Lord and meditate on him with undivided yoga, he becomes before long the lifter out of the ocean of mortal samsara.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna begins his ladder of practices with the simplest instruction.
bg_2.sanskrit: मय्येव मन आधत्स्व मयि बुद्धिं निवेशय । निवसिष्यसि मय्येव अत ऊर्ध्वं न संशयः ॥
bg_2.translation: Fix your mind on me alone, let your understanding settle in me; from then on you will dwell in me. Of this there is no doubt.
bg_2.line: Rest your mind in me, settle your thinking in me, and you will live in me.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Fix the mind, which thinks, and the intellect, which decides, on the Lord in his cosmic form; after the body falls you will dwell in him as his self, without doubt.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Arjuna asks which devotee is best; Krishna offers a ladder of practices.
bg_2.sanskrit: अथ चित्तं समाधातुं न शक्नोषि मयि स्थिरम् । अभ्यासयोगेन ततो मामिच्छाप्तुं धनञ्जय ॥
bg_2.translation: If you cannot fix your mind steadily on me, then seek to reach me by the yoga of practice, Dhananjaya.
bg_2.line: If you can't keep your mind fixed yet, then reach for it through regular practice.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Shankara: practice is withdrawing the mind from everything and fixing it again and again on the one object; by that yoga seek to reach the Lord.

prasang.title_en: Form or formless: which devotee is best, and the ways to reach him
prasang.summary: Krishna says devotion to a personal form is easier, then offers a ladder: fix your mind; if not, practise; if not, work for me; if not, let go of results. Letting go brings peace at once.
prasang.lesson: If the ideal is too hard, take the next step down, and keep going.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Arjuna asks which devotee is best; Krishna offers a ladder of practices.
bg_2.sanskrit: अभ्यासेऽप्यसमर्थोऽसि मत्कर्मपरमो भव । मदर्थमपि कर्माणि कुर्वन् सिद्धिमवाप्स्यसि ॥
bg_2.translation: If you are unable even to practise, be intent on doing work for my sake. Even by doing actions for me, you will reach perfection.
bg_2.line: If even practice is too hard, just do your work for my sake. That alone takes you far.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Shankara: if you cannot manage the yoga of practice, be devoted to doing actions for the Lord; through purity of mind, yoga and knowledge, even that leads to perfection.

prasang.title_en: Form or formless: which devotee is best, and the ways to reach him
prasang.summary: Krishna says devotion to a personal form is easier, then offers a ladder: fix your mind; if not, practise; if not, work for me; if not, let go of results. Letting go brings peace at once.
prasang.lesson: If the ideal is too hard, take the next step down, and keep going.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Arjuna asks which devotee is best; Krishna offers a ladder of practices.
bg_2.sanskrit: अथैतदप्यशक्तोऽसि कर्तुं मद्योगमाश्रितः । सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं ततः कुरु यतात्मवान् ॥
bg_2.translation: If you cannot do even this, then taking refuge in my yoga and with self restrained, give up the fruit of all actions.
bg_2.line: And if even that's beyond you, then simply let go of the results of what you do.
bg_2.misuse: Letting go of results is not giving up on goals or planning; it's releasing the anxious grip.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Shankara: if you cannot even work for the Lord's sake, then, relying on offering all actions to him, with mind controlled, renounce the fruit of all actions.

prasang.title_en: Form or formless: which devotee is best, and the ways to reach him
prasang.summary: Krishna says devotion to a personal form is easier, then offers a ladder: fix your mind; if not, practise; if not, work for me; if not, let go of results. Letting go brings peace at once.
prasang.lesson: If the ideal is too hard, take the next step down, and keep going.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Arjuna asks which devotee is best; Krishna offers a ladder of practices.
bg_2.sanskrit: श्रेयो हि ज्ञानमभ्यासाज्ज्ञानाद्ध्यानं विशिष्यते । ध्यानात्कर्मफलत्यागस्त्यागाच्छान्तिरनन्तरम् ॥
bg_2.translation: Knowledge is better than mere practice; meditation is better than knowledge; giving up the fruit of action is better than meditation. From that renunciation, peace follows immediately.
bg_2.line: Practice is good, understanding better, meditation better still. But letting go of results brings peace at once.
bg_2.misuse: Not 'stop caring how things turn out'. Peace comes from releasing the grip, not from indifference.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Shankara reads the ranking as praise of renouncing the fruit, meant for one who cannot manage the higher means of 12.8-11; Ramanuja reads each step as the easier means leading to the next.

prasang.title_en: Form or formless: which devotee is best, and the ways to reach him
prasang.summary: Krishna says devotion to a personal form is easier, then offers a ladder: fix your mind; if not, practise; if not, work for me; if not, let go of results. Letting go brings peace at once.
prasang.lesson: If the ideal is too hard, take the next step down, and keep going.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, describing the qualities of the person dear to God.
bg_2.sanskrit: सन्तुष्टः सततं योगी यतात्मा दृढनिश्चयः । मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥
bg_2.translation: ever content, steady in practice, self-controlled, firm in resolve, with mind and understanding given to me, that devotee of mine is dear to me.
bg_2.line: Always content, self-disciplined, firm in resolve, heart and mind given to the divine: such a person is dear to me.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Shankara: ever content whether or not the body's needs are met, of firm conviction about the truth of the self, with mind and intellect offered to the Lord.

prasang.title_en: The marks of one dear to God
prasang.summary: Krishna lists the marks of one dear to him: no hatred, friendly and compassionate, forgiving, content, disturbing no one and disturbed by no one, the same in praise and blame.
prasang.lesson: Kindness without hatred, steadiness in praise and blame: that's what's loved.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, describing the qualities of the person dear to God.
bg_2.sanskrit: यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः । हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः ॥
bg_2.translation: One from whom the world does not shrink and who does not shrink from the world, who is free from elation, impatience, fear and agitation, is dear to me.
bg_2.line: Unsettle no one, be unsettled by no one, free of elation, resentment, fear and agitation.
bg_2.misuse: Not disturbing others doesn't mean never disagreeing; it means not causing needless harm.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Shankara glosses amarsha as intolerance and udvega as agitation; one free of these four is dear to the Lord. Ramanuja takes them as feelings directed at other beings.

prasang.title_en: The marks of one dear to God
prasang.summary: Krishna lists the marks of one dear to him: no hatred, friendly and compassionate, forgiving, content, disturbing no one and disturbed by no one, the same in praise and blame.
prasang.lesson: Kindness without hatred, steadiness in praise and blame: that's what's loved.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, describing the qualities of the person dear to God.
bg_2.sanskrit: अनपेक्षः शुचिर्दक्ष उदासीनो गतव्यथः । सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥
bg_2.translation: One who expects nothing, is pure, capable, unconcerned and untroubled, who has given up all self-centred undertakings, that devotee of mine is dear to me.
bg_2.line: Wanting nothing extra, clean within and without, capable, unbothered, not chasing every new venture: dear to me.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Shankara: without dependence on body, senses or objects; one who has given up every undertaking prompted by desire for results here or hereafter.

prasang.title_en: The marks of one dear to God
prasang.summary: Krishna lists the marks of one dear to him: no hatred, friendly and compassionate, forgiving, content, disturbing no one and disturbed by no one, the same in praise and blame.
prasang.lesson: Kindness without hatred, steadiness in praise and blame: that's what's loved.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, describing the qualities of the person dear to God.
bg_2.sanskrit: यो न हृष्यति न द्वेष्टि न शोचति न काङ्क्षति । शुभाशुभपरित्यागी भक्तिमान्यः स मे प्रियः ॥
bg_2.translation: One who neither rejoices nor hates, neither grieves nor craves, who has let go of both good and bad, and is full of devotion, is dear to me.
bg_2.line: Not swinging between thrill and hate, grief and craving, letting go of 'good' and 'bad' outcomes: dear to me.
bg_2.misuse: Not feeling grief is not the goal; the verse is about not being swept away by it.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Shankara: he does not exult on getting the desired, nor hate the undesired, nor grieve at loss, nor long for what he lacks; he has given up good and bad actions.

prasang.title_en: The marks of one dear to God
prasang.summary: Krishna lists the marks of one dear to him: no hatred, friendly and compassionate, forgiving, content, disturbing no one and disturbed by no one, the same in praise and blame.
prasang.lesson: Kindness without hatred, steadiness in praise and blame: that's what's loved.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, describing the qualities of the person dear to God.
bg_2.sanskrit: समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा मानापमानयोः । शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु समः सङ्गविवर्जितः ॥
bg_2.translation: One who is the same to enemy and friend, in honour and dishonour, in cold and heat, in pleasure and pain, and free from attachment,
bg_2.line: The same to friend and foe, in respect and insult, heat and cold, pleasure and pain.
bg_2.misuse: Being the same in insult doesn't mean tolerating abuse; it means your worth isn't decided by it.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Part of the marks of the devotee dear to God (12.13-20); the sentence completes in 12.19. Shankara applies it to the renunciate established in knowledge.

prasang.title_en: The marks of one dear to God
prasang.summary: Krishna lists the marks of one dear to him: no hatred, friendly and compassionate, forgiving, content, disturbing no one and disturbed by no one, the same in praise and blame.
prasang.lesson: Kindness without hatred, steadiness in praise and blame: that's what's loved.

bg_2.speaker: Krishna
bg_2.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, describing the qualities of the person dear to God.
bg_2.sanskrit: तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिर्मौनी सन्तुष्टो येनकेनचित् । अनिकेतः स्थिरमतिर्भक्तिमान्मे प्रियो नरः ॥
bg_2.translation: to whom blame and praise are equal, who is silent, content with whatever comes, without a fixed home, steady in mind and full of devotion, that person is dear to me.
bg_2.line: Praise and blame weigh the same. Quiet, content with what comes, rooted in steadiness, not status.
bg_2.misuse: Not 'never ask for credit'. You can advocate for yourself without letting praise or blame define you.
bg_2.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_2.our_note: Shankara: content with whatever maintains the body, without a fixed dwelling, of steady understanding about the highest truth; such a devotee is dear to the Lord.

prasang.title_en: The marks of one dear to God
prasang.summary: Krishna lists the marks of one dear to him: no hatred, friendly and compassionate, forgiving, content, disturbing no one and disturbed by no one, the same in praise and blame.
prasang.lesson: Kindness without hatred, steadiness in praise and blame: that's what's loved.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the body as a field, and what true knowledge consists of.
bg_3.sanskrit: इन्द्रियार्थेषु वैराग्यमनहङ्कार एव च । जन्ममृत्युजराव्याधिदुःखदोषानुदर्शनम् ॥
bg_3.translation: detachment from sense objects, absence of ego, and seeing clearly the pain and flaw in birth, death, old age and sickness,
bg_3.line: Not chasing pleasures, not puffed up, and clear-eyed about birth, death, old age and illness.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: reflecting on the defect of pain in each of birth, death, old age and disease produces dispassion toward body and sense pleasures and turns the mind to the inner self.

prasang.title_en: The field and the knower of the field
prasang.summary: Krishna calls the body the field and the self its knower, then lists what real knowledge looks like: humility, no pretence, patience, honesty, clear sight of ageing and illness.
prasang.lesson: Real knowledge shows up as character: humility, patience, honesty.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on nature and spirit, and seeing the same self in all.
bg_3.sanskrit: ध्यानेनात्मनि पश्यन्ति केचिदात्मानमात्मना । अन्ये सांख्येन योगेन कर्मयोगेन चापरे ॥
bg_3.translation: Some see the self in the self by the self through meditation; others by the path of knowledge; and others by the yoga of action.
bg_3.line: Some find the truth by meditation, some by thinking it through, some by selfless work.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: the best see by meditation, the middling by discriminating knowledge of the gunas and the self, others by action offered to the Lord, which leads to knowledge through purity of mind.

prasang.title_en: Nature and spirit
prasang.summary: Nature does the acting; the self witnesses. Some reach the truth by meditation, some by reason, some by work, some by listening. Whoever sees the same divine in all beings stops harming themselves.
prasang.lesson: See the same presence in everyone and you stop wounding yourself.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on nature and spirit, and seeing the same self in all.
bg_3.sanskrit: अन्ये त्वेवमजानन्तः श्रुत्वाऽन्येभ्य उपासते । तेऽपि चातितरन्त्येव मृत्युं श्रुतिपरायणाः ॥
bg_3.translation: Others, not knowing this, worship having heard it from others; they too cross beyond death, devoted to what they have heard.
bg_3.line: Others, not knowing these paths, learn by listening to others, and they too cross over.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: others, unable to know by any of these means, hear from teachers and worship with faith; even they cross over death, so how much more those who can discriminate.

prasang.title_en: Nature and spirit
prasang.summary: Nature does the acting; the self witnesses. Some reach the truth by meditation, some by reason, some by work, some by listening. Whoever sees the same divine in all beings stops harming themselves.
prasang.lesson: See the same presence in everyone and you stop wounding yourself.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on nature and spirit, and seeing the same self in all.
bg_3.sanskrit: समं सर्वेषु भूतेषु तिष्ठन्तं परमेश्वरम् । विनश्यत्स्वविनश्यन्तं यः पश्यति स पश्यति ॥
bg_3.translation: One who sees the Supreme Lord abiding equally in all beings, the undying within the dying, truly sees.
bg_3.line: Whoever sees the same undying presence in all beings, even as they perish, truly sees.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: the supreme Lord is the same in all beings from Brahma to the unmoving, and does not perish when they perish; the one who sees this alone sees, all others see wrongly.

prasang.title_en: Nature and spirit
prasang.summary: Nature does the acting; the self witnesses. Some reach the truth by meditation, some by reason, some by work, some by listening. Whoever sees the same divine in all beings stops harming themselves.
prasang.lesson: See the same presence in everyone and you stop wounding yourself.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on nature and spirit, and seeing the same self in all.
bg_3.sanskrit: समं पश्यन्हि सर्वत्र समवस्थितमीश्वरम् । न हिनस्त्यात्मनाऽऽत्मानं ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥
bg_3.translation: Seeing the Lord equally present everywhere, one does not injure the self by the self, and so reaches the highest goal.
bg_3.line: Seeing the divine equally everywhere, you stop wounding yourself through yourself.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: the ignorant 'kill the self' by taking the body for the self and not knowing their own nature; the one who sees the Lord everywhere does not, and reaches the highest.

prasang.title_en: Nature and spirit
prasang.summary: Nature does the acting; the self witnesses. Some reach the truth by meditation, some by reason, some by work, some by listening. Whoever sees the same divine in all beings stops harming themselves.
prasang.lesson: See the same presence in everyone and you stop wounding yourself.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on nature and spirit, and seeing the same self in all.
bg_3.sanskrit: यथा सर्वगतं सौक्ष्म्यादाकाशं नोपलिप्यते । सर्वत्रावस्थितो देहे तथाऽऽत्मा नोपलिप्यते ॥
bg_3.translation: As the all-pervading sky, because of its subtlety, is not stained, so the self, present in every body, is not stained.
bg_3.line: Like the sky, untouched by everything that moves through it, the self stays unstained.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: as space, though everywhere, is not touched by what it contains because it is subtle, so the self, though in every body, is not touched by the body's actions and their fruits.

prasang.title_en: Nature and spirit
prasang.summary: Nature does the acting; the self witnesses. Some reach the truth by meditation, some by reason, some by work, some by listening. Whoever sees the same divine in all beings stops harming themselves.
prasang.lesson: See the same presence in everyone and you stop wounding yourself.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna explains the three qualities: clarity, restlessness and dullness.
bg_3.sanskrit: तमस्त्वज्ञानजं विद्धि मोहनं सर्वदेहिनाम् । प्रमादालस्यनिद्राभिस्तन्निबध्नाति भारत ॥
bg_3.translation: Know tamas to be born of ignorance, deluding all embodied beings. It binds through heedlessness, laziness and sleep, Bharata.
bg_3.line: Dullness, born of ignorance, ties you down through carelessness, laziness and too much sleep.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: tamas, born of ignorance, deludes all the embodied and binds through heedlessness, sloth and sleep.

prasang.title_en: Sattva, rajas, tamas: the three gunas
prasang.summary: Sattva binds through attachment to happiness and knowledge, rajas through craving and activity, tamas through laziness and sleep. Each shows itself in recognisable signs.
prasang.lesson: Notice which mood is running you: clarity, restlessness or dullness.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna explains the three qualities: clarity, restlessness and dullness.
bg_3.sanskrit: लोभः प्रवृत्तिरारम्भः कर्मणामशमः स्पृहा । रजस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे भरतर्षभ ॥
bg_3.translation: Greed, activity, the undertaking of actions, restlessness and craving: these arise when rajas increases, best of the Bharatas.
bg_3.line: When restlessness rules: greed, constant activity, starting project after project, craving and no peace.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: ashama is the absence of calm, a ceaseless stirring of joy and craving; spriha is thirst for everything in general. These signs show that rajas has risen.

prasang.title_en: Sattva, rajas, tamas: the three gunas
prasang.summary: Sattva binds through attachment to happiness and knowledge, rajas through craving and activity, tamas through laziness and sleep. Each shows itself in recognisable signs.
prasang.lesson: Notice which mood is running you: clarity, restlessness or dullness.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna explains the three qualities: clarity, restlessness and dullness.
bg_3.sanskrit: अप्रकाशोऽप्रवृत्तिश्च प्रमादो मोह एव च । तमस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे कुरुनन्दन ॥
bg_3.translation: Darkness, inertia, heedlessness and delusion: these arise when tamas increases, joy of the Kurus.
bg_3.line: When dullness rules: darkness, sluggishness, carelessness and confusion.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: aprakasha is lack of discrimination, apravritti its effect, lack of effort; heedlessness and delusion follow. These are the signs that tamas has risen.

prasang.title_en: Sattva, rajas, tamas: the three gunas
prasang.summary: Sattva binds through attachment to happiness and knowledge, rajas through craving and activity, tamas through laziness and sleep. Each shows itself in recognisable signs.
prasang.lesson: Notice which mood is running you: clarity, restlessness or dullness.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Arjuna asks how one beyond the three qualities lives; Krishna answers.
bg_3.sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचप्रकाशं च प्रवृत्तिं च मोहमेव च पाण्डव । न द्वेष्टि सम्प्रवृत्तानि न निवृत्तानि काङ्क्षति ॥
bg_3.translation: The Blessed Lord said: One who does not hate clarity, activity or delusion when they arise, Pandava, nor longs for them when they cease,
bg_3.line: Don't hate your moods when they come, or long for them when they go.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: the knower does not think 'a tamasic notion has arisen in me, I am deluded' and hate it, nor long for clarity when it goes; these are marks known to oneself, not visible to others.

prasang.title_en: Going beyond the gunas
prasang.summary: One beyond the qualities does not hate moods when they come or long for them when they go, sits like a witness, and is the same in praise and blame, honour and insult.
prasang.lesson: Let moods come and go without fighting or chasing them.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Arjuna asks how one beyond the three qualities lives; Krishna answers.
bg_3.sanskrit: उदासीनवदासीनो गुणैर्यो न विचाल्यते । गुणा वर्तन्त इत्येव योऽवतिष्ठति नेङ्गते ॥
bg_3.translation: who sits like one unconcerned, unshaken by the qualities, who knows 'it is only the qualities moving' and stays firm without wavering,
bg_3.line: Sit like a witness, unshaken, knowing it's just moods moving through, and stay steady.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: the knower sits like a neutral party, not moved from his own nature by the gunas, knowing 'the gunas, turned into body, senses and objects, act on one another'.

prasang.title_en: Going beyond the gunas
prasang.summary: One beyond the qualities does not hate moods when they come or long for them when they go, sits like a witness, and is the same in praise and blame, honour and insult.
prasang.lesson: Let moods come and go without fighting or chasing them.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Arjuna asks how one beyond the three qualities lives; Krishna answers.
bg_3.sanskrit: मानापमानयोस्तुल्यस्तुल्यो मित्रारिपक्षयोः । सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी गुणातीतः स उच्यते ॥
bg_3.translation: the same in honour and dishonour, the same to friend and foe, who has given up all self-driven undertakings: such a person is said to have gone beyond the qualities.
bg_3.line: The same in respect and disrespect, to friend and foe, letting go of the need to start everything: free.
bg_3.misuse: Not 'tolerate disrespect'. It means your steadiness doesn't depend on how others treat you.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: he gives up all undertakings for seen and unseen results, keeping only what maintains the body; these qualities, practised with effort by the seeker, become natural marks in the realised.

prasang.title_en: Going beyond the gunas
prasang.summary: One beyond the qualities does not hate moods when they come or long for them when they go, sits like a witness, and is the same in praise and blame, honour and insult.
prasang.lesson: Let moods come and go without fighting or chasing them.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna describes worldly life as an upside-down tree to be cut with detachment.
bg_3.sanskrit: निर्मानमोहा जितसङ्गदोषा अध्यात्मनित्या विनिवृत्तकामाः । द्वन्द्वैर्विमुक्ताः सुखदुःखसंज्ञै र्गच्छन्त्यमूढाः पदमव्ययं तत् ॥
bg_3.translation: Free from pride and delusion, with the fault of attachment conquered, ever dwelling in the self, desires turned away, freed from the pairs called pleasure and pain, the undeluded reach that eternal state.
bg_3.line: Free of pride and delusion, past the pull of attachment, the steady reach what doesn't fade.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: These are the qualities of those who, having taken refuge in the primal Person, reach the unchanging goal: free of pride and delusion, devoted to contemplating the self, desires wholly gone.

prasang.title_en: The tree of worldly life, and the way out
prasang.summary: The world is an ashvattha tree with roots above and branches below; cut it with detachment and seek the source. The free of pride and delusion reach it.
prasang.lesson: Pride and clinging keep us tangled; detachment cuts through.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna on the individual soul as a part of the divine.
bg_3.sanskrit: ममैवांशो जीवलोके जीवभूतः सनातनः । मनःषष्ठानीन्द्रियाणि प्रकृतिस्थानि कर्षति ॥
bg_3.translation: An eternal part of me becomes the living soul in the world of the living, and draws to itself the mind and the five senses that rest in nature.
bg_3.line: Every living being is an eternal part of me, says Krishna.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: 'part' is figurative, like the space in a jar being a part of space; the soul is the Lord himself seen through a limiting adjunct. Ramanuja takes the soul as a real and eternal part, a mode of the Lord.

prasang.title_en: The individual soul
prasang.summary: Each living being is an eternal part of Krishna, carrying mind and senses from body to body, seen only by the eye of wisdom.
prasang.lesson: You are a part of something eternal.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna on his power sustaining the world and dwelling in every heart.
bg_3.sanskrit: सर्वस्य चाहं हृदि सन्निविष्टो मत्तः स्मृतिर्ज्ञानमपोहनं च । वेदैश्च सर्वैरहमेव वेद्यो वेदान्तकृद्वेदविदेव चाहम् ॥
bg_3.translation: I am seated in the hearts of all. From me come memory, knowledge and their loss. I alone am what is to be known by all the Vedas; I am the author of Vedanta and the knower of the Vedas.
bg_3.line: I am seated in every heart. Memory, knowledge and their fading come from me.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: The Lord dwells as the self in the hearts of all; memory and knowledge, and their loss, come from him according to beings' deeds.

prasang.title_en: The Supreme Lord and his power
prasang.summary: Krishna is the light of sun and moon, the nourishment of plants, the digestive fire, and is seated in every heart.
prasang.lesson: The sacred is seated in every heart.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, listing the qualities that free us and those that bind.
bg_3.sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचअभयं सत्त्वसंशुद्धिः ज्ञानयोगव्यवस्थितिः । दानं दमश्च यज्ञश्च स्वाध्यायस्तप आर्जवम् ॥
bg_3.translation: The Blessed Lord said: Fearlessness, purity of heart, steadfastness in knowledge and yoga, charity, self-control, sacrifice, study, austerity and uprightness,
bg_3.line: Fearlessness, a clean heart, steady learning, generosity, self-control, study and straightforwardness.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: these are the divine endowment; fearlessness is first, and purity of the inner organ is dealing without deceit. Krishna tells Arjuna in 16.5 that he is born to this nature.

prasang.title_en: Divine and demonic qualities, and where they lead
prasang.summary: Krishna lists the divine qualities (fearlessness, truth, no anger, compassion, forgiveness, humility) and the demonic ones (hypocrisy, arrogance, anger, harshness), and reassures Arjuna he has the good ones.
prasang.lesson: Character is a list you can practise: courage, truth, kindness, no arrogance.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, listing the qualities that free us and those that bind.
bg_3.sanskrit: अहिंसा सत्यमक्रोधस्त्यागः शान्तिरपैशुनम् । दया भूतेष्वलोलुप्त्वं मार्दवं ह्रीरचापलम् ॥
bg_3.translation: non-violence, truth, freedom from anger, renunciation, peace, absence of slander, compassion for beings, freedom from greed, gentleness, modesty, absence of fickleness,
bg_3.line: No harm, truthfulness, no anger, no gossip, compassion for all, no greed, gentleness, modesty, no fidgeting.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: akrodha is calming the anger that arises when one is abused or struck; achapala is not moving speech, hands and feet without purpose.

prasang.title_en: Divine and demonic qualities, and where they lead
prasang.summary: Krishna lists the divine qualities (fearlessness, truth, no anger, compassion, forgiveness, humility) and the demonic ones (hypocrisy, arrogance, anger, harshness), and reassures Arjuna he has the good ones.
prasang.lesson: Character is a list you can practise: courage, truth, kindness, no arrogance.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, listing the qualities that free us and those that bind.
bg_3.sanskrit: तेजः क्षमा धृतिः शौचमद्रोहो नातिमानिता । भवन्ति सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातस्य भारत ॥
bg_3.translation: vigour, forgiveness, fortitude, purity, freedom from malice and from excessive pride: these belong to one born with the divine nature, Bharata.
bg_3.line: Vigour, forgiveness, fortitude, cleanliness, no malice, no arrogance: the marks of a good nature.
bg_3.misuse: Forgiveness here is a strength, not an obligation to stay in harm's way.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: tejas is boldness, not brightness of skin; kshama is the absence of inner agitation when abused or struck; dhriti is the function of mind that lifts up the tired body and senses.

prasang.title_en: Divine and demonic qualities, and where they lead
prasang.summary: Krishna lists the divine qualities (fearlessness, truth, no anger, compassion, forgiveness, humility) and the demonic ones (hypocrisy, arrogance, anger, harshness), and reassures Arjuna he has the good ones.
prasang.lesson: Character is a list you can practise: courage, truth, kindness, no arrogance.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, listing the qualities that free us and those that bind.
bg_3.sanskrit: दैवी सम्पद्विमोक्षाय निबन्धायासुरी मता । मा शुचः सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातोऽसि पाण्डव ॥
bg_3.translation: The divine nature leads to freedom, the demonic to bondage. Do not grieve, Pandava; you are born with the divine nature.
bg_3.line: Good qualities free you; harsh ones bind. Don't worry; you were born with the good.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Seeing Arjuna wonder which nature is his, the Lord says: do not grieve, you are born for the divine endowment.

prasang.title_en: Divine and demonic qualities, and where they lead
prasang.summary: Krishna lists the divine qualities (fearlessness, truth, no anger, compassion, forgiveness, humility) and the demonic ones (hypocrisy, arrogance, anger, harshness), and reassures Arjuna he has the good ones.
prasang.lesson: Character is a list you can practise: courage, truth, kindness, no arrogance.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna describes the mind of greed and arrogance and where it leads.
bg_3.sanskrit: चिन्तामपरिमेयां च प्रलयान्तामुपाश्रिताः । कामोपभोगपरमा एतावदिति निश्चिताः ॥
bg_3.translation: Clinging to immeasurable worries that end only at death, taking the enjoyment of desires as the highest aim, convinced that this is all,
bg_3.line: Clinging to worries that only end at death, they believe owning and enjoying is all there is.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: those of demonic nature are given over to cares without measure that end only with death, and are sure that enjoyment of desires is the highest human goal.

prasang.title_en: The demonic nature and its downfall
prasang.summary: Krishna portrays people driven by endless desire and worry, bound by hundreds of hopes, always counting 'this I have, that I'll get', proud of wealth and birth.
prasang.lesson: The mind of 'more' never rests; see it in yourself before it rules you.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna describes the mind of greed and arrogance and where it leads.
bg_3.sanskrit: आशापाशशतैर्बद्धाः कामक्रोधपरायणाः । ईहन्ते कामभोगार्थमन्यायेनार्थसञ्चयान् ॥
bg_3.translation: bound by hundreds of ties of hope, given over to desire and anger, they strive to amass wealth by unjust means for the enjoyment of desires.
bg_3.line: Tied by a hundred ropes of hope, pushed by desire and anger, they pile up wealth by any means.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: bound by hundreds of nooses of hope and dragged about by them, taking desire and anger as their refuge, they strive to gather wealth by unjust means.

prasang.title_en: The demonic nature and its downfall
prasang.summary: Krishna portrays people driven by endless desire and worry, bound by hundreds of hopes, always counting 'this I have, that I'll get', proud of wealth and birth.
prasang.lesson: The mind of 'more' never rests; see it in yourself before it rules you.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna describes the mind of greed and arrogance and where it leads.
bg_3.sanskrit: इदमद्य मया लब्धमिमं प्राप्स्ये मनोरथम् । इदमस्तीदमपि मे भविष्यति पुनर्धनम् ॥
bg_3.translation: 'This I have gained today; this desire I shall fulfil. This wealth is mine, and this too shall be mine.'
bg_3.line: 'I got this today, I'll get that next. This is mine, and more will be mine.' The mind of more.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: this is the thinking of those of demonic nature: this I have got now, this wish I shall attain, this wealth is mine and that too will be.

prasang.title_en: The demonic nature and its downfall
prasang.summary: Krishna portrays people driven by endless desire and worry, bound by hundreds of hopes, always counting 'this I have, that I'll get', proud of wealth and birth.
prasang.lesson: The mind of 'more' never rests; see it in yourself before it rules you.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna describes the mind of greed and arrogance and where it leads.
bg_3.sanskrit: आढ्योऽभिजनवानस्मि कोऽन्योऽस्ति सदृशो मया । यक्ष्ये दास्यामि मोदिष्य इत्यज्ञानविमोहिताः ॥
bg_3.translation: 'I am rich and well-born. Who else is equal to me? I will sacrifice, I will give, I will rejoice': so they say, deluded by ignorance.
bg_3.line: 'I'm rich, well-born; who else is like me?' So speaks the deluded mind.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Those of demonic nature think: I am wealthy and of high birth, none is my equal; even their giving and sacrifice are for self-display.

prasang.title_en: The demonic nature and its downfall
prasang.summary: Krishna portrays people driven by endless desire and worry, bound by hundreds of hopes, always counting 'this I have, that I'll get', proud of wealth and birth.
prasang.lesson: The mind of 'more' never rests; see it in yourself before it rules you.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna describes the mind of greed and arrogance and where it leads.
bg_3.sanskrit: आत्मसम्भाविताः स्तब्धा धनमानमदान्विताः । यजन्ते नामयज्ञैस्ते दम्भेनाविधिपूर्वकम् ॥
bg_3.translation: Self-conceited, stubborn, filled with the pride and intoxication of wealth, they perform sacrifices in name only, with hypocrisy and against the rules.
bg_3.line: Self-important, stubborn, drunk on money and status, they give for show.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Esteemed only by themselves, unbending, intoxicated by wealth and honour, they perform sacrifices in name only, for show and without regard to the rule.

prasang.title_en: The demonic nature and its downfall
prasang.summary: Krishna portrays people driven by endless desire and worry, bound by hundreds of hopes, always counting 'this I have, that I'll get', proud of wealth and birth.
prasang.lesson: The mind of 'more' never rests; see it in yourself before it rules you.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna names the three gates to self-ruin and how to live instead.
bg_3.sanskrit: त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः । कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ॥
bg_3.translation: Threefold is the gate of hell that destroys the self: desire, anger and greed. Therefore one should give up these three.
bg_3.line: Desire, anger and greed: three gates to self-ruin. Close all three.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: these three are the door to hell and destroy the self, meaning they leave a person unfit for any human goal; giving them up is the root of all good.

prasang.title_en: Leave what scripture forbids; follow what it guides
prasang.summary: Desire, anger and greed are the three gates to ruin; leaving them, one does what is truly good. Krishna points to scripture as a guide for what to do.
prasang.lesson: Desire, anger, greed: close the three gates.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna names the three gates to self-ruin and how to live instead.
bg_3.sanskrit: एतैर्विमुक्तः कौन्तेय तमोद्वारैस्त्रिभिर्नरः । आचरत्यात्मनः श्रेयस्ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥
bg_3.translation: Released from these three gates of darkness, Kaunteya, a person does what is good for the self and so reaches the highest goal.
bg_3.line: Freed from these three dark gates, you do what's truly good for you and reach the highest.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Freed from desire, anger and greed, the gates to the darkness of hell, a person practises what is good for the self and so reaches liberation.

prasang.title_en: Leave what scripture forbids; follow what it guides
prasang.summary: Desire, anger and greed are the three gates to ruin; leaving them, one does what is truly good. Krishna points to scripture as a guide for what to do.
prasang.lesson: Desire, anger, greed: close the three gates.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Arjuna asks about faith outside the rules; Krishna explains faith follows nature.
bg_3.sanskrit: सत्त्वानुरूपा सर्वस्य श्रद्धा भवति भारत । श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः ॥
bg_3.translation: Everyone's faith follows their nature, Bharata. A person is made of faith; as a person's faith is, so is that person.
bg_3.line: You are made of what you deeply believe. As your faith is, so are you.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
