bg_3.our_note: Shankara: sattva here is the inner organ shaped by past impressions; faith follows it, and a person is known by the faith they hold. It introduces the three kinds of faith by guna.

prasang.title_en: Faith, and harsh austerity against scripture
prasang.summary: Everyone's faith matches their nature; a person is made of their faith. Harsh self-torment against scripture is condemned.
prasang.lesson: You become what you deeply believe.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna on three kinds of food, effort, speech and giving.
bg_3.sanskrit: आयुःसत्त्वबलारोग्यसुखप्रीतिविवर्धनाः । रस्याः स्निग्धाः स्थिरा हृद्या आहाराः सात्त्विकप्रियाः ॥
bg_3.translation: Foods that increase life, vitality, strength, health, happiness and cheerfulness, that are flavourful, soothing, nourishing and agreeable, are dear to the sattvic.
bg_3.line: Food that builds life, strength, health, cheer and calm: that's the food of a clear mind.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Foods that promote life, energy, strength, health, happiness and satisfaction are liked by the sattvic; one can know one's own guna by one's taste in food.

prasang.title_en: Three kinds of food, offering, austerity and giving
prasang.summary: Food, offering, austerity and giving each come in three kinds. Speech should be true, kind and helpful; giving should expect nothing back; effort for show doesn't last.
prasang.lesson: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna on three kinds of food, effort, speech and giving.
bg_3.sanskrit: सत्कारमानपूजार्थं तपो दम्भेन चैव यत् । क्रियते तदिह प्रोक्तं राजसं चलमध्रुवम् ॥
bg_3.translation: Austerity practised to gain respect, honour and reverence, and with show, is called rajasic; it is unstable and fleeting.
bg_3.line: Effort made for respect, status or show is shaky and doesn't last.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: austerity practised for praise, honour and worship, with display, gives a fleeting and uncertain result and is rajasic.

prasang.title_en: Three kinds of food, offering, austerity and giving
prasang.summary: Food, offering, austerity and giving each come in three kinds. Speech should be true, kind and helpful; giving should expect nothing back; effort for show doesn't last.
prasang.lesson: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna on three kinds of food, effort, speech and giving.
bg_3.sanskrit: मूढग्राहेणात्मनो यत्पीडया क्रियते तपः । परस्योत्सादनार्थं वा तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥
bg_3.translation: Austerity performed out of foolish obstinacy, with self-torture, or to harm another, is called tamasic.
bg_3.line: Discipline done through stubborn self-torment, or to harm another, is the dark kind.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Austerity undertaken with a deluded notion, by torturing oneself, or to destroy another, is tamasic.

prasang.title_en: Three kinds of food, offering, austerity and giving
prasang.summary: Food, offering, austerity and giving each come in three kinds. Speech should be true, kind and helpful; giving should expect nothing back; effort for show doesn't last.
prasang.lesson: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna on three kinds of food, effort, speech and giving.
bg_3.sanskrit: यत्तु प्रत्युपकारार्थं फलमुद्दिश्य वा पुनः । दीयते च परिक्लिष्टं तद्दानं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥
bg_3.translation: But a gift given in expectation of a return, or with a view to reward, or given reluctantly, is called rajasic.
bg_3.line: Giving to get something back, or giving grudgingly, isn't really giving.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: given so that the other will help in return, or aiming at an unseen reward, or with reluctance; such a gift is rajasic.

prasang.title_en: Three kinds of food, offering, austerity and giving
prasang.summary: Food, offering, austerity and giving each come in three kinds. Speech should be true, kind and helpful; giving should expect nothing back; effort for show doesn't last.
prasang.lesson: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Arjuna asks what true renunciation is; Krishna answers.
bg_3.sanskrit: एतान्यपि तु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलानि च । कर्तव्यानीति मे पार्थ निश्चितं मतमुत्तमम् ॥
bg_3.translation: But even these actions should be done giving up attachment and fruits. This, Partha, is my definite and highest view.
bg_3.line: Even good work should be done without clinging to it or its rewards. That's my settled view.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Even these purifying actions, sacrifice, gift and austerity, are to be done giving up attachment and their fruits; this is the Lord's definite and best view.

prasang.title_en: What true renunciation is
prasang.summary: Krishna says good acts shouldn't be dropped; dropping duty out of fear or confusion gains nothing; real renunciation is giving up clinging to results, since no embodied being can stop acting.
prasang.lesson: Don't drop what matters out of fear; drop the clinging instead.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Arjuna asks what true renunciation is; Krishna answers.
bg_3.sanskrit: नियतस्य तु संन्यासः कर्मणो नोपपद्यते । मोहात्तस्य परित्यागस्तामसः परिकीर्तितः ॥
bg_3.translation: Renunciation of obligatory action is not proper. Its abandonment out of delusion is declared tamasic.
bg_3.line: Walking away from a real responsibility out of confusion is the darkest kind of letting go.
bg_3.misuse: Not 'you can never leave'. Leaving thoughtfully is different from abandoning out of confusion.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Giving up obligatory action is not right for the unknowing, since it purifies; abandoning it through delusion is tamasic.

prasang.title_en: What true renunciation is
prasang.summary: Krishna says good acts shouldn't be dropped; dropping duty out of fear or confusion gains nothing; real renunciation is giving up clinging to results, since no embodied being can stop acting.
prasang.lesson: Don't drop what matters out of fear; drop the clinging instead.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Arjuna asks what true renunciation is; Krishna answers.
bg_3.sanskrit: दुःखमित्येव यत्कर्म कायक्लेशभयात्त्यजेत् । स कृत्वा राजसं त्यागं नैव त्यागफलं लभेत् ॥
bg_3.translation: One who gives up work because it is painful, out of fear of bodily strain, performs rajasic renunciation and does not gain its fruit.
bg_3.line: Dropping a duty just because it's hard or you fear the strain isn't freedom. It gains you nothing.
bg_3.misuse: Not 'never quit'. Leaving for good reasons is wise; this warns against fleeing out of fear alone.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: one who abandons obligatory work as painful, from fear of bodily trouble, makes a rajasic renunciation and does not gain liberation, the fruit of renunciation with knowledge.

prasang.title_en: What true renunciation is
prasang.summary: Krishna says good acts shouldn't be dropped; dropping duty out of fear or confusion gains nothing; real renunciation is giving up clinging to results, since no embodied being can stop acting.
prasang.lesson: Don't drop what matters out of fear; drop the clinging instead.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Arjuna asks what true renunciation is; Krishna answers.
bg_3.sanskrit: कार्यमित्येव यत्कर्म नियतं क्रियतेऽर्जुन । सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलं चैव स त्यागः सात्त्विको मतः ॥
bg_3.translation: When necessary work is done simply because it ought to be done, Arjuna, giving up attachment and the fruit, that renunciation is considered sattvic.
bg_3.line: Do what must be done because it must be done, letting go of clinging and the payoff.
bg_3.misuse: Not 'never question your duties'. Choose them wisely, then do them without clinging.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: When obligatory action is done because it ought to be done, giving up attachment and also the fruit, that renunciation is sattvic.

prasang.title_en: What true renunciation is
prasang.summary: Krishna says good acts shouldn't be dropped; dropping duty out of fear or confusion gains nothing; real renunciation is giving up clinging to results, since no embodied being can stop acting.
prasang.lesson: Don't drop what matters out of fear; drop the clinging instead.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Arjuna asks what true renunciation is; Krishna answers.
bg_3.sanskrit: न द्वेष्ट्यकुशलं कर्म कुशले नानुषज्जते । त्यागी सत्त्वसमाविष्टो मेधावी छिन्नसंशयः ॥
bg_3.translation: The wise renouncer, full of clarity and free of doubt, does not hate disagreeable work nor cling to agreeable work.
bg_3.line: The wise don't hate unpleasant work or cling to pleasant work. Doubts gone, they just do it.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: He does not hate work that is unpleasant, nor is he attached to pleasant work; filled with sattva, wise, his doubts cut by knowledge of the self.

prasang.title_en: What true renunciation is
prasang.summary: Krishna says good acts shouldn't be dropped; dropping duty out of fear or confusion gains nothing; real renunciation is giving up clinging to results, since no embodied being can stop acting.
prasang.lesson: Don't drop what matters out of fear; drop the clinging instead.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Arjuna asks what true renunciation is; Krishna answers.
bg_3.sanskrit: न हि देहभृता शक्यं त्यक्तुं कर्माण्यशेषतः । यस्तु कर्मफलत्यागी स त्यागीत्यभिधीयते ॥
bg_3.translation: It is not possible for an embodied being to give up action entirely. But one who gives up the fruit of action is called a renouncer.
bg_3.line: No one with a body can give up action completely. Letting go of the payoff is the real renouncing.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: one who identifies with the body cannot abandon action completely; so the one who gives up the fruit while doing obligatory work is called a renouncer, by way of praise.

prasang.title_en: What true renunciation is
prasang.summary: Krishna says good acts shouldn't be dropped; dropping duty out of fear or confusion gains nothing; real renunciation is giving up clinging to results, since no embodied being can stop acting.
prasang.lesson: Don't drop what matters out of fear; drop the clinging instead.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Right after naming the five causes of any action, Krishna warns about the person who ignores four of them.
bg_3.sanskrit: तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः । पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्मतिः ॥
bg_3.translation: That being so, whoever, through an untrained understanding, sees himself alone as the doer does not truly see.
bg_3.line: If you think you alone made it happen, or alone made it fail, you're not seeing the whole picture.
bg_3.misuse: Not a way to dodge responsibility; you are still one of the five causes.
bg_3.verified_with: data tr.hi (Gita Press)
bg_3.our_note: One who, with an intellect untrained by scripture and teacher, sees the pure actionless self as the agent, when the five causes are the agents, does not see; he is of perverted understanding.

prasang.title_en: What makes an action happen
prasang.summary: Every action has five causes: the setting, the doer, the instruments, the efforts, and providence. Seeing oneself as the only doer is a mistake.
prasang.lesson: You are one cause among five; own your part, not the whole outcome.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
bg_3.sanskrit: सर्वभूतेषु येनैकं भावमव्ययमीक्षते । अविभक्तं विभक्तेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि सात्त्विकम् ॥
bg_3.translation: The knowledge by which one sees one imperishable being in all beings, undivided in the divided, know that knowledge to be sattvic.
bg_3.line: Clear understanding sees one undivided life in all beings, though they appear separate.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: The knowledge that sees the one changeless self, undivided in all the divided bodies, is sattvic.

prasang.title_en: Knowledge, action, doer, intellect, resolve and happiness by the three gunas
prasang.summary: Krishna describes clear, restless and dull versions of action, doer, judgement, resolve and happiness: the best joy is poison first and nectar later; the restless kind is nectar first and poison later.
prasang.lesson: Choose the joy that's hard at first and sweet later.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
bg_3.sanskrit: नियतं सङ्गरहितमरागद्वेषतः कृतम् । अफलप्रेप्सुना कर्म यत्तत्सात्त्विकमुच्यते ॥
bg_3.translation: Action that is obligatory, done without attachment, without love or hatred, by one who does not crave its fruit, is called sattvic.
bg_3.line: Good action is steady, done without clinging, not driven by like or dislike, or by what you'll get.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Obligatory action done without attachment, not prompted by love or hatred, by one who does not desire its fruit, is sattvic.

prasang.title_en: Knowledge, action, doer, intellect, resolve and happiness by the three gunas
prasang.summary: Krishna describes clear, restless and dull versions of action, doer, judgement, resolve and happiness: the best joy is poison first and nectar later; the restless kind is nectar first and poison later.
prasang.lesson: Choose the joy that's hard at first and sweet later.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
bg_3.sanskrit: यत्तु कामेप्सुना कर्म साहङ्कारेण वा पुनः । क्रियते बहुलायासं तद्राजसमुदाहृतम् ॥
bg_3.translation: But action done by one seeking desires, or with ego, or with great strain, is called rajasic.
bg_3.line: Work done with huge strain, for ego or pleasure, is the restless kind.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Action done by one longing for its fruit, or with egoism, with great effort, is rajasic.

prasang.title_en: Knowledge, action, doer, intellect, resolve and happiness by the three gunas
prasang.summary: Krishna describes clear, restless and dull versions of action, doer, judgement, resolve and happiness: the best joy is poison first and nectar later; the restless kind is nectar first and poison later.
prasang.lesson: Choose the joy that's hard at first and sweet later.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
bg_3.sanskrit: अनुबन्धं क्षयं हिंसामनपेक्ष्य च पौरुषम् । मोहादारभ्यते कर्म यत्तत्तामसमुच्यते ॥
bg_3.translation: Action undertaken out of delusion, without regard to consequence, loss, injury to others, or one's own ability, is called tamasic.
bg_3.line: Action begun in confusion, without weighing consequences, cost, harm or your own capacity, is dark action.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Action started from non-discrimination, without regard to what follows, to loss, to harm to living beings, and to one's own ability, is tamasic.

prasang.title_en: Knowledge, action, doer, intellect, resolve and happiness by the three gunas
prasang.summary: Krishna describes clear, restless and dull versions of action, doer, judgement, resolve and happiness: the best joy is poison first and nectar later; the restless kind is nectar first and poison later.
prasang.lesson: Choose the joy that's hard at first and sweet later.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
bg_3.sanskrit: रागी कर्मफलप्रेप्सुर्लुब्धो हिंसात्मकोऽशुचिः । हर्षशोकान्वितः कर्ता राजसः परिकीर्तितः ॥
bg_3.translation: The doer who is passionate, eager for the fruits of work, greedy, harmful, impure, and swayed by joy and sorrow, is called rajasic.
bg_3.line: Hungry for results, greedy, willing to harm, unclean, tossed by joy and grief: the restless kind of doer.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Attached, desiring the fruit of action, covetous, given to injuring, impure, elated at success and grieved at failure: such a doer is rajasic.

prasang.title_en: Knowledge, action, doer, intellect, resolve and happiness by the three gunas
prasang.summary: Krishna describes clear, restless and dull versions of action, doer, judgement, resolve and happiness: the best joy is poison first and nectar later; the restless kind is nectar first and poison later.
prasang.lesson: Choose the joy that's hard at first and sweet later.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
bg_3.sanskrit: अयुक्तः प्राकृतः स्तब्धः शठो नैष्कृतिकोऽलसः । विषादी दीर्घसूत्री च कर्ता तामस उच्यते ॥
bg_3.translation: The doer who is undisciplined, vulgar, obstinate, deceitful, malicious, lazy, despondent and procrastinating, is called tamasic.
bg_3.line: Careless, crude, stubborn, deceitful, spiteful, lazy, gloomy and always putting things off: the dull kind of doer.
bg_3.misuse: A mirror for your own habits, not a label for anyone with depression or burnout.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: vishadi is one always sunk in dejection, dirghasutri one who puts off for a month what should be done today; such a doer is tamasic.

prasang.title_en: Knowledge, action, doer, intellect, resolve and happiness by the three gunas
prasang.summary: Krishna describes clear, restless and dull versions of action, doer, judgement, resolve and happiness: the best joy is poison first and nectar later; the restless kind is nectar first and poison later.
prasang.lesson: Choose the joy that's hard at first and sweet later.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
bg_3.sanskrit: यया धर्ममधर्मं च कार्यं चाकार्यमेव च । अयथावत्प्रजानाति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ राजसी ॥
bg_3.translation: The understanding by which one wrongly knows right and wrong, what should and should not be done, that understanding, Partha, is rajasic.
bg_3.line: A mind clouded by restlessness can't quite tell right from wrong, or what to do from what to avoid.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: The intellect by which one understands dharma and adharma, what should and should not be done, not as they are, is rajasic.

prasang.title_en: Knowledge, action, doer, intellect, resolve and happiness by the three gunas
prasang.summary: Krishna describes clear, restless and dull versions of action, doer, judgement, resolve and happiness: the best joy is poison first and nectar later; the restless kind is nectar first and poison later.
prasang.lesson: Choose the joy that's hard at first and sweet later.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
bg_3.sanskrit: अधर्मं धर्ममिति या मन्यते तमसाऽऽवृता । सर्वार्थान्विपरीतांश्च बुद्धिः सा पार्थ तामसी ॥
bg_3.translation: The understanding which, wrapped in darkness, thinks wrong is right and sees all things in reverse, Partha, is tamasic.
bg_3.line: A mind wrapped in darkness takes wrong for right and sees everything upside down.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Covered by tamas, the intellect regards adharma as dharma and understands all things contrary to what they are.

prasang.title_en: Knowledge, action, doer, intellect, resolve and happiness by the three gunas
prasang.summary: Krishna describes clear, restless and dull versions of action, doer, judgement, resolve and happiness: the best joy is poison first and nectar later; the restless kind is nectar first and poison later.
prasang.lesson: Choose the joy that's hard at first and sweet later.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
bg_3.sanskrit: धृत्या यया धारयते मनःप्राणेन्द्रियक्रियाः । योगेनाव्यभिचारिण्या धृतिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी ॥
bg_3.translation: The firmness by which one holds the workings of the mind, breath and senses through unwavering yoga, that firmness, Partha, is sattvic.
bg_3.line: True resolve holds mind, breath and senses steady through unwavering practice.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: The firmness, always joined to concentration, by which the functions of mind, breath and senses are kept from going the wrong way, is sattvic.

prasang.title_en: Knowledge, action, doer, intellect, resolve and happiness by the three gunas
prasang.summary: Krishna describes clear, restless and dull versions of action, doer, judgement, resolve and happiness: the best joy is poison first and nectar later; the restless kind is nectar first and poison later.
prasang.lesson: Choose the joy that's hard at first and sweet later.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
bg_3.sanskrit: यया तु धर्मकामार्थान् धृत्या धारयतेऽर्जुन । प्रसङ्गेन फलाकाङ्क्षी धृतिः सा पार्थ राजसी ॥
bg_3.translation: But the firmness by which one holds to duty, pleasure and wealth with attachment, craving their fruits, Arjuna, that firmness, Partha, is rajasic.
bg_3.line: Clinging to duty, pleasure and wealth for what they'll bring you is restless resolve.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: The firmness by which one holds fast to duty, pleasure and wealth, desiring their fruit as occasion arises, is rajasic.

prasang.title_en: Knowledge, action, doer, intellect, resolve and happiness by the three gunas
prasang.summary: Krishna describes clear, restless and dull versions of action, doer, judgement, resolve and happiness: the best joy is poison first and nectar later; the restless kind is nectar first and poison later.
prasang.lesson: Choose the joy that's hard at first and sweet later.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
bg_3.sanskrit: यया स्वप्नं भयं शोकं विषादं मदमेव च । न विमुञ्चति दुर्मेधा धृतिः सा पार्थ तामसी ॥
bg_3.translation: The firmness by which a dull-minded person does not let go of sleep, fear, grief, despondency and pride, that firmness, Partha, is tamasic.
bg_3.line: Stubbornly holding on to sleep, fear, grief, despair and pride is the dark kind of resolve.
bg_3.misuse: Not a judgement on depression or grief; it names the habit of clinging to them as if they were safety.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: The firmness by which one of poor understanding does not give up sleep, fear, grief, dejection and arrogance is tamasic.

prasang.title_en: Knowledge, action, doer, intellect, resolve and happiness by the three gunas
prasang.summary: Krishna describes clear, restless and dull versions of action, doer, judgement, resolve and happiness: the best joy is poison first and nectar later; the restless kind is nectar first and poison later.
prasang.lesson: Choose the joy that's hard at first and sweet later.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
bg_3.sanskrit: सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं श्रृणु मे भरतर्षभ । अभ्यासाद्रमते यत्र दुःखान्तं च निगच्छति ॥
bg_3.translation: Now hear from me the three kinds of happiness, best of the Bharatas: the happiness one comes to enjoy through practice, and in which one reaches the end of sorrow.
bg_3.line: There is a joy you grow into through practice, one that brings sorrow to an end.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Hear of the threefold happiness: that in which one delights by repeated practice and surely comes to the end of sorrow is described next.

prasang.title_en: Knowledge, action, doer, intellect, resolve and happiness by the three gunas
prasang.summary: Krishna describes clear, restless and dull versions of action, doer, judgement, resolve and happiness: the best joy is poison first and nectar later; the restless kind is nectar first and poison later.
prasang.lesson: Choose the joy that's hard at first and sweet later.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
bg_3.sanskrit: यदग्रे चानुबन्धे च सुखं मोहनमात्मनः । निद्रालस्यप्रमादोत्थं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥
bg_3.translation: The happiness that deludes the self in the beginning and in the end, arising from sleep, laziness and heedlessness, is called tamasic.
bg_3.line: Pleasure from sleep, laziness and carelessness dulls you from start to finish.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: The happiness that deludes the self at the beginning and at the end, born of sleep, sloth and negligence, is tamasic.

prasang.title_en: Knowledge, action, doer, intellect, resolve and happiness by the three gunas
prasang.summary: Krishna describes clear, restless and dull versions of action, doer, judgement, resolve and happiness: the best joy is poison first and nectar later; the restless kind is nectar first and poison later.
prasang.lesson: Choose the joy that's hard at first and sweet later.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
bg_3.sanskrit: स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः । स्वकर्मनिरतः सिद्धिं यथा विन्दति तच्छृणु ॥
bg_3.translation: Each person, devoted to his own work, attains perfection. Hear how one devoted to his own work finds perfection.
bg_3.line: Devoted to your own work, you reach fulfilment. Here's how.
bg_3.misuse: Not 'stay in the job your community or birth assigned'. 'Your own work' means the work that fits your nature.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: devoted to the work proper to him, a person gains the perfection of fitness for knowledge. Ramanuja likewise takes one's own work, done as worship, as the means.

prasang.title_en: Duties by nature, and their fruit
prasang.summary: After listing duties by varna, Krishna says one reaches perfection through one's own work done as worship, and that one's own path, though imperfect, beats another's, since every undertaking has flaws.
prasang.lesson: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna on the steadiness of one established in knowledge.
bg_3.sanskrit: असक्तबुद्धिः सर्वत्र जितात्मा विगतस्पृहः । नैष्कर्म्यसिद्धिं परमां संन्यासेनाधिगच्छति ॥
bg_3.translation: One whose understanding is unattached everywhere, who has mastered himself and is free from desire, reaches through renunciation the supreme perfection of freedom from action.
bg_3.line: Unattached everywhere, self-mastered, free of craving: that's the highest freedom.
bg_3.misuse: Unattached is not uncaring; it doesn't ask you to step back from family or friends.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: With intellect unattached to sons, wife and the rest, self subdued, thirst gone, he attains by renunciation, that is by right knowledge, the supreme perfection of freedom from action.

prasang.title_en: Established in knowledge
prasang.summary: Free of ego, force, arrogance, desire, anger and possessiveness, one becomes peaceful, neither grieving nor craving, the same to all.
prasang.lesson: Drop the 'mine' and peace follows.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna on the steadiness of one established in knowledge.
bg_3.sanskrit: अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम् । विमुच्य निर्ममः शान्तो ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥
bg_3.translation: Having given up ego, force, arrogance, desire, anger and possessiveness, free from the sense of 'mine' and peaceful, one becomes fit to be one with Brahman.
bg_3.line: Let go of ego, force, arrogance, desire, anger and possessiveness. Without 'mine', you become peaceful.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: having given up even the possessions kept for the body's upkeep, as a renunciate without 'mine' and at peace, he becomes fit for being Brahman.

prasang.title_en: Established in knowledge
prasang.summary: Free of ego, force, arrogance, desire, anger and possessiveness, one becomes peaceful, neither grieving nor craving, the same to all.
prasang.lesson: Drop the 'mine' and peace follows.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna on the steadiness of one established in knowledge.
bg_3.sanskrit: ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति । समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु मद्भक्तिं लभते पराम् ॥
bg_3.translation: Become one with Brahman, serene in self, one neither grieves nor craves. The same to all beings, one gains supreme devotion to me.
bg_3.line: Serene within, they neither grieve nor crave, and treat all beings alike.
bg_3.misuse: Not 'don't grieve'. It describes a serenity that grows, not a rule against sorrow.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: having attained Brahman and a serene self, he does not grieve over any loss or long for anything; he gains the supreme devotion which is knowledge. Ramanuja reads supreme devotion as the direct fruit of seeing the self.

prasang.title_en: Established in knowledge
prasang.summary: Free of ego, force, arrogance, desire, anger and possessiveness, one becomes peaceful, neither grieving nor craving, the same to all.
prasang.lesson: Drop the 'mine' and peace follows.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Near the end, Krishna tells Arjuna that a busy, working life is no barrier.
bg_3.sanskrit: सर्वकर्माण्यपि सदा कुर्वाणो मद्व्यपाश्रयः । मत्प्रसादादवाप्नोति शाश्वतं पदमव्ययम् ॥
bg_3.translation: Even while always doing every kind of work, the one who leans on me reaches the eternal, imperishable home by my grace.
bg_3.line: Doing all their work while leaning on me, they reach the lasting home, by my grace.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Even one who always does all actions, taking the Lord as his whole refuge, attains by the Lord's grace the eternal state.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna's final counsel: act with devotion, reflect, choose, and take refuge.
bg_3.sanskrit: चेतसा सर्वकर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्परः । बुद्धियोगमुपाश्रित्य मच्चित्तः सततं भव ॥
bg_3.translation: Mentally resigning all actions to me, holding me as the highest, relying on the yoga of understanding, keep your mind always on me.
bg_3.line: Inwardly hand all your work to the divine, hold it as your goal, and keep your mind on it.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: With discriminating mind give up all actions to the Lord; hold him as the supreme, resort to the yoga of steady understanding and keep the mind on him.

prasang.title_en: Action with devotion: surrender
prasang.summary: Krishna urges Arjuna to offer all action, warns that ego will only trip him, tells him to reflect fully and then choose, and finally to take refuge in him alone and not grieve.
prasang.lesson: Reflect fully, choose freely, and set down the fear.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna's final counsel: act with devotion, reflect, choose, and take refuge.
bg_3.sanskrit: मच्चित्तः सर्वदुर्गाणि मत्प्रसादात्तरिष्यसि । अथ चेत्त्वमहङ्कारान्न श्रोष्यसि विनङ्क्ष्यसि ॥
bg_3.translation: Fixing your mind on me, you will cross over all obstacles by my grace. But if out of ego you will not listen, you will perish.
bg_3.line: Heart turned to the divine, you'll cross every obstacle. Refuse out of ego, and you'll be lost.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: with mind on the Lord you will cross all the hard places of samsara by his grace; if from ego, thinking yourself learned, you do not heed, you will be ruined.

prasang.title_en: Action with devotion: surrender
prasang.summary: Krishna urges Arjuna to offer all action, warns that ego will only trip him, tells him to reflect fully and then choose, and finally to take refuge in him alone and not grieve.
prasang.lesson: Reflect fully, choose freely, and set down the fear.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Krishna's final counsel: act with devotion, reflect, choose, and take refuge.
bg_3.sanskrit: तमेव शरणं गच्छ सर्वभावेन भारत । तत्प्रसादात्परां शान्तिं स्थानं प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतम् ॥
bg_3.translation: Take refuge in Him alone with your whole being, Bharata. By His grace you will attain supreme peace and the eternal abode.
bg_3.line: Take refuge in the divine with all your being. By that grace you'll find supreme peace.
bg_3.misuse: Surrender is trust, not giving up your judgement or your effort.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: go for refuge with your whole being to the Lord who dwells in the hearts of all; by his grace you will gain the highest peace and the eternal state. Ramanuja reads it as the call to surrender to the inner ruler.

prasang.title_en: Action with devotion: surrender
prasang.summary: Krishna urges Arjuna to offer all action, warns that ego will only trip him, tells him to reflect fully and then choose, and finally to take refuge in him alone and not grieve.
prasang.lesson: Reflect fully, choose freely, and set down the fear.

bg_3.speaker: Krishna
bg_3.setting: Before his final words, Krishna tells Arjuna why he is saying them.
bg_3.sanskrit: सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः श्रृणु मे परमं वचः । इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम् ॥
bg_3.translation: Hear once more my highest word, the most secret of all: you are deeply loved by me, and so I will tell you what is good for you.
bg_3.line: Listen once more to my deepest word: you are truly dear to me.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Shankara: the Lord repeats the most secret teaching not from fear or for gain but because Arjuna is firmly dear. Ramanuja: it introduces the final word on devotion.

bg_3.speaker: Sanjaya
bg_3.setting: Sanjaya's closing words to the blind king, after narrating the whole dialogue.
bg_3.sanskrit: यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः । तत्र श्रीर्विजयो भूतिर्ध्रुवा नीतिर्मतिर्मम ॥
bg_3.translation: Wherever there is Krishna, the lord of yoga, and wherever there is Partha, the archer, there are fortune, victory, prosperity and sound policy. This is my conviction.
bg_3.line: Where wisdom and skilled effort stand together, there is fortune, victory, wellbeing and steady justice.
bg_3.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
bg_3.our_note: Sanjaya's closing conviction: where the Lord of yoga and the bow-bearing Partha are, there fortune, victory, increase and unfailing right conduct abide. Later teachers draw the lesson of grace joined to effort.

prasang.title_en: The glory of the Gita
prasang.summary: Krishna asks if Arjuna's confusion is gone; Arjuna says yes and that he will act. Sanjaya rejoices and declares that where Krishna and Arjuna stand, victory follows.
prasang.lesson: Clarity, once found, turns into action.

bh_1.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh_1.setting: From the opening section on fools: why some people cannot be reasoned with.
bh_1.sanskrit: अज्ञः सुखमाराध्यः सुखतरमाराध्यते विशेषज्ञः । ज्ञानलवदुर्विदग्धं ब्रह्मापि तं नरं न रञ्जयति ॥
bh_1.translation: An ignorant person is easily won over; an expert, more easily still. But a person puffed up by a scrap of knowledge not even Brahma, the Creator, can satisfy.
bh_1.line: The ignorant can be taught and the expert persuaded. The half-knower not even God can convince.
bh_1.misuse: Not a licence to dismiss everyone who disagrees with you as a half-knower; check yourself first.
bh_1.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 3; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.3
bh_1.our_note: Opening of the murkha-paddhati. A mirror as much as a verdict on others.

prasang.title_en: Nitishatakam: On fools and the half-learned
prasang.summary: Twelve verses on the futility of arguing with the closed or half-educated mind, framed as satire. The poet admits his own early arrogance (Niti 8) and ends by preferring wild mountains to the company of fools.
prasang.lesson: Spend your effort where it can land; some minds will not move, and the first one to check is yours.

bh_1.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh_1.setting: From the section on fools, on the stubborn mind.
bh_1.sanskrit: प्रसह्य मणिमुद्धरेन्मकरवक्त्रदंष्ट्राङ्कुरा- त्समुद्रमपि संतरेत्प्रचलदूर्मिमालाकुलम् । भुजङ्गमपि कोपितं शिरसि पुष्पवद्धारये- न्न तु प्रतिनिविष्टमूर्खजनचित्तमाराधयेत् ॥
bh_1.translation: One might wrench a jewel from between a crocodile's teeth, swim an ocean tossing with rows of waves, wear an angry snake on one's head like a flower; but one cannot win over the mind of a fool who has dug in.
bh_1.line: You can pull a gem from a crocodile's jaws, but you cannot change a mind that has dug in.
bh_1.misuse: Use it to stop exhausting yourself in arguments, not to write people off.
bh_1.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 4; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.4; Kosambi 1948 no. 9 (OCR match)
bh_1.our_note: Murkha-paddhati: three impossible things are easier than pleasing the pratinivishta murkha.

prasang.title_en: Nitishatakam: On fools and the half-learned
prasang.summary: Twelve verses on the futility of arguing with the closed or half-educated mind, framed as satire. The poet admits his own early arrogance (Niti 8) and ends by preferring wild mountains to the company of fools.
prasang.lesson: Spend your effort where it can land; some minds will not move, and the first one to check is yours.

bh_1.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh_1.setting: The poet looks back on his own youthful arrogance.
bh_1.sanskrit: यदा किञ्चिज्ज्ञोऽहं गज इव मदान्धः समभवम् तदा सर्वज्ञोऽस्मीत्यभवदवलिप्तं मम मनः । यदा किञ्चित्किञ्चिद्बुधजनसकाशादवगतम् तदा मूर्खोऽस्मीति ज्वर इव मदो मे व्यपगतः ॥
bh_1.translation: When I knew a little, I was blind with pride like an elephant in rut, and my mind swelled: 'I know everything.' When, little by little, I learned from the wise, I realised 'I am a fool', and my pride left me like a fever.
bh_1.line: When I knew a little, I thought I knew everything. Learning from the wise, my fever of pride broke.
bh_1.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 8; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.8; Kosambi 1948 no. 5 (OCR match)
bh_1.our_note: First-person confession; the cure named is the company of the learned.

prasang.title_en: Nitishatakam: On fools and the half-learned
prasang.summary: Twelve verses on the futility of arguing with the closed or half-educated mind, framed as satire. The poet admits his own early arrogance (Niti 8) and ends by preferring wild mountains to the company of fools.
prasang.lesson: Spend your effort where it can land; some minds will not move, and the first one to check is yours.

bh_1.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh_1.setting: Closing verse of the section on fools.
bh_1.sanskrit: वरं पर्वतदुर्गेषु भ्रान्तं वनचरैः सह । न मूर्खजनसम्पर्कः सुरेन्द्रभवनेष्वपि ॥
bh_1.translation: Better to wander mountain passes with the creatures of the forest than to keep company with fools, even in the palace of Indra.
bh_1.line: Better to roam wild hills with animals than to live in a palace among fools.
bh_1.misuse: About the company you choose to keep, not contempt for people.
bh_1.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 14; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.14; Kosambi 1948 no. 320 (OCR match)
bh_1.our_note: Close of the murkha-paddhati; a generic maxim on company.

prasang.title_en: Nitishatakam: On fools and the half-learned
prasang.summary: Twelve verses on the futility of arguing with the closed or half-educated mind, framed as satire. The poet admits his own early arrogance (Niti 8) and ends by preferring wild mountains to the company of fools.
prasang.lesson: Spend your effort where it can land; some minds will not move, and the first one to check is yours.

bh_1.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh_1.setting: From the section praising learning, addressed to proud rulers.
bh_1.sanskrit: हर्तुर्याति न गोचरं किमपि शं पुष्णाति यत् सर्वदा- ऽप्यर्थिभ्यः प्रतिपाद्यमानमनिशं प्राप्नोति वृद्धिं पराम् । कल्पान्तेष्वपि न प्रयाति निधनं विद्याख्यमन्तर्धनं येषां तान् प्रति मानमुज्झत नृपाः कस्तैः सह स्पर्धते ॥
bh_1.translation: It never comes within a thief's sight; it always nourishes some deep good; given to those who ask, it grows greater; even at the end of an age it does not perish. Kings, drop your pride before those who own this inner wealth called learning. Who can compete with them?
bh_1.line: Learning is wealth no thief can see. It grows when you give it away and never perishes.
bh_1.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 16; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.16; Kosambi 1948 no. 15 (OCR match)
bh_1.our_note: Vidvat-paddhati, addressed to kings: drop your pride before the learned.

prasang.title_en: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
prasang.summary: Bhartrihari praises learning as wealth no thief can take and speech as the one lasting ornament, then turns to good company and the three kinds of people who face obstacles. It ends with the 'sword's-edge vow' of the good.
prasang.lesson: What you learn and how you speak are the wealth no one can take from you.

bh_1.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh_1.setting: From the section praising learning: what fate cannot take.
bh_1.sanskrit: अम्भोजिनीवनविहारविलासमेव हंसस्य हन्ति नितरां कुपितो विधाता । न त्वस्य दुग्धजलभेदविधौ प्रसिद्धां वैदग्ध्यकीर्तिमपहर्तुमसौ समर्थः ॥
bh_1.translation: An angry Creator may destroy the swan's delight of roaming its lotus pond, but he cannot take away its famous skill of separating milk from water.
bh_1.line: Fate can take away the swan's lake. It cannot take its gift of telling milk from water.
bh_1.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 18; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.18; Kosambi 1948 no. 38 (OCR match)
bh_1.our_note: Vidvat-paddhati: Vidhata can remove circumstances, never vaidagdhya.

prasang.title_en: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
prasang.summary: Bhartrihari praises learning as wealth no thief can take and speech as the one lasting ornament, then turns to good company and the three kinds of people who face obstacles. It ends with the 'sword's-edge vow' of the good.
prasang.lesson: What you learn and how you speak are the wealth no one can take from you.

bh_1.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh_1.setting: From the section praising learning: the one ornament that lasts.
bh_1.sanskrit: केयूराणि न भूषयन्ति पुरुषं हारा न चन्द्रोज्ज्वला न स्नानं न विलेपनं न कुसुमं नालङ्कृता मूर्धजाः । वाण्येका समलङ्करोति पुरुषं या संस्कृता धार्यते क्षीयन्ते खलु भूषणानि सततं वाग्भूषणं भूषणम् ॥
bh_1.translation: Armlets do not adorn a person, nor necklaces bright as the moon, nor bathing, nor perfume, nor flowers, nor dressed hair. Speech alone, refined and well held, truly adorns a person. Ornaments wear away; the ornament of speech is the real ornament.
bh_1.line: Jewellery wears out. Well-chosen speech is the one ornament that lasts.
bh_1.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 19; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.19
bh_1.our_note: Vidvat-paddhati.

prasang.title_en: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
prasang.summary: Bhartrihari praises learning as wealth no thief can take and speech as the one lasting ornament, then turns to good company and the three kinds of people who face obstacles. It ends with the 'sword's-edge vow' of the good.
prasang.lesson: What you learn and how you speak are the wealth no one can take from you.

bh_1.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh_1.setting: From the section praising learning.
bh_1.sanskrit: विद्या नाम नरस्य रूपमधिकं प्रच्छन्नगुप्तं धनं विद्या भोगकरी यशस्सुखकरी विद्या गुरूणां गुरुः । विद्या बन्धुजनो विदेशगमने विद्या परा देवता विद्या राजसु पूजिता न तु धनं विद्याविहीनः पशुः ॥
bh_1.translation: Learning is a person's greater beauty, a hidden and guarded treasure. Learning brings enjoyment, fame and happiness; it is the teacher of teachers. In a foreign land learning is your kin; learning is the highest deity. Kings honour learning, not wealth. Without learning a person is little more than an animal.
bh_1.line: In a foreign land, what you have learned is your family: a treasure no one can see.
bh_1.misuse: The last phrase is a poet's jab, not a judgement on people without schooling.
bh_1.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 20; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.20; Kosambi 1948 no. 70 (OCR match)
bh_1.our_note: Vidvat-paddhati. The verse ends 'one without learning is a beast', which the line rightly leaves out.

prasang.title_en: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
prasang.summary: Bhartrihari praises learning as wealth no thief can take and speech as the one lasting ornament, then turns to good company and the three kinds of people who face obstacles. It ends with the 'sword's-edge vow' of the good.
prasang.lesson: What you learn and how you speak are the wealth no one can take from you.

bh_1.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh_1.setting: From the section praising learning: a list of 'if you have this, what need of that'.
bh_1.sanskrit: क्षान्तिश्चेत् कवचेन किं किमरिभिः क्रोधोऽस्ति चेद्देहिनां ज्ञातिश्चेदनलेन किं यदि सुहृद् दिव्यौषधैः किं फलम् । किं सर्पैर्यदि दुर्जनाः किमु धनैर्विद्या न वन्द्या यदि व्रीडा चेत्किमु भूषणैः सुकविता यद्यस्ति राज्येन किम् ॥
bh_1.translation: If you have forbearance, what need of armour? If you have anger, what need of enemies? If you have kinsmen, what need of fire? If a friend, what need of magic medicines? If the wicked are around, what need of snakes? If spotless learning, what need of riches? If modesty, what need of ornaments? If fine poetry, what need of a kingdom?
bh_1.line: With patience, who needs armour? With anger, who needs enemies? With a true friend, who needs medicine?
bh_1.misuse: Forbearance protects you; it is not permission for others to keep hurting you.
bh_1.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 21; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.21
bh_1.our_note: A 'kim' list. The original also says 'with kinsmen, what need of fire', a bitter aside the line omits.

bh_1.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh_1.setting: From the section praising learning: on good company.
bh_1.sanskrit: जाड्यं धियो हरति सिञ्चति वाचि सत्यं मानोन्नतिं दिशति पापमपाकरोति । चेतः प्रसादयति दिक्षु तनोति कीर्तिं सत्सङ्गतिः कथय किं न करोति पुंसाम् ॥
bh_1.translation: Good company takes dullness from the mind, sprinkles truth into speech, raises one's dignity, removes wrongdoing, clears the heart and spreads one's good name in every direction. Tell me, what does good company not do for a person?
bh_1.line: Good company clears the mind, puts truth in your speech and lifts your spirit. What does it not do?
bh_1.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 23; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.23; Kosambi 1948 no. 42 (OCR match)
bh_1.our_note: The classic satsangati verse.

bh_1.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh_1.setting: From the section praising learning: the blessings of a good life.
bh_1.sanskrit: सूनुः सच्चरितः सती प्रियतमा स्वामी प्रसादोन्मुखः स्निग्धं मित्रमवञ्चकः परिजनो निष्क्लेशलेशं मनः । आकारो रुचिरः स्थिरश्च विभवो विद्यावदातं मुखं तुष्टे विष्टपकष्टहारिणि हरौ सम्प्राप्यते देहिना ॥
bh_1.translation: A son of good conduct, a devoted and loving wife, a gracious master, an affectionate friend, kinsfolk who do not cheat, a mind without a trace of strain, a pleasing form, lasting prosperity, a face bright with learning: these come to the one with whom Hari, remover of the world's troubles, is pleased.
bh_1.line: A good child, a loving spouse, a kind boss, a true friend, a mind at ease: count these as grace.
bh_1.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 25; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.25; Kosambi 1948 no. 807 (OCR match)
bh_1.our_note: The list is of what divine favour looks like in a householder's life. Sanskrit has 'son' and 'wife'; the line's neutral words are right.

bh_1.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh_1.setting: From the section praising learning: the path every tradition shares.
bh_1.sanskrit: प्राणाघातान्निवृत्तिः परधनहरणे संयमः सत्यवाक्यं काले शक्त्या प्रदानं युवतिजनकथामूकभावः परेषाम् । तृष्णास्रोतोविभङ्गो गुरुषु च विनयः सर्वभूतानुकम्पा सामान्यः सर्वशास्त्रेष्वनुपहतविधिः श्रेयसामेष पन्थाः ॥
bh_1.translation: Refraining from taking life, restraint from seizing others' wealth, truthful speech, timely giving as one is able, silence in gossip about others' wives, breaking the current of craving, humility before elders, compassion for all beings: this is the common path to the good, unbroken in all the scriptures.
bh_1.line: Harm no one, take nothing that isn't yours, speak truly, give in time, cut craving, be kind to all.
bh_1.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 26; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.26; Kosambi 1948 no. 3 (OCR match)
bh_1.our_note: Shreyasam esha panthah: the common path.

prasang.summary: Bhartrihari praises learning as wealth no thief can take and speech as the one lasting ornament, then turns to good company and the three kinds of people who face obstacles. It ends with the 'sword's-edge vow' of the good.

bh_1.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh_1.setting: From the section praising learning: the three kinds of people.
bh_1.sanskrit: प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन नीचैः प्रारभ्य विघ्नविहता विरमन्ति मध्याः ॥ विघ्नैः पुनः पुनरपि प्रतिहन्यमानाः प्रारब्धमुत्तमगुणा न परित्यजन्ति ॥
bh_1.translation: The lowest do not begin at all, for fear of obstacles. The middling begin, but stop when obstacles strike. The best, struck by obstacles again and again, do not give up what they have begun.
bh_1.line: Some never start for fear of obstacles; some quit when obstacles hit. The best keep going.
bh_1.misuse: Perseverance is not refusing ever to change course; weigh honestly whether the goal still deserves you.
bh_1.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 27; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.27; Kosambi 1948 no. 277 (OCR match)
bh_1.our_note: Also found in the Mudrarakshasa. Blesses perseverance; ranks the hesitant as 'low', so not for someone already ashamed of not starting.

prasang.title_en: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
prasang.summary: Bhartrihari praises learning as wealth no thief can take and speech as the one lasting ornament, then turns to good company and the three kinds of people who face obstacles. It ends with the 'sword's-edge vow' of the good.
prasang.lesson: What you learn and how you speak are the wealth no one can take from you.

bh_1.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh_1.setting: Closing verse of the section praising learning: the 'sword's-edge vow' of the good.
bh_1.sanskrit: असन्तो नाभ्यर्थ्याः सुहृदपि न याच्यः कृशधनः प्रिया न्याय्या वृत्तिर्मलिनमसुभङ्गेऽप्यसुकरम् । विपद्युच्चैः स्थेयं पदमनुविधेयं च महतां सतां केनोद्दिष्टं विषममसिधाराव्रतमिदम् ॥
bh_1.translation: Do not ask the wicked for favours; do not ask a friend of slender means for money; love a just way of earning; do nothing base even when life is at stake; stand tall in trouble; follow in the footsteps of the great. Who taught the good this vow, hard as walking a sword's edge?
bh_1.line: Don't beg favours from the wicked or money from a struggling friend. Stand tall in hard times.
bh_1.misuse: 'Even when life is at stake' is the poet's intensity; no principle asks you to harm yourself.
bh_1.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 28; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.28; Kosambi 1948 no. 18 (OCR match)
bh_1.our_note: The asidhara-vrata of the good. 'Even at the cost of life' is rhetorical intensity.

bh_1.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh_1.setting: From the section on honour and spirit, contrasting a dog and an elephant.
bh_1.sanskrit: लाङ्गूलचालनमधश्चरणावपातं भूमौ निपत्य वदनोदरदर्शनं च । श्वा पिण्डदस्य कुरुते गजपुङ्गवस्तु धीरं विलोकयति चाटुशतैश्च भुङ्क्ते ॥
bh_1.translation: The dog wags its tail, falls at the feet of whoever feeds it, rolls on the ground showing its mouth and belly; the lordly elephant looks on steadily and eats only after a hundred coaxing words.
bh_1.line: The dog grovels before whoever feeds it. The elephant waits with quiet dignity.
bh_1.misuse: Dignity, not arrogance: it does not mean making others beg you.
bh_1.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 31; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.31; Kosambi 1948 no. 57 (OCR match)
bh_1.our_note: Mana-shaurya-paddhati.

prasang.title_en: Nitishatakam: Honour and spirit
prasang.summary: Images of the lion and the elephant celebrate self-respect and inborn spirit. Some verses lean toward intolerance of insult, a warrior-king ideal.
prasang.lesson: Keep your dignity without needing to win every fight.

bh_1.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh_1.setting: From the section on wealth: how the world treats someone who has lost money.
bh_1.sanskrit: तानीन्द्रियाण्यविकलानि तदेव नाम सा बुद्धिरप्रतिहता वचनं तदेव । अर्थोष्मणा विरहितः पुरुषः क्षणेन सोऽप्यन्य एव भवतीति विचित्रमेतत् ॥
bh_1.translation: The same faculties, unimpaired; the same name; the same unclouded mind; the same speech. Yet a man deprived of the warmth of wealth becomes, in a moment, someone else. How strange!
bh_1.line: Same person, same mind, same voice. Lose money, and people suddenly treat you as someone else.
bh_1.misuse: The verse mocks how the world sees you; it does not measure your worth.
bh_1.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 40; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.40; Kosambi 1948 no. 512 (OCR match)
bh_1.our_note: Artha-paddhati. The wonder, 'vichitram etat', is aimed at the world's judgement.

prasang.title_en: Nitishatakam: On wealth
prasang.summary: A wry look at money: how the world flatters the rich and forgets the broke, wealth's three destinies, and how distance and neglect ruin what we value. It closes with advice to the chataka bird not to plead before every cloud.
prasang.lesson: Money changes how others see you, not who you are. Give it, enjoy it, or lose it.

bh_1.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh_1.setting: From the section on wealth: a satire on how money buys reputation.
bh_1.sanskrit: यस्यास्ति वित्तं स नरः कुलीनः स पण्डितः स श्रुतवान् गुणज्ञः । स एव वक्ता स च दर्शनीयः सर्वे गुणाः काञ्चनमाश्रयन्ति ॥
bh_1.translation: Whoever has wealth is well-born, learned, well-read and a judge of merit; he is the eloquent one, the handsome one. All virtues take shelter in gold.
bh_1.line: Have money and suddenly you are wise, well-born and charming. All virtues seem to lodge in gold.
bh_1.misuse: Satire on the world's flattery, not advice to chase money.
bh_1.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 41; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.41; Kosambi 1948 no. 521 (OCR match)
bh_1.our_note: Satire. Read flat, it says the opposite of what the poet means.

prasang.title_en: Nitishatakam: On wealth
prasang.summary: A wry look at money: how the world flatters the rich and forgets the broke, wealth's three destinies, and how distance and neglect ruin what we value. It closes with advice to the chataka bird not to plead before every cloud.

bh_1.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh_1.setting: From the section on wealth: how good things are slowly lost.
bh_1.sanskrit: दौर्मन्त्र्यान्नृपतिर्विनश्यति यतिः सङ्गात् सुतो लालनाद् विप्रोऽनध्ययनात् कुलं कुतनयाच्छीलं खलोपासनात् । ह्रीर्मद्यादनवेक्षणादपि कृषिः स्नेहः प्रवासाश्र- यान्मैत्री चाप्रणयात् समृद्धिरनयात् त्यागः प्रमादाद्धनम् ॥
bh_1.translation: A king is ruined by bad counsel, an ascetic by attachment, a son by spoiling, a brahmin by neglecting study, a family by a wayward son, character by serving the wicked, modesty by drink, farming by neglect, affection by living far away, friendship by lack of warmth, prosperity by bad conduct, and wealth by careless spending.
bh_1.line: Affection fades with distance, friendship without warmth, wealth with carelessness, a child with spoiling.
bh_1.misuse: Distance strains affection; it does not doom it. The verse is a call to tend what you love.
bh_1.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 42; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.42; Kosambi 1948 no. 23 (OCR match)
bh_1.our_note: A list of twelve ruins. 'Affection is lost by living away' may sting readers abroad.

bh_1.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh_1.setting: From the section on wealth.
bh_1.sanskrit: दानं भोगो नाशस्तिस्रो गतयो भवन्ति वित्तस्य । यो न ददाति न भुङ्क्ते तस्य तृतीया गतिर्भवति ॥
bh_1.translation: Wealth has three destinies: giving, enjoying and loss. Whoever neither gives nor enjoys it meets the third.
bh_1.line: Money goes one of three ways: given, enjoyed, or lost. Neither give nor enjoy it, and it is lost.
bh_1.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 43; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.43; Kosambi 1948 no. 50 (OCR match)
bh_1.our_note: Artha-paddhati.

bh_1.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh_1.setting: From the section on wealth: how need changes what we value.
bh_1.sanskrit: परिक्षीणः कश्चित्स्पृहयति यवानां प्रसृतये स पश्चात् सम्पूर्णः कलयति धरित्रीं तृणसमाम् । अतश्चानैकान्त्याद्गुरुलघुतयाऽर्थेषु धनिना- मवस्था वस्तूनि प्रथयति च सङ्कोचयति च ॥
bh_1.translation: A man who has lost everything longs for a handful of barley; later, when full, he counts the whole earth as straw. Because nothing is fixed, a person's condition makes things look great or small.
bh_1.line: Starving, a handful of grain is everything. Full, the whole earth looks like straw.
bh_1.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 45; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.45; Kosambi 1948 no. 12 (OCR match)
bh_1.our_note: Artha-paddhati.

bh_1.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh_1.setting: From the section on wealth, advice to a ruler on caring for people.
bh_1.sanskrit: राजन् दुधुक्षसि यदि क्षितिधेनुमेतां तेनाद्य वत्समिव लोकममुं पुषाण । तस्मिंश्च सम्यगनिशं परिपोष्यमाणे नानाफलैः फलति कल्पलतेव भूमिः ॥
bh_1.translation: O king, if you wish to milk this cow, the earth, first nourish the people as one feeds the calf. When they are well and constantly cared for, the earth bears every kind of fruit, like a wish-granting vine.
bh_1.line: Want results from your people? Nourish them first, as you feed the calf before milking.
bh_1.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 46; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.46; Kosambi 1948 no. 58 (OCR match)
bh_1.our_note: Artha-paddhati, counsel to a king.

prasang.summary: A wry look at money: how the world flatters the rich and forgets the broke, wealth's three destinies, and how distance and neglect ruin what we value. It closes with advice to the chataka bird not to plead before every cloud.
prasang.lesson: Money changes how others see you, not who you are. Give it, enjoy it, or lose it.

bh_1.speaker: Bhartrihari
bh_1.setting: From the section on wealth: on keeping your dignity before the rich.
bh_1.sanskrit: यद्धात्रा निजभालपट्टलिखितं स्तोकं महद्वा धनं तत् प्राप्नोति मरुस्थलेऽपि नितरां मेरौ ततो नाधिकम् । तद्धीरो भव वित्तवत्सु कृपणां वृत्तिं वृथा मा कृथाः कूपे पश्य पयोनिधावपि घटो गृह्णाति तुल्यं जलम् ॥
bh_1.translation: Whatever wealth, small or great, the Creator has written on your forehead, you will get it even in a desert, and no more even on Mount Meru. So be steady; do not play the beggar before the rich for nothing. Look: a pot draws the same water from a well as from the ocean.
bh_1.line: A pot draws the same water from a well or the ocean. Keep your dignity before the rich.
bh_1.misuse: Not a reason to stop working or asking for fair pay; a reason not to grovel.
bh_1.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 49; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.49
bh_1.our_note: The verse grounds dignity in the doctrine that one's portion is written. The line keeps the dignity and leaves out fate, which is the safer use.
