prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

mbh_1.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nala and Damayanti
mbh_1.speaker: Narrator (Brihadashva)
mbh_1.setting: King Nala, possessed by the spirit of the dice, keeps gambling against his brother.
mbh_1.sanskrit: यथायथा हि नृपतिः पुष्करेणैव जीयते / तथातथाऽस्य वै द्यूते रागो भूयोऽभिवर्धते
mbh_1.translation: The more the king kept losing to Pushkara, the more his passion for the dice grew.
mbh_1.line: The more Nala lost, the harder he found it to stop playing.
mbh_1.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section LIX (section number inferred from data offset; meaning read from the Sanskrit)
mbh_1.our_note: Nala, entered by Kali, cannot stop; the tradition reads the compulsion as possession, a force riding him, and he later recovers everything.

prasang.title_en: Nala and Damayanti
prasang.summary: King Nala, possessed by the spirit Kali, gambles away his kingdom to his brother and abandons Damayanti in the forest. Years of separation and disguise follow, until Nala masters the dice and the two are reunited.
prasang.lesson: Compulsions can take everything. Loyalty and patience can still bring you home.

mbh_1.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nala and Damayanti
mbh_1.speaker: Damayanti
mbh_1.setting: Nala has lost everything at dice; Damayanti follows him into the forest and will not leave.
mbh_1.sanskrit: न च भार्यासमं किंचिन्नरस्यार्तस्य भेषजम् / नित्यं हि सर्वदुःखेषु सत्यमेतद्व्रवीमि ते
mbh_1.translation: There is no medicine like a wife for a man in pain, in every kind of sorrow. I tell you this truly.
mbh_1.line: In every sorrow, no medicine works like a partner who stays by your side.
mbh_1.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section LXI (section number inferred from data offset; meaning read from the Sanskrit)
mbh_1.our_note: Damayanti refusing to leave Nala in the forest. Spoken by the wife of herself.

prasang.title_en: Nala and Damayanti
prasang.summary: King Nala, possessed by the spirit Kali, gambles away his kingdom to his brother and abandons Damayanti in the forest. Years of separation and disguise follow, until Nala masters the dice and the two are reunited.
prasang.lesson: Compulsions can take everything. Loyalty and patience can still bring you home.

mbh_1.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Shibi and the dove
mbh_1.speaker: The hawk (Indra in disguise)
mbh_1.setting: A hawk demands the dove King Shibi is sheltering, arguing that rules can clash.
mbh_1.sanskrit: गुरुलाघवमाज्ञाय धर्माधर्मविनिश्चये / यतो भूयांस्ततो राजन्कुरु धर्मविनिश्चयम्
mbh_1.translation: When deciding between right and wrong, weigh what is heavier against what is lighter, and choose the course where the greater good lies.
mbh_1.line: When two duties pull against each other, weigh them, and choose the one that does more good.
mbh_1.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CXXXI (section number inferred from data offset; meaning read from the Sanskrit)
mbh_1.our_note: The hawk says this to make Shibi hand over the dove. Shibi accepts the weighing but keeps his refuge-duty and offers his own flesh. The principle is sound; the speaker is using it to tempt.

prasang.title_en: King Shibi and the dove
prasang.summary: A frightened dove flies to King Shibi for refuge; a hawk demands it back as its rightful food. Shibi offers the hawk anything else, finally his own flesh weighed against the dove, and climbs onto the scale himself. The birds reveal themselves as gods.
prasang.lesson: When duties collide, weigh them honestly, and keep your word to those who trust you.

mbh_1.speaker: Ashtavakra
mbh_1.setting: Twelve-year-old Ashtavakra is stopped at King Janaka's gate because he is 'only a boy'.
mbh_1.sanskrit: न ज्ञायते कायवृद्ध्या विवृद्धि- / र्यथाऽष्ठीला शाल्मलेः संप्रवृद्धाः / ह्रस्वोऽल्पकायः फलितो विवृद्धो / यश्चाफलस्तस्य न वृद्धभावः
mbh_1.translation: Growth isn't measured by the size of the body. A short tree that bears fruit has grown; a tall one that bears none has not.
mbh_1.line: Growth isn't size. A small tree bearing fruit has grown more than a tall, empty one.
mbh_1.our_note: Ashtavakra to the gatekeeper who bars him as a child.

prasang.title_en: Ashtavakra at Janaka's court
prasang.summary: Ashtavakra, born bent in eight places by his father's curse, learns at twelve that his father drowned after losing a debate to the court sage Bandi. Turned away at the gate as a child, he argues his way in and defeats Bandi.
prasang.lesson: Age and appearance don't measure wisdom. Don't dismiss anyone for being young.

mbh_1.speaker: Ashtavakra
mbh_1.setting: Twelve-year-old Ashtavakra is stopped at King Janaka's gate because he is 'only a boy'.
mbh_1.sanskrit: न तेन स्थविरो भवति येनास्य पलितं शिरः / बालोपि यः प्रजानाति तं देवाः स्थविरं विदुः
mbh_1.translation: A person is not old because his head is grey. The one who truly understands, even if young, is the one the gods call an elder.
mbh_1.line: Grey hair doesn't make anyone wise. Whoever understands, however young, is the real elder.
mbh_1.our_note: Ashtavakra at Janaka's gate; the same maxim is in Manu 2.156. He goes on to prove it by defeating Bandi in debate.

prasang.title_en: Ashtavakra at Janaka's court
prasang.summary: Ashtavakra, born bent in eight places by his father's curse, learns at twelve that his father drowned after losing a debate to the court sage Bandi. Turned away at the gate as a child, he argues his way in and defeats Bandi.
prasang.lesson: Age and appearance don't measure wisdom. Don't dismiss anyone for being young.

mbh_1.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Bhima and Hanuman
mbh_1.speaker: Hanuman
mbh_1.setting: Hanuman, having humbled his proud younger brother Bhima, sends him off with advice.
mbh_1.sanskrit: न हि धर्ममविज्ञाय वृद्धाननुपसेव्य च / धर्मो वै वेदितुं शक्यो बृहस्पतिसमैरपि
mbh_1.translation: Without learning what is right and sitting with those who have lived longer, no one can know it, not even someone as wise as Brihaspati.
mbh_1.line: No one, however brilliant, knows what is right without learning and listening to those who've lived it.
mbh_1.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CL (section number inferred from data offset; meaning read from the Sanskrit)
mbh_1.our_note: Hanuman to Bhima after humbling him.

prasang.title_en: Bhima meets Hanuman
prasang.summary: Searching for a flower for Draupadi, mighty Bhima finds an old monkey blocking the path and orders it to move. Told to lift its tail himself, he cannot budge it. The monkey is his elder brother Hanuman, who embraces him and teaches him.
prasang.lesson: Strength without humility is blind. The one blocking your path may be family.

mbh_1.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nahusha's questions
mbh_1.speaker: Nahusha asks; Yudhishthira answers
mbh_1.setting: King Nahusha, cursed into a python for his arrogance, holds Bhima captive and questions Yudhishthira.
mbh_1.sanskrit: क्वचिद्दानप्रयोगाद्धि सत्यमेव विशिष्यते / सत्यवाक्याच्च राजेनद्र क्वचिद्दानं विशिष्यते
mbh_1.translation: Sometimes truth outweighs giving, and sometimes giving outweighs truth. Likewise, harmlessness can matter more than pleasant speech. It depends on what the situation requires.
mbh_1.line: Sometimes honesty matters more than generosity, sometimes the reverse. It depends on what's at stake.
mbh_1.our_note: Yudhishthira on the relative weight of virtues.

prasang.title_en: Nahusha the python and Yudhishthira's answers
prasang.summary: A giant python seizes Bhima. It is King Nahusha, once lord of heaven, cursed for making sages carry his palanquin. He frees Bhima after Yudhishthira answers his questions on goodness, and is freed himself.
prasang.lesson: Success can blind anyone. What makes a person good is conduct, not birth.

mbh_1.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nahusha's questions
mbh_1.speaker: Nahusha
mbh_1.setting: King Nahusha, cursed into a python for his arrogance, holds Bhima captive and questions Yudhishthira.
mbh_1.sanskrit: सुप्रज्ञमपि चेच्छूरमृद्धिर्मोहयते नरम् / वर्तमानः सुखे सर्वो नावैतीति मतिर्मम
mbh_1.translation: Prosperity deludes a person, however wise and brave. Anyone living in comfort fails to notice it happening. That is my view.
mbh_1.line: Success can blind even the wise and brave. In comfort, nobody notices it happening.
mbh_1.our_note: Nahusha, fallen from Indra's seat into a python's body, speaks from experience of aishvarya-mada.

prasang.title_en: Nahusha the python and Yudhishthira's answers
prasang.summary: A giant python seizes Bhima. It is King Nahusha, once lord of heaven, cursed for making sages carry his palanquin. He frees Bhima after Yudhishthira answers his questions on goodness, and is freed himself.
prasang.lesson: Success can blind anyone. What makes a person good is conduct, not birth.

mbh_1.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nahusha's questions
mbh_1.speaker: Nahusha
mbh_1.setting: King Nahusha, cursed into a python for his arrogance, holds Bhima captive and questions Yudhishthira.
mbh_1.sanskrit: अहं हि दिवि दिव्येन विमानन चरन्पुरा / अभिमानेन मत्तः सन्कंचिन्नान्यमचिन्तयम्
mbh_1.translation: Once I moved through the sky in a celestial chariot, drunk on pride, and gave no thought to anyone else.
mbh_1.line: When I was riding high, drunk on pride, I stopped thinking about anyone but myself.
mbh_1.our_note: Nahusha's confession: abhimana made him yoke the sages to his palanquin, and Agastya's curse followed.

prasang.title_en: Nahusha the python and Yudhishthira's answers
prasang.summary: A giant python seizes Bhima. It is King Nahusha, once lord of heaven, cursed for making sages carry his palanquin. He frees Bhima after Yudhishthira answers his questions on goodness, and is freed himself.
prasang.lesson: Success can blind anyone. What makes a person good is conduct, not birth.

mbh_1.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nahusha's questions
mbh_1.speaker: Nahusha
mbh_1.setting: King Nahusha, cursed into a python for his arrogance, holds Bhima captive and questions Yudhishthira.
mbh_1.sanskrit: सत्यं दमस्तपो योगमहिंसा ज्ञाननित्यता / साधकानि सतां पुंसां न जातिर्नकुलं नृप
mbh_1.translation: Truth, self-control, discipline, steadiness, harmlessness and constant learning are what make a person good, O king, not birth or family.
mbh_1.line: Truth, self-control and kindness make a person good, not their birth or family.
mbh_1.our_note: The epic's clear statement that conduct, not jati or kula, makes the good person.

prasang.title_en: Nahusha the python and Yudhishthira's answers
prasang.summary: A giant python seizes Bhima. It is King Nahusha, once lord of heaven, cursed for making sages carry his palanquin. He frees Bhima after Yudhishthira answers his questions on goodness, and is freed himself.
prasang.lesson: Success can blind anyone. What makes a person good is conduct, not birth.

mbh_1.speaker: Narayana
mbh_1.setting: The child on the banyan explains to Markandeya why he revealed himself.
mbh_1.sanskrit: सर्वमेकार्णवं दृष्ट्वा नष्टं स्थावरजङ्गमम् / विक्लबोसि मया ज्ञातस्ततस्ते दर्शितं जगत्
mbh_1.translation: Seeing everything, moving and unmoving, lost in a single ocean, you were distressed. I knew it, and so I showed you the world.
mbh_1.line: When everything was flooded and you were frightened, I knew. So I showed you the world inside me.
mbh_1.verified_with: Ganguli (sacred-texts) section checked for context; Sanskrit read directly (Ganguli Vana Parva CLXXXIX; data 3.192)
mbh_1.our_note: Narayana as the child on the banyan leaf to Markandeya after the pralaya vision.

prasang.title_en: Markandeya and the child on the banyan leaf
prasang.summary: At the end of an age, the sage Markandeya drifts alone over a flooded world and sees a radiant child on a banyan branch. The child draws him inside his body, where he sees all the worlds, then asks if he has been resting, tired. Narayana explains he showed himself because he saw Markandeya's distress. Markandeya tells the Pandavas that this child is Krishna, sitting with them.
prasang.lesson: When everything you knew is underwater, you have not been forgotten; you are being held.

mbh_1.speaker: Markandeya
mbh_1.setting: Markandeya reveals that the child he saw is their own kinsman, Krishna, sitting with them.
mbh_1.sanskrit: सर्वेषामेव भूतानां पिता माता च माधवः / गच्छध्वमेनं शरणं शरण्यं कौरवर्षभाः
mbh_1.translation: Madhava is the father and the mother of all beings. Go to him for refuge, best of the Kurus; he is the refuge.
mbh_1.line: He is father and mother to every being. Go to him for shelter.
mbh_1.verified_with: Ganguli (sacred-texts) section checked for context; Sanskrit read directly
mbh_1.our_note: Markandeya to the Pandavas.

prasang.title_en: Markandeya and the child on the banyan leaf
prasang.summary: At the end of an age, the sage Markandeya drifts alone over a flooded world and sees a radiant child on a banyan branch. The child draws him inside his body, where he sees all the worlds, then asks if he has been resting, tired. Narayana explains he showed himself because he saw Markandeya's distress. Markandeya tells the Pandavas that this child is Krishna, sitting with them.
prasang.lesson: When everything you knew is underwater, you have not been forgotten; you are being held.

mbh_1.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
mbh_1.setting: In Mithila, a meat-seller famed for wisdom teaches a proud ascetic what goodness really is.
mbh_1.sanskrit: न च कामान्न संरम्भान्न द्वेषाद्धर्ममुत्सृजेत् / प्रिये नातिभृशं हृष्येदप्रिये न च संज्वरेत्
mbh_1.translation: Never give up what is right out of desire, rage or hatred. Don't be overjoyed by what pleases you, nor burn with distress at what does not.
mbh_1.line: Don't drop your principles out of desire, rage or hatred, and don't overreact to good news or bad.
mbh_1.our_note: The hunter's account of shishtachara, the conduct of the good.

prasang.title_en: Vyadha Gita: the butcher who taught a sage
prasang.summary: A proud ascetic, Kaushika, is sent to learn from a meat-seller in Mithila. The butcher teaches him plain goodness: don't return evil, repent and resolve, keep envy away, care for your parents, and don't spend your one life making enemies.
prasang.lesson: Wisdom lives in ordinary people doing ordinary work honestly. Care for your parents.

mbh_1.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
mbh_1.setting: In Mithila, a meat-seller famed for wisdom teaches a proud ascetic what goodness really is.
mbh_1.sanskrit: यत्कल्याणमभिध्यायेत्तत्रात्मानं नियोजयेत् / न पापं प्रति पापः स्यात्साधुरेव सदा भवेत्
mbh_1.translation: Keep your mind on what is good and commit yourself to it. Do not become wicked in return for wickedness; always remain good.
mbh_1.line: Don't become bad because someone was bad to you. Stay good.
mbh_1.misuse: Staying good does not mean staying silent or unprotected.
mbh_1.our_note: Shishtachara: the good do not answer papa with papa. It forbids becoming like the wrongdoer, not resisting him.

mbh_1.sanskrit: न लोके राजते मूर्खः केवलात्मप्रशंसया / अपिचेह मृजाहीनः कृतविद्यः प्रकाशते
mbh_1.translation: A fool does not shine in the world by praising himself; but a truly accomplished person shines even without polish.
mbh_1.line: Self-praise never made anyone shine; real ability shows even without polish.
mbh_1.our_note: Shishtachara.

mbh_1.setting: In Mithila, a meat-seller famed for wisdom teaches a proud ascetic what goodness really is.
mbh_1.sanskrit: विकर्मणा तप्यमानः पापाद्विपरिमुच्यते / न तत्कुर्यां पुनरिति द्वितीयात्परिमुच्यते
mbh_1.translation: One who feels remorse for a wrong deed is freed from that wrong; by resolving 'I will not do it again', he is freed from the second.
mbh_1.line: Regret frees you from a mistake; resolving 'never again' frees you from repeating it.
mbh_1.our_note: The hunter on how wrongdoing is undone: anutapa, then the resolve of non-repetition. Parallel to Manu 11.230.

mbh_1.setting: In Mithila, a meat-seller famed for wisdom teaches a proud ascetic what goodness really is.
mbh_1.sanskrit: पापं चेत्पुरुषः कृत्वा कल्याणमभिपद्यते / मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यो महाभ्रेणेव चन्द्रमाः
mbh_1.translation: If a person who has done wrong turns to doing good, he is freed from all his wrongs, like the moon coming out from behind a great cloud.
mbh_1.line: Turn to doing good after a wrong, and you come out like the moon from behind a cloud.
mbh_1.our_note: Shishtachara teaching on release from papa by turning to kalyana.

mbh_1.sanskrit: वेदस्योपनिषत्सत्यं सत्यस्योपनिषद्दमः / दमस्योपनिषत्त्यागः शिष्टाचारेषु नित्यदा
mbh_1.translation: The essence of the Veda is truth; the essence of truth is self-control; the essence of self-control is letting go. This is always the way of the good.
mbh_1.line: The heart of wisdom is truth; the heart of truth is self-control; the heart of self-control is letting go.
mbh_1.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCVII (sacred-texts); section mapped by offset, line not checked word by word
mbh_1.our_note: Upanishad here means the inner secret or essence.

mbh_1.setting: In Mithila, a meat-seller famed for wisdom teaches a proud ascetic what goodness really is.
mbh_1.sanskrit: त्रीण्येव तु पदान्याहुः सतां वृत्तमनुस्मरन् / न चैव द्रुह्येद्दद्याच्च सत्यं चैव सदा वदेत्
mbh_1.translation: Recalling the conduct of the good, the wise name just three steps: never betray anyone, give, and always speak the truth.
mbh_1.line: Good people walk three steps: never betray anyone, give generously, and always tell the truth.
mbh_1.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCVII (sacred-texts); section mapped by offset, line not checked word by word
mbh_1.our_note: Shishtachara in three padas.

mbh_1.sanskrit: अनसूयुः कृतज्ञश्च कल्याणान्येव सेवते / सुखानि धर्ममर्थं च स्वर्गं च लभते नरः
mbh_1.translation: The person who is free of envy and grateful keeps to what is good, and finds happiness, right living, prosperity and heaven.
mbh_1.line: Let go of envy and stay grateful, and good things keep finding their way to you.
mbh_1.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCIX (section number inferred from data offset; meaning read from the Sanskrit)

mbh_1.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
mbh_1.setting: In Mithila, a meat-seller famed for wisdom teaches a proud ascetic what goodness really is.
mbh_1.sanskrit: न हिंस्यात्सर्वभूतानि मैत्रायणगतश्चरेत् / नेदं जीवितमासाद्यवैरं कुर्वीत केनचित्
mbh_1.translation: Do not harm any living being; move through life with friendliness. Having been given this life, do not make an enemy of anyone.
mbh_1.line: You've been given this one life. Don't spend it making enemies.
mbh_1.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCXII (sacred-texts); section mapped by offset, line not checked word by word
mbh_1.our_note: The hunter's closing counsel on ahimsa and maitri.

mbh_1.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Satyabhama
mbh_1.speaker: Draupadi
mbh_1.setting: Satyabhama asks Draupadi for a charm to control her husband; Draupadi says control destroys love.
mbh_1.sanskrit: उद्विग्नस्य कुतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम् / न जातु वशगो भर्ता स्त्रियाः स्यान्मन्त्रकारणात्
mbh_1.translation: How can someone who feels anxious and watched have any peace? And without peace, where is happiness? No husband is ever truly won over by charms and tricks.
mbh_1.line: No one can be at peace while being managed or manipulated. Without peace, love has nowhere to grow.
mbh_1.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCXXXIII (section number inferred from data offset; meaning read from the Sanskrit)
mbh_1.our_note: Draupadi tells Satyabhama that a husband who suspects charms fears his wife like a snake in the house. The chapter around it lays out a wife's duties of service, so only this point travels.

prasang.title_en: Draupadi and Satyabhama on marriage
prasang.summary: Krishna's wife Satyabhama asks Draupadi what charm keeps her five husbands devoted. Draupadi says charms and manipulation destroy trust, then describes her own exhaustive care of the household.
prasang.lesson: Love can't be managed or manipulated into place; trust grows only where no one feels controlled.

mbh_1.speaker: Vyasa
mbh_1.setting: Late in the forest exile, Vyasa visits the Pandavas and comforts the despondent Yudhishthira.
mbh_1.sanskrit: सुखस्यानन्तरं दुःखं दुःखस्यानन्तरं सुखम् / पर्यायेणोपसर्पन्ते नरं नेमिमरा इव
mbh_1.translation: After happiness comes sorrow, and after sorrow, happiness. They come round to a person in turn, like the spokes of a wheel to the rim.
mbh_1.line: After sorrow, happiness comes round again, the way each spoke of a wheel comes back to the top.
mbh_1.verified_with: Ganguli (Project Gutenberg #15474), Vana Parva section CCLIX; Sanskrit read directly
mbh_1.our_note: Vyasa to the despondent Yudhishthira late in the exile.

mbh_1.speaker: Draupadi
mbh_1.setting: Exiled in the forest, with ten thousand hungry sages arriving and no food left, Draupadi calls Krishna in her mind.
mbh_1.sanskrit: कृष्णकृष्ण महाबाहो देवकीनन्दनाव्यय / वासुदेव जगन्नाथ प्रणतार्तिविनाशन
mbh_1.translation: Krishna, Krishna, mighty-armed son of Devaki, imperishable one, Vasudeva, lord of the world, you who destroy the pain of those who bow to you.
mbh_1.line: Krishna, Krishna... you who take away the pain of everyone who bows to you.
mbh_1.misuse: Calling on God in a crisis is prayer, not a promise that help will come in a particular form or time.
mbh_1.verified_with: Ganguli (sacred-texts) section checked for context; Sanskrit read directly (Ganguli Vana Parva CCLXI–CCLXII, Draupadi-harana)
mbh_1.our_note: Draupadi's stuti when Durvasa arrives and the vessel is empty.

prasang.title_en: Draupadi's call and the single leaf of greens
prasang.summary: Duryodhana sends the short-tempered sage Durvasa and ten thousand disciples to the exiled Pandavas after Draupadi has eaten and the sun-given pot is empty. With no way to feed them, Draupadi calls Krishna in her mind. He arrives at once, asks to be fed first, eats one leaf of greens stuck to the pot, and the sages, bathing in the river, suddenly feel full and flee.
prasang.lesson: When you have nothing left to offer, calling out is enough; help can come from a single leaf.

mbh_1.speaker: Draupadi
mbh_1.setting: Draupadi's prayer when Durvasa's sages come to be fed and the pot is empty.
mbh_1.sanskrit: वरेण्य वरदानन्त अगतीनां गतिप्रद / पुराणपुरुष प्राणमनोवृत्त्याद्यगोचर
mbh_1.translation: Most worthy, giver of boons, endless one, you who give a way to those who have no way; ancient Person, beyond the reach of breath, mind and thought.
mbh_1.line: You give a way to those who have no way.
mbh_1.misuse: A way, not necessarily the one we wanted; keep taking practical steps too.
mbh_1.verified_with: Ganguli (sacred-texts) section checked for context; Sanskrit read directly
mbh_1.our_note: Draupadi's stuti.

mbh_1.speaker: Draupadi
mbh_1.setting: Draupadi's prayer in the forest, with no food and no one to turn to.
mbh_1.sanskrit: सर्वाध्यक्ष पराध्यक्ष त्वामहं शरणं गता / पाहि मां कृपया देव शरणागतवत्सल
mbh_1.translation: Overseer of all, highest overseer, I have come to you for refuge. Protect me in your kindness, O God, you who love those who come for refuge.
mbh_1.line: I have come to you for shelter. Look after me with kindness; you love those who come to you.
mbh_1.verified_with: Ganguli (sacred-texts) section checked for context; Sanskrit read directly
mbh_1.our_note: Draupadi's stuti.

mbh_1.speaker: Krishna
mbh_1.setting: After the sages have fled, Krishna explains why he came.
mbh_1.sanskrit: भवतामापदं ज्ञात्वा ऋषेः परमकोपनात् / द्रौपद्या चिन्तितः पार्था अहं सत्वरमागतः
mbh_1.translation: Knowing your danger from that very wrathful sage, and because Draupadi thought of me, sons of Pritha, I came quickly.
mbh_1.line: I knew you were in trouble. Draupadi thought of me, so I came quickly.
mbh_1.misuse: Not a promise that every prayer is answered the same day; it shows that being thought of moves him.
mbh_1.verified_with: Ganguli (sacred-texts) section checked for context; Sanskrit read directly
mbh_1.our_note: Krishna after the sages have left satisfied.

mbh_1.speaker: the Pandavas and Draupadi
mbh_1.setting: Relieved after Krishna saves them from Durvasa's anger.
mbh_1.sanskrit: त्वया नाथेन गोविन्द दुस्तरामापदं विभो / तीर्णाः प्लवमिवासाद्य मज्जमाना महार्णवे
mbh_1.translation: With you as our protector, Govinda, lord, we have crossed this impassable danger, like the drowning who reach a boat in the great ocean.
mbh_1.line: With you beside us we got through it, like drowning people who reach a boat.
mbh_1.verified_with: Ganguli (sacred-texts) section checked for context; Sanskrit read directly
mbh_1.our_note: The Pandavas' thanks.

mbh_1.speaker: Savitri
mbh_1.setting: Savitri follows Yama, the lord of death, as he carries away her husband Satyavan.
mbh_1.sanskrit: प्राहुः साप्तपदं मैत्रं बुधास्तत्त्वार्थदर्शिनः / मित्रतां च पुरस्कृत्य किंचिद्वक्ष्यामि तच्छृणु
mbh_1.translation: The wise, who see what is true, say that walking seven steps together makes people friends. On the strength of that friendship, let me say something; please listen.
mbh_1.line: The wise say that walking seven steps together makes two people friends.
mbh_1.our_note: Savitri claims friendship with Yama so that he will hear her.

prasang.title_en: Savitri and Satyavan
prasang.summary: Princess Savitri marries Satyavan knowing he will die within a year. On the fated day she follows Yama, the lord of death, speaking such wisdom about goodness and friendship that he grants boon after boon, until she wins back her husband's life.
prasang.lesson: Steady love and clear speech can face even death. Determination carries what fear would drop.

mbh_1.speaker: Savitri
mbh_1.setting: Savitri follows Yama, the lord of death, as he carries away her husband Satyavan.
mbh_1.sanskrit: सतां सकृत्संगतमीप्सितं परं / ततः परं मित्रमिति प्रचक्षते / न चाफलं सत्पुरुषेण संगतं / ततः सतां संनिवसेत्समागमे
mbh_1.translation: Even one meeting with good people is something to wish for; friendship with them is better still. Time with a good person is never wasted, so live among the good.
mbh_1.line: Even one meeting with a good person is a gift. Time with good people is never wasted.
mbh_1.our_note: Savitri to Yama as she follows him; her words on satsanga win his boons.

prasang.title_en: Savitri and Satyavan
prasang.summary: Princess Savitri marries Satyavan knowing he will die within a year. On the fated day she follows Yama, the lord of death, speaking such wisdom about goodness and friendship that he grants boon after boon, until she wins back her husband's life.

mbh_1.speaker: Savitri
mbh_1.setting: Savitri follows Yama, the lord of death, as he carries away her husband Satyavan.
mbh_1.sanskrit: अद्रोहः सर्वभूतेषु कर्मणा मनसा गिरा / अनुग्रहश्च दानं च सतां धर्मः सनातनः
mbh_1.translation: To bear no ill will toward any being in deed, thought or word, to help, and to give: this is the timeless way of the good.
mbh_1.line: Wish no one harm in what you do, think or say. Help, and give. That's the way of good people.
mbh_1.our_note: Savitri's definition of sanatana dharma to Yama.

prasang.title_en: Savitri and Satyavan
prasang.summary: Princess Savitri marries Satyavan knowing he will die within a year. On the fated day she follows Yama, the lord of death, speaking such wisdom about goodness and friendship that he grants boon after boon, until she wins back her husband's life.

mbh_1.speaker: Savitri
mbh_1.setting: Savitri follows Yama, the lord of death, as he carries away her husband Satyavan.
mbh_1.sanskrit: सौहदात्सर्वभूतानां विश्वासो नाम जायते / तस्मात्सत्सु विशेपेण विश्वासं कुरुते जनः
mbh_1.translation: Trust is born from goodwill toward all beings. That is why people place their trust above all in the good.
mbh_1.line: Trust grows out of goodwill. People trust those who wish everyone well.
mbh_1.our_note: Savitri to Yama.

prasang.title_en: Savitri and Satyavan
prasang.summary: Princess Savitri marries Satyavan knowing he will die within a year. On the fated day she follows Yama, the lord of death, speaking such wisdom about goodness and friendship that he grants boon after boon, until she wins back her husband's life.

mbh_1.speaker: Savitri
mbh_1.setting: Savitri follows Yama, the lord of death, as he carries away her husband Satyavan.
mbh_1.sanskrit: आर्यजुष्टमिदं वृत्तमिति विज्ञाय शाश्वतम् / सन्तः परार्थं कुर्वाणा नावेक्षन्ति प्रतिक्रियाः
mbh_1.translation: Knowing this to be the noble, timeless way, the good keep working for others' sake without looking for anything in return.
mbh_1.line: Good people help others without keeping score or waiting for something back.
mbh_1.misuse: Helping without keeping score is different from letting others use you; boundaries still matter.
mbh_1.our_note: Savitri on the conduct of the noble.

prasang.title_en: Savitri and Satyavan

prasang.lesson: Steady love and clear speech can face even death. Determination carries what fear would drop.

mbh_1.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh_1.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
mbh_1.sanskrit: किंस्वित्प्रवसतो मित्रं किंस्विन्मित्रं गृहे सतः / आतुरस् च किं मित्रं किंस्विन्मित्रं मरिष्यतः विद्या प्रवसतो मित्रं भार्या मित्रं गृहे सतः / आतुरस्य भिषङ्भित्रं दानं मित्रं मरिष्यतः
mbh_1.translation: Yaksha: 'Who is the friend of one away from home? Who is the friend of one at home? Who is the friend of the sick? Who is the friend of one about to die?' Yudhishthira: 'Learning is the friend of one abroad; a spouse is the friend at home; the doctor is the friend of the sick; what one has given is the friend of the dying.'
mbh_1.line: Abroad, your learning is your friend; at home, your spouse; when ill, a doctor; at the end, what you gave.
mbh_1.our_note: Yaksha Prashna. The line's 'spouse' for bharya is right.

prasang.title_en: Yaksha Prashna: the questions at the lake
prasang.summary: One by one, four Pandavas drink from a lake against a voice's warning and fall dead. Yudhishthira answers the Yaksha's riddles instead, and when offered one brother's life, chooses his stepmother's son Nakula, out of fairness.

mbh_1.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh_1.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
mbh_1.sanskrit: किंस्विदेकपदं धर्म्यं किंस्विदेकपदं यशः / किंस्विदेकपदं स्वर्ग्यं किंस्विदेकपदं सुखम् दाक्ष्यमेकपदं धर्म्यं दानमेकपदं यशः / सत्यमेकपदं स्वर्ग्यं शीलमेकपदंसुखम्
mbh_1.translation: Yaksha: 'What single step leads to righteousness? What single step to good name? What single step to heaven? What single step to happiness?' Yudhishthira: 'Competence is the one step to righteousness; giving, to good name; truth, to heaven; good character, to happiness.'
mbh_1.line: Competence is the way to goodness, giving to a good name, truth to heaven, good character to happiness.
mbh_1.our_note: Yaksha Prashna; generic.

prasang.title_en: Yaksha Prashna: the questions at the lake
prasang.summary: One by one, four Pandavas drink from a lake against a voice's warning and fall dead. Yudhishthira answers the Yaksha's riddles instead, and when offered one brother's life, chooses his stepmother's son Nakula, out of fairness.

mbh_1.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh_1.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
mbh_1.sanskrit: किंनु हित्वाप्रियो भवति किंनु हित्वा न शोचति / किंनु हित्वाऽर्थवान्भवति किंनु हित्वा सुखी भवेत् मानं हित्वाप्रियो भवति क्रोधं हित्वा न शोचति / कामं हित्वाऽर्थवान्भवति लोमं हित्वा सुखी भवेत्
mbh_1.translation: Yaksha: 'Giving up what does one become loved? Giving up what does one stop grieving? Giving up what does one become rich? Giving up what does one become happy?' Yudhishthira: 'Give up pride and you become loved; give up anger and you do not grieve; give up desire and you become rich; give up greed and you become happy.'
mbh_1.line: Drop pride, be loved. Drop anger, no regrets. Drop craving, be rich. Drop greed, be happy.
mbh_1.our_note: A Yaksha Prashna answer listing four renunciations and their fruits.

prasang.title_en: Yaksha Prashna: the questions at the lake
prasang.summary: One by one, four Pandavas drink from a lake against a voice's warning and fall dead. Yudhishthira answers the Yaksha's riddles instead, and when offered one brother's life, chooses his stepmother's son Nakula, out of fairness.

mbh_1.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh_1.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
mbh_1.sanskrit: तपः किंलक्षणं प्रोक्तं को दमश्च प्रकीर्तितः / क्षमा च का परा प्रोक्ता का च ह्रीः परिकीर्तिता तपः स्वधर्मवर्तित्वं मनसो दमनं दमः / क्षमा द्वन्द्वसहिष्णुत्वंहीरकार्यनिवर्तनम्
mbh_1.translation: Yaksha: 'What is called austerity? What is self-restraint? What is the highest forbearance? What is shame?' Yudhishthira: 'Austerity is staying true to one's own duty; restraint is taming the mind; forbearance is bearing life's opposites; shame is turning back from what should not be done.'
mbh_1.line: Real restraint is taming the mind; real patience is bearing life's ups and downs.
mbh_1.our_note: Yaksha Prashna. Kshama here is dvandva-sahishnuta, bearing life's pairs, not bearing a wrongdoer.

prasang.title_en: Yaksha Prashna: the questions at the lake
prasang.summary: One by one, four Pandavas drink from a lake against a voice's warning and fall dead. Yudhishthira answers the Yaksha's riddles instead, and when offered one brother's life, chooses his stepmother's son Nakula, out of fairness.

mbh_1.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh_1.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
mbh_1.sanskrit: किं ज्ञानं प्रोच्यते राजन्कः शमश्च प्रकीर्तितः / दया च का परा प्रोक्ता किं चार्जवमुदाहृतम् ज्ञानं तत्त्वार्थसम्बोधः शमश्चित्तप्रशान्तता / दयासर्वसुखैपित्वमार्जवं समचित्तता
mbh_1.translation: Yaksha: 'What is called knowledge? What is calm? What is the highest compassion? What is straightforwardness?' Yudhishthira: 'Knowledge is understanding things as they truly are; calm is a quiet mind; compassion is wishing happiness for all; straightforwardness is an even mind.'
mbh_1.line: Calm is simply a quiet mind. Compassion is wishing every being well.
mbh_1.our_note: Yaksha Prashna definitions.

prasang.title_en: Yaksha Prashna: the questions at the lake
prasang.summary: One by one, four Pandavas drink from a lake against a voice's warning and fall dead. Yudhishthira answers the Yaksha's riddles instead, and when offered one brother's life, chooses his stepmother's son Nakula, out of fairness.
prasang.lesson: Answer life's questions with a steady mind, and let kindness outweigh advantage.

mbh_1.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh_1.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
mbh_1.sanskrit: कः शत्रुर्दुर्जयः पुंसां कश्चव्याधिरनन्तकः / कीदृशश्च स्मृतः साधुरसाधुः कीदृशः स्मृतः क्रोधः सुदुर्जयः शत्रुर्लोभोव्याधिरनन्तकः / सर्वभूतहितः साधुरसाधुर्निर्दयः स्मृतः
mbh_1.translation: Yaksha: 'Which enemy is hardest to conquer? Which disease has no end? Who is considered good, and who is not?' Yudhishthira: 'Anger is the enemy hardest to conquer; greed is the disease without end; one who wants the good of all beings is good; one without compassion is not.'
mbh_1.line: Anger is the enemy hardest to defeat; greed is the illness that never ends.
mbh_1.our_note: A Yaksha Prashna answer.

prasang.title_en: Yaksha Prashna: the questions at the lake
prasang.summary: One by one, four Pandavas drink from a lake against a voice's warning and fall dead. Yudhishthira answers the Yaksha's riddles instead, and when offered one brother's life, chooses his stepmother's son Nakula, out of fairness.
prasang.lesson: Answer life's questions with a steady mind, and let kindness outweigh advantage.

mbh_1.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh_1.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
mbh_1.sanskrit: किं स्थैर्यमृषिभिः प्रोक्तं किं च धैर्यमुदाहृतम् / स्नानं च किं परं प्रोक्तं दानं च किमिहोच्यते स्वधर्मे स्थिरता स्थैर्यं धैर्यमिन्द्रियनिग्रहः / स्नानं मनोमलत्यागो दानं वै भूतरक्षणम्
mbh_1.translation: Yaksha: 'What do the sages call steadiness? What is fortitude? What is the best bath? What is true giving?' Yudhishthira: 'Steadiness is standing firm in one's duty; fortitude is mastery of the senses; the best bath is washing away the mind's impurities; true giving is protecting living beings.'
mbh_1.line: The best bath is washing the mind clean; the truest gift is protecting others.
mbh_1.our_note: Yaksha Prashna definitions.

prasang.title_en: Yaksha Prashna: the questions at the lake
prasang.summary: One by one, four Pandavas drink from a lake against a voice's warning and fall dead. Yudhishthira answers the Yaksha's riddles instead, and when offered one brother's life, chooses his stepmother's son Nakula, out of fairness.
prasang.lesson: Answer life's questions with a steady mind, and let kindness outweigh advantage.

mbh_1.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh_1.setting: Asked by the Yaksha what makes a person truly learned, Yudhishthira points to action.
mbh_1.sanskrit: पठकाः पाठकाश्चैव ये चान्ये शास्त्रचिन्तकाः / सर्वे व्यसनिनो मूर्खा यः क्रियावान्स पण्डितः
mbh_1.translation: Readers, teachers and all others who merely mull over scripture are addicts and fools; the one who acts on it is the truly learned one.
mbh_1.line: Reading and talking about wisdom isn't wisdom. The one who acts on it is wise.
mbh_1.misuse: Not anti-learning; it is against learning that never becomes action.
mbh_1.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCCXI (sacred-texts) (Ganguli: brahmanahood is by conduct, not birth or study)
mbh_1.our_note: Yaksha Prashna: kriyavan is the pandita.

prasang.title_en: Yaksha Prashna: the questions at the lake
prasang.summary: One by one, four Pandavas drink from a lake against a voice's warning and fall dead. Yudhishthira answers the Yaksha's riddles instead, and when offered one brother's life, chooses his stepmother's son Nakula, out of fairness.
prasang.lesson: Answer life's questions with a steady mind, and let kindness outweigh advantage.

mbh_1.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh_1.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
mbh_1.sanskrit: प्रियवचनवादी किं लभते / विमृशितकार्यकरः किं लभते / बहुमित्रकरः किं लभते / धर्मे रतः किं लभते कथय प्रियवचनवादी प्रीयो भवति / विमृशितकार्यकरोऽधिकं जयति / बहुमित्रकरः सुखं वसत / यश्च धर्मरतः स गतिं लभते
mbh_1.translation: Yaksha: 'What does one gain by speaking kindly? By acting after careful thought? By making many friends? By devotion to what is right?' Yudhishthira: 'One who speaks kindly is loved; one who acts after careful thought wins more; one with many friends lives happily; one devoted to what is right reaches the goal.'
mbh_1.line: Speak kindly and you'll be loved; think before acting and you'll win more; make friends and live happily.
mbh_1.our_note: One of the Yaksha's question sets; a generic niti answer.

prasang.title_en: Yaksha Prashna: the questions at the lake
prasang.summary: One by one, four Pandavas drink from a lake against a voice's warning and fall dead. Yudhishthira answers the Yaksha's riddles instead, and when offered one brother's life, chooses his stepmother's son Nakula, out of fairness.
prasang.lesson: Answer life's questions with a steady mind, and let kindness outweigh advantage.

mbh_1.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh_1.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
mbh_1.sanskrit: कोमोदतेकिमाश्चर्यं कः पन्थाः का च वार्तिका / वद मे चतुरः प्रश्नान्मृता जीवन्तु बान्धवाः अहन्यहनि भूतानि गच्छन्तीह यमालयम् / शेषाः स्थावरमिच्छन्ति किमाश्चर्यमतः परम्
mbh_1.translation: Yaksha: 'Who is happy? What is the wonder? What is the path? What is the news?' Yudhishthira (on the wonder): 'Day after day, living beings go to the house of Death, yet those who remain want to stay forever. What could be more wondrous than that?'
mbh_1.line: Every day people die, yet the rest of us live as if we never will. That is the wonder.
mbh_1.our_note: The famous 'kim ashcharyam' answer.

prasang.title_en: Yaksha Prashna: the questions at the lake
prasang.summary: One by one, four Pandavas drink from a lake against a voice's warning and fall dead. Yudhishthira answers the Yaksha's riddles instead, and when offered one brother's life, chooses his stepmother's son Nakula, out of fairness.
prasang.lesson: Answer life's questions with a steady mind, and let kindness outweigh advantage.

mbh_1.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh_1.setting: Asked by the Yaksha 'What is the path?', Yudhishthira answers at the lake.
mbh_1.sanskrit: तर्कोऽप्रतिष्ठः श्रुतयो विभिन्ना / नैको मुनिर्यस्य मतं प्रमाणम् / धर्मस्य तत्त्वं निहितं गुहायां / महाजनो येन गतःस पन्था
mbh_1.translation: Reasoning has no firm footing; the scriptures disagree; there is no single sage whose word settles it. The truth of dharma is hidden in a cave. The path is the one the great have walked.
mbh_1.line: When arguments go in circles and experts disagree, follow the path good people have walked.
mbh_1.misuse: Not blind conformity; it means learning from people whose lives show integrity.
mbh_1.our_note: 'Mahajano yena gatah sa panthah': mahajana is traditionally taken as the great and good, not simply the crowd.

prasang.title_en: Yaksha Prashna: the questions at the lake
prasang.summary: One by one, four Pandavas drink from a lake against a voice's warning and fall dead. Yudhishthira answers the Yaksha's riddles instead, and when offered one brother's life, chooses his stepmother's son Nakula, out of fairness.
prasang.lesson: Answer life's questions with a steady mind, and let kindness outweigh advantage.

mbh_1.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh_1.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
mbh_1.sanskrit: पृथ्वी विभाण्डं गगनं पिघानं / सूर्याग्निना रात्रिदिवेन्धनेन / मासर्तुदर्वीपरिघट्टनेन / भूतानि कालः पचतीति वार्ता
mbh_1.translation: With the earth as the pot and the sky as its lid, with the sun as the fire and days and nights as the fuel, stirring with the ladle of months and seasons, Time is cooking all beings: that is the news.
mbh_1.line: The only real news: time is slowly cooking us all, day by day, season by season.
mbh_1.our_note: The 'ka varta' answer.

prasang.title_en: Yaksha Prashna: the questions at the lake
prasang.summary: One by one, four Pandavas drink from a lake against a voice's warning and fall dead. Yudhishthira answers the Yaksha's riddles instead, and when offered one brother's life, chooses his stepmother's son Nakula, out of fairness.
prasang.lesson: Answer life's questions with a steady mind, and let kindness outweigh advantage.

mbh_1.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh_1.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
mbh_1.sanskrit: व्याख्याता मे त्वया प्रश्ना यथातत्वं परंतप / पुरुषं त्विदानींव्याख्याहि यश्च सर्वधनी नरः तुल्ये प्रियाप्रिये यस् सुखदुःखे तथैव च / अतीतानागते चोभे सवै पुरुष उच्येत
mbh_1.translation: Yaksha: 'You have answered my questions truly. Now tell me who is truly a person, and who possesses every wealth.' Yudhishthira: 'One to whom the pleasant and the unpleasant, joy and sorrow, past and future are all alike: he is called a true person.'
mbh_1.line: Truly whole is the one who meets pleasant and unpleasant, joy and sorrow, past and future with an even mind.
mbh_1.our_note: Yaksha Prashna.

prasang.title_en: Yaksha Prashna: the questions at the lake
prasang.summary: One by one, four Pandavas drink from a lake against a voice's warning and fall dead. Yudhishthira answers the Yaksha's riddles instead, and when offered one brother's life, chooses his stepmother's son Nakula, out of fairness.
prasang.lesson: Answer life's questions with a steady mind, and let kindness outweigh advantage.

mbh_1.speaker: Yudhishthira
mbh_1.setting: Offered one brother's life, Yudhishthira picks his stepmother's son Nakula over mighty Bhima and Arjuna.
mbh_1.sanskrit: आनृशंस्यं परो धर्मः परमार्थाच्चमे मतम् / आनृशंस्यं चिकीर्षामि नकुलो यक्ष जीवतु
mbh_1.translation: Kindness is the highest dharma, higher in my view than even the highest gain. I want to act with kindness: let Nakula live, Yaksha.
mbh_1.line: I hold kindness higher than even the greatest advantage.
mbh_1.our_note: Offered one brother's life, he picks Nakula so that Madri, like Kunti, keeps a son. The Yaksha then restores all four.

prasang.title_en: Yaksha Prashna: the questions at the lake
prasang.summary: One by one, four Pandavas drink from a lake against a voice's warning and fall dead. Yudhishthira answers the Yaksha's riddles instead, and when offered one brother's life, chooses his stepmother's son Nakula, out of fairness.
prasang.lesson: Answer life's questions with a steady mind, and let kindness outweigh advantage.

mbh_1.ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Sanjaya's counsel
mbh_1.speaker: Sanjaya
mbh_1.setting: Sent by Dhritarashtra, Sanjaya urges Yudhishthira not to go to war for a kingdom.
mbh_1.sanskrit: लब्ध्वाऽपीमां पृथिवीं सागरान्तां / जरामृत्यू नैव हि त्वं प्रजह्याः / प्रियाप्रिये सुखदुःखे च राज- / न्नैवं विद्वान्नैव युद्धं कुरु त्वम्
mbh_1.translation: Even if you win this whole earth to the edge of the sea, you will not escape old age and death, or the pleasant and unpleasant, joy and sorrow.
mbh_1.line: Win the whole world and you still won't escape old age, death, joy and sorrow.
mbh_1.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section XXVII (section number inferred from data offset; meaning read from the Sanskrit)
mbh_1.our_note: Sanjaya speaks as Dhritarashtra's envoy, urging the robbed Pandavas to drop their claim. Yudhishthira and Krishna answer that this is dharma-talk in the service of injustice.

prasang.title_en: Sanjaya's plea for peace
prasang.summary: Dhritarashtra's envoy Sanjaya begs Yudhishthira not to fight for a kingdom: life is short, and no conquest saves anyone from age, loss or death.
prasang.lesson: No victory exempts you from old age, grief and death. Count what winning will cost.

mbh_1.speaker: Vidura
mbh_1.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
mbh_1.sanskrit: अभियुक्तं बलवता दुर्बलं हीनसाधनम् / हृतस्वं कामिनं चोरमाविशन्ति प्रजागराः
mbh_1.translation: Sleeplessness takes hold of a weak man attacked by a stronger one, of one without resources, of one who has lost his wealth, of the lustful, and of the thief.
mbh_1.line: Sleepless nights come to the overpowered, the stripped, the craving and the guilty.
mbh_1.our_note: Vidura's first answer when the king says he cannot sleep; he asks, with an edge, which of these the king is.

prasang.title_en: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
prasang.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

mbh_2.speaker: Vidura
mbh_2.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
mbh_2.sanskrit: क्षिप्रं विजानाति चिरं श्रृणोति / विज्ञाय चार्यं भजते न कामात् / नासंपृष्टो व्युपयुङ्क्ते परार्थे / तत्प्रज्ञानं प्रथमं पण्डितस्य
mbh_2.translation: He understands quickly, listens patiently, acts on understanding and not on impulse, and does not meddle in other people's affairs unasked: this is the first mark of a wise person.
mbh_2.line: Understand quickly, listen long, act from judgement not impulse, and stay out of others' business unless asked.
mbh_2.our_note: Vidura's first mark of the pandita.

prasang.title_en: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
prasang.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

mbh_2.speaker: Vidura
mbh_2.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
mbh_2.sanskrit: नाप्राप्यमभिवाञ्छन्ति नष्टं नेच्छन्ति शोचितुम् / आपत्सु च न मुह्यन्ति नराः पण्डितबुद्धयः
mbh_2.translation: The wise do not long for what cannot be had, do not choose to keep grieving over what is lost, and do not lose their heads in misfortune.
mbh_2.line: Don't chase what can't be had, don't keep mourning what is gone, and don't lose your head in trouble.
mbh_2.our_note: Vidura's description of pandita-buddhi; a generic maxim that describes more than it comforts.

prasang.title_en: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool

mbh_2.speaker: Vidura
mbh_2.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
mbh_2.sanskrit: निश्चित्य यः प्रक्रमते नान्तर्वसति कर्मणः / अवन्ध्यकालो वश्यात्मा स वै पण्डित उच्यते
mbh_2.translation: One who begins only after deciding, does not stop halfway through the work, does not waste time and keeps himself in hand, is called wise.
mbh_2.line: Decide, then begin. Don't stall halfway, don't waste time, and keep yourself steady.
mbh_2.our_note: Vidura's mark of the pandita in action.

prasang.title_en: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
prasang.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

mbh_2.speaker: Vidura
mbh_2.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
mbh_2.sanskrit: न हृष्यत्यात्मसंमाने नावमानेन तप्यते / गाङ्गो ह्रद इवाक्षोभ्यो यः स पण्डित उच्यते
mbh_2.translation: One who is not elated when honoured, nor pained when slighted, and who stays unruffled like a deep pool of the Ganga, is called wise.
mbh_2.line: Don't swell with praise or burn at a slight; stay deep and still like a river pool.
mbh_2.our_note: Vidura's pandita, akshobhya like a deep pool of the Ganga.

prasang.title_en: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
prasang.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

mbh_2.speaker: Vidura
mbh_2.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
mbh_2.sanskrit: संसारयति कृत्यानि सर्वत्र विचिकित्सते / चिरं करोति क्षिप्रार्थे स मूढो भरतर्षभ
mbh_2.translation: He drags out what needs doing, doubts everything, and is slow where speed is needed: such a person is a fool, best of the Bharatas.
mbh_2.line: Stretching tasks out, doubting everything, going slow when speed matters: that is what foolishness looks like.
mbh_2.our_note: From Vidura's marks of the mudha; a verdict, safe only where the reader has asked to be pushed.

prasang.title_en: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
prasang.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

mbh_2.speaker: Vidura
mbh_2.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
mbh_2.sanskrit: परं क्षिपति दोषेण वर्तमानः स्वयं तथा / यश्च क्रुध्यत्यनीशानः स च मूढतमो नरः
mbh_2.translation: One who blames another for a fault he himself has, and one who rages when he has no power to act, is the greatest of fools.
mbh_2.line: Blaming others for your own fault, or raging where you have no power, is the height of folly.
mbh_2.our_note: Vidura's mudhatama. The second half would wound someone who is powerless against a real wrong.

prasang.title_en: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
prasang.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

mbh_2.speaker: Vidura
mbh_2.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
mbh_2.sanskrit: एकः क्षमावतां दोषो द्वितीयो नोपपद्यते / यदेनं क्षमया युक्तमशक्तं मन्यते जनः सोऽस्य दोषो न मन्तव्यः क्षमा हि परमं बलम् / क्षमा गुणो ह्यशक्तानां शक्तानां भूषणं क्षमा
mbh_2.translation: The forgiving have one fault and no second: people take a forgiving person to be weak. That should not be counted against him, for forgiveness is the greatest strength. In the weak it is a virtue; in the strong it is an ornament.
mbh_2.line: People may mistake your forgiveness for weakness. It isn't. Forgiveness is the greatest strength.
mbh_2.misuse: Forgiving is not the same as staying in harm's way or excusing abuse.
mbh_2.our_note: Vidura's praise of kshama. The Mahabharata sets this beside Prahlada's teaching that forgiveness is not always right.

prasang.title_en: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool

prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

mbh_2.speaker: Vidura
mbh_2.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
mbh_2.sanskrit: षड्दोषाः पुरुषेणेह हातव्या भूतिमिच्छता / निद्रा तन्द्री भयं क्रोध आलस्यं दीर्घसूत्रता
mbh_2.translation: Six faults must be given up by anyone who wants to prosper: too much sleep, drowsiness, fear, anger, laziness and procrastination.
mbh_2.line: Six habits block every rise: oversleeping, drowsiness, fear, anger, laziness and procrastination.
mbh_2.our_note: Vidura's six doshas. Sleep here means excess sleep.

prasang.title_en: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
prasang.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

mbh_2.speaker: Vidura
mbh_2.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
mbh_2.sanskrit: आरोग्यमानृण्यमविप्रवासः / सद्भिर्मनुष्यैः सह संप्रयोगः / स्वप्रत्यया वृत्तिरभीतवासः / षट् जीवलोकस्य सुखानि राजन्
mbh_2.translation: Health, freedom from debt, living at home, the company of good people, a livelihood of one's own, and living without fear: these, O king, are the six joys of this world.
mbh_2.line: Health, no debt, home, good people, work of your own, a life without fear: that is real happiness.
mbh_2.our_note: Vidura's six sukhas of the living world. Avipravasa is not having to live away from home, which may sting readers abroad.

prasang.title_en: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
prasang.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

mbh_2.speaker: Vidura
mbh_2.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
mbh_2.sanskrit: ईर्षुर्धृणी नसन्तुष्टः क्रोधनो नित्यशङ्कितः / परभाग्योपजीवी च षडेते नित्यदुःखिताः
mbh_2.translation: The envious, the scornful, the discontented, the short-tempered, the ever-suspicious, and one who lives off another's fortune: these six are always unhappy.
mbh_2.line: Envy, scorn, discontent, short temper, constant suspicion, living off others' luck: six sure roads to misery.
mbh_2.our_note: Vidura's six nitya-duhkhitas. 'Ghrini' is read here as one given to aversion.

prasang.title_en: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
prasang.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

mbh_2.speaker: Vidura
mbh_2.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
mbh_2.sanskrit: अष्टौ गुमाः पुरुषं दीपयन्ति / प्रज्ञा च कौल्यं च दमः श्रुतं च / पराक्रमश्चाबहुभाषिता च / दानं यथाशक्ति कृतज्ञता च
mbh_2.translation: Eight qualities make a person shine: wisdom, a good upbringing, self-control, learning, courage, speaking little, giving as much as one can, and gratitude.
mbh_2.line: Eight things make a person shine: wisdom, upbringing, self-control, learning, courage, few words, generosity, gratitude.
mbh_2.our_note: Vidura's list.

prasang.title_en: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
prasang.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

mbh_2.speaker: Vidura
mbh_2.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
mbh_2.sanskrit: दश धर्मं न जानन्ति धृतराष्ट्र निबोध तान् / मत्तः प्रमत्त उन्मत्तः श्रान्तः क्रुद्धो बुभुक्षितः त्वरमाणश्च लुब्धश्च भीतः कामी च ते दश / तस्मादेतेषु भावेषु न प्रसञ्जेत पण्डितः
mbh_2.translation: Ten people do not know what is right, Dhritarashtra; hear who they are: the drunk, the careless, the deranged, the exhausted, the angry, the starving, the hurried, the greedy, the frightened and the lustful. So a wise person does not let himself be caught in these states.
mbh_2.line: Don't decide when you are angry, exhausted, hungry, rushed, greedy or afraid; right and wrong blur then.
mbh_2.our_note: Vidura's list of ten who do not know dharma. Some recensions and the Gita Press reading take the last line as 'do not keep company with such persons'; this edition reads 'these states'.

prasang.title_en: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
prasang.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

mbh_2.speaker: Vidura
mbh_2.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
mbh_2.sanskrit: न वैरमुद्दिपयति प्रशान्तं / न दर्पमारोहति शान्तिमेति / न दुर्गतोऽस्मीति करोत्यकार्यं / तमार्यशीलं परमाहुरार्याः
mbh_2.translation: He does not rekindle a quarrel that has died down, does not climb onto his pride, stays calm, and does not do wrong telling himself 'I am in a bad way': the noble call such conduct the best.
mbh_2.line: Don't rake up settled quarrels, don't ride your pride, and don't excuse wrongdoing because times are hard.
mbh_2.our_note: Vidura's description of arya-shila.

prasang.title_en: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
prasang.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

mbh_2.speaker: Vidura
mbh_2.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
mbh_2.sanskrit: न स्वे सुखे वै कुरुते प्रहर्षं / नान्यस्य दुःखे भवति प्रहृष्टः / दत्त्वा न पश्चात्कुरुतेऽनुतापं / स कथ्यते सत्पुरुषार्यशीलः
mbh_2.translation: He does not gloat over his own happiness, takes no pleasure in another's sorrow, and does not regret what he has given: such a person is called good and noble.
mbh_2.line: Don't gloat over your joy, don't enjoy another's pain, and never regret what you gave.
mbh_2.our_note: Vidura's arya-shila.

prasang.title_en: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
prasang.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

mbh_2.speaker: Vidura
mbh_2.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
mbh_2.sanskrit: तथैव योगविहितं यत्तु कर्म न सिध्यति / उपाययुक्तं मेधावी न तत्र ग्लपयेन्मनः
mbh_2.translation: And if a task undertaken with the right means and done with proper method still does not succeed, the wise person should not let his mind sink over it.
mbh_2.line: If you did it the right way and it still failed, don't let your mind sink.
mbh_2.our_note: Vidura on action: when upaya and yoga were sound and the work still did not succeed, the medhavi does not let the mind wilt.

prasang.title_en: Vidura Niti: careful action and wounding words
prasang.summary: Vidura continues through the night: weigh an action before you start it, don't sink when honest effort fails, and remember that words wound deeper than axes.
prasang.lesson: Think before acting; if you did it right and it failed, don't sink. Guard your tongue.

mbh_2.speaker: Vidura
mbh_2.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
mbh_2.sanskrit: किं नु मे स्यादिदं कृत्वा किं नु मे स्यादकुर्वतः / इति कर्माणि सञ्चिन्त्य कुर्याद्वा पुरुषो न वा
mbh_2.translation: 'What will happen to me if I do this? What will happen if I don't?' Thinking actions through this way, a person should then act, or not act.
mbh_2.line: Before acting, ask two questions: what happens if I do this, and what happens if I don't?
mbh_2.verified_with: Gita Press vulgate text in data; this verse is not in Ganguli's section XXXIV
mbh_2.our_note: Vidura on deliberate action.

prasang.title_en: Vidura Niti: careful action and wounding words
prasang.summary: Vidura continues through the night: weigh an action before you start it, don't sink when honest effort fails, and remember that words wound deeper than axes.
prasang.lesson: Think before acting; if you did it right and it failed, don't sink. Guard your tongue.

mbh_2.speaker: Vidura
mbh_2.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
mbh_2.sanskrit: य ईर्षुः परवित्तेषु रूपे वीर्ये कुलान्वये / सुखसौभाग्यसत्कारे तस्य व्याधिरनन्तकः
mbh_2.translation: One who envies others their wealth, looks, strength, family, happiness, good fortune or honours suffers from a disease without end.
mbh_2.line: Envying others' wealth, looks, luck or praise is a sickness that never ends.
mbh_2.verified_with: Gita Press vulgate text in data; not found in Ganguli's section XXXIV or XXXV
mbh_2.our_note: Vidura on irshya.

prasang.title_en: Vidura Niti: careful action and wounding words
prasang.summary: Vidura continues through the night: weigh an action before you start it, don't sink when honest effort fails, and remember that words wound deeper than axes.
prasang.lesson: Think before acting; if you did it right and it failed, don't sink. Guard your tongue.

mbh_2.speaker: Vidura
mbh_2.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
mbh_2.sanskrit: आक्रोशपरिवादाभ्यां विहिंसन्त्यबुधा बुधान् / वक्ता पापमुपादत्ते क्षममाणो विमुच्यते
mbh_2.translation: Fools wound the wise with abuse and slander. The one who speaks takes on the wrong; the one who bears it patiently is set free.
mbh_2.line: When someone abuses you, the wrong stays with the speaker; the one who bears it walks free.
mbh_2.misuse: Bearing an insult calmly does not mean accepting ongoing abuse.
mbh_2.our_note: Vidura on akrosha and parivada: the speaker takes up the papa and the forbearing one is released from his own.

prasang.title_en: Vidura Niti: careful action and wounding words
prasang.summary: Vidura continues through the night: weigh an action before you start it, don't sink when honest effort fails, and remember that words wound deeper than axes.
prasang.lesson: Think before acting; if you did it right and it failed, don't sink. Guard your tongue.

mbh_2.speaker: Vidura
mbh_2.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
mbh_2.sanskrit: रोहते सायकैर्विद्धं वनं परशुना हतम् / वाचा दुरुक्तं बीभत्सं न संरोहति वाक्क्षतम्
mbh_2.translation: A forest pierced by arrows or felled by the axe grows back; but a wound made by cruel, ugly words does not heal.
mbh_2.line: A forest cut down grows back. A wound made with harsh words does not heal.
mbh_2.our_note: Vidura's warning against harsh speech; it also tells the wounded that the wound is real.

prasang.title_en: Vidura Niti: careful action and wounding words
prasang.summary: Vidura continues through the night: weigh an action before you start it, don't sink when honest effort fails, and remember that words wound deeper than axes.
prasang.lesson: Think before acting; if you did it right and it failed, don't sink. Guard your tongue.

mbh_2.speaker: Vidura
mbh_2.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
mbh_2.sanskrit: न देवा यष्टिमादाय रक्षन्ति पशुपालवत् / यं तु रक्षितुमिच्छन्ति बुद्ध्या संयोजयन्ति तम्
mbh_2.translation: The gods do not guard a person with a stick in hand, the way a herdsman guards cattle. Whomever they wish to protect, they endow with good judgement.
mbh_2.line: The gods don't stand guard with a stick; whom they protect, they give clear judgement.
mbh_2.our_note: Vidura: daiva protects through buddhi; the paired verse says those the gods would ruin lose their judgement.

prasang.title_en: Vidura Niti: Keshini's choice and the tests of character
prasang.summary: Vidura tells how Prahlada judged honestly against his own son when Princess Keshini set two suitors a test, then gives aphorisms: gold is tested by fire, friends by hard times, and a clear conscience lets you sleep.
prasang.lesson: Character shows under pressure. Do by day what will let you sleep at night.

mbh_2.speaker: Vidura
mbh_2.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
mbh_2.sanskrit: तृणोल्कया ज्ञायते जातरूपं / वृत्तेन भद्रो व्यवहारेण साधुः / शूरो भयेष्वर्थकृच्छ्रेषु धीरः / कृच्छ्रेष्वापत्सु सुहृदश्चारयश्च
mbh_2.translation: Gold is known by a flame of straw; a good person by conduct, an honest one by dealings, a brave one in danger, a steady one in money troubles, and friends and enemies in hard times.
mbh_2.line: Gold shows in fire, character in conduct, courage in danger, and true friends in hard times.
mbh_2.our_note: Vidura's tests of character.

prasang.title_en: Vidura Niti: Keshini's choice and the tests of character
prasang.summary: Vidura tells how Prahlada judged honestly against his own son when Princess Keshini set two suitors a test, then gives aphorisms: gold is tested by fire, friends by hard times, and a clear conscience lets you sleep.
prasang.lesson: Character shows under pressure. Do by day what will let you sleep at night.

mbh_2.speaker: Vidura
mbh_2.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
mbh_2.sanskrit: जरा रूपं हरति हि धैर्यमाशा / मृत्युः प्राणान्धर्मचर्यामसूया / क्रोधः श्रियं शीलमनार्यसेवा / ह्रियं कामः सर्वमेवाभिमानः
mbh_2.translation: Age steals beauty, craving steals patience, death takes life, envy takes goodness, anger takes prosperity, bad company takes character, lust takes shame, and pride takes everything.
mbh_2.line: Craving steals your patience, anger your fortune, bad company your character, and pride takes everything.
mbh_2.our_note: Vidura's list of what steals what; the full verse begins with age taking beauty and death taking life.

prasang.title_en: Vidura Niti: Keshini's choice and the tests of character
prasang.summary: Vidura tells how Prahlada judged honestly against his own son when Princess Keshini set two suitors a test, then gives aphorisms: gold is tested by fire, friends by hard times, and a clear conscience lets you sleep.
prasang.lesson: Character shows under pressure. Do by day what will let you sleep at night.

mbh_2.speaker: Vidura
mbh_2.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
mbh_2.sanskrit: दिवसेनैव तत्कुर्याद्येन रात्रौ सुखं वसेत् / अष्टमासेन तत्कुर्याद्येन वर्षाः सुखं वसेत् पूर्वे वयसि तत्कुर्याद्येन वृद्धः सुखं वसेत् / यावज्जीवं तु तत्कुर्याद्येन प्रेत्य सुखं वसेत्
mbh_2.translation: Do during the day what lets you sleep in peace at night; do in the eight dry months what lets you live comfortably through the rains. Do in youth what makes old age comfortable, and do all your life what brings peace after death.
mbh_2.line: Do today what lets you sleep tonight, and in youth what lets you rest in old age.
mbh_2.our_note: Said to a king who cannot sleep because of what he has allowed; the full verse extends to doing lifelong what gives peace after death.

prasang.title_en: Vidura Niti: Keshini's choice and the tests of character
prasang.summary: Vidura tells how Prahlada judged honestly against his own son when Princess Keshini set two suitors a test, then gives aphorisms: gold is tested by fire, friends by hard times, and a clear conscience lets you sleep.
prasang.lesson: Character shows under pressure. Do by day what will let you sleep at night.

mbh_2.speaker: Vidura, quoting the sage Atreya
mbh_2.setting: Vidura retells a sage's answer to the gods, to calm the anxious King Dhritarashtra.
mbh_2.sanskrit: आक्रुश्यमानो नाक्रोशेन्मन्युरेव तितिक्षतः / आक्रोष्टारं निर्दहति सुकृतं चास्य विन्दति
mbh_2.translation: When insulted, do not insult back. The anger held in by one who forbears burns up the one who insulted him, and the forbearer gains his merit.
mbh_2.line: Insulted, don't insult back. The one who holds back keeps their worth; the insulter loses his.
mbh_2.misuse: Not a wish for harm to come to the other person; the point is your own restraint.
mbh_2.our_note: Atreya's teaching to the Sadhyas as retold by Vidura. The text grants that the forbearer has manyu, and says it works on the abuser by itself.

prasang.title_en: Vidura Niti: Atreya and the Sadhyas, on insult and anger
prasang.summary: Vidura retells the sage Atreya's answer to the gods: don't insult back, hold your tongue, choose your company. He adds that anger is a bitter drink and that kin who stand together survive storms.
prasang.lesson: When insulted, don't insult back. Swallow anger, and stand with your own people.

mbh_2.speaker: Vidura
mbh_2.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
mbh_2.sanskrit: सन्तापाद्भ्रश्यते रूपं सन्तापाद्भ्रश्यते बलम् / सन्तापाद्भ्रश्यते ज्ञानं सन्तापाद्व्याधिमृच्छति अनवाप्यं च शोकेन शरीरं चोपतप्यते / अमित्राश्च प्रहृष्यन्ति मा स्म शोके मनः कृथाः
mbh_2.translation: Brooding destroys beauty, brooding destroys strength, brooding destroys understanding, brooding brings on illness. Grief does not get you what you want; it only wears out the body and gladdens your enemies. Do not give your mind to grief.
mbh_2.line: Brooding drains your looks, strength and judgement, makes you ill, and changes nothing. Don't give your mind to it.
mbh_2.our_note: Vidura on santapa and shoka to the anxious king.

prasang.title_en: Vidura Niti: Atreya and the Sadhyas, on insult and anger
prasang.summary: Vidura retells the sage Atreya's answer to the gods: don't insult back, hold your tongue, choose your company. He adds that anger is a bitter drink and that kin who stand together survive storms.
prasang.lesson: When insulted, don't insult back. Swallow anger, and stand with your own people.

mbh_2.speaker: Dhritarashtra asks; Vidura answers
mbh_2.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
mbh_2.sanskrit: नित्योद्विग्नमिदं सर्वं नित्योद्विग्रमिदं मनः / यत्तत्पदमनुद्विग्नं तन्मे वद महामते नान्यत्र विद्यातपसो नान्यत्रेन्द्रियनिग्रहात् / नान्यत्र लोभसन्त्यागाच्छान्तिं पश्यामि तेऽनघ
mbh_2.translation: Dhritarashtra: 'Everything is always unsettled, and this mind is always unsettled. Wise one, tell me of the state that is free from unrest.' Vidura: 'I see no peace for you apart from learning and discipline, apart from mastering the senses, apart from giving up greed.'
mbh_2.line: Peace comes from learning, discipline, mastering your senses, and letting go of always wanting more.
mbh_2.our_note: Dhritarashtra's question is one of the plainest statements of anxiety in the epic; Vidura's reply names vidya, tapas, indriya-nigraha and lobha-tyaga.

prasang.title_en: Vidura Niti: Atreya and the Sadhyas, on insult and anger
prasang.summary: Vidura retells the sage Atreya's answer to the gods: don't insult back, hold your tongue, choose your company. He adds that anger is a bitter drink and that kin who stand together survive storms.
prasang.lesson: When insulted, don't insult back. Swallow anger, and stand with your own people.

mbh_2.speaker: Vidura
mbh_2.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
mbh_2.sanskrit: महानप्येकजो वृक्षो बलवान्सुप्रतिष्ठितः / प्रसह्य एव वातेन सस्कन्धो मर्दितुं क्षणात् अथ ये सहिता वृक्षाः सङ्घशः सुप्रतिष्ठिताः / ते हि शीघ्रतमान्वातान्सहन्तेन्योन्यसंश्रयात्
mbh_2.translation: A single tree, however great, strong and deep-rooted, can be wrenched out trunk and all by the wind in a moment. But trees that stand together, rooted in a cluster, withstand the fiercest winds by leaning on one another.
mbh_2.line: A lone tree falls to the storm; trees that stand together hold each other up.
mbh_2.our_note: Vidura on the strength of united kinsmen.

prasang.title_en: Vidura Niti: Atreya and the Sadhyas, on insult and anger
prasang.summary: Vidura retells the sage Atreya's answer to the gods: don't insult back, hold your tongue, choose your company. He adds that anger is a bitter drink and that kin who stand together survive storms.
prasang.lesson: When insulted, don't insult back. Swallow anger, and stand with your own people.

mbh_2.speaker: Vidura
mbh_2.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
mbh_2.sanskrit: अव्याधिजं कटुकं शीर्षरोगि / पापानुबन्धं परुषं तीक्ष्णमुष्णम् / सतां पेयं यन्न पिबन्त्यसन्तो / मन्युं महाराज पिब प्रशाम्य
mbh_2.translation: It is bitter without being a medicine, it gives you a headache, it leads to wrongdoing; it is harsh, sharp and hot. The good drink it down; the bad cannot. That is anger. Drink it, great king, and be at peace.
mbh_2.line: Anger is a bitter drink the wise swallow and the foolish can't. Swallow it and find peace.
mbh_2.misuse: Swallowing anger means not acting it out, not denying a real hurt.
mbh_2.our_note: The Sanskrit word is manyu. Vidura asks the king, who holds the power, to swallow his own resentment; it is not counsel to the injured party.

prasang.title_en: Vidura Niti: Atreya and the Sadhyas, on insult and anger
