meera_1.verified_with: own reading of the Rajasthani/Braj; Kavitakosh transcription
meera_1.our_note: Meera's sharanagati in a single line.

meera_1.speaker: Meera
meera_1.sanskrit: पन्थ निहारूँ डगर भुवारूँ, ऊभी मारग जोय।
meera_1.translation: I watch the road, I sweep the path, standing there looking down the way.
meera_1.line: I watch the road and sweep the path, standing there, looking for you.
meera_1.verified_with: own reading of the Rajasthani/Braj; Kavitakosh transcription
meera_1.our_note: Meera waiting for Krishna; the waiting itself is her service.

meera_1.speaker: Meera
meera_1.sanskrit: तुम गुणवंत सुसाहिब कहिये मोमें औगुण सारा।। म्हारे घर आओ प्रीतम प्यारा।। मैं निगुणी कछु गुण नहिं जानूं तुम सा बगसणहारा।।
meera_1.translation: You are called the virtuous, gracious master; in me are all the faults. (Come to my house, beloved.) I have no merit, I know no virtues; you are the one who forgives.
meera_1.line: You are all goodness; I am full of faults. I have no merit, but you are the one who forgives.
meera_1.verified_with: own reading of the Rajasthani/Braj; Kavitakosh transcription
meera_1.our_note: Dainya before the beloved Lord; the confession rests on his forgiving nature.

meera_1.ref: Meera pada "Tum suno ji mharo arji"
meera_1.ref_label: Meera pada "Tum suno ji mharo arji"
meera_1.speaker: Meera
meera_1.setting: Meera, cut off by her own family, asks to be heard.
meera_1.sanskrit: तुम सुणो जी म्हारो अरजी। भवसागर में बही जात हूँ काढ़ो तो थारी मरजी।
meera_1.translation: Please hear my plea. I am being swept away in the ocean of the world; pull me out, if you will.
meera_1.line: "Hear me. I am being swept away. Pull me out."
meera_1.verified_with: own reading of the Rajasthani/Braj; cross-checked where possible against Meera Brihat Padavali scan (archive.org)
meera_1.our_note: Meera's cry for rescue, leaving the outcome to the Lord's will.

meera_1.ref: Meera pada "Tanak Hari chitvau ji mori or"
meera_1.ref_label: Meera pada "Tanak Hari chitvau ji mori or"
meera_1.speaker: Meera
meera_1.setting: Meera, waiting for an answer that does not come.
meera_1.sanskrit: तनक हरि चितवौ जी मोरी ओर। हम चितवत तुम चितवत नाहीं मन के बड़े कठोर। मेरे आसा चितनि तुम्हरी और न दूजी ठौर।
meera_1.translation: Hari, look my way, just a little. I keep looking at you, and you do not look back; how hard your heart is! All my hope is in your glance; I have no other place.
meera_1.line: "Look my way, just a little. All my hope is here." Waiting without an answer is allowed to hurt.
meera_1.verified_with: own reading of the Rajasthani/Braj; cross-checked where possible against Meera Brihat Padavali scan (archive.org)
meera_1.our_note: Loving complaint (upalambha) to the Lord who seems not to answer.

meera_1.ref: Meera pada "Hari mere jivan pran adhar"
meera_1.ref_label: Meera pada "Hari mere jivan pran adhar"
meera_1.speaker: Meera
meera_1.setting: Meera on what holds her up.
meera_1.sanskrit: हरि मेरे जीवन प्राण अधार। और आसरो नांही तुम बिन, तीनू लोक मंझार।।
meera_1.translation: Hari, you are the support of my life and breath. In all three worlds I have no shelter but you.
meera_1.line: When nothing else holds you up, there is still a support for your life and breath.
meera_1.verified_with: own reading of the Rajasthani/Braj; cross-checked where possible against Meera Brihat Padavali scan (archive.org)

meera_1.speaker: Meera
meera_1.setting: Meera speaks to her own mind.
meera_1.sanskrit: मन रे परसि हरि के चरन। सुभग सीतल कमल- कोमल त्रिविध - ज्वाला- हरन।
meera_1.translation: O mind, touch Hari's feet: lovely, cool, soft as lotus, taking away the threefold fire.
meera_1.line: Mind, rest at Hari's feet: cool, soft as a lotus, taking away every burning.
meera_1.verified_with: own reading of the Rajasthani/Braj; Kavitakosh transcription
meera_1.our_note: Self-address to the mind; the three fires are the adhyatmika, adhibhautika and adhidaivika sufferings.

meera_1.speaker: Meera
meera_1.sanskrit: पायो जी म्हें तो राम रतन धन पायो। वस्तु अमोलक दी म्हारे सतगुरू, किरपा कर अपनायो॥ जनम-जनम की पूँजी पाई, जग में सभी खोवायो। खरच न खूटै चोर न लूटै, दिन-दिन बढ़त सवायो॥
meera_1.translation: I have found the jewel-wealth of Ram's name. My true teacher gave me a priceless thing and in kindness made me his own. I found the savings of many lives and lost all the world's. Spending does not exhaust it, no thief can steal it; it grows day by day.
meera_1.line: I found the treasure of the name. Spending never empties it, no thief can steal it, it grows every day.
meera_1.misuse: Inner wealth, not a money promise.
meera_1.verified_with: own reading of the Rajasthani/Braj; Kavitakosh transcription
meera_1.our_note: Meera's joy at receiving the name through her guru's grace.

meera_1.ref: Meera pada "Koi kahiyau re prabhu aavan ki"
meera_1.ref_label: Meera pada "Koi kahiyau re prabhu aavan ki"
meera_1.speaker: Meera
meera_1.setting: Meera, waiting for someone who neither comes nor writes.
meera_1.sanskrit: ए दोउ नैण कह्यो नहिं मानै, नदियां बहै जैसे सावन की।
meera_1.translation: These two eyes will not listen to me; they flow like rivers in the monsoon.
meera_1.line: "My eyes will not listen; they flow like monsoon rivers."
meera_1.verified_with: own reading of the Rajasthani/Braj; cross-checked where possible against Meera Brihat Padavali scan (archive.org)
meera_1.our_note: Meera's tears in waiting for Krishna. Human in wording.

rahim_1.speaker: Rahim
rahim_1.setting: Rahim on a love so close it needs no news.
rahim_1.sanskrit: जेहिं रहीम तन-मन दियो, कियो हिए बिच भौन। तासों दुख-सुख कहन की, रही बात अब कौन॥
rahim_1.translation: Rahim says: to the one who has been given body and mind, who has made a home in the heart, what joy or sorrow is left that needs telling?
rahim_1.line: The one who lives in your heart already knows your joys and sorrows. Nothing needs explaining.
rahim_1.our_note: Complete self-giving: the indwelling beloved already knows. Read of God in the bhakti sense, though the doha also fits human love.

rahim_1.speaker: Rahim
rahim_1.setting: Rahim on humility after a fall.
rahim_1.sanskrit: दिव्य दीनता के रसहिं, का जानै जग अन्धु। भली बिचारी दीनता, दीनबन्धु-से बन्धु॥
rahim_1.translation: What does the blind world know of the divine sweetness of being low? Poor humble lowliness is good: it brings a friend like the Friend of the lowly.
rahim_1.line: Being brought low has one gift: the Friend of the lowly comes close.
rahim_1.misuse: Not a call to accept humiliation; about the closeness found in low times.
rahim_1.our_note: Dinata as a bhakti virtue: humility before God draws Dinabandhu near. It praises humility toward the Lord, not submission to people.

rahim_1.speaker: Rahim
rahim_1.sanskrit: दुख नर सुनि हाँसी करैं, धरैं रहीम न धीर। कही सुनैं सुनि-सुनि करैं, ऐसे वे रघुवीर॥
rahim_1.translation: Rahim says: people laugh when they hear of your sorrow and do not keep you steady. Raghuvir listens to what you say, and having listened, acts. That is how he is.
rahim_1.line: People may laugh at your sorrow. There is one who listens, and having listened, helps.
rahim_1.our_note: Rahim: tell your sorrow to Rama, not to the world; he alone hears and helps.

rahim_1.speaker: Rahim
rahim_1.sanskrit: रहिमन सुधि सबते भली, लगै जो बारम्बार। बिछुरे मानुष फिरि मिलैं, यहै जानि अवतार॥
rahim_1.translation: Rahim says: remembering is best of all, when it comes again and again. People who were separated meet again; know that this is why God takes birth.
rahim_1.line: Remembering is a kind of nearness. People who were parted do meet again.
rahim_1.our_note: Rahim praises sudhi, remembrance. The second line's sense (reunion, and its link to avatar) is read variously; treated here as hope of meeting again.

rcm_1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_1.setting: One of five opening prayers; this one is to Shiva.
rcm_1.sanskrit: कुंद इंदु सम देह उमा रमन करुना अयन। जाहि दीन पर नेह करउ कृपा मर्दन मयन ॥
rcm_1.translation: Fair as the jasmine and the moon, beloved of Uma, home of compassion, who loves the lowly: may the destroyer of Kama show me grace.
rcm_1.line: Shiva, home of compassion, loves the lowly. May he be kind to me.
rcm_1.verified_with: Awadhi read directly; Gita Press Hindi (Poddar) in data tr.hi
rcm_1.our_note: Tulsidas's invocation: fair as jasmine and moon, Uma's lord, abode of karuna, who has affection for the deen, may the crusher of Kama be gracious.

rcm_1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_1.setting: Tulsidas, opening the Manas, on why the company we keep matters.
rcm_1.sanskrit: बिनु सतसंग बिबेक न होई। राम कृपा बिनु सुलभ न सोई॥ सतसंगत मुद मंगल मूला। सोई फल सिधि सब साधन फूला ॥
rcm_1.translation: Without good company there is no clear judgement, and by Ram's grace alone such company comes easily. Good company is the root of joy and well-being; finding it is the fruit, and every other practice is only the flower.
rcm_1.line: Without good company, there is no clear judgement.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Satsang is the root of joy and blessing and the fruit of all sadhana; viveka is impossible without it, and it is had by Ram's kripa.

prasang.title_en: Tulsidas on good company and difficult people
prasang.summary: Before the story begins, Tulsidas bows to good people and, with gentle irony, to troublesome ones too. He describes how each acts, why company shapes us, and how the wise take the good and leave the rest, like the swan taking milk from water.
prasang.lesson: The people around you shape your judgement; choose them, and take the good from everyone.

rcm_1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_1.setting: Tulsidas, opening the Manas, on how company shapes people.
rcm_1.sanskrit: सठ सुधरहिं सतसंगति पाई। पारस परस कुधात सुहाई॥ बिधि बस सुजन कुसंगत परहीं। फनि मनि सम निज गुन अनुसरहीं ॥
rcm_1.translation: Even the crooked improve in good company, the way base metal turns to gold at the touch of the philosopher's stone. And if by chance good people fall among bad company, they keep their own nature, like the jewel in a cobra's hood that never takes on its poison.
rcm_1.line: Good company can change the worst of us; the good keep their light even in bad company.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Tulsidas: the wicked are reformed by satsang as base metal by the paras stone; if by fate the good fall into bad company they follow their own virtue like the serpent's gem.

prasang.title_en: Tulsidas on good company and difficult people
prasang.summary: Before the story begins, Tulsidas bows to good people and, with gentle irony, to troublesome ones too. He describes how each acts, why company shapes us, and how the wise take the good and leave the rest, like the swan taking milk from water.
prasang.lesson: The people around you shape your judgement; choose them, and take the good from everyone.

rcm_1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_1.setting: Tulsidas, opening the Manas, on seeing good and bad in the world.
rcm_1.sanskrit: जड़ चेतन गुन दोषमय बिस्व कीन्ह करतार। संत हंस गुन गहहिं पय परिहरि बारि बिकार ॥
rcm_1.translation: The Creator made this world, living and lifeless, a mix of virtues and faults. But the wise, like the swan, take the milk of virtue and leave behind the water of faults.
rcm_1.line: The world is a mix of good and bad. Like the swan, take the milk and leave the water.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: The Creator made the world of guna and dosha together; saints, like the hamsa, take the milk of virtue and leave the water of fault.

prasang.title_en: Tulsidas on good company and difficult people
prasang.summary: Before the story begins, Tulsidas bows to good people and, with gentle irony, to troublesome ones too. He describes how each acts, why company shapes us, and how the wise take the good and leave the rest, like the swan taking milk from water.
prasang.lesson: The people around you shape your judgement; choose them, and take the good from everyone.

rcm_1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_1.setting: Tulsidas bows to every creature before he begins.
rcm_1.sanskrit: आकर चारि लाख चौरासी। जाति जीव जल थल नभ बासी॥ सीय राममय सब जग जानी। करउँ प्रनाम जोरि जुग पानी ॥
rcm_1.translation: The eight million four hundred thousand kinds of beings, living in water, on land and in the sky: knowing the whole world to be full of Sita and Ram, I bow to them with folded hands.
rcm_1.line: Seeing the whole world as full of Sita and Ram, I bow to every being with folded hands.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_1.our_note: Tulsidas: the four classes and 84 lakh kinds of beings in water, land and sky, knowing all the world as Siya Ram maya, I salute with joined palms.

rcm_1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_1.setting: Tulsidas, before beginning his poem, on how people judge their own work.
rcm_1.sanskrit: निज कबित्त केहि लाग न नीका। सरस होउ अथवा अति फीका॥ जे पर भनिति सुनत हरषाहीं। ते बर पुरुष बहुत जग नाहीं ॥
rcm_1.translation: Who does not like their own poetry, whether it is rich or utterly flat? But people who are delighted by someone else's work are rare in this world.
rcm_1.line: Everyone loves their own work. Rare is the person who is truly glad about someone else's.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Tulsidas: to whom is his own verse not pleasing, be it rich or flat; but those excellent men who rejoice on hearing another's composition are few in the world.

prasang.title_en: Tulsidas on loving our own work
prasang.summary: Tulsidas calls his own poetry plain and asks readers to forgive it. Along the way he notes that everyone loves their own work, that few are glad at another's success, and that most people swell only with their own rising waters.
prasang.lesson: Notice whether you can be glad at someone else's good work, not only your own.

rcm_1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_1.setting: Tulsidas, introducing his work, on how rarely people rejoice at someone else's rise.
rcm_1.sanskrit: जग बहु नर सर सरि सम भाई। जे निज बाढ़ि बढ़हि जल पाई॥ सज्जन सकृत सिंधु सम कोई। देखि पूर बिधु बाढ़इ जोई ॥
rcm_1.translation: Brother, most people in the world are like ponds and rivers: they swell only when their own waters rise. Rare is the good soul who, like the ocean, surges with joy on seeing another's moon grow full.
rcm_1.line: Most of us swell only at our own rise. Rare is the one who surges at another's.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Tulsidas: most are like ponds and rivers that swell with their own water; the rare sajjan is like the sea, rising at the sight of the full moon.

prasang.title_en: Tulsidas on loving our own work
prasang.summary: Tulsidas calls his own poetry plain and asks readers to forgive it. Along the way he notes that everyone loves their own work, that few are glad at another's success, and that most people swell only with their own rising waters.
prasang.lesson: Notice whether you can be glad at someone else's good work, not only your own.

rcm_1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_1.setting: Among his opening salutations, Tulsidas names what Shiva and Parvati are to him.
rcm_1.sanskrit: गुर पितु मातु महेस भवानी। प्रनवउँ दीनबंधु दिन दानी॥ सेवक स्वामि सखा सिय पी के। हित निरुपधि सब बिधि तुलसी के ॥
rcm_1.translation: I bow to Mahesh and Bhavani, my teacher, father and mother, friends of the lowly, giving every day; servants, masters and friends of Sita's lord, true well-wishers of Tulsi in every way, without any motive.
rcm_1.line: Shiva and Parvati are my teacher, father and mother: friends of the lowly, giving every day.
rcm_1.verified_with: Awadhi read directly; Gita Press Hindi (Poddar) in data tr.hi
rcm_1.our_note: Tulsidas bows to Mahesh and Bhavani as his guru, father and mother, deenbandhu and daily givers, servants and friends of Sita's lord, his guileless benefactors.

rcm_1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_1.setting: Tulsidas on why the name matters even more than the form.
rcm_1.sanskrit: रूप बिसेष नाम बिनु जानें। करतल गत न परहिं पहिचानें॥ सुमिरिअ नाम रूप बिनु देखें। आवत हृदयँ सनेह बिसेषें ॥
rcm_1.translation: Even a particular form is not recognised without its name, though it sit in the palm of your hand. But remember the name without seeing the form, and a special love rises in the heart.
rcm_1.line: Remember the name even when you cannot see the form, and love wells up in the heart.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_1.our_note: Tulsidas on name and form: a form is not known without its name though it lie in the palm; the name remembered without the form brings the form into the heart with special love.

rcm_1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_1.setting: Tulsidas, praising the name of Ram before he begins the story.
rcm_1.sanskrit: राम नाम मनिदीप धरु जीह देहरीं द्वार। तुलसी भीतर बाहेरहुँ जौं चाहसि उजिआर ॥
rcm_1.translation: Tulsi says: if you want light both inside and outside, place the name of Ram like a jewelled lamp on the threshold of your tongue.
rcm_1.line: Want light inside and out? Keep Ram's name like a lamp on the doorstep of your tongue.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_1.our_note: Tulsidas: place the gem-lamp of Ram nam on the doorsill of the tongue if you want light inside and out. The tongue is the threshold between inner and outer.

rcm_1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_1.setting: Tulsidas on the name in a frightening age.
rcm_1.sanskrit: नाम कामतरु काल कराला। सुमिरत समन सकल जग जाला॥ राम नाम कलि अभिमत दाता। हित परलोक लोक पितु माता ॥
rcm_1.translation: The name is a wish-fulfilling tree in a terrible time; remembering it stills the whole tangle of the world. In this age the name of Ram gives what the heart rightly wants; it is a well-wisher for this world and the next, a father and a mother.
rcm_1.line: The name of Ram is a father and a mother, a well-wisher in this world and the next.
rcm_1.misuse: Devotion is not a promise of a particular outcome, and it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_1.our_note: Tulsidas: the name is a kalpataru in the dreadful age, its remembrance quiets the world's snare; Ram nam grants the desired in Kali and is well-wisher, father and mother here and hereafter.

rcm_1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_1.setting: Tulsidas on what is left when every other practice feels out of reach.
rcm_1.sanskrit: नहिं कलि करम न भगति बिबेकू। राम नाम अवलंबन एकू॥ कालनेमि कलि कपट निधानू। नाम सुमति समरथ हनुमानू ॥
rcm_1.translation: In this age there is no ritual action, no devotion and no discernment left to lean on; the name of Ram is the one support. In the age of Kali, the name is the clever Hanuman against Kalanemi, the master of deceit.
rcm_1.line: When no practice, devotion or wisdom seems within reach, the name of Ram is still a support.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_1.our_note: Tulsidas: in Kali there is no karma, bhakti or viveka to rely on; Ram nam is the only support, the wise and able Hanuman against Kalanemi, the store of deceit.

rcm_1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_1.setting: Tulsidas, before beginning the story, on how the name works however it is said.
rcm_1.sanskrit: भायँ कुभायँ अनख आलस हूँ। नाम जपत मंगल दिसि दसहूँ॥ सुमिरि सो नाम राम गुन गाथा। करउँ नाइ रघुनाथहि माथा ॥॥
rcm_1.translation: Said with love or without it, even in irritation or laziness, repeating the name brings good in all ten directions. Remembering that name, I bow my head to Raghunath and begin his story.
rcm_1.line: With love or without, even irritated or lazy: say the name, and good comes from every side.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_1.our_note: Tulsidas: with good feeling or bad, in annoyance or even sloth, japa of the name brings mangal in all ten directions.

rcm_1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_1.setting: Tulsidas admits his own faults before telling the story.
rcm_1.sanskrit: मोरि सुधारिहि सो सब भाँती। जासु कृपा नहिं कृपाँ अघाती॥ राम सुस्वामि कुसेवकु मोसो। निज दिसि देखि दयानिधि पोसो ॥
rcm_1.translation: He will set right everything about me, he whose kindness never tires of being kind. Ram is a good master and I am a poor servant, yet the ocean of compassion looks at it from his own side and cares for me.
rcm_1.line: I am a poor servant; he is a good master who looks from his side and still cares for me.
rcm_1.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_1.our_note: Tulsidas: he whose kindness is never sated with being kind will mend me in every way; Ram is the good master and I the bad servant, yet he looks to his own nature and nourishes me.

rcm_1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_1.setting: Tulsidas on why he dares to write at all.
rcm_1.sanskrit: सठ सेवक की प्रीति रुचि रखिहहिं राम कृपालु। उपल किए जलजान जेहिं सचिव सुमति कपि भालु ॥
rcm_1.translation: Kind Ram will honour the love and the wish of even a foolish servant, he who made stones into boats and monkeys and bears into wise ministers.
rcm_1.line: He made stones float and monkeys wise. He will honour even a clumsy servant's love.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_1.our_note: Tulsidas on why he dares to write: gracious Ram will keep the love and liking of a dull servant, he who made rocks into ships and monkeys and bears into counsellors.

rcm_1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_1.setting: Tulsidas, aware his words are clumsy, trusts that Ram reads the heart.
rcm_1.sanskrit: सुनि अवलोकि सुचित चख चाही। भगति मोरि मति स्वामि सराही॥ कहत नसाइ होइ हियँ नीकी। रीझत राम जानि जन जी की ॥
rcm_1.translation: Hearing, looking and weighing it with care, my Lord praised the devotion in my mind. What is badly said is still good in the heart; Ram is pleased because he knows what his servant means.
rcm_1.line: Even when it comes out badly, he hears what you meant.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_1.our_note: Tulsidas: what is spoiled in the telling is good in the heart, and Ram is pleased, knowing his servant's mind.

rcm_1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_1.setting: Tulsidas on how Ram remembers his devotees.
rcm_1.sanskrit: रहति न प्रभु चित चूक किए की। करत सुरति सय बार हिए की॥ जेहिं अघ बधेउ ब्याध जिमि बाली। फिरि सुकंठ सोइ कीन्हि कुचाली ॥
rcm_1.translation: The Lord does not keep a mistake in his mind; he remembers the heart a hundred times over. The very wrong for which he struck Bali like a hunter, Sugriva later did too.
rcm_1.line: He does not keep your mistake in mind. He remembers your heart a hundred times.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_1.our_note: Tulsidas: the Lord's mind does not hold the wrong done and recalls the heart's feeling a hundred times; the very offence for which Bali was slain Sugriva repeated, and Ram overlooked it.

rcm_1.speaker: Narrator
rcm_1.setting: Back from testing Ram and lying about it, Sati realises Shiva knows everything.
rcm_1.sanskrit: हृदयँ सोचु समुझत निज करनी। चिंता अमित जाइ नहिं बरनी॥ कृपासिंधु सिव परम अगाधा। प्रगट न कहेउ मोर अपराधा ॥
rcm_1.translation: Remembering what she had done, her heart was full of a worry beyond telling. 'Shiva, an ocean of compassion, deep beyond measure, did not speak my fault aloud.'
rcm_1.line: Shiva, an ocean of compassion, never named her mistake aloud.
rcm_1.misuse: Not naming a fault is mercy, not a model for never talking about problems in a relationship.
rcm_1.verified_with: Awadhi read directly; Gita Press Hindi (Poddar) in data tr.hi
rcm_1.our_note: Sati reflects on her own act with boundless chinta: Shiva, fathomless ocean of grace, did not openly state my aparadha.

prasang.title_en: Sati doubts, tests and hides it
prasang.summary: Sati sees Shiva bow to Ram, a grieving prince searching the forest, and cannot believe Ram is divine. Ignoring Shiva's advice, she tests Ram by taking Sita's form, is found out, and then lies to Shiva about it. Shiva quietly withdraws from her, and she lives with a guilt she cannot speak.
prasang.lesson: Doubt can be honest; hiding what you did is what breaks trust.

rcm_1.speaker: Narrator
rcm_1.setting: Sati realises Shiva has withdrawn from her after she lied to him.
rcm_1.sanskrit: संकर रुख अवलोकि भवानी। प्रभु मोहि तजेउ हृदयँ अकुलानी॥ निज अघ समुझि न कछु कहि जाई। तपइ अवाँ इव उर अधिकाई ॥
rcm_1.translation: Reading Shiva's manner, Sati knew he had left her in his heart, and she was shaken. Knowing the fault was her own, she could say nothing, but inside her heart burned like a potter's kiln.
rcm_1.line: When you know the fault is yours, words fail, and the heart burns quietly like a kiln.
rcm_1.misuse: Guilt is a signal to make amends, not a sentence to burn forever.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Sati reads Shiva's withdrawal and, knowing her own offence of testing Ram and concealing it, can say nothing; her heart smoulders like a kiln.

prasang.title_en: Sati doubts, tests and hides it
prasang.summary: Sati sees Shiva bow to Ram, a grieving prince searching the forest, and cannot believe Ram is divine. Ignoring Shiva's advice, she tests Ram by taking Sita's form, is found out, and then lies to Shiva about it. Shiva quietly withdraws from her, and she lives with a guilt she cannot speak.
prasang.lesson: Doubt can be honest; hiding what you did is what breaks trust.

rcm_1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_1.setting: Tulsidas, after Sati hides the truth from her husband Shiva, on what deceit does to love.
rcm_1.sanskrit: जलु पय सरिस बिकाइ देखहु प्रीति कि रीति भलि। बिलग होइ रसु जाइ कपट खटाई परत पुनि ॥
rcm_1.translation: See love's lovely way: water mixed with milk sells at the price of milk. But let the sourness of deceit fall in, and the water separates and the sweetness is gone.
rcm_1.line: Love turns water into milk. One drop of deceit, and it curdles.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Tulsidas comments on Sati concealing her test of Ram from Shiva: in true love water gets the price of milk, and the sourness of kapat splits them.

prasang.title_en: Sati doubts, tests and hides it
prasang.summary: Sati sees Shiva bow to Ram, a grieving prince searching the forest, and cannot believe Ram is divine. Ignoring Shiva's advice, she tests Ram by taking Sita's form, is found out, and then lies to Shiva about it. Shiva quietly withdraws from her, and she lives with a guilt she cannot speak.
prasang.lesson: Doubt can be honest; hiding what you did is what breaks trust.

rcm_1.speaker: Shiva
rcm_1.setting: Shiva, when Sati wants to attend her father's ceremony uninvited, where Shiva is resented.
rcm_1.sanskrit: जदपि मित्र प्रभु पितु गुर गेहा। जाइअ बिनु बोलेहुँ न सँदेहा॥ तदपि बिरोध मान जहँ कोई। तहाँ गएँ कल्यानु न होई ॥
rcm_1.translation: It is true that one may go uninvited to the home of a friend, a master, a father or a teacher. Yet where someone holds hostility toward you, no good comes of going there.
rcm_1.line: You may visit family without an invitation. But where there is hostility toward you, going brings no good.
rcm_1.misuse: Not a rule to cut off family; a caution about walking into known hostility.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Shiva to Sati before Daksha's yajna: to a friend, master, father or guru one may go unasked, yet where there is virodh no good comes. The arc bears him out: Sati is insulted there.

prasang.title_en: Sati goes to her father's sacrifice uninvited
prasang.summary: Sati's father Daksha holds a great sacrifice and invites everyone except Shiva and her. Shiva warns her that going where there is hostility brings no good, but she goes. Her father ignores her and insults her husband in front of everyone, and the visit ends in catastrophe.
prasang.lesson: You may go to family without an invitation, but not into open hostility; listen to that warning.

rcm_1.speaker: Narada
rcm_1.setting: Narada tells Parvati's worried parents what Shiva is like.
rcm_1.sanskrit: संभु सहज समरथ भगवाना। एहि बिबाहँ सब बिधि कल्याना॥ दुराराध्य पै अहहिं महेसू। आसुतोष पुनि किएँ कलेसू ॥
rcm_1.translation: Shambhu is by nature the all-capable Lord; in this marriage there is good of every kind. Mahesh is hard to win by worship, yet he is quickly pleased when one takes on hardship.
rcm_1.line: Shiva may seem hard to reach, but sincere effort pleases him quickly.
rcm_1.verified_with: Awadhi read directly; Gita Press Hindi (Poddar) in data tr.hi
rcm_1.our_note: Narada to Himavan: Shambhu is by nature the able Lord and this marriage is auspicious in every way; Mahesh is hard to propitiate, yet soon pleased when austerity is done.

prasang.title_en: Parvati holds to her choice
prasang.summary: Reborn as Parvati, Sati resolves to marry Shiva and spends years in austerity. The seven sages come to test her, mocking Shiva as a homeless ascetic and offering her a better match. She answers that gold keeps its nature even in fire, and that the heart wants the one it has chosen.
prasang.lesson: Persistence is choosing the same thing again each day, even when others call it foolish.

rcm_1.speaker: Himavan
rcm_1.setting: Parvati's mother Maina is frantic about her daughter's future. Her husband answers.
rcm_1.sanskrit: प्रिया सोचु परिहरहु सबु सुमिरहु श्रीभगवान। पारबतिहि निरमयउ जेहिं सोइ करिहि कल्यान ॥
rcm_1.translation: Beloved, put away all this worry and remember the Lord. He who made Parvati will bring about her good.
rcm_1.line: Let go of this worry and remember God. The one who made our daughter will look after her.
rcm_1.misuse: Himavan then advises a concrete step (Parvati's tapas, 1.68); trust sits beside action, not instead of it.
rcm_1.verified_with: Awadhi read directly; Gita Press Hindi (Poddar) in data tr.hi
rcm_1.our_note: Himavan to the distraught Maina: beloved, leave all worry and remember Shri Bhagavan; he who fashioned Parvati will do her good. He then counsels Parvati's tapas.

prasang.title_en: Parvati holds to her choice
prasang.summary: Reborn as Parvati, Sati resolves to marry Shiva and spends years in austerity. The seven sages come to test her, mocking Shiva as a homeless ascetic and offering her a better match. She answers that gold keeps its nature even in fire, and that the heart wants the one it has chosen.
prasang.lesson: Persistence is choosing the same thing again each day, even when others call it foolish.

rcm_1.speaker: Voice from the sky (Brahma)
rcm_1.setting: After years of austerity, Parvati is worn thin. A voice from the sky speaks.
rcm_1.sanskrit: भयउ मनोरथ सुफल तव सुनु गिरिराजकुमारि। परिहरु दुसह कलेस सब अब मिलिहहिं त्रिपुरारि ॥
rcm_1.translation: Daughter of the mountain king, listen: your longing has borne fruit. Now give up all these unbearable hardships; Tripurari will be yours.
rcm_1.line: Your longing has borne fruit. Put down these hard struggles now; he will be yours.
rcm_1.verified_with: Awadhi read directly; Gita Press Hindi (Poddar) in data tr.hi
rcm_1.our_note: Brahma's voice from the sky after Parvati's long tapas: your wish is fulfilled, daughter of the mountain king; leave all this unbearable hardship, Tripurari will be yours.

prasang.title_en: Parvati holds to her choice
prasang.summary: Reborn as Parvati, Sati resolves to marry Shiva and spends years in austerity. The seven sages come to test her, mocking Shiva as a homeless ascetic and offering her a better match. She answers that gold keeps its nature even in fire, and that the heart wants the one it has chosen.
prasang.lesson: Persistence is choosing the same thing again each day, even when others call it foolish.

rcm_1.speaker: Narrator
rcm_1.setting: Shiva wanders, teaching and singing of Ram, after Sati is gone.
rcm_1.sanskrit: कतहुँ मुनिन्ह उपदेसहिं ग्याना। कतहुँ राम गुन करहिं बखाना॥ जदपि अकाम तदपि भगवाना। भगत बिरह दुख दुखित सुजाना ॥
rcm_1.translation: Somewhere he taught knowledge to sages, somewhere he told of Ram's virtues. Though free of all desire, the wise Lord was pained by separation from his devotee.
rcm_1.line: Though beyond all desire, the Lord still grieved at being parted from his devotee.
rcm_1.verified_with: Awadhi read directly; Gita Press Hindi (Poddar) in data tr.hi
rcm_1.our_note: After Sati's death Shiva roams, teaching jnana to sages and telling Ram's virtues; though akama, the wise Lord is grieved by the grief of separation from his bhakta.

prasang.title_en: Shiva's grief turns to Ram's name
prasang.summary: After Sati is gone, Shiva wanders, teaching and singing of Ram, repeating his name. Though beyond desire, he still grieves the loss of his devotee. Seeing his steady love, Ram appears, grateful and kind, praises Shiva's vow and asks him to marry Parvati.
prasang.lesson: Grief and devotion can walk together; steady love in loss is seen.

rcm_1.speaker: Parvati
rcm_1.setting: The seven sages come to test Parvati and ask why she is doing such hard tapas.
rcm_1.sanskrit: मनु हठ परा न सुनइ सिखावा। चहत बारि पर भीति उठावा॥ नारद कहा सत्य सोइ जाना। बिनु पंखन्ह हम चहहिं उड़ाना ॥ देखहु मुनि अबिबेकु हमारा। चाहिअ सदा सिवहि भरतारा ॥
rcm_1.translation: 'My mind has set itself stubbornly and will not hear advice; it wants to build a wall on water. Taking Narada's word as true, I want to fly without wings. Look at my foolishness, sages: I want only Shiva as my husband, always.'
rcm_1.line: Call it foolish if you like: my heart wants only Shiva, always.
rcm_1.verified_with: Awadhi read directly; Gita Press Hindi (Poddar) in data tr.hi
rcm_1.our_note: Parvati to the Saptarishis: my mind is obstinate and hears no teaching, it would raise a wall on water; holding Narada's word true I would fly without wings; see my aviveka, I want Shiva always as husband.

prasang.title_en: Parvati holds to her choice
prasang.summary: Reborn as Parvati, Sati resolves to marry Shiva and spends years in austerity. The seven sages come to test her, mocking Shiva as a homeless ascetic and offering her a better match. She answers that gold keeps its nature even in fire, and that the heart wants the one it has chosen.
prasang.lesson: Persistence is choosing the same thing again each day, even when others call it foolish.

rcm_1.speaker: Parvati
rcm_1.setting: Parvati answers the sages who mock her resolve to win Shiva through years of austerity.
rcm_1.sanskrit: सत्य कहेहु गिरिभव तनु एहा। हठ न छूट छूटै बरु देहा॥ कनकउ पुनि पषान तें होई। जारेहुँ सहजु न परिहर सोई ॥
rcm_1.translation: You speak truly: this body was born of a mountain, so its resolve will not break, even if the body does. Gold too is born of stone, and even in fire it does not give up its nature.
rcm_1.line: Gold comes from stone, and even in fire it stays gold. Hold to what you are.
rcm_1.misuse: Steadiness is not stubbornness; keep checking that the goal is still worth it.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Parvati to the Saptarishis who test her by running down Shiva and Narada: born of the mountain, her hath will not leave though the body may. Read as ananya nishtha.

prasang.title_en: Parvati holds to her choice
prasang.summary: Reborn as Parvati, Sati resolves to marry Shiva and spends years in austerity. The seven sages come to test her, mocking Shiva as a homeless ascetic and offering her a better match. She answers that gold keeps its nature even in fire, and that the heart wants the one it has chosen.
prasang.lesson: Persistence is choosing the same thing again each day, even when others call it foolish.

rcm_1.speaker: Parvati
rcm_1.setting: Parvati, after the sages list Shiva's faults and offer her a 'better' match.
rcm_1.sanskrit: महादेव अवगुन भवन बिष्नु सकल गुन धाम। जेहि कर मनु रम जाहि सन तेहि तेही सन काम ॥
rcm_1.translation: Grant that Mahadev is a house of faults and Vishnu the home of every virtue. Still, the one a heart has settled on is the one it wants.
rcm_1.line: Others may list the faults. The heart wants the one it has chosen.
rcm_1.misuse: Choosing for yourself still means listening honestly to those who care.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Parvati to the Saptarishis: let Mahadev be a house of faults and Vishnu of all virtues; whose mind delights in whom, with him alone is its concern. Read as ananya nishtha and faith in the guru's word.

prasang.title_en: Parvati holds to her choice
prasang.summary: Reborn as Parvati, Sati resolves to marry Shiva and spends years in austerity. The seven sages come to test her, mocking Shiva as a homeless ascetic and offering her a better match. She answers that gold keeps its nature even in fire, and that the heart wants the one it has chosen.
prasang.lesson: Persistence is choosing the same thing again each day, even when others call it foolish.

rcm_1.speaker: Parvati
rcm_1.setting: Sitting beside Shiva under the banyan on Kailash, Parvati asks him to clear her old doubt.
rcm_1.sanskrit: जासु भवनु सुरतरु तर होई। सहि कि दरिद्र जनित दुखु सोई॥ ससिभूषन अस हृदयँ बिचारी। हरहु नाथ मम मति भ्रम भारी ॥
rcm_1.translation: 'Can one whose home is beneath the wishing tree suffer the pain of poverty? Thinking this over in your heart, Moon-crowned Lord, take away the heavy confusion of my mind.'
rcm_1.line: One who lives under the wishing tree need not suffer want. You are my shelter: clear my confusion.
rcm_1.verified_with: Awadhi read directly; Gita Press Hindi (Poddar) in data tr.hi
rcm_1.our_note: Parvati to Shiva on Kailash: can one whose house is under the kalpataru bear the pain born of poverty; thinking so, moon-crested one, remove the great delusion of my mind.

prasang.title_en: Parvati asks, and Shiva answers with reassurance
prasang.summary: On Kailash, Parvati sits beside Shiva and, still carrying her old doubt from her life as Sati, asks how a grieving prince can be God. Shiva is moved to tears, reassures her that there is no doubt left in her heart, and explains that the formless becomes form out of love for devotees. Her confusion lifts 'like autumn heat under moonlight'.
prasang.lesson: Honest doubt, asked with love, is met with patience, not blame.

rcm_1.speaker: Shiva
rcm_1.setting: Shiva answers Parvati's question: how can the formless God be a prince grieving in a forest?
rcm_1.sanskrit: सगुनहि अगुनहि नहिं कछु भेदा। गावहिं मुनि पुरान बुध बेदा॥ अगुन अरूप अलख अज जोई। भगत प्रेम बस सगुन सो होई ॥
rcm_1.translation: There is no difference between God with form and God without form: so say the sages, the Puranas, the learned and the Vedas. The One without qualities, without form, unseen and unborn, takes on form out of love for his devotees.
rcm_1.line: The formless, unseen, unborn One takes on a form out of love for his devotees.
rcm_1.verified_with: Awadhi read directly; Gita Press Hindi (Poddar) in data tr.hi
rcm_1.our_note: Shiva to Parvati: between saguna and aguna there is no difference, say munis, Puranas and Vedas; the aguna, formless, unseen, unborn becomes saguna under the sway of the bhakta's love.

prasang.title_en: Parvati asks, and Shiva answers with reassurance
prasang.summary: On Kailash, Parvati sits beside Shiva and, still carrying her old doubt from her life as Sati, asks how a grieving prince can be God. Shiva is moved to tears, reassures her that there is no doubt left in her heart, and explains that the formless becomes form out of love for devotees. Her confusion lifts 'like autumn heat under moonlight'.
prasang.lesson: Honest doubt, asked with love, is met with patience, not blame.

rcm_1.speaker: Shiva
rcm_1.setting: Shiva tells Parvati what Ram's name does.
rcm_1.sanskrit: बिबसहुँ जासु नाम नर कहहीं। जनम अनेक रचित अघ दहहीं॥ सादर सुमिरन जे नर करहीं। भव बारिधि गोपद इव तरहीं ॥
rcm_1.translation: Even saying his name helplessly burns away wrongs built up over many lives; and those who remember him with reverence cross the ocean of worldly life as if it were a cow's hoofprint.
rcm_1.line: Those who remember him with love cross life's ocean as easily as a puddle in a hoofprint.
rcm_1.misuse: Praise of remembrance, not a promise that life's problems will vanish; practical help still matters.
rcm_1.verified_with: Awadhi read directly; Gita Press Hindi (Poddar) in data tr.hi
rcm_1.our_note: Shiva: men who say his name even helplessly burn the sins amassed in many births; those who remember with reverence cross bhavasagar like a cow's footprint.

prasang.title_en: Parvati asks, and Shiva answers with reassurance
prasang.summary: On Kailash, Parvati sits beside Shiva and, still carrying her old doubt from her life as Sati, asks how a grieving prince can be God. Shiva is moved to tears, reassures her that there is no doubt left in her heart, and explains that the formless becomes form out of love for devotees. Her confusion lifts 'like autumn heat under moonlight'.
prasang.lesson: Honest doubt, asked with love, is met with patience, not blame.

rcm_1.speaker: Parvati
rcm_1.setting: Shiva has finished answering; Parvati, holding his feet, tells him what his words did.
rcm_1.sanskrit: ससि कर सम सुनि गिरा तुम्हारी। मिटा मोह सरदातप भारी॥ तुम्ह कृपाल सबु संसउ हरेऊ। राम स्वरूप जानि मोहि परेऊ ॥
rcm_1.translation: 'Hearing your words, cool as moonbeams, the heavy autumn heat of my delusion is gone. Kind one, you took away all my doubt, and I came to know Ram's true nature.'
rcm_1.line: Your words fell like cool moonlight. The heat of my confusion is gone; you took away every doubt.
rcm_1.verified_with: Awadhi read directly; Gita Press Hindi (Poddar) in data tr.hi
rcm_1.our_note: Parvati to Shiva: hearing your speech like moon-rays, the heavy autumn heat of my moha is gone; gracious one, you removed all doubt and I have come to know Ram's true nature.

prasang.title_en: Parvati asks, and Shiva answers with reassurance
prasang.summary: On Kailash, Parvati sits beside Shiva and, still carrying her old doubt from her life as Sati, asks how a grieving prince can be God. Shiva is moved to tears, reassures her that there is no doubt left in her heart, and explains that the formless becomes form out of love for devotees. Her confusion lifts 'like autumn heat under moonlight'.
prasang.lesson: Honest doubt, asked with love, is met with patience, not blame.

rcm_1.speaker: Vishnu
rcm_1.setting: Vishnu, asked by the love-struck sage Narada for a handsome face, explains why he won't grant it.
rcm_1.sanskrit: कुपथ माग रुज ब्याकुल रोगी। बैद न देइ सुनहु मुनि जोगी॥ एहि बिधि हित तुम्हार मैं ठयऊ। कहि अस अंतरहित प्रभु भयऊ ॥
rcm_1.translation: Listen, sage: when a sick man in distress begs for food that will harm him, the doctor does not give it. In the same way I have resolved to do what is truly good for you.
rcm_1.line: A good doctor won't give the patient what he begs for if it will harm him.
rcm_1.misuse: Not every refusal is for your good; this is a way to reframe, not a reason to accept harm.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Narada, proud of having conquered Kama, is seized by desire; the Lord, as a physician guarding his devotee from pride, refuses the boon for his good.

prasang.title_en: Narada's pride and the monkey face
prasang.summary: Narada conquers desire in meditation and cannot stop telling people about it. Vishnu creates a city and a princess's swayamvara; Narada falls for her and asks Vishnu for a beautiful face. Vishnu, like a doctor refusing harmful food, gives him a monkey's face instead, and Narada is laughed out of the hall until he sees what his pride has done.
prasang.lesson: The moment you boast of beating a weakness, it has found another way in.

rcm_1.speaker: Narrator
rcm_1.setting: King Manu, who ruled well for a lifetime, sees that old age has come and something essential was missed.
rcm_1.sanskrit: होइ न बिषय बिराग भवन बसत भा चौथपन॥ हृदयँ बहुत दुख लाग जनम गयउ हरिभगति बिनु ॥
rcm_1.translation: Old age came while he lived at home, yet the pull of pleasures had not faded. His heart grieved deeply that his life had gone by without devotion to Hari.
rcm_1.line: Old age arrived at home, the cravings stayed, and he grieved for the years spent elsewhere.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Manu, a righteous king, finds the fourth stage of life upon him with no vairagya from sense objects and grieves that his birth has gone without Hari bhakti; he leaves for tapas.

prasang.title_en: Manu and Shatarupa ask late in life
prasang.summary: King Manu and Queen Shatarupa realise in old age that a whole life has passed without what mattered most to them. They hand over the kingdom, go to the forest and practise austerity for years. When Vishnu offers a boon, Manu hesitates like a poor man before the wishing tree, then asks for a son like God himself.
prasang.lesson: It is not too late to turn towards what matters, but it takes courage to ask for it.

rcm_1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_1.setting: Tulsidas, as a king is taken in by an old enemy disguised as a holy man.
rcm_1.sanskrit: तुलसी देखि सुबेषु भूलहिं मूढ़ न चतुर नर। सुंदर केकिहि पेखु बचन सुधा सम असन अहि ॥
rcm_1.translation: It is not only fools who are taken in by a fine appearance; the clever are too. Look at the beautiful peacock: its voice is like nectar, and it eats snakes.
rcm_1.line: Even the clever are fooled by a fine look. The peacock sings like nectar and eats snakes.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Tulsidas on King Pratapbhanu deceived by the false ascetic: seeing a good guise not only fools but clever men are misled; see the peacock, nectar-voiced and a snake-eater.

rcm_1.speaker: Kausalya
rcm_1.setting: Kausalya, shown her newborn's cosmic form, asks him to be simply her baby.
rcm_1.sanskrit: माता पुनि बोली सो मति डोली तजहु तात यह रूपा। कीजै सिसुलीला अति प्रियसीला यह सुख परम अनूपा॥ सुनि बचन सुजाना रोदन ठाना होइ बालक सुरभूपा। यह चरित जे गावहिं हरिपद पावहिं ते न परहिं भवकूपा ॥
rcm_1.translation: Then the mother spoke, her mind unsettled: 'Child, put away this form. Play as a little child, so dear to the heart; that joy is beyond compare.' Hearing her, the wise Lord began to cry and became a baby. Those who sing this story reach Hari's feet and do not fall into the well of worldly life.
rcm_1.line: Put away the grand form, child. Just be little with me; there is no joy like it.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: At Ram's birth Kausalya, overwhelmed by the four-armed form, asks him to give it up and do shishu lila; the Lord becomes an infant and cries. Vatsalya bhava is preferred to aishvarya.

prasang.title_en: Kausalya and the child who ran from dinner
prasang.summary: At his birth Ram shows Kausalya his cosmic form, and she asks him instead to be simply a baby. Later scenes are pure childhood: the boy runs off mid-meal, curd on his face, dusty from play, while his father laughs and his mother chases him. When she once glimpses the whole universe in him again, she asks only to be spared that and keep her child.
prasang.lesson: The grandest thing about a child may be the ordinary hours of childhood itself.

rcm_1.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_1.setting: Tulsidas watches Kausalya with her baby.
rcm_1.sanskrit: ब्यापक ब्रह्म निरंजन निर्गुन बिगत बिनोद। सो अज प्रेम भगति बस कौसल्या कें गोद ॥
rcm_1.translation: The all-pervading, stainless, formless Absolute, beyond all play, the unborn one, lies in Kausalya's lap, won over by love and devotion.
rcm_1.line: The infinite one lies in a mother's lap, won over by love.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_1.our_note: Tulsidas: the all-pervading, stainless, attributeless, unborn Brahman, beyond play, rests in Kausalya's lap under the sway of prema bhakti. Nirguna made saguna by love.

rcm_1.speaker: Dasharath
rcm_1.setting: King Dasharath, who had his sons late in life, is asked to send young Ram away with a sage.
rcm_1.sanskrit: सब सुत प्रिय मोहि प्रान की नाईं। राम देत नहिं बनइ गोसाईं॥ कहँ निसिचर अति घोर कठोरा। कहँ सुंदर सुत परम किसोरा ॥
rcm_1.translation: All my sons are dear to me as life, and Ram I cannot bring myself to give. Where are those terrible, cruel demons, and where my tender, boyish son?
rcm_1.line: Every child is dear as life, and some partings a parent can hardly bear to make.
rcm_1.misuse: Love that never lets go can hold a child back; in the story he does let Ram go.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Dasharath to Vishwamitra: all my sons are dear as life and Ram I cannot give. In the arc Vasishtha persuades him and he sends both boys with the sage.

prasang.title_en: Dasharath lets his sons go
prasang.summary: The sage Vishwamitra asks King Dasharath to send the teenage Ram and Lakshman to protect his forest rites from demons. Dasharath, who had his sons late in life, offers land, cows, treasure, even his own life instead. Vasishtha reasons with him, and he finally embraces the boys and hands them over.
prasang.lesson: Parents protect children best by letting them go when the time comes.

rcm_1.speaker: Narrator
rcm_1.setting: Ram, standing before Shiva's bow, sees Sita's anguish and knows the moment won't wait.
rcm_1.sanskrit: देखी बिपुल बिकल बैदेही। निमिष बिहात कलप सम तेही। तृषित बारि बिनु जो तनु त्यागा। मुएँ करइ का सुधा तड़ागा ॥ का बरषा सब कृषी सुखानें। समय चुकें पुनि का पछितानें॥ अस जियँ जानि जानकी देखी। प्रभु पुलके लखि प्रीति बिसेषी ॥
rcm_1.translation: He saw Vaidehi in deep distress, each moment passing like an age. If a thirsty man dies for want of water, what use is a lake of nectar after he is gone? What use is rain when the crops have dried? What use is regret once the moment has passed? Knowing this, he looked at Janaki, and seeing her deep love, he thrilled.
rcm_1.line: What use is rain after the crops have dried? Act while the moment is still here.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Seeing Sita's anguish, Ram reflects that help after the hour is worthless and moves to lift the bow; the lines are quoted as niti on timely action.

prasang.title_en: Janaka's despair and the bow
prasang.summary: Ten thousand kings fail to lift Shiva's bow, and Janaka cries out that the earth has no heroes left. Lakshman bristles; Vishwamitra sends Ram forward. Ram sees Sita's anguish, knows that rain after the crops have dried is useless, lifts the bow and breaks it in a moment.
prasang.lesson: Some moments do not wait; when it is time, act.

rcm_1.speaker: Lakshman
rcm_1.setting: Lakshman, when the furious sage Parashurama keeps boasting of his past deeds.
rcm_1.sanskrit: सूर समर करनी करहिं कहि न जनावहिं आपु। बिद्यमान रन पाइ रिपु कायर कथहिं प्रतापु ॥
rcm_1.translation: The truly brave prove themselves by what they do in battle; they do not announce themselves. Cowards, finding an enemy in front of them, talk about their own prowess.
rcm_1.line: The capable let their work speak. It is the insecure who keep announcing what they can do.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Lakshman's retort to Parashurama's boasting. A true saying, used in the scene as a taunt that provokes the sage further.

prasang.title_en: Parashurama's rage, Lakshman's taunts, Ram's calm
prasang.summary: Parashurama storms into the wedding hall furious that Shiva's bow is broken. Lakshman answers every threat with a joke, and each reply feeds the fire. Ram steps in with soft words, takes the blame on himself, and calmly points out that an old bow broke at a touch; the sage's anger finally turns to recognition.
prasang.lesson: Clever replies feed anger; calm, humble words put it out.

rcm_1.speaker: Narrator
rcm_1.setting: As Lakshman's retorts inflame the furious sage Parashurama, Ram steps in.
rcm_1.sanskrit: लखन उतर आहुति सरिस भृगुबर कोपु कृसानु। बढ़त देखि जल सम बचन बोले रघुकुलभानु ॥
rcm_1.translation: Seeing Parashurama's fire of anger rise with each of Lakshman's replies, which fell on it like offerings of ghee, Ram, sun of the Raghu line, spoke words like water.
rcm_1.line: Sharp replies feed an angry fire like ghee. Answer with words like water.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Lakshman's retorts are oblations into Parashurama's fire; Ram, seeing it rise, speaks cooling words. The doha shows Ram's sheel and skill in speech.

prasang.title_en: Parashurama's rage, Lakshman's taunts, Ram's calm
prasang.summary: Parashurama storms into the wedding hall furious that Shiva's bow is broken. Lakshman answers every threat with a joke, and each reply feeds the fire. Ram steps in with soft words, takes the blame on himself, and calmly points out that an old bow broke at a touch; the sage's anger finally turns to recognition.
prasang.lesson: Clever replies feed anger; calm, humble words put it out.

rcm_1.speaker: Lakshman
rcm_1.setting: Lakshman, half-teasing, to the raging sage Parashurama.
rcm_1.sanskrit: लखन कहेउ हँसि सुनहु मुनि क्रोधु पाप कर मूल। जेहि बस जन अनुचित करहिं चरहिं बिस्व प्रतिकूल ॥
rcm_1.translation: Lakshman laughed and said, 'Listen, sage: anger is the root of wrongdoing. In its grip people do what they shouldn't and set themselves against the whole world.'
rcm_1.line: Anger is the root of wrongdoing; in its grip we do what we shouldn't.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: A true maxim, but Lakshman says it laughing, as a taunt to an enraged sage; in the scene it inflames rather than cools.

prasang.title_en: Parashurama's rage, Lakshman's taunts, Ram's calm
prasang.summary: Parashurama storms into the wedding hall furious that Shiva's bow is broken. Lakshman answers every threat with a joke, and each reply feeds the fire. Ram steps in with soft words, takes the blame on himself, and calmly points out that an old bow broke at a touch; the sage's anger finally turns to recognition.
prasang.lesson: Clever replies feed anger; calm, humble words put it out.

rcm_1.speaker: Lakshman
rcm_1.setting: Lakshman to Parashurama, who is enraged that Shiva's bow has been broken.
rcm_1.sanskrit: मैं तुम्हार अनुचर मुनिराया। परिहरि कोपु करिअ अब दाया॥ टूट चाप नहिं जुरिहि रिसाने। बैठिअ होइहिं पाय पिराने ॥
rcm_1.translation: Great sage, I am your servant; give up your anger and be kind. A broken bow won't mend because you are angry. You must be tired of standing; do sit down.
rcm_1.line: A broken bow won't mend because you are angry. Sit down.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Lakshman's vyangya to Parashurama: mock politeness that stokes the sage further. True as a saying, but it is the ghee in this scene, not the water.

prasang.title_en: Parashurama's rage, Lakshman's taunts, Ram's calm
prasang.summary: Parashurama storms into the wedding hall furious that Shiva's bow is broken. Lakshman answers every threat with a joke, and each reply feeds the fire. Ram steps in with soft words, takes the blame on himself, and calmly points out that an old bow broke at a touch; the sage's anger finally turns to recognition.
prasang.lesson: Clever replies feed anger; calm, humble words put it out.

rcm_1.speaker: Narrator
rcm_1.setting: King Janaka, famous for his detachment, as his daughter Sita leaves home after her wedding.
rcm_1.sanskrit: सीय बिलोकि धीरता भागी। रहे कहावत परम बिरागी॥ लीन्हि रायँ उर लाइ जानकी। मिटी महामरजाद ग्यान की ॥
rcm_1.translation: He was known as supremely detached, yet on seeing Sita his composure fled. The king held Janaki to his heart, and the great banks of his wisdom gave way.
rcm_1.line: Known for his calm, he held his daughter close as she left, and all his wisdom gave way.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Janaka, called param viragi, loses dhirata on seeing Sita leave; the great boundary of his gyan is washed away by love. Tulsidas honours the love, he does not fault it.

prasang.title_en: Janaka says goodbye to his daughter
prasang.summary: After the wedding the time comes for Sita to leave Mithila. The palace, even the pet parrots, are in tears. Janaka, known everywhere for his detachment, holds his daughter and loses all composure; his ministers have to remind him it is time.
prasang.lesson: Even the wisest parent breaks a little when a child leaves home; that is love.

rcm_1.speaker: Ram
rcm_1.setting: Ram, told he alone will be crowned heir, feels uneasy about his brothers.
rcm_1.sanskrit: जनमे एक संग सब भाई। भोजन सयन केलि लरिकाई॥ करनबेध उपबीत बिआहा। संग संग सब भए उछाहा ॥ बिमल बंस यहु अनुचित एकू। बंधु बिहाइ बड़ेहि अभिषेकू॥ प्रभु सप्रेम पछितानि सुहाई। हरउ भगत मन कै कुटिलाई ॥
rcm_1.translation: We brothers were born together; we ate, slept and played together as children; ear-piercing, sacred thread and weddings were all celebrated side by side. In this spotless family only this one thing is wrong: that the eldest alone is crowned, leaving his brothers aside. (Tulsidas:) May the Lord's loving regret take the crookedness out of his devotees' hearts.
rcm_1.line: We grew up together, every milestone shared. Why should one brother alone be crowned?
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: On hearing of his coronation Ram feels loving regret that the eldest alone is anointed; Tulsidas prays that this regret remove the crookedness of devotees' hearts.

prasang.title_en: Ram's unease on the eve of his crowning
prasang.summary: Dasharath, noticing grey hairs, decides to crown Ram heir, and the whole city celebrates. When Vasishtha brings Ram the news, Ram's first thought is not joy but unease: the brothers were born, raised and married together, so why should only the eldest be crowned?
prasang.lesson: Real affection for siblings feels uneasy when one is favoured over the rest.

rcm_1.speaker: Narrator
rcm_1.setting: Manthara, Kaikeyi's maid, finishes turning the queen against Ram.
rcm_1.sanskrit: सुनत बात मृदु अंत कठोरी। देति मनहुँ मधु माहुर घोरी॥ कहइ चेरि सुधि अहइ कि नाहीं। स्वामिनि कहिहु कथा मोहि पाहीं ॥
rcm_1.translation: Her words were soft to hear but harsh in their outcome, as if she were giving poison dissolved in honey. The maid said, 'Mistress, do you remember the story you once told me?'
rcm_1.line: Some advice is soft to hear and harsh in its end: poison dissolved in honey.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Tulsidas on Manthara's speech to Kaikeyi: soft to hear, harsh in its end, like honey mixed with poison.

prasang.title_en: Manthara poisons Kaikeyi's mind
prasang.summary: Kaikeyi is first delighted that Ram will be crowned; she loves him like her own son. Her maid Manthara works on her slowly, with sighs, hints and sweet-sounding fears about her future, until Kaikeyi believes her enemy is her only friend and goes to the sulking chamber to demand her two boons.
prasang.lesson: Advice that flatters your fears can turn a good heart; check who benefits from it.

rcm_1.speaker: Ram
rcm_1.setting: Ram, told by Kaikeyi that Bharat will be crowned and he exiled, answers her calmly.
rcm_1.sanskrit: भरतु प्रानप्रिय पावहिं राजू। बिधि सब बिधि मोहि सनमुख आजू॥ जौं न जाउँ बन ऐसेहु काजा। प्रथम गनिअ मोहि मूढ़ समाजा ॥
rcm_1.translation: ...and Bharat, dear to me as life, will have the kingdom. Fate is favouring me in every way today. If I would not go to the forest even for such a cause, count me first among fools.
rcm_1.line: My beloved brother gets the throne. Fate is favouring me in every way today.
rcm_1.misuse: Grace in loss is not pretending it doesn't hurt.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Ram to Kaikeyi: sages' company in the forest, his father's command, her wish and Bharat's kingship all favour him; not to go for such a cause would be folly.

prasang.title_en: Ram hears he is to be exiled
prasang.summary: Ram is called to his father's room and finds him collapsed. Kaikeyi tells him the terms. Ram smiles: his brother gets the throne, he gets to meet sages in the forest, and he can keep his father's word. Kaikeyi reads his plain words as cunning, and Ram walks out feeling, the poet says, like an elephant freed from its post.
prasang.lesson: A lost role can be met with grace; sometimes it even feels like freedom.

rcm_1.speaker: Narrator
rcm_1.setting: Kaikeyi hears Ram's plain, gracious words and reads them as cunning.
rcm_1.sanskrit: सहज सकल रघुबर बचन कुमति कुटिल करि जान। चलइ जोंक जल बक्रगति जद्यपि सलिलु समान ॥
rcm_1.translation: Raghuvar's words were simple by nature, but the ill-minded queen took them as crooked, as a leech moves crookedly even through still, even water.
rcm_1.line: A twisted mind reads straight words as crooked, as a leech wriggles through still water.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Ram's words were sahaj, but Kaikeyi in her kumati took them as crooked, as a leech moves crookedly even in level water.

prasang.title_en: Ram hears he is to be exiled
prasang.summary: Ram is called to his father's room and finds him collapsed. Kaikeyi tells him the terms. Ram smiles: his brother gets the throne, he gets to meet sages in the forest, and he can keep his father's word. Kaikeyi reads his plain words as cunning, and Ram walks out feeling, the poet says, like an elephant freed from its post.
prasang.lesson: A lost role can be met with grace; sometimes it even feels like freedom.

rcm_1.speaker: Narrator
rcm_1.setting: Ram, walking to his mother's palace after being exiled, feels lighter, not crushed.
rcm_1.sanskrit: नव गयंदु रघुबीर मनु राजु अलान समान। छूट जानि बन गवनु सुनि उर अनंदु अधिकान ॥
rcm_1.translation: Raghuvir's mind was like a newly captured elephant, and the crown like the post it is tethered to. Hearing he must go to the forest, he felt himself set free, and joy rose in his heart.
rcm_1.line: The crown had been a tether. Losing it, he felt like an elephant set free.
rcm_1.misuse: Losing a role can free you; that does not make every loss a gift.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Ram's mind is a newly caught elephant and the kingdom its tying post; hearing of the forest he knows himself released and his heart's joy increases.

prasang.title_en: Ram hears he is to be exiled
prasang.summary: Ram is called to his father's room and finds him collapsed. Kaikeyi tells him the terms. Ram smiles: his brother gets the throne, he gets to meet sages in the forest, and he can keep his father's word. Kaikeyi reads his plain words as cunning, and Ram walks out feeling, the poet says, like an elephant freed from its post.
prasang.lesson: A lost role can be met with grace; sometimes it even feels like freedom.

rcm_1.speaker: Narrator
rcm_1.setting: Kausalya hears her son must go into exile and is torn between duty and love.
rcm_1.sanskrit: धरम सनेह उभयँ मति घेरी। भइ गति साँप छुछुंदरि केरी॥ राखउँ सुतहि करउँ अनुरोधू। धरमु जाइ अरु बंधु बिरोधू ॥
rcm_1.translation: Duty and love together hemmed in her mind; she was like the snake that has seized a muskrat. 'If I insist and keep my son, duty is lost and the brothers fall out...'
rcm_1.line: Caught between duty and love, like a snake that can neither swallow nor let go.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Kausalya's mind is besieged by dharma and sneha, like the snake with the muskrat it can neither swallow nor release: keeping her son breaks dharma and divides the brothers.

prasang.title_en: Kausalya lets her son go
prasang.summary: Ram comes to his mother as she is preparing for his coronation. Torn between duty and love, she decides not to hold him back with 'false affection', blesses him and asks only that he not forget her. As he leaves she wonders aloud whether she will live to see his face again.
prasang.lesson: Letting a child go with your blessing is love at its hardest.

rcm_1.speaker: Kausalya
rcm_1.setting: Kausalya, choosing not to hold her son back, sends him into exile with her blessing.
rcm_1.sanskrit: यह बिचारि नहिं करउँ हठ झूठ सनेहु बढ़ाइ। मानि मातु कर नात बलि सुरति बिसरि जनि जाइ ॥
rcm_1.translation: Thinking this over, I will not insist out of false affection. I bless you, son; only keep the bond of a mother, and don't forget me.
rcm_1.line: I won't hold you back with false affection. Go, son. Just don't forget your mother.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Kausalya, weighing dharma, decides not to press Ram with a show of affection that would make him fail his father's word; she only asks him to keep the tie of a mother.

prasang.title_en: Kausalya lets her son go
prasang.summary: Ram comes to his mother as she is preparing for his coronation. Torn between duty and love, she decides not to hold him back with 'false affection', blesses him and asks only that he not forget her. As he leaves she wonders aloud whether she will live to see his face again.
prasang.lesson: Letting a child go with your blessing is love at its hardest.

rcm_1.speaker: Kausalya
rcm_1.setting: Kausalya blesses Ram as he leaves for fourteen years in the forest.
rcm_1.sanskrit: देव पितर सब तुम्हहि गोसाईं। राखहुँ पलक नयन की नाईं॥ अवधि अंबु प्रिय परिजन मीना। तुम्ह करुनाकर धरम धुरीना ॥
rcm_1.translation: May all the gods and ancestors guard you, my lord, the way eyelids guard the eyes. The term of your exile is the water, and your loved ones are the fish in it; you are kind and steadfast in what is right.
rcm_1.line: May you be guarded the way eyelids guard the eyes.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Kausalya's blessing to Ram: may devas and pitris keep you as the lids keep the eye; the term of exile is water and your dear ones the fish, so return in time.

rcm_1.speaker: Kausalya
rcm_1.setting: Kausalya, as Ram, Sita and Lakshman take leave, wonders if she will live to see them again.
rcm_1.sanskrit: फिरिहि दसा बिधि बहुरि कि मोरी। देखिहउँ नयन मनोहर जोरी। सुदिन सुघरी तात कब होइहि। जननी जिअत बदन बिधु जोइहि ॥
rcm_1.translation: O Fate, will my fortune ever turn again? Will I see this lovely pair with my own eyes once more? Son, when will that good day, that blessed hour come, when your mother, still alive, sees your moon-like face again?
rcm_1.line: When will that day come, when your mother, still living, sees your face again?
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Kausalya at the leave-taking: will my condition turn again, when will the blessed hour come that the mother, still living, sees your moon-like face.

prasang.title_en: Kausalya lets her son go
prasang.summary: Ram comes to his mother as she is preparing for his coronation. Torn between duty and love, she decides not to hold him back with 'false affection', blesses him and asks only that he not forget her. As he leaves she wonders aloud whether she will live to see his face again.
prasang.lesson: Letting a child go with your blessing is love at its hardest.

rcm_1.speaker: Sumitra
rcm_1.setting: Sumitra tells her son Lakshman to follow Ram into exile.
rcm_1.sanskrit: अवध तहाँ जहँ राम निवासू। तहँइँ दिवसु जहँ भानु प्रकासू॥ जौं पै सीय रामु बन जाहीं। अवध तुम्हार काजु कछु नाहीं ॥
rcm_1.translation: Ayodhya is wherever Ram lives; day is wherever the sun shines. If Sita and Ram really go to the forest, you have nothing to do in Ayodhya.
rcm_1.line: Home is wherever your people are, as day is wherever the sun shines.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Sumitra to Lakshman: Avadh is where Ram dwells; if Sita and Ram go to the forest you have no work here. For the devotee the Lord's presence is home.

prasang.title_en: Sumitra sends Lakshman with Ram
prasang.summary: Ram asks Lakshman to stay and care for their old father and grieving mothers; Lakshman cannot imagine life apart from him. He goes to his mother Sumitra, afraid she will stop him. Instead she tells him that home is wherever Ram is, as day is wherever the sun shines, and gives him one piece of advice for the road.
prasang.lesson: Home is where your people are; a good send-off gives values, not just tears.

rcm_1.speaker: Sumitra
rcm_1.setting: Sumitra's parting advice to her son as he leaves home for fourteen years.
rcm_1.sanskrit: रागु रोषु इरिषा मदु मोहू। जनि सपनेहुँ इन्ह के बस होहू॥ सकल प्रकार बिकार बिहाई। मन क्रम बचन करेहु सेवकाई ॥
rcm_1.translation: Never, even in a dream, fall under the sway of attachment, anger, envy, pride or delusion. Leaving every such distortion behind, serve Sita and Ram with mind, word and deed.
rcm_1.line: A mother's send-off: never let attachment, anger, envy, pride or delusion rule you, even in dreams.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Sumitra's parting teaching to Lakshman: do not even in dream fall under raga, rosha, irsha, mada and moha; giving up every vikara, serve Sita and Ram in thought, deed and word.

prasang.title_en: Sumitra sends Lakshman with Ram
prasang.summary: Ram asks Lakshman to stay and care for their old father and grieving mothers; Lakshman cannot imagine life apart from him. He goes to his mother Sumitra, afraid she will stop him. Instead she tells him that home is wherever Ram is, as day is wherever the sun shines, and gives him one piece of advice for the road.
prasang.lesson: Home is where your people are; a good send-off gives values, not just tears.

rcm_1.speaker: Lakshman
rcm_1.setting: Lakshman, keeping watch at night, to Guha who blames Kaikeyi for Ram sleeping on the ground.
rcm_1.sanskrit: बोले लखन मधुर मृदु बानी। ग्यान बिराग भगति रस सानी॥ काहु न कोउ सुख दुख कर दाता। निज कृत करम भोग सबु भ्राता ॥
rcm_1.translation: Then Lakshman spoke in a sweet, gentle voice, steeped in knowledge, detachment and devotion: "No one is the giver of another's joy or sorrow, brother. Everyone lives out the fruit of their own actions."
rcm_1.line: No one else is the giver of your joy or sorrow. You live out the fruit of your own actions.
rcm_1.misuse: Not "you deserve your suffering"; it is about not handing your peace to others.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: The Lakshman Gita: Guha grieves at Ram on the ground and blames Kaikeyi; Lakshman answers with jnana and vairagya that each one tastes his own karma.

prasang.title_en: Lakshman and Guha by the sleeping Ram
prasang.summary: On the first night of exile, Guha the boatmen's chief sees Ram and Sita sleeping on grass and weeps with anger at Kaikeyi. Lakshman, keeping watch, tells him no one gives us joy or sorrow; we live out our own actions, so don't blame anyone needlessly.
prasang.lesson: Before blaming someone for your pain, look at the whole chain of causes, including yourself.

rcm_1.speaker: Lakshman
rcm_1.setting: Lakshman, continuing his night talk with Guha, after comparing the world to a dream.
rcm_1.sanskrit: अस बिचारि नहिं कीजिअ रोसू। काहुहि बादि न देइअ दोसू॥ मोह निसाँ सबु सोवनिहारा। देखिअ सपन अनेक प्रकारा ॥
rcm_1.translation: Thinking this through, do not give way to anger, and do not blame anyone without reason. Everyone is asleep in the night of delusion, and in sleep they see dreams of many kinds.
rcm_1.line: Think it through: don't give way to anger, and don't blame anyone needlessly.
rcm_1.misuse: Not blaming is not the same as excusing harm.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Continuing the Lakshman Gita: therefore do not be angry or fault anyone in vain; all sleep in the night of moha and see many dreams.

prasang.title_en: Lakshman and Guha by the sleeping Ram
prasang.summary: On the first night of exile, Guha the boatmen's chief sees Ram and Sita sleeping on grass and weeps with anger at Kaikeyi. Lakshman, keeping watch, tells him no one gives us joy or sorrow; we live out our own actions, so don't blame anyone needlessly.
prasang.lesson: Before blaming someone for your pain, look at the whole chain of causes, including yourself.

rcm_1.speaker: Ram
rcm_1.setting: Ram, when the charioteer Sumantra begs him to return to Ayodhya as the king wished.
rcm_1.sanskrit: धरमु न दूसर सत्य समाना। आगम निगम पुरान बखाना॥ मैं सोइ धरमु सुलभ करि पावा। तजें तिहूँ पुर अपजसु छावा ॥
rcm_1.translation: "The scriptures all say there is no duty equal to truth. I have found that duty easily within my reach. If I abandon it, disgrace will spread through all three worlds."
rcm_1.line: There is no duty higher than truth. Abandoning it costs more than anything it saves.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Ram to Sumantra, who begs him to return: Agama, Nigama and Purana declare no dharma equal to satya; I have got that dharma easily, and to leave it would spread ill fame.

prasang.title_en: Lakshman and Guha by the sleeping Ram
prasang.summary: On the first night of exile, Guha the boatmen's chief sees Ram and Sita sleeping on grass and weeps with anger at Kaikeyi. Lakshman, keeping watch, tells him no one gives us joy or sorrow; we live out our own actions, so don't blame anyone needlessly.
prasang.lesson: Before blaming someone for your pain, look at the whole chain of causes, including yourself.

rcm_1.speaker: Kevat
rcm_1.setting: The boatman Kevat, having ferried Ram across the Ganga, refuses the ring offered as fare.
rcm_1.sanskrit: नाथ आजु मैं काह न पावा। मिटे दोष दुख दारिद दावा॥ बहुत काल मैं कीन्हि मजूरी। आजु दीन्ह बिधि बनि भलि भूरी ॥
rcm_1.translation: Lord, what have I not received today? The fire of my faults, sorrows and poverty is put out. I have worked for wages a long time; today Providence has paid me fully and well.
rcm_1.line: I've worked for wages all my life. Today I was paid in full.
rcm_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_1.our_note: Kevat refuses Sita's ring: what have I not gained today; long have I laboured for wages, and today vidhi has paid me richly. His wage is having washed Ram's feet.

prasang.title_en: Kevat washes Ram's feet
prasang.summary: At the Ganga, a boatman refuses to take Ram across until he can wash his feet, joking that if the dust of those feet turned a stone into a woman, it might turn his boat, his family's livelihood, into one too. Ram laughs and agrees. On the far bank Sita offers her ring as fare, and Kevat refuses: after a lifetime of wages, today he has been paid in full.
prasang.lesson: Some exchanges can't be priced; gratitude can be payment enough.

rcm_2.speaker: Valmiki
rcm_2.setting: Valmiki ends his list of the hearts Ram lives in.
rcm_2.sanskrit: जाहि न चाहिअ कबहुँ कछु तुम्ह सन सहज सनेहु। बसहु निरंतर तासु मन सो राउर निज गेहु ॥
rcm_2.translation: One who never wants anything from you and simply loves you: live in that mind always; it is your own home.
rcm_2.line: The one who wants nothing from you and simply loves you: that heart is your own home.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_2.our_note: Valmiki ends his list of Ram's dwelling places: he who never wants anything and has natural love for you, dwell forever in his mind; that is your own house.

rcm_2.speaker: Sumantra
rcm_2.setting: Sumantra returns alone to the grieving king Dasharath and steadies him.
rcm_2.sanskrit: जनम मरन सब दुख सुख भोगा। हानि लाभु प्रिय मिलन बियोगा॥ काल करम बस होहिं गोसाईं। बरबस राति दिवस की नाईं ॥ सुख हरषहिं जड़ दुख बिलखाहीं। दोउ सम धीर धरहिं मन माहीं॥ धीरज धरहु बिबेकु बिचारी। छाड़िअ सोच सकल हितकारी ॥
rcm_2.translation: Birth and death, joy and sorrow, loss and gain, meeting and parting with those we love: these come under the sway of time and action, as surely as night and day. The foolish rejoice in good times and wail in bad; the steady hold both alike in the mind. Hold on to your courage, think with discernment, and let go of worry, you who care for everyone.
rcm_2.line: Gain and loss, meeting and parting come like day and night. The steady hold both alike.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Sumantra tries to steady Dasharath with the teaching of kala and karma. The teaching is sound, but in the arc the king cannot take it in and dies of separation.

rcm_2.speaker: Kausalya
rcm_2.setting: Kausalya comforts Bharat, who has come home to find his father dead and his brother exiled.
rcm_2.sanskrit: अजहुँ बच्छ बलि धीरज धरहू। कुसमउ समुझि सोक परिहरहू॥ जनि मानहु हियँ हानि गलानी। काल करम गति अघटित जानी ॥
rcm_2.translation: My child, bless you, hold on to courage even now. Seeing that the times are bad, set aside your grief. Knowing that the course of time and karma cannot be turned, don't take this loss as your shame.
rcm_2.line: Hold on, child. The times turned against us. Don't carry this loss as your shame.
rcm_2.misuse: Easing shame is not denying responsibility where it is real.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Kausalya, herself bereaved, comforts Bharat: knowing the course of kala and karma to be unalterable, do not take loss and glani to heart.

prasang.title_en: Bharat comes home to grief
prasang.summary: Bharat returns from his uncle's home to a silent city. His mother tells him proudly what she arranged; he learns his father is dead and his brother exiled because of him. Overwhelmed with shame he goes to Kausalya, expecting blame, and she embraces him as if Ram had come back, telling him not to carry the loss as his shame.
prasang.lesson: When someone is drowning in guilt for what others did, an embrace helps more than blame.

rcm_2.speaker: Narrator
rcm_2.setting: After the king's funeral, the royal guru Vasishtha gathers the court to counsel the grieving Bharat.
rcm_2.sanskrit: कहत राम गुन सील सुभाऊ। सजल नयन पुलकेउ मुनिराऊ॥ बहुरि लखन सिय प्रीति बखानी। सोक सनेह मगन मुनि ग्यानी ॥
rcm_2.translation: As he spoke of Ram's goodness, gentleness and nature, the great sage's eyes filled with tears and he trembled. Then, praising the love of Lakshman and Sita, the wise sage was lost in sorrow and affection.
rcm_2.line: Even the wise old teacher's eyes filled with tears as he spoke of the ones he loved.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Vasishtha, counselling the court after the king's rites, is himself drowned in shoka and sneha while praising Ram's nature and the love of Lakshman and Sita.

rcm_2.ref_label: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand (data 2.165 doha; Gita Press 2.171)
rcm_2.speaker: Vasishtha
rcm_2.setting: Bharat has come home to find his father dead and Ram exiled. Vasishtha, grieving too, consoles him.
