rcm_2.sanskrit: सुनहु भरत भावी प्रबल बिलखि कहेउ मुनिनाथ। हानि लाभु जीवनु मरनु जसु अपजसु बिधि हाथ ॥
rcm_2.translation: Listen, Bharat, said the sage, himself in tears: what is to be is powerful. Loss and gain, life and death, honour and dishonour all rest in the Creator's hands.
rcm_2.line: Loss and gain, life and death, praise and blame: much of it was never in your hands.
rcm_2.misuse: Said to lift a grieving son's guilt, not to excuse inaction. Your effort is still one of the five causes of any outcome (Gita 18.14).
rcm_2.verified_with: data tr.hi (Gita Press)
rcm_2.our_note: Vasishtha, himself in tears, to Bharat: bhavi is strong; hani, labh, jivan, maran, jas and apjas are in vidhi's hands. Spoken to free a blameless son of guilt.

prasang.title_en: Bharat refuses the throne
prasang.summary: After the funeral, Vasishtha, the ministers and Kausalya all urge Bharat to rule, as his father wished. Bharat says the advice is right and his heart still isn't at peace; the crown means nothing without Ram. He decides to go to the forest, admit his fault, and trust his brother to forgive.
prasang.lesson: When head and heart disagree, go and face the person you think you wronged.

rcm_2.speaker: Bharat
rcm_2.setting: Bharat, urged by his teacher and mother to accept the throne, explains why he cannot.
rcm_2.sanskrit: तुम्ह तौ देहु सरल सिख सोई। जो आचरत मोर भल होई॥ जद्यपि यह समुझत हउँ नीकें। तदपि होत परितोष न जी कें ॥
rcm_2.translation: You give me simple advice, the kind that would do me good if I followed it. Though I understand it well, my heart is not at peace.
rcm_2.line: I understand your advice perfectly. My heart still isn't at peace.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Bharat respectfully grants that guru and mother advise what is good for him, yet says his heart finds no paritosh in it; his peace lies only in going to Ram.

prasang.title_en: Bharat refuses the throne
prasang.summary: After the funeral, Vasishtha, the ministers and Kausalya all urge Bharat to rule, as his father wished. Bharat says the advice is right and his heart still isn't at peace; the crown means nothing without Ram. He decides to go to the forest, admit his fault, and trust his brother to forgive.
prasang.lesson: When head and heart disagree, go and face the person you think you wronged.

rcm_2.speaker: Bharat
rcm_2.setting: Bharat resolves to go to the forest and face the brother he believes he has wronged.
rcm_2.sanskrit: जद्यपि मैं अनभल अपराधी। भै मोहि कारन सकल उपाधी॥ तदपि सरन सनमुख मोहि देखी। छमि सब करिहहिं कृपा बिसेषी ॥
rcm_2.translation: Though I am at fault and guilty, and all this trouble came about because of me, still, seeing me come before him for refuge, Ram will forgive everything and show me special kindness.
rcm_2.line: I am at fault. Still I will go to him face to face, trusting his heart to forgive.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Bharat's dainya: he counts himself the root of the calamity yet trusts Ram's nature to forgive one who comes for sharan. The tradition holds Bharat blameless.

prasang.title_en: Bharat refuses the throne
prasang.summary: After the funeral, Vasishtha, the ministers and Kausalya all urge Bharat to rule, as his father wished. Bharat says the advice is right and his heart still isn't at peace; the crown means nothing without Ram. He decides to go to the forest, admit his fault, and trust his brother to forgive.
prasang.lesson: When head and heart disagree, go and face the person you think you wronged.

rcm_2.speaker: Guha
rcm_2.setting: Guha, ready to block Bharat's army at the river, listens to an elder who urges caution.
rcm_2.sanskrit: सुनि गुह कहइ नीक कह बूढ़ा। सहसा करि पछिताहिं बिमूढ़ा॥ भरत सुभाउ सीलु बिनु बूझें। बड़ि हित हानि जानि बिनु जूझें ॥
rcm_2.translation: Guha said, 'The old man speaks well. Fools act in haste and repent. To fight without knowing Bharat's character and nature would do great harm to our own good.'
rcm_2.line: Fools act in haste and repent. Know someone's nature before you fight them.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Guha, ready to fight Bharat for Ram's sake, accepts the old man's counsel: fools act in haste and repent; first learn Bharat's sheel and intent.

prasang.title_en: Guha nearly fights Bharat
prasang.summary: Seeing Bharat's army approach the Ganga, Guha assumes he is coming to kill Ram and prepares his men to die fighting. An old man reads the omens and says Bharat comes to bring Ram back. Guha agrees that fools act in haste and repent, goes to meet Bharat with gifts, and the two embrace.
prasang.lesson: Find out someone's intent before you prepare for war with them.

rcm_2.speaker: Bharat
rcm_2.setting: At Prayag, Bharat, on his way to bring Ram back, asks the holy rivers for a boon.
rcm_2.sanskrit: अरथ न धरम न काम रुचि गति न चहउँ निरबान। जनम-जनम रति राम पद यह बरदानु न आन ॥
rcm_2.translation: I have no taste for wealth, duty or pleasure, nor do I seek liberation. Birth after birth, love for Ram's feet: that is the boon, and no other.
rcm_2.line: Not wealth, not pleasure, not even liberation: only love for Ram, life after life.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_2.our_note: Bharat at Prayag to Triveni: I have no relish for artha, dharma or kama, nor do I want nirvana; birth after birth, love for Ram's feet is the boon, no other.

rcm_2.speaker: Triveni (a voice from the rivers)
rcm_2.setting: Bharat is consumed by shame over the exile; the holy rivers answer him.
rcm_2.sanskrit: तात भरत तुम्ह सब बिधि साधू। राम चरन अनुराग अगाधू॥ बादि गलानि करहु मन माहीं। तुम्ह सम रामहि कोउ प्रिय नाहीं ॥
rcm_2.translation: Child Bharat, you are good in every way; your love for Ram's feet is boundless. You torment yourself with guilt for nothing; no one is dearer to Ram than you.
rcm_2.line: You torment yourself with guilt for nothing. No one is dearer to Ram than you.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_2.our_note: Triveni answers Bharat: child, you are sadhu in every way with fathomless love for Ram's feet; in vain you feel glani, none is as dear to Ram as you.

rcm_2.speaker: Bharadwaj
rcm_2.setting: The sage Bharadwaj to Bharat, who is consumed by shame over what his mother did.
rcm_2.sanskrit: तुम्ह गलानि जियँ जनि करहु समुझि मातु करतूति। तात कैकइहि दोसु नहिं गई गिरा मति धूति ॥
rcm_2.translation: Don't eat yourself up with shame remembering your mother's deed. Child, Kaikeyi is not at fault either; the goddess of speech clouded her mind.
rcm_2.line: Don't eat yourself up with shame for what someone else in your family did.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Bharadwaj to Bharat: feel no glani over Kaikeyi's deed; even she is not at fault, since Saraswati deluded her mind for the gods' purpose.

prasang.title_en: Bharadwaj lifts Bharat's shame
prasang.summary: At Prayag Bharat meets the sage Bharadwaj, too ashamed to speak. The sage tells him not to eat himself up over his mother's deed and that what Bharat sees as a stain is a lesson for everyone. Bharat answers that he fears neither the world's talk nor the afterlife; only the thought that Ram suffers because of him keeps him awake.
prasang.lesson: You are not your family's mistakes; carry only what is yours.

rcm_2.speaker: Bharadwaj
rcm_2.setting: On his way to find Ram, Bharat confides his grief and guilt to the sage Bharadwaj.
rcm_2.sanskrit: भरत बचन सुनि मुनि सुखु पाई। सबहिं कीन्हि बहु भाँति बड़ाई॥ तात करहु जनि सोचु बिसेषी। सब दुखु मिटिहि राम पग देखी ॥
rcm_2.translation: Hearing Bharat's words the sage was happy, and everyone praised him in many ways. 'Child, don't worry so much. All your sorrow will lift when you see Ram's feet.'
rcm_2.line: Don't worry so much. Your sorrow will lift the moment you see him again.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Bharadwaj, pleased with Bharat's words: child, do not grieve so much; all sorrow will vanish on seeing Ram's feet.

rcm_2.speaker: Brihaspati
rcm_2.setting: The gods' teacher warns Indra not to scheme against Bharat.
rcm_2.sanskrit: जद्यपि सम नहिं राग न रोषू। गहहिं न पाप पूनु गुन दोषू॥ करम प्रधान बिस्व करि राखा। जो जस करइ सो तस फलु चाखा ॥
rcm_2.translation: Though Ram is impartial, without attachment or anger, and does not take on anyone's sin, merit, virtue or fault, he has made action the governing law of the world: whatever one does, one tastes the fruit of it.
rcm_2.line: The world runs on action: as you do, so you reap.
rcm_2.misuse: Read as encouragement to act well, not as judgement on anyone's misfortune.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Brihaspati to Indra: the Lord is even, without raga or rosha, yet he has made the world karma-pradhan; whoever does as he does tastes such fruit. A warning against plotting.

prasang.title_en: Brihaspati checks Indra's envy
prasang.summary: Indra, king of the gods, fears that Bharat's devotion will bring Ram back and spoil the gods' plans, and wants to trick him. His teacher Brihaspati tells him that the world runs on action, that harming a good person backfires, and that his anxiety comes from his own self-interest, not from Bharat.
prasang.lesson: Your fear of someone else's goodness usually says more about your interests than theirs.

rcm_2.speaker: Brihaspati
rcm_2.setting: The gods' teacher Brihaspati to Indra, who fears Bharat's rising virtue and wants to scheme against him.
rcm_2.sanskrit: सत्यसंध प्रभु सुर हितकारी। भरत राम आयस अनुसारी॥ स्वारथ बिबस बिकल तुम्ह होहू। भरत दोसु नहिं राउर मोहू ॥
rcm_2.translation: The Lord is true to his word and kind to the gods, and Bharat follows Ram's wishes. You are anxious for nothing, gripped by self-interest. The fault is not Bharat's; it is your own confusion.
rcm_2.line: You're anxious because of your own interests. The fault isn't theirs; it's your confusion.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Brihaspati checks Indra, who fears Bharat's love will bring Ram back and wants to plot: you are distraught through selfishness; the fault is not Bharat's but your moha.

prasang.title_en: Brihaspati checks Indra's envy
prasang.summary: Indra, king of the gods, fears that Bharat's devotion will bring Ram back and spoil the gods' plans, and wants to trick him. His teacher Brihaspati tells him that the world runs on action, that harming a good person backfires, and that his anxiety comes from his own self-interest, not from Bharat.
prasang.lesson: Your fear of someone else's goodness usually says more about your interests than theirs.

rcm_2.speaker: A voice from the sky
rcm_2.setting: Lakshman, convinced Bharat is coming to attack, grabs his bow; a heavenly voice stops him.
rcm_2.sanskrit: अनुचित उचित काजु किछु होऊ। समुझि करिअ भल कह सबु कोऊ। सहसा करि पाछे पछिताहीं। कहहिं बेद बुध ते बुध नाहीं ॥
rcm_2.translation: Whatever needs doing, right or wrong, think it through first, then act; everyone calls that good. Those who act in haste and regret afterward, the wise say, are not wise at all.
rcm_2.line: Think before you act. Acting in haste and regretting later is not wisdom.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: The akashvani praises Lakshman's strength, then counsels that any deed, fit or unfit, be done after reflection; haste followed by regret is not wisdom.

prasang.title_en: Dasharath's two promises
prasang.summary: Dasharath finds Kaikeyi in the sulking chamber and, eager to please her, swears by Ram to grant anything. She asks for Bharat's coronation and fourteen years of exile for Ram. Bound by his word and his love, the king spends the night begging, raging and grieving, and by morning cannot speak.
prasang.lesson: Promise only what you have thought through; a rash vow can cost what you love most.

rcm_2.speaker: Bharat
rcm_2.setting: Bharat walks toward Ram at Chitrakoot, afraid of being rejected.
rcm_2.sanskrit: जौं परिहरहिं मलिन मनु जानी। जौं सनमानहिं सेवकु मानी॥ मोरें सरन रामहि की पनही। राम सुस्वामि दोसु सब जनही ॥
rcm_2.translation: Whether he casts me off, knowing my mind to be soiled, or honours me as his servant, my refuge is Ram's sandals. Ram is a good master; the fault is all his servant's.
rcm_2.line: Whether he turns me away or takes me in, my refuge is still at his feet.
rcm_2.misuse: Surrender here comes after effort and honest reflection; it is not a reason to stop acting or to stay in harm's way.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_2.our_note: Bharat on the road to Chitrakoot: whether he abandons me as foul-minded or honours me as servant, my shelter is Ram's sandals; Ram is the good master, all fault is the servant's.

rcm_2.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_2.setting: Bharat walks toward Ram, slowed by shame, quickened by love.
rcm_2.sanskrit: फेरति मनहुँ मातु कृत खोरी। चलत भगति बल धीरज धोरी॥ जब समुझत रघुनाथ सुभाऊ। तब पथ परत उताइल पाऊ ॥
rcm_2.translation: It was as if his mother's wrong held him back, while the strength of devotion drove him on like a patient ox. Whenever he remembered Raghunath's nature, his feet moved faster on the path.
rcm_2.line: Shame slowed him. But whenever he remembered Ram's nature, his feet moved faster.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_2.our_note: Tulsidas: his mother's misdeed seems to turn him back, the strength of bhakti bears him on; when he thinks of Raghunath's nature his feet fall quickly on the path.

rcm_2.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_2.setting: The whole of Ayodhya arrives at Chitrakoot, each person grieving in their own way.
rcm_2.sanskrit: आरत लोग राम सबु जाना। करुनाकर सुजान भगवाना॥ जो जेहि भायँ रहा अभिलाषी। तेहि तेहि कै तसि तसि रुख राखी ॥
rcm_2.translation: The all-knowing, compassionate Lord understood all the people in distress. Whatever each one was longing for, in that very way he met them.
rcm_2.line: He understood each hurting person, and met each one in the way they longed for.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_2.our_note: At Chitrakoot the compassionate, all-knowing Lord knew all the people to be distressed, and kept regard for each according to the feeling with which each longed.

rcm_2.speaker: Narrator
rcm_2.setting: At Chitrakoot Ram greets the three queens, and goes first to Kaikeyi, who caused his exile.
rcm_2.sanskrit: प्रथम राम भेंटी कैकेई। सरल सुभायँ भगति मति भेई॥ पग परि कीन्ह प्रबोधु बहोरी। काल करम बिधि सिर धरि खोरी ॥ भेटीं रघुबर मातु सब करि प्रबोधु परितोषु। अंब ईस आधीन जगु काहु न देइअ दोषु ॥
rcm_2.translation: Ram met Kaikeyi first of all, and with his simple nature and devotion soothed her mind. Falling at her feet, he laid the blame on time, karma and fate, and comforted her. Then he met all the mothers and comforted each: 'Mother, the world is in God's hands; we should blame no one.'
rcm_2.line: He went first to the one who had wronged him, and comforted her.
rcm_2.misuse: Forgiving is not pretending the harm didn't happen.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: At Chitrakoot Ram meets Kaikeyi first, who is consumed by remorse, and consoles her by putting the blame on kala, karma and vidhi: the world is in God's hands, blame no one.

prasang.title_en: The brothers meet at Chitrakoot
prasang.summary: Bharat walks barefoot to Chitrakoot and falls at Ram's feet; Ram lifts him into his arms. Ram learns his father has died and grieves. When the queens arrive, Ram goes first to Kaikeyi, who caused it all, falls at her feet and comforts her, blaming no one.
prasang.lesson: Forgiveness can mean going first to the person who hurt you and putting them at ease.

rcm_2.speaker: Vasishtha
rcm_2.setting: Vasishtha, at the Chitrakoot assembly, asks Ram to decide because those grieving cannot.
rcm_2.sanskrit: आरत कहहिं बिचारि न काऊ। सूझ जुआरिहि आपन दाऊ॥ सुनि मुनि बचन कहत रघुराऊ॥ नाथ तुम्हारेहि हाथ उपाऊ ॥
rcm_2.translation: People in distress never speak after weighing things; a gambler sees only his own throw. Hearing the sage, Raghunath said, 'Master, the way forward is in your hands.'
rcm_2.line: People in distress never speak with judgement; the gambler sees only his own throw.
rcm_2.misuse: Not a reason to dismiss people who are hurting; a reason to wait before deciding.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Vasishtha includes himself among the distressed and so asks Ram to decide what is good for all. It is humility about one's own judgement, not a dismissal of those who suffer.

prasang.title_en: The family council at Chitrakoot
prasang.summary: Vasishtha asks how Ram can be brought home, noting that grieving people cannot judge well. Bharat recalls a brother who never broke his heart and let him win at games, and blames himself. Ram tells him his shame is needless, that love and hostility cannot be hidden, and asks him to say freely what he wants.
prasang.lesson: In family conflict, let each speak; name love plainly; lift needless shame.

rcm_2.speaker: Bharat
rcm_2.setting: Bharat, before the assembly at Chitrakoot, speaks of his elder brother.
rcm_2.sanskrit: सिसुपन तें परिहरेउँ न संगू। कबहुँ न कीन्ह मोर मन भंगू॥ मैं प्रभु कृपा रीति जियँ जोही। हारेहूँ खेल जितावहिं मोही ॥
rcm_2.translation: Since childhood I never left his side, and he never once broke my heart. I have seen the way of his kindness: even when I lost at games, he made me win.
rcm_2.line: Since childhood he never broke my heart. Even when I lost at games, he let me win.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Bharat before the assembly recalls Ram's affection from childhood: he never left Ram's company, and Ram never hurt his feelings, letting him win even lost games.

prasang.title_en: The family council at Chitrakoot
prasang.summary: Vasishtha asks how Ram can be brought home, noting that grieving people cannot judge well. Bharat recalls a brother who never broke his heart and let him win at games, and blames himself. Ram tells him his shame is needless, that love and hostility cannot be hidden, and asks him to say freely what he wants.
prasang.lesson: In family conflict, let each speak; name love plainly; lift needless shame.

rcm_2.speaker: Ram
rcm_2.setting: Ram to Bharat, who blames himself for the exile and their father's death.
rcm_2.sanskrit: तात जायँ जियँ करहु गलानी। ईस अधीन जीव गति जानी॥ तीनि काल तिभुअन मत मोरें। पुन्यसिलोक तात तर तोरें ॥
rcm_2.translation: Brother, you torment your heart with shame for nothing; know that a soul's course is in God's hands. In my view, all the virtuous of past, present and future, in all three worlds, stand below you.
rcm_2.line: You torment yourself with shame for nothing. In my eyes you stand above them all.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Ram to Bharat at Chitrakoot: you feel glani in vain, the jiva's course is under Ishvara; in my view the holy of all three times and worlds are beneath you.

prasang.title_en: The family council at Chitrakoot
prasang.summary: Vasishtha asks how Ram can be brought home, noting that grieving people cannot judge well. Bharat recalls a brother who never broke his heart and let him win at games, and blames himself. Ram tells him his shame is needless, that love and hostility cannot be hidden, and asks him to say freely what he wants.
prasang.lesson: In family conflict, let each speak; name love plainly; lift needless shame.

rcm_2.speaker: Ram
rcm_2.setting: Ram reassures Bharat, who is tormented by guilt over his mother's scheme.
rcm_2.sanskrit: कहउँ सुभाउ सत्य सिव साखी। भरत भूमि रह राउरि राखी॥ तात कुतरक करहु जनि जाएँ। बैर पेम नहिं दुरइ दुराएँ ॥
rcm_2.translation: "I tell you truly, with Shiva as witness: the earth stays safe because you hold it. Don't torment yourself with needless doubts, brother. Hostility and love cannot be hidden, however you try."
rcm_2.line: Stop torturing yourself with doubts. Love and hostility cannot be hidden; people know which you carry.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Ram swears with Shiva as witness that the earth stands by Bharat's keeping, and tells him not to reason falsely against himself: enmity and love are never concealed.

prasang.title_en: The family council at Chitrakoot
prasang.summary: Vasishtha asks how Ram can be brought home, noting that grieving people cannot judge well. Bharat recalls a brother who never broke his heart and let him win at games, and blames himself. Ram tells him his shame is needless, that love and hostility cannot be hidden, and asks him to say freely what he wants.
prasang.lesson: In family conflict, let each speak; name love plainly; lift needless shame.

rcm_2.speaker: Bharat
rcm_2.setting: Bharat, once Ram and their teacher have reassured him, admits what his dread was made of.
rcm_2.sanskrit: अपडर डरेउँ न सोच समूलें। रबिहि न दोसु देव दिसि भूलें॥ मोर अभागु मातु कुटिलाई। बिधि गति बिषम काल कठिनाई ॥
rcm_2.translation: "I was afraid of imagined fears; my worry had no root at all. If one loses one's direction, the sun is not to blame. It was my misfortune, my mother's crookedness, the hard turn of fate and the difficulty of the times..."
rcm_2.line: I was frightened by fears I had imagined. My worry had no root at all.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Bharat, reassured by Ram and the guru, says he feared from apdar, his own false apprehension, and that the fault lay in his fortune and the times, never in Ram.

prasang.title_en: The family council at Chitrakoot
prasang.summary: Vasishtha asks how Ram can be brought home, noting that grieving people cannot judge well. Bharat recalls a brother who never broke his heart and let him win at games, and blames himself. Ram tells him his shame is needless, that love and hostility cannot be hidden, and asks him to say freely what he wants.
prasang.lesson: In family conflict, let each speak; name love plainly; lift needless shame.

rcm_2.speaker: Kausalya
rcm_2.setting: Kausalya, to Sita's mother at Chitrakoot, on Bharat's character.
rcm_2.sanskrit: जानउँ सदा भरत कुलदीपा। बार बार मोहि कहेउ महीपा॥ कसें कनकु मनि पारिखि पाएँ। पुरुष परिखिअहिं समयँ सुभाएँ ॥
rcm_2.translation: I have always known Bharat to be the lamp of our family; the king told me so again and again. Gold is known on the touchstone and a gem when a jeweller comes; a person is tested by time and shows his nature.
rcm_2.line: Gold is proved on the touchstone. People are proved by time.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Kausalya to Sunayana in praise of Bharat: gold is tested by rubbing, a gem by the jeweller, and a man by his nature in the hour of trial.

prasang.title_en: Janaka's family joins the council
prasang.summary: Sita's parents arrive and the two families grieve together. Kausalya tells Sunayana that people, like gold, are proved by time. Janaka asks Bharat to decide, and Bharat declines: duty and self-interest pull apart, hatred is blind and love cannot reason, so he will follow Ram's wish. His few words leave the whole court in awe.
prasang.lesson: When you are too close to a decision, say so, and speak briefly and honestly.

rcm_2.speaker: Bharat
rcm_2.setting: Bharat, asked by Janaka what should be done, explains why he can't judge his own case.
rcm_2.sanskrit: आगम निगम प्रसिद्ध पुराना। सेवाधरमु कठिन जगु जाना॥ स्वामि धरम स्वारथहि बिरोधू। बैरु अंध प्रेमहि न प्रबोधू ॥
rcm_2.translation: The Vedas, scriptures and Puranas say, and the world knows, that the duty of service is hard. Duty to one's master and self-interest pull against each other; hatred is blind, and love has no judgement.
rcm_2.line: Duty and self-interest pull against each other. Hatred is blind, and love can't reason.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Bharat to Janaka: scripture and the world know seva dharma is hard; the master's duty opposes self-interest; enmity is blind and love has no discernment. So he leaves the decision to others.

prasang.title_en: Janaka's family joins the council
prasang.summary: Sita's parents arrive and the two families grieve together. Kausalya tells Sunayana that people, like gold, are proved by time. Janaka asks Bharat to decide, and Bharat declines: duty and self-interest pull apart, hatred is blind and love cannot reason, so he will follow Ram's wish. His few words leave the whole court in awe.
prasang.lesson: When you are too close to a decision, say so, and speak briefly and honestly.

rcm_2.speaker: Narrator
rcm_2.setting: Janaka and his court react to Bharat's reply.
rcm_2.sanskrit: भरत बचन सुनि देखि सुभाऊ। सहित समाज सराहत राऊ॥ सुगम अगम मृदु मंजु कठोरे। अरथु अमित अति आखर थोरे ॥
rcm_2.translation: Hearing Bharat's words and seeing his nature, Janaka and his court praised him. His words were easy yet deep, gentle yet firm: few in syllables, boundless in meaning.
rcm_2.line: Easy yet deep, gentle yet firm: few words, boundless meaning.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Janaka and his court praise Bharat's reply: easy and unfathomable, soft, lovely and firm, of endless meaning in very few syllables.

prasang.title_en: Janaka's family joins the council
prasang.summary: Sita's parents arrive and the two families grieve together. Kausalya tells Sunayana that people, like gold, are proved by time. Janaka asks Bharat to decide, and Bharat declines: duty and self-interest pull apart, hatred is blind and love cannot reason, so he will follow Ram's wish. His few words leave the whole court in awe.
prasang.lesson: When you are too close to a decision, say so, and speak briefly and honestly.

rcm_2.speaker: Bharat
rcm_2.setting: Bharat speaks to Ram before the whole assembly at Chitrakoot.
rcm_2.sanskrit: प्रभु पितु मातु सुहृद गुर स्वामी। पूज्य परम हित अंतरजामी॥ सरल सुसाहिबु सील निधानू। प्रनतपाल सर्बग्य सुजानू ॥ समरथ सरनागत हितकारी। गुनगाहकु अवगुन अघ हारी॥ स्वामि गोसाँइहि सरिस गोसाईं। मोहि समान मैं साइँ दोहाईं ॥
rcm_2.translation: Lord, you are father, mother, friend, teacher and master, worthy of worship, my highest good, knower of my heart; a simple, gentle master, a treasure of good nature, protector of those who bow, all-knowing and wise; mighty, a friend to those who seek refuge, one who values merits and removes faults and sins. There is no master like my master, and, I swear by my master, no one like me.
rcm_2.line: You are father, mother, friend, teacher, master: the one who values what is good in us and lifts our faults.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_2.our_note: Bharat before the assembly: Lord, you are father, mother, friend, guru and master, protector of the surrendered, taker of virtues and remover of faults; no master is like mine.

rcm_2.speaker: Bharat
rcm_2.setting: Before the whole family council, Bharat admits he came against orders and thanks Ram for his kindness.
rcm_2.sanskrit: कृपाँ भलाईं आपनी नाथ कीन्ह भल मोर। दूषन भे भूषन सरिस सुजसु चारु चहुँ ओर ॥
rcm_2.translation: Lord, by your own kindness and goodness you have done me good: my faults became like ornaments, and a good name has spread all around me.
rcm_2.line: Through your kindness, even my faults were turned into something good.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Bharat to Ram: Lord, by your own grace and goodness you did me good; my blemishes became like ornaments and fair fame spread on all four sides.

rcm_2.speaker: Bharat
rcm_2.setting: Bharat, in front of the council, speaks of how Ram treats those who come to him.
rcm_2.sanskrit: तेउ सुनि सरन सामुहें आए। सकृत प्रनामु किहें अपनाए॥ देखि दोष कबहुँ न उर आने। सुनि गुन साधु समाज बखाने ॥
rcm_2.translation: Even such people, hearing of you, came before you for shelter, and with a single bow you made them your own. You saw their faults but never kept them in your heart; you heard their virtues and praised them among the good.
rcm_2.line: Come once, bow once, and you are taken in. Your faults are seen, but never held against you.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Bharat on Ram's nature: even the worst, coming before you for sharan, you made your own at a single pranam; you never took their faults to heart and praised their virtues among the good.

rcm_2.speaker: Bharat
rcm_2.setting: Bharat admits he came to Chitrakoot against his father's order.
rcm_2.sanskrit: सोक सनेहँ कि बाल सुभाएँ। आयउँ लाइ रजायसु बाएँ॥ तबहुँ कृपाल हेरि निज ओरा। सबहि भाँति भल मानेउ मोरा ॥
rcm_2.translation: Whether out of grief, love or childishness, I came here against your will. Even then, kind one, you looked at it from your own side and took everything I did as good.
rcm_2.line: I came out of grief and love, even against your wish, and you took it all kindly.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_2.our_note: Bharat: from grief, affection or childishness I came setting the command aside; even so, gracious one, looking to your own nature you counted it good in every way.

rcm_2.speaker: Ram
rcm_2.setting: Bharat blames himself for his mother's scheme; Ram answers him in front of the elders.
rcm_2.sanskrit: करम बचन मानस बिमल तुम्ह समान तुम्ह तात। गुर समाज लघु बंधु गुन कुसमयँ किमि कहि जात ॥
rcm_2.translation: Brother, in deed, word and mind you are spotless; the only one like you is you. But how can I praise a younger brother's goodness in front of our elders, at a hard time like this?
rcm_2.line: In what you do, say and think, you are clean. There is no one like you.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Ram to Bharat before the elders: in karma, vachan and manas you are pure, your like is only you; how can a younger brother's virtues be told in the guru's assembly at such a time.

rcm_2.speaker: Ram
rcm_2.setting: Ram asks Bharat to rule in his place for fourteen years.
rcm_2.sanskrit: जानि तुम्हहि मृदु कहउँ कठोरा। कुसमयँ तात न अनुचित मोरा॥ होहिं कुठायँ सुबंधु सहाए। ओड़िअहिं हाथ असनिहु के धाए ॥
rcm_2.translation: Knowing you are gentle, I still say something hard; in hard times, brother, it isn't wrong of me. In bad times it is good brothers who help; it is the hands that rise to block a thunderbolt.
rcm_2.line: In bad times, good siblings are the hands that rise to block the blow.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Ram, knowing Bharat's tenderness, asks him the hard thing, to rule in his absence: in an evil hour good brothers are the help, as the hands ward off even the thunderbolt.

prasang.title_en: Ram and Bharat settle it
prasang.summary: Ram tells Bharat that keeping their father's word is the duty of both brothers, and that the leader must be like the mouth, taking in only to nourish the whole body. He asks him to rule in his place, knowing it is the harder task. Bharat accepts, asking only for Ram's sandals to keep him going.
prasang.lesson: A good resolution gives each person a role and something to hold on to.

rcm_2.speaker: Bharat
rcm_2.setting: Bharat accepts Ram's wish that he return to Ayodhya, but asks for one thing to carry.
rcm_2.sanskrit: अब कृपाल जस आयसु होई। करौं सीस धरि सादर सोई॥ सो अवलंब देव मोहि देई। अवधि पारु पावौं जेहि सेई ॥
rcm_2.translation: Now, gracious one, whatever you command I will do, holding it on my head with respect. But give me something to lean on, Lord, something I can serve, so that I can get through these years.
rcm_2.line: Give me something to hold on to, so I can get through these years.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Bharat: now, gracious one, whatever you order I will do with it on my head; but give me, Lord, an avalamb by serving which I may reach the far shore of the term. Ram gives his padukas.

rcm_2.speaker: Ram
rcm_2.setting: Ram, sending Bharat back to govern Ayodhya in his place, on what a leader should be.
rcm_2.sanskrit: मुखिआ मुखु सो चाहिऐ खान पान कहुँ एक। पालइ पोषइ सकल अँग तुलसी सहित बिबेक ॥
rcm_2.translation: A leader should be like the mouth: it alone eats and drinks, yet with good sense it nourishes and sustains every limb of the body.
rcm_2.line: A leader is like the mouth: it takes in, but only to nourish the whole body.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Ram's parting counsel on rajadharma to Bharat: the chief should be like the mouth, which alone eats and drinks yet with viveka sustains all the limbs.

prasang.title_en: Ram and Bharat settle it
prasang.summary: Ram tells Bharat that keeping their father's word is the duty of both brothers, and that the leader must be like the mouth, taking in only to nourish the whole body. He asks him to rule in his place, knowing it is the harder task. Bharat accepts, asking only for Ram's sandals to keep him going.
prasang.lesson: A good resolution gives each person a role and something to hold on to.

rcm_2.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_2.setting: Bharat rules Ayodhya for fourteen years from a hut, taking nothing for himself.
rcm_2.sanskrit: तेहिं पुर बसत भरत बिनु रागा। चंचरीक जिमि चंपक बागा॥ रमा बिलासु राम अनुरागी। तजत बमन जिमि जन बड़भागी ॥
rcm_2.translation: Bharat lives in that city without attachment, like a bee in a champak garden. Fortunate lovers of Ram turn from the luxuries of wealth as one turns from vomit.
rcm_2.line: He lived amid the riches like a bee in a champak garden, untouched by them.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Bharat dwells in Ayodhya without raga like a bee in a champak grove; fortunate lovers of Ram renounce Lakshmi's pleasures as vomit.

prasang.title_en: Bharat rules from a hut for fourteen years
prasang.summary: Bharat places Ram's sandals on the throne and lives outside the city in a hut, sleeping on grass, fasting, governing only as a caretaker. The palace's riches are all around him and do not touch him, like a bee in a champak garden.
prasang.lesson: You can live amid plenty without being owned by it.

rcm_2.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_2.setting: Indra's son Jayant, disguised as a crow, attacks Sita; when he finally falls at Ram's feet, Ram lets him go.
rcm_2.sanskrit: कीन्ह मोह बस द्रोह जद्यपि तेहि कर बध उचित। प्रभु छाड़ेउ करि छोह को कृपाल रघुबीर सम ॥
rcm_2.translation: Though out of delusion he had done harm, and punishment would have been just, the Lord let him go out of tenderness. Who is as kind as Raghubir?
rcm_2.line: He had done wrong, and still, when he came for shelter, the Lord let him go out of tenderness.
rcm_2.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_2.our_note: Jayant, as a crow, wounds Sita and is chased by Ram's arrow through the worlds; taking refuge, he is spared his life but, in the Manas, loses one eye. Mercy with a consequence.

prasang.title_en: Jayant the crow: shelter for the offender
prasang.summary: Indra's son, disguised as a crow, pecks Sita's foot to test Ram's power. Ram's straw arrow chases him through every world; no god will shelter him. Narada sends him back to Ram, where he falls at his feet admitting he reaped what he sowed. Ram lets him go with the loss of one eye.
prasang.lesson: Consequences may remain, but the one who turns back is still taken in.

rcm_2.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_2.setting: Sutikshna, lost in love, wanders and dances on the path; Ram watches.
rcm_2.sanskrit: अबिरल प्रेम भगति मुनि पाई। प्रभु देखैं तरु ओट लुकाई॥ अतिसय प्रीति देखि रघुबीरा। प्रगटे हृदयँ हरन भव भीरा ॥
rcm_2.translation: The sage had found unbroken loving devotion; the Lord watched him, hidden behind a tree. Seeing his overflowing love, Raghubir, who removes the fears of the world, appeared in his heart.
rcm_2.line: The Lord hid behind a tree to watch his devotee's joy.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_2.our_note: Sutikshna, having gained unbroken prema bhakti, dances on the path; the Lord watches hidden behind a tree and, seeing his great love, manifests in his heart.

prasang.title_en: Sutikshna runs to meet Ram
prasang.summary: A young sage hears Ram is near and runs out, sure he has no devotion, wisdom or discipline worth anything, trusting only that Ram loves those with nowhere else to go. Lost in love he wanders, dances, forgets the way; Ram watches from behind a tree, then lifts him up and holds him. Asked for a boon, the sage says only: may this one pride never leave me, that I am his.
prasang.lesson: You don't have to feel qualified; the one with nowhere else to go is the one he loves.

rcm_2.speaker: Ram
rcm_2.setting: Ram describes the devotee he cannot resist.
rcm_2.sanskrit: मम गुन गावत पुलक सरीरा। गदगद गिरा नयन बह नीरा॥ काम आदि मद दंभ न जाकें। तात निरंतर बस मैं ताकें ॥
rcm_2.translation: Singing of my qualities, the body thrills, the voice chokes, tears flow from the eyes; in whom there is no lust, pride or pretence: in their power, brother, I live always.
rcm_2.line: The one whose voice catches and eyes fill at my name, without pride or pretence: I am theirs.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_2.our_note: Ram to Lakshman, ending the teaching on bhakti: he whose body thrills singing my virtues, voice choked and eyes streaming, free of kama, mada and dambha, I am ever in his power.

rcm_2.speaker: Ram
rcm_2.setting: Ram ends his teaching on devotion.
rcm_2.sanskrit: बचन कर्म मन मोरि गति भजनु करहिं निःकाम। तिन्ह के हृदय कमल महुँ करउँ सदा बिश्राम ॥
rcm_2.translation: Those for whom I am the goal in word, deed and mind, who worship without wanting anything: in the lotus of their heart I rest always.
rcm_2.line: In the heart of the one who loves without wanting anything back, I rest always.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_2.our_note: Ram to Lakshman: those whose refuge I am in vachan, karma and mana, who worship nishkama, in the lotus of their heart I always rest.

rcm_2.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_2.setting: Ram finds the old vulture Jatayu dying after fighting Ravana for Sita.
rcm_2.sanskrit: कर सरोज सिर परसेउ कृपासिंधु रघुबीर। निरखि राम छबि धाम मुख बिगत भई सब पीर ॥
rcm_2.translation: Raghubir, the ocean of kindness, touched his head with his lotus hand. Gazing at Ram's face, the home of beauty, all his pain was gone.
rcm_2.line: He touched the dying bird's head, and looking at that face, all his pain was gone.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_2.our_note: Raghuvir, ocean of grace, strokes Jatayu's head with his lotus hand; looking at Ram's lovely face the vulture's whole pain departs.

prasang.title_en: Jatayu dies in Ram's lap
prasang.summary: Searching for Sita, Ram finds the old vulture who fought Ravana to save her, dying. Ram touches his head and the bird's pain leaves. Jatayu refuses Ram's offer to heal him: the one whose name people pray to say at death is in front of his eyes. He asks only for devotion, and Ram, in tears, performs his last rites with his own hands.
prasang.lesson: Nothing you do for love is small; it is honoured like family.

rcm_2.speaker: Ram
rcm_2.setting: Ram to the dying vulture Jatayu, who gave his life trying to save Sita.
rcm_2.sanskrit: परहित बस जिन्ह के मन माहीं। तिन्ह कहुँ जग दुर्लभ कछु नाहीं॥ तनु तिज तात जाहु मम धामा। देउँ काह तुम्ह पूरनकामा ॥
rcm_2.translation: "For those whose minds are ruled by the good of others, nothing in the world is out of reach. Leave this body, friend, and go to my abode; what can I give you, who already have everything?"
rcm_2.line: For someone whose heart is set on the good of others, nothing in the world is out of reach.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Ram to the dying Jatayu, who fought Ravana for Sita: to those in whose mind par hit dwells nothing is hard to obtain; leave the body and go to my abode, you who lack nothing.

prasang.title_en: Jatayu's last fight and Ram's grief
prasang.summary: Ram returns to an empty hut and searches the forest, asking birds and trees if they have seen Sita. He finds the old vulture Jatayu dying; he had fought Ravana alone to stop the abduction. Ram tells him that for one whose heart is set on others' good, nothing is out of reach, and performs his funeral rites himself, as a son would.
prasang.lesson: Standing up for someone matters, even when you cannot win.

rcm_2.speaker: Narrator
rcm_2.setting: Ram has just given the dying vulture Jatayu the final blessing usually sought by sages.
rcm_2.sanskrit: कोमल चित अति दीनदयाला। कारन बिनु रघुनाथ कृपाला॥ गीध अधम खग आमिष भोगी। गति दीन्ही जो जाचत जोगी ॥
rcm_2.translation: Raghunath is tender-hearted, kind to the lowly, gracious without needing a reason. To a vulture, a lowly bird that ate flesh, he gave the end that yogis beg for.
rcm_2.line: His heart is tender, and his kindness doesn't need a reason.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Of Jatayu: Raghunath is soft-hearted, most compassionate to the deen and gracious without cause; to a vulture, a low bird eating flesh, he gave the gati yogis ask for.

rcm_2.speaker: Shabari and Ram
rcm_2.setting: The old forest woman Shabari, who waited years for Ram, says she is too lowly even to praise him.
rcm_2.sanskrit: अधम ते अधम अधम अति नारी। तिन्ह महँ मैं मतिमंद अघारी॥ कह रघुपति सुनु भामिनि बाता। मानउँ एक भगति कर नाता ॥
rcm_2.translation: Shabari: 'Among the lowest of the low, women are counted lowest, and among them I am the dullest, Lord.' Ram said: 'Listen to me, good woman: I recognise only one kinship, the kinship of devotion.'
rcm_2.line: I don't measure people the way the world does. The only kinship I recognise is love.
rcm_2.misuse: The first half is Shabari's harsh self-description, which Ram's reply overturns; never show it on its own.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Shabari calls herself lowest among women, who are counted lowest of the low; Ram replies, listen, bhamini, I honour only the relation of bhakti, and then lists what does not count: caste, family, wealth, skill.

rcm_2.speaker: Ram
rcm_2.setting: Ram to Shabari, the forest woman of no rank, on the forms of devotion (seventh and eighth).
rcm_2.sanskrit: सातवँ सम मोहि मय जग देखा। मोतें संत अधिक करि लेखा॥ आठवँ जथालाभ संतोषा। सपनेहुँ नहिं देखइ परदोषा ॥
rcm_2.translation: The seventh is to see the whole world as filled with me, and to regard good people as greater than me. The eighth is to be content with whatever comes, and never, even in a dream, to look for faults in others.
rcm_2.line: Be content with what comes, and don't go looking for faults in others, not even in your dreams.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: The seventh and eighth of the nine forms of bhakti Ram teaches Shabari: seeing the world as Ram-filled and saints as greater than him; contentment with what is got and no fault-finding.

prasang.title_en: Ram visits Shabari
prasang.summary: An old forest woman, Shabari, has waited years for Ram. When he comes she washes his feet and feeds him roots and fruit, and he praises every bite. He tells her he recognises only the bond of devotion and describes nine forms of it, ending with contentment, not hunting faults, and being simple and without guile.
prasang.lesson: What counts is the heart you bring, not who you are on paper.

rcm_2.speaker: Ram
rcm_2.setting: Ram to Shabari, completing the nine forms of devotion.
rcm_2.sanskrit: नवम सरल सब सन छलहीना। मम भरोस हियँ हरष न दीना॥ नव महुँ एकउ जिन्ह कें होई। नारि पुरुष सचराचर कोई ॥
rcm_2.translation: The ninth is to be simple and free of guile with everyone, to keep trust in me in your heart, and to be neither elated nor downcast. Whoever has even one of these nine, man or woman or any creature at all...
rcm_2.line: Be simple and without guile with everyone, neither carried away by joy nor crushed by setbacks.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Ram completes navadha bhakti for Shabari: simplicity and guilelessness with all, trust in me, neither harsha nor dainya; whoever has even one of the nine is dear to me.

prasang.title_en: Ram visits Shabari
prasang.summary: An old forest woman, Shabari, has waited years for Ram. When he comes she washes his feet and feeds him roots and fruit, and he praises every bite. He tells her he recognises only the bond of devotion and describes nine forms of it, ending with contentment, not hunting faults, and being simple and without guile.
prasang.lesson: What counts is the heart you bring, not who you are on paper.

rcm_2.speaker: Ram
rcm_2.setting: Ram has just said: whoever has even one of the nine forms, woman or man or any being, ...
rcm_2.sanskrit: सोइ अतिसय प्रिय भामिनि मोरें। सकल प्रकार भगति दृढ़ तोरें॥ जोगि बृंद दुरलभ गति जोई। तो कहुँ आजु सुलभ भइ सोई ॥
rcm_2.translation: ...that one is most dear to me, good lady; and in you every kind of devotion is firm. The state that is hard even for yogis has today become easy for you.
rcm_2.line: You are most dear to me. What even yogis struggle to reach has become easy for you today.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_2.our_note: Ram to Shabari: whoever has even one of the nine, woman or man, is most dear to me, and in you all are firm; the gati rare for hosts of yogis is easy for you today.

prasang.title_en: Shabari's wait and the nine forms of devotion
prasang.summary: An old woman of the forest has waited years for Ram on her teacher's word. When he comes she falls at his feet, washes them, and feeds him fruit he praises again and again. She says she does not know how to praise him; he answers that he recognises only the kinship of devotion, teaches her the nine forms of devotion, and tells her that whoever has even one of them is most dear to him.
prasang.lesson: Your simple offering is enough; love, not status, is the only kinship that counts.

rcm_2.speaker: Ram
rcm_2.setting: Ram to Lakshman in the spring forest near Pampa lake.
rcm_2.sanskrit: तात तीनि अति प्रबल खल काम क्रोध अरु लोभ। मुनि बिग्यान धाम मन करहिं निमिष महुँ छोभ ॥
rcm_2.translation: Brother, three enemies are exceedingly strong: desire, anger and greed. In an instant they unsettle even the minds of sages who are homes of wisdom.
rcm_2.line: Desire, anger and greed can unsettle even the wisest mind in a moment.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Ram to Lakshman at Pampa: kama, krodha and lobha are three most powerful villains that agitate in a moment the minds of munis who are abodes of wisdom.

prasang.title_en: Ram at Pampa on desire, anger and greed
prasang.summary: Grieving, Ram walks with Lakshman through spring forests by Lake Pampa and describes the season as an army of desire. He names desire, anger and greed as three forces that can unsettle even the wisest mind in a moment, and notes that fruit-laden trees bow, as generous people do when they prosper.
prasang.lesson: Desire, anger and greed can unsettle anyone; knowing that is half the defence.

rcm_2.speaker: Shiva
rcm_2.setting: Shiva tells Parvati what he himself has found.
rcm_2.sanskrit: उमा कहउँ मैं अनुभव अपना। सत हरि भजनु जगत सब सपना॥ पुनि प्रभु गए सरोबर तीरा। पंपा नाम सुभग गंभीरा ॥
rcm_2.translation: Uma, I tell you my own experience: worship of Hari is real, and the whole world is a dream.
rcm_2.line: I tell you from my own experience: love for God is real; the rest passes like a dream.
rcm_2.misuse: Not 'nothing in your life matters'; Shiva is naming what lasts.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_2.our_note: Shiva to Uma: I tell my own anubhava, Hari bhajan is true and all the world a dream.

rcm_2.speaker: Ram
rcm_2.setting: Narada hesitates to ask Ram for a boon.
rcm_2.sanskrit: जानहु मुनि तुम्ह मोर सुभाऊ। जन सन कबहुँ कि करऊँ दुराऊ॥ कवन बस्तु असि प्रिय मोहि लागी। जो मुनिबर न सकहुँ तुम्ह मागी ॥ जन कहुँ कछु अदेय नहिं मोरें। अस बिस्वास तजहु जनि भोरें॥ तब नारद बोले हरषाई। अस बर मागउँ करउँ ढिठाई ॥
rcm_2.translation: 'You know my nature, sage: do I ever hide anything from my own? What thing is so dear to me that you could not ask for it? There is nothing I would withhold from my own; never let go of this trust.' Then Narada, delighted, said: 'I will be bold and ask this boon.'
rcm_2.line: Do I ever hide anything from my own? Never let go of this trust.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_2.our_note: Ram to the hesitant Narada: you know my nature, do I ever hide anything from my servant; there is nothing I would not give my own. Narada then asks for love of the Name. Read with the next verses, where Ram explains a refusal.

rcm_2.speaker: Ram
rcm_2.setting: Narada asks why Ram stopped his marriage; Ram explains how he guards those who rely on him.
rcm_2.sanskrit: तब बिबाह मैं चाहउँ कीन्हा। प्रभु केहि कारन करै न दीन्हा॥ सुनु मुनि तोहि कहउँ सहरोसा। भजहिं जे मोहि तजि सकल भरोसा ॥ करउँ सदा तिन्ह कै रखवारी। जिमि बालक राखइ महतारी॥ गह सिसु बच्छ अनल अहि धाई। तहँ राखइ जननी अरगाई ॥
rcm_2.translation: 'When I wanted to marry, Lord, why did you not let me?' 'Listen, sage, I tell you gladly: those who worship me, giving up every other reliance, I always guard, as a mother guards her child. When the little child runs to grab fire or a snake, the mother pulls it back.'
rcm_2.line: Those who rely on me, I guard always, as a mother pulls her child back from the fire.
rcm_2.misuse: A mother's protection includes saying no; this is not a promise that nothing painful will happen. Devotion is not a promise of a particular outcome, and it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_2.our_note: Narada asks why Ram prevented his marriage; Ram: those who worship me giving up all other trust I guard always, as a mother holds back the child running at fire or snake.

rcm_2.speaker: Ram
rcm_2.setting: Ram continues explaining how he cares for different devotees.
rcm_2.sanskrit: प्रौढ़ भएँ तेहि सुत पर माता। प्रीति करइ नहिं पाछिलि बाता॥ मोरें प्रौढ़ तनय सम ग्यानी। बालक सुत सम दास अमानी ॥ जनहि मोर बल निज बल ताही। दुहु कहँ काम क्रोध रिपु आही॥ यह बिचारि पंडित मोहि भजहीं। पाएहुँ ग्यान भगति नहिं तजहीं ॥
rcm_2.translation: When the son is grown, the mother loves him but no longer as before. The wise are like my grown sons; the humble servant is like my little child. My servant has my strength; the wise one relies on his own. Both face the enemies of desire and anger. Knowing this, the wise worship me, and even after gaining knowledge they do not give up devotion.
rcm_2.line: The humble devotee is like my little child, and has my strength to lean on.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_2.our_note: Ram: the jnani is like my grown son and the prideless servant like my infant; my servant has my strength, the jnani his own, and both face kama and krodha. So the wise keep bhakti even after jnana.

rcm_2.speaker: Ram
rcm_2.setting: Ram, asked by the sage Narada what marks a good person.
rcm_2.sanskrit: निज गुन श्रवन सुनत सकुचाहीं। पर गुन सुनत अधिक हरषाहीं॥ सम सीतल नहिं त्यागहिं नीती। सरल सुभाउ सबहि सन प्रीति ॥
rcm_2.translation: They shrink when they hear their own praises and are delighted to hear the praises of others. They are even-tempered and calm, never abandon what is right, are simple by nature and kind to all.
rcm_2.line: Good people squirm at their own praise and light up when others are praised.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Ram to Narada on the marks of saints: abashed at hearing their own virtues, glad at others', even and cool, never leaving niti, simple and loving to all.

prasang.title_en: Ram tells Narada the marks of a good person
prasang.summary: Narada asks Ram what marks a truly good person. Ram lists them: free of the six inner enemies, content, steady, generous with respect and seeking none, squirming at their own praise and glad at others', even-tempered and simple with everyone.
prasang.lesson: Good people are uncomfortable with their own praise and glad at others'.

rcm_2.speaker: Hanuman
rcm_2.setting: Hanuman asks Ram not to let his faults stand between them.
rcm_2.sanskrit: जदपि नाथ बहु अवगुन मोरें। सेवक प्रभुहि परै जनि भोरें॥ नाथ जीव तव मायाँ मोहा। सो निस्तरइ तुम्हारेहिं छोहा ॥
rcm_2.translation: Though I have many faults, Lord, let the servant not slip from the master's memory. Lord, every soul is bewildered by your illusion; it is freed only by your tenderness.
rcm_2.line: I have many faults, Lord. Don't let your servant slip from your mind.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_2.our_note: Hanuman on recognising Ram: though I have many faults, Lord, let the servant not fall from the master's mind; the jiva is deluded by your maya and crosses only by your kindness.

prasang.title_en: Hanuman meets Ram
prasang.summary: Sent by a frightened Sugriva, Hanuman goes disguised as a brahmin to question two strangers. When Ram names himself, Hanuman recognises his Lord, falls at his feet speechless, then gently complains that Ram forgot him. He says he knows no method of worship and relies on Ram as a child relies on its mother. Ram lifts him up, holds him, cools him with his own tears, and tells him he is twice as dear as Lakshman.
prasang.lesson: You don't need the right method; being his is enough, and he weeps to have you back.

rcm_2.speaker: Hanuman
rcm_2.setting: Hanuman explains why he relies on Ram alone.
rcm_2.sanskrit: ता पर मैं रघुबीर दोहाई। जानउँ नहिं कछु भजन उपाई॥ सेवक सुत पति मातु भरोसें। रहइ असोच बनइ प्रभु पोसें ॥
rcm_2.translation: And on top of that, I swear by Raghubir, I know no method of worship. A servant relies on his master, a child on its mother, and lives free of worry; the master has to look after him.
rcm_2.line: A child relies on its mother and stops worrying; she has to look after it.
rcm_2.misuse: Surrender here comes after effort and honest reflection; it is not a reason to stop acting or to stay in harm's way.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_2.our_note: Hanuman: I know no means of bhajan; the servant on the master and the son on the mother rely and stay free of care, and the Lord must nourish them.

prasang.title_en: Hanuman meets Ram
prasang.summary: Sent by a frightened Sugriva, Hanuman goes disguised as a brahmin to question two strangers. When Ram names himself, Hanuman recognises his Lord, falls at his feet speechless, then gently complains that Ram forgot him. He says he knows no method of worship and relies on Ram as a child relies on its mother. Ram lifts him up, holds him, cools him with his own tears, and tells him he is twice as dear as Lakshman.
prasang.lesson: You don't need the right method; being his is enough, and he weeps to have you back.

rcm_2.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_2.setting: Hanuman falls at Ram's feet in his true form.
rcm_2.sanskrit: अस कहि परेउ चरन अकुलाई। निज तनु प्रगटि प्रीति उर छाई॥ तब रघुपति उठाई उर लावा। निज लोचन जल सींचि जुड़ावा ॥
rcm_2.translation: Saying this he fell at his feet in distress, showing his own form, his heart full of love. Then Raghupati lifted him up, held him to his heart, and cooled him with the tears of his own eyes.
rcm_2.line: Ram lifted him up, held him close, and cooled him with his own tears.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_2.our_note: Hanuman falls at Ram's feet, showing his own form; Raghupati raises him, clasps him to his heart and soothes him with the water of his own eyes.

prasang.title_en: Hanuman meets Ram
prasang.summary: Sent by a frightened Sugriva, Hanuman goes disguised as a brahmin to question two strangers. When Ram names himself, Hanuman recognises his Lord, falls at his feet speechless, then gently complains that Ram forgot him. He says he knows no method of worship and relies on Ram as a child relies on its mother. Ram lifts him up, holds him, cools him with his own tears, and tells him he is twice as dear as Lakshman.
prasang.lesson: You don't need the right method; being his is enough, and he weeps to have you back.

rcm_2.speaker: Ram
rcm_2.setting: Hanuman, ashamed that he did not recognise Ram at first, falls weeping at his feet.
rcm_2.sanskrit: सुनु कपि जियँ मानसि जनि ऊना। तैं मम प्रिय लछिमन ते दूना॥ समदरसी मोहि कह सब कोऊ। सेवक प्रिय अनन्य गति सोऊ ॥
rcm_2.translation: Listen, Hanuman: don't let your heart feel small. You are twice as dear to me as Lakshman. Everyone calls me impartial, yet the one who serves me is dear to me, because he has no other refuge.
rcm_2.line: Don't feel small. You are twice as dear to me as my own brother.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Hanuman, ashamed at not recognising his Lord, falls at Ram's feet; Ram lifts him: do not feel diminished, you are twice as dear as Lakshman; the ananya servant is dear to me.

rcm_2.speaker: Sugriva
rcm_2.setting: Sugriva has just given Ram the scarf Sita dropped; Ram is weeping.
rcm_2.sanskrit: कह सुग्रीव सुनहु रघुबीरा। तजहु सोच मन आनहु धीरा॥ सब प्रकार करिहउँ सेवकाई। जेहि बिधि मिलिहि जानकी आई ॥
rcm_2.translation: Sugriva said: Listen, Raghuvir. Put aside your worry and steady your heart. I will serve you in every way, whatever it takes for Janaki to come back to you.
rcm_2.line: Put down your worry and steady your heart. I'll help you in every way I can.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Ram weeps on seeing Sita's cloth; Sugriva says leave sorrow, bring dhira to your mind, I will serve in every way so that Janaki comes back to you.

rcm_2.speaker: Ram
rcm_2.setting: Ram to Sugriva, as they swear friendship by the fire.
rcm_2.sanskrit: जे न मित्र दुख होहिं दुखारी। तिन्हहि बिलोकत पातक भारी॥ निज दुख गिरि सम रज करि जाना। मित्रक दुख रज मेरु समाना ॥
rcm_2.translation: Those who are not pained by a friend's pain commit a grave wrong just by being seen. A true friend treats his own mountain of sorrow as a speck of dust, and his friend's speck of sorrow as a mountain.
rcm_2.line: A real friend treats his own troubles as dust and his friend's troubles as a mountain.
rcm_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_2.our_note: Ram to Sugriva on mitra dharma: it is sin even to look at those not grieved by a friend's grief; one's own mountain of sorrow is dust beside a friend's speck.

prasang.title_en: Ram and Sugriva become friends
prasang.summary: Hanuman, sent to check whether the two strangers are Bali's spies, recognises Ram and brings him to Sugriva, who has been driven out by his brother. Before a fire as witness they become friends, and Ram describes what friendship asks: your friend's small trouble is a mountain, your own is dust; steer him right, hide his faults, love him more in hard times.
prasang.lesson: A friend treats your trouble as bigger than their own.

rcm_3.speaker: Ram
rcm_3.setting: Ram to Sugriva on what a friend actually does.
rcm_3.sanskrit: जिन्ह कें असि मति सहज न आई। ते सठ कत हठि करत मिताई॥ कुपथ निवारि सुपंथ चलावा। गुन प्रगटै अवगुनन्हि दुरावा ॥
rcm_3.translation: Why do those who lack this natural feeling force themselves into friendships? A friend turns you back from the wrong path and sets you on the right one, makes your good qualities known and keeps your faults to himself.
rcm_3.line: A friend steers you off the wrong path, speaks of your strengths, and keeps your faults private.
rcm_3.misuse: Keeping faults private means discretion, not covering up harm.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Ram on the friend: he keeps you from the evil path and leads you on the good, displays your virtues and conceals your faults; those without this feeling should not press friendship.

prasang.title_en: Ram and Sugriva become friends
prasang.summary: Hanuman, sent to check whether the two strangers are Bali's spies, recognises Ram and brings him to Sugriva, who has been driven out by his brother. Before a fire as witness they become friends, and Ram describes what friendship asks: your friend's small trouble is a mountain, your own is dust; steer him right, hide his faults, love him more in hard times.
prasang.lesson: A friend treats your trouble as bigger than their own.

rcm_3.speaker: Ram
rcm_3.setting: Ram to Sugriva on the marks of a good friend.
rcm_3.sanskrit: देत लेत मन संक न धरई। बल अनुमान सदा हित करई॥ बिपति काल कर सतगुन नेहा। श्रुति कह संत मित्र गुन एहा ॥
rcm_3.translation: He gives and takes without suspicion, always does you good as far as he is able, and in hard times loves you a hundred times more. These, say the scriptures, are the qualities of a good friend.
rcm_3.line: A good friend gives without keeping score, and loves you a hundredfold more in hard times.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Ram: he has no doubt in giving and taking, always does good according to his strength, and in time of calamity loves a hundred times more; the Veda calls these a good friend's marks.

prasang.title_en: Ram and Sugriva become friends
prasang.summary: Hanuman, sent to check whether the two strangers are Bali's spies, recognises Ram and brings him to Sugriva, who has been driven out by his brother. Before a fire as witness they become friends, and Ram describes what friendship asks: your friend's small trouble is a mountain, your own is dust; steer him right, hide his faults, love him more in hard times.
prasang.lesson: A friend treats your trouble as bigger than their own.

rcm_3.speaker: Ram
rcm_3.setting: Ram to Sugriva on the signs of a false friend.
rcm_3.sanskrit: आगें कह मृदु बचन बनाई। पाछें अनहित मन कुटिलाई॥ जाकर िचत अहि गति सम भाई। अस कुमित्र परिहरेहिं भलाई ॥
rcm_3.translation: One who says sweet, made-up words to your face but wishes you ill behind your back, with a crooked mind; whose heart moves like a snake, brother: it is best to leave such a false friend.
rcm_3.line: Sweet to your face, harmful behind your back: it is best to walk away from such a friend.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Ram: he who speaks soft contrived words in front and is crooked and ill-wishing behind, whose mind moves like a snake, such a kumitra is better abandoned.

prasang.title_en: Ram and Sugriva become friends
prasang.summary: Hanuman, sent to check whether the two strangers are Bali's spies, recognises Ram and brings him to Sugriva, who has been driven out by his brother. Before a fire as witness they become friends, and Ram describes what friendship asks: your friend's small trouble is a mountain, your own is dust; steer him right, hide his faults, love him more in hard times.
prasang.lesson: A friend treats your trouble as bigger than their own.

rcm_3.speaker: Sugriva
rcm_3.setting: Sugriva, after Ram promises to help him, sees his feud with his brother Bali differently.
rcm_3.sanskrit: बालि परम हित जासु प्रसादा। मिलेहु राम तुम्ह समन बिषादा॥ सपनें जेहि सन होइ लराई। जागें समुझत मन सकुचाई ॥
rcm_3.translation: Bali is in fact my greatest benefactor: through him I met you, who end all sorrow. Now if I fought him even in a dream, I'd feel ashamed on waking.
rcm_3.line: If I fought my brother even in a dream, I'd feel ashamed on waking.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Sugriva says he would now be ashamed to fight Bali even in a dream. Ram smiles and says his own word will not prove false. The tradition reads this as kshanik vairagya: the feud continues.

prasang.title_en: Sugriva and Bali: brothers split by a misunderstanding
prasang.summary: Bali chased a demon into a cave and told Sugriva to wait a fortnight. Sugriva waited a month; blood flowed out, he assumed Bali dead, sealed the cave and was made king. Bali fought his way out, decided his brother had betrayed him, and drove him out. Later, safe with Ram, Sugriva says that if he fought his brother even in a dream he'd be ashamed on waking.
prasang.lesson: Brothers can become enemies over one misread moment; ask before you assume betrayal.

rcm_3.speaker: Ram
rcm_3.setting: Ram consoles Tara, weeping over her husband Bali's body.
rcm_3.sanskrit: तारा बिकल देखि रघुराया। दीन्ह ग्यान हरि लीन्ही माया॥ छिति जल पावक गगन समीरा। पंच रचित अति अधम सरीरा ॥ प्रगट सो तनु तव आगे सोवा। जीव नित्य केहि लगि तुम्ह रोवा॥ उपजा ग्यान चरन तब लागी। लीन्हेसि परम भगति बर मागी ॥
rcm_3.translation: Seeing Tara distraught, Raghunath gave her wisdom and took away her delusion: 'This body is made of five elements, earth, water, fire, sky and air, and it is a lowly thing. That body lies here before you, asleep; the self is eternal. For whom are you weeping?' When understanding dawned, she bowed at his feet and asked for the gift of devotion.
rcm_3.line: The body of five elements lies before you; the self lives on. For whom do you weep?
rcm_3.misuse: This is comfort for later, not a reason to stop someone from grieving.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Ram gives the distraught Tara jnana and removes her maya: the body is of five elements, the jiva eternal. The understanding comes by his grace, and she asks for bhakti.

prasang.title_en: Ram consoles Tara
prasang.summary: After Bali's death his wife Tara weeps over his body. Ram speaks to her gently: the body is made of five elements and lies here before her, but the self is not only this body; for whom is she weeping? Comforted, she asks for devotion, and Bali's son Angad is made heir.
prasang.lesson: Grief needs time; later, perspective on what is lost and what endures can comfort.

rcm_3.speaker: Ram
rcm_3.setting: Ram to Lakshman, watching the monsoon from Mount Pravarshana.
rcm_3.sanskrit: बरषहिं जलद भूमि निअराएँ। जथा नवहिं बुध बिद्या पाएँ। बूँद अघात सहहिं गिरि कैसे। खल के बचन संत सह जैसें ॥
rcm_3.translation: The clouds hang low as they rain, the way the wise bow when they gain learning. The mountains bear the beating of the raindrops the way the good bear the harsh words of the wicked.
rcm_3.line: Mountains take the pounding rain the way steady people take harsh words.
rcm_3.misuse: Bearing words calmly is not the same as accepting mistreatment.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Ram's monsoon similes to Lakshman: clouds bend low as the wise bow on gaining vidya; hills endure the drops as saints endure the words of the wicked.

prasang.title_en: Ram's monsoon and autumn lessons
prasang.summary: Waiting out the rains on a mountain, Ram points out lessons to Lakshman in each sight: clouds bow low when full, mountains take the rain as the steady take harsh words, small streams swagger, ponds fill drop by drop, autumn sun dries the puddles as contentment dries greed, and fish panic as the water shrinks.
prasang.lesson: Nature keeps teaching: steadiness, humility, patience, and saving for the dry season.

rcm_3.speaker: Ram
rcm_3.setting: Ram to Lakshman, watching the monsoon.
rcm_3.sanskrit: छुद्र नदीं भरि चलीं तोराई। जस थोरेहुँ धन खल इतराई॥ भूमि परत भा ढाबर पानी। जनु जीवहि माया लपटानी ॥
rcm_3.translation: Little streams swell and rush along, bursting their banks, the way a petty person swaggers on a little money. Rainwater falling on the ground turns muddy, as the soul is clouded once it is wrapped in illusion.
rcm_3.line: Little streams overflow after one rain, the way small minds swagger after a little money.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Ram's monsoon similes: small rivers fill and break their banks as the base man is puffed up by a little wealth; water turns muddy on the ground as the jiva is wrapped by maya.

prasang.title_en: Ram's monsoon and autumn lessons
prasang.summary: Waiting out the rains on a mountain, Ram points out lessons to Lakshman in each sight: clouds bow low when full, mountains take the rain as the steady take harsh words, small streams swagger, ponds fill drop by drop, autumn sun dries the puddles as contentment dries greed, and fish panic as the water shrinks.
prasang.lesson: Nature keeps teaching: steadiness, humility, patience, and saving for the dry season.

rcm_3.speaker: Ram
rcm_3.setting: Ram to Lakshman, as the rains end and autumn clears the sky.
rcm_3.sanskrit: उदित अगस्ति पंथ जल सोषा। जिमि लोभहिं सोषइ संतोषा॥ सरिता सर निर्मल जल सोहा। संत हृदय जस गत मद मोहा ॥
rcm_3.translation: Agastya's star rises and dries the water on the roads, as contentment dries up greed. Rivers and lakes shine with clear water, like the heart of a good person freed from pride and confusion.
rcm_3.line: Contentment dries up greed the way the autumn sun dries the puddles.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Ram's autumn similes: Agastya rises and dries the water of the paths as santosha dries lobha; rivers and lakes are clear like a saint's heart free of mada and moha.

prasang.title_en: Ram's monsoon and autumn lessons
prasang.summary: Waiting out the rains on a mountain, Ram points out lessons to Lakshman in each sight: clouds bow low when full, mountains take the rain as the steady take harsh words, small streams swagger, ponds fill drop by drop, autumn sun dries the puddles as contentment dries greed, and fish panic as the water shrinks.
prasang.lesson: Nature keeps teaching: steadiness, humility, patience, and saving for the dry season.

rcm_3.speaker: Ram
rcm_3.setting: Ram, describing autumn to Lakshman, as the ponds begin to shrink.
rcm_3.sanskrit: पंक न रेनु सोह असि धरनी। नीति निपुन नृप कै जसि करनी॥ जल संकोच बिकल भइँ मीना। अबुध कुटुंबी जिमि धनहीना ॥
rcm_3.translation: With neither mud nor dust, the earth looks like the work of a wise king. As the water shrinks, the fish grow restless, like a thoughtless householder when the money runs out.
rcm_3.line: Fish panic as the pond shrinks, like a careless household when the money runs out.
rcm_3.misuse: Not a judgement on anyone struggling with money; a nudge to plan for dry seasons.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Autumn simile: the fish are troubled as the water lessens, like an unwise householder without wealth. The word abudh, unwise, carries a judgement.

prasang.title_en: Ram's monsoon and autumn lessons
prasang.summary: Waiting out the rains on a mountain, Ram points out lessons to Lakshman in each sight: clouds bow low when full, mountains take the rain as the steady take harsh words, small streams swagger, ponds fill drop by drop, autumn sun dries the puddles as contentment dries greed, and fish panic as the water shrinks.
prasang.lesson: Nature keeps teaching: steadiness, humility, patience, and saving for the dry season.

rcm_3.speaker: Sugriva
rcm_3.setting: Sugriva, having forgotten his promise to Ram amid royal comforts, apologises to an angry Lakshman.
rcm_3.sanskrit: नाथ विषय सम मद कछु नाहीं। मुनि मन मोह करइ छन माहीं। सुनत बिनीत बचन सुख पावा। लछिमन तेहि बहु बिधि समुझावा ॥
rcm_3.translation: Lord, there is no intoxicant like the pleasures of the senses; they cloud even a sage's mind in an instant. Hearing his humble words, Lakshman was pleased and reassured him in many ways.
rcm_3.line: No drink intoxicates like comfort. It can cloud even a wise mind in a moment.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Sugriva, having forgotten Ram's work in the pleasures of kingship, confesses to Lakshman that there is no mada like vishaya. Humility is accepted and he is reassured.

prasang.title_en: Sugriva forgets his promise
prasang.summary: The rains end and Sugriva, now king, has forgotten his promise to search for Sita. Ram is hurt; Lakshman storms into the city in anger. Hanuman had already nudged Sugriva, who comes out, admits that comfort intoxicated him, and sends search parties in every direction.
prasang.lesson: Success and comfort make us forget who helped us; admit it quickly and make it right.

rcm_3.speaker: Sampati
rcm_3.setting: The old vulture Sampati tells the despairing monkeys how he lost his wings.
rcm_3.sanskrit: तेज न सहि सक सो फिरि आवा। मैं अभिमानी रबि निअरावा॥ जरे पंख अति तेज अपारा। परेउँ भूमि करि घोर चिकारा ॥
rcm_3.translation: He (Jatayu) could not bear the sun's heat and turned back; I, being proud, flew on towards the sun. My wings burned in its boundless blaze, and I fell to the earth with a terrible cry.
rcm_3.line: My brother turned back from the sun. I, in my pride, flew closer, and my wings burned.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Sampati tells the vanaras: Jatayu could not bear the heat and returned; I, abhimani, went near the sun, my wings burned and I fell crying to the earth. The Manas makes pride the cause.

prasang.title_en: Sampati's burned wings
prasang.summary: The search party, past its deadline with no news, sits down by the sea to die. A huge old vulture, Sampati, overhears them talking of his brother Jatayu. He tells them how pride once made him fly too close to the sun and burn his wings; a sage told him they would grow back when he helped Ram's messengers. He tells them where Sita is, and his wings grow back as he speaks.
prasang.lesson: Even after the fall your pride caused, you can still be useful, and hope can return.

rcm_3.speaker: Sampati
rcm_3.setting: Sampati, his wings regrown, urges the monkeys who had given up the search.
rcm_3.sanskrit: जो नाघइ सत जोजन सागर। करइ सो राम काज मति आगर॥ मोहि बिलोकि धरहु मन धीरा। राम कृपाँ कस भयउ सरीरा ॥
rcm_3.translation: Whoever can leap the hundred-league ocean, wise and capable, will do Ram's work. Look at me and take heart: see what Ram's grace has done to my body.
rcm_3.line: Look at me and take heart. My burned wings have grown back.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Sampati to the despairing monkeys: whoever leaps the hundred yojanas will do Ram's work; look at me and take courage, see what my body has become by Ram's kripa.

prasang.title_en: Sampati's burned wings
prasang.summary: The search party, past its deadline with no news, sits down by the sea to die. A huge old vulture, Sampati, overhears them talking of his brother Jatayu. He tells them how pride once made him fly too close to the sun and burn his wings; a sage told him they would grow back when he helped Ram's messengers. He tells them where Sita is, and his wings grow back as he speaks.
prasang.lesson: Even after the fall your pride caused, you can still be useful, and hope can return.

rcm_3.speaker: Sampati
rcm_3.setting: The monkeys despair at the ocean; the old vulture Sampati rouses them.
rcm_3.sanskrit: पापिउ जाकर नाम सुमिरहीं। अति अपार भवसागर तरहीं॥ तासु दूत तुम्ह तजि कदराई राम हृदयँ धरि करहु उपाई ॥
rcm_3.translation: Even sinners who remember his name cross the boundless ocean of the world. You are his messengers: give up your timidity, keep Ram in your heart and find a way.
rcm_3.line: Drop your timidity. Keep Ram in your heart and find a way.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_3.our_note: Sampati to the vanaras: sinners who remember his name cross the shoreless bhavasagar; you are his envoys, leave cowardice, keep Ram in your heart and make the effort.

rcm_3.speaker: Jambavant
rcm_3.setting: The old bear Jambavant to Hanuman, who sits silent while others say the ocean is too wide.
rcm_3.sanskrit: कवन सो काज कठिन जग माहीं। जो नहिं होइ तात तुम्ह पाहीं॥ राम काज लगि तव अवतारा। सुनतहिं भयउ पर्बताकारा ॥
rcm_3.translation: "What task in the world is too hard for you, my son? You were born for Ram's work." Hearing this, Hanuman grew to the size of a mountain.
rcm_3.line: What task in the world is too hard for you? You were made for this.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Jambavant rouses the silent Hanuman: what work is hard for you, your very birth is for Ram's task. Strength returns when he is reminded of whose work it is.

prasang.title_en: Jambavant reminds Hanuman of his strength
prasang.summary: Nobody can leap the ocean. Old Jambavant admits honestly that he is no longer young. Then he turns to the silent Hanuman and asks why he sits quiet: what task in the world is too hard for him? Hanuman grows to the size of a mountain.
prasang.lesson: Sometimes we need someone else to remind us what we can do; and the old can be that someone.

rcm_3.speaker: Hanuman
rcm_3.setting: Mid-leap, the mountain Mainaka rises and offers Hanuman a rest.
rcm_3.sanskrit: हनूमान तेहि परसा कर पुनि कीन्ह प्रनाम। राम काजु कीन्हें बिनु मोहि कहाँ बिश्राम ॥
rcm_3.translation: Hanuman touched it with his hand, bowed to it, and said: how can I rest until I have done Ram's work?
rcm_3.line: He thanked the mountain and said: how can I rest before Ram's work is done?
rcm_3.misuse: About commitment to a task that matters; rest is allowed, and Hanuman thanks the one who offers it.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_3.our_note: Mainaka rises from the sea to rest Hanuman; he touches it, bows, and says: without doing Ram's work, where is rest for me. Courtesy and resolve together.

rcm_3.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_3.setting: Sanskrit prayer opening the Sundar Kand, recited daily by many.
rcm_3.sanskrit: नान्या स्पृहा रघुपते हृदयेऽस्मदीये सत्यं वदामि च भवानखिलान्तरात्मा। भक्तिं प्रयच्छ रघुपुंगव निर्भरां मे कामादिदोषरहितं कुरु मानसं च ॥
rcm_3.translation: Raghupati, I tell you truly, and you are the inner self of all: there is no other longing in my heart. Give me full devotion, best of the Raghus, and make my mind free of desire and the other faults.
