rcm_3.line: There is no other longing in my heart. Give me full devotion, and a mind free of craving.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_3.our_note: Tulsidas's mangalacharan to Sundar Kand: Raghupati, there is no other desire in my heart, I speak truly and you are the inner self of all; grant me full bhakti and a mind free of kama and other faults.

rcm_3.speaker: Narrator
rcm_3.setting: Hanuman, leaping the ocean, is blocked by Surasa, who opens her jaws to swallow him.
rcm_3.sanskrit: जस जस सुरसा बदनु बढ़ावा। तासु दून कपि रूप देखावा॥ सत जोजन तेहिं आनन कीन्हा। अति लघु रूप पवनसुत लीन्हा ॥
rcm_3.translation: As Surasa widened her mouth, Hanuman showed a form twice as large. She made her mouth a hundred leagues wide; then Hanuman took a very tiny form.
rcm_3.line: As the obstacle grew, he grew twice as big. Then he made himself tiny and slipped through.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Surasa, sent by the gods to test Hanuman's strength and wit, widens her mouth; he doubles, then turns tiny, enters and leaves. She blesses him as fit for Ram's work.

prasang.title_en: Hanuman meets Surasa on the way
prasang.summary: Leaping the ocean, Hanuman refuses to rest on a friendly mountain until the work is done. Surasa blocks him and opens her jaws; he doubles his size each time she widens them, then shrinks tiny and slips in and out. A demon that catches flyers by grabbing their shadows tries the same trick, and he sees through it at once.
prasang.lesson: Meet obstacles with flexibility: sometimes bigger, sometimes smaller, never stuck.

rcm_3.speaker: Lankini
rcm_3.setting: Lankini, guardian of Lanka, struck down by Hanuman, recognises him and blesses him.
rcm_3.sanskrit: तात स्वर्ग अपबर्ग सुख धरिअ तुला एक अंग। तूल न ताहि सकल मिलि जो सुख लव सतसंग ॥
rcm_3.translation: Friend, put all the joys of heaven and liberation on one side of the scale: together they cannot match the joy of a single moment of good company.
rcm_3.line: All of heaven on one side of the scale can't outweigh one moment in good company.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Lankini, struck by Hanuman and recalling Brahma's sign, counts the touch of a saint her great merit: heaven and apavarga in one pan do not weigh a moment of satsang.

prasang.title_en: Lankini at the gate of Lanka
prasang.summary: Entering Lanka at night as small as a mosquito, Hanuman is caught by Lankini, the city's guardian. One blow of his fist floors her; she remembers a prophecy that this means the city's end, and blesses him: a moment of good company outweighs heaven, and if he carries Ram in his heart, poison will turn to nectar.
prasang.lesson: Carry what you love into the hard place, and the hard place changes.

rcm_3.speaker: Lankini
rcm_3.setting: Lanka's gatekeeper, humbled by Hanuman, sends him into the city with a blessing.
rcm_3.sanskrit: प्रबिसि नगर कीजे सब काजा। हृदयँ राखि कोसलपुर राजा॥ गरल सुधा रिपु करहिं मिताई। गोपद सिंधु अनल सितलाई ॥
rcm_3.translation: Enter the city and do all your work, holding the king of Kosala in your heart. For such a one, poison turns to nectar, enemies become friends, the ocean shrinks to a hoofprint, and fire turns cool.
rcm_3.line: Walk into the hard task carrying what you love in your heart, and even poison turns to nectar.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Lankini blesses Hanuman: enter the city and do all your work keeping Kosala's king in your heart; for him on whom Ram looks with grace, poison is nectar and foes are friends.

prasang.title_en: Lankini at the gate of Lanka
prasang.summary: Entering Lanka at night as small as a mosquito, Hanuman is caught by Lankini, the city's guardian. One blow of his fist floors her; she remembers a prophecy that this means the city's end, and blesses him: a moment of good company outweighs heaven, and if he carries Ram in his heart, poison will turn to nectar.
prasang.lesson: Carry what you love into the hard place, and the hard place changes.

rcm_3.speaker: Vibhishan
rcm_3.setting: Vibhishan, living among the wicked, wonders if Ram could care for him.
rcm_3.sanskrit: तामस तनु कछु साधन नाहीं। प्रीत न पद सरोज मन माहीं॥ अब मोहि भा भरोस हनुमंता। बिनु हरिकृपा मिलहिं नहिं संता ॥
rcm_3.translation: 'I have a demon's body and no spiritual practice, no love for his lotus feet in my mind. But now I have hope, Hanuman: without Hari's grace one does not meet the good.'
rcm_3.line: I have no practice and no love to speak of. But meeting you tells me grace has found me.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_3.our_note: Vibhishan to Hanuman: my body is tamasa, I have no sadhana nor love for his feet; yet now I have confidence, Hanuman, for without Hari's kripa saints are not met.

prasang.title_en: Hanuman finds a devotee in Lanka
prasang.summary: Searching Lanka by night, Hanuman wonders how a good person could live there, then hears someone wake saying 'Ram, Ram'. Vibhishan fears he has no practice or love worth Ram's notice; Hanuman, joking that no one wants to hear a monkey's name before breakfast, says that Ram showed kindness even to him, and weeps remembering it. The two talk of Ram late into the night and find a rest beyond words.
prasang.lesson: In a hostile place, one friend who shares your faith can be enough.

rcm_3.speaker: Hanuman
rcm_3.setting: Hanuman, after joking that no one wants to hear a monkey's name before breakfast, speaks of Ram's kindness to him.
rcm_3.sanskrit: अस मैं अधम सखा सुनु मोहू पर रघुबीर। कीन्हीं कृपा सुमिरि गुन भरे बिलोचन नीर ॥
rcm_3.translation: Listen, friend: I am that lowly, and yet on me Raghubir showed kindness. Remembering his goodness, his eyes filled with tears.
rcm_3.line: Even on someone as ordinary as me, he showed kindness. Remembering it, Hanuman wept.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_3.our_note: Hanuman consoles Vibhishan by his own case: a fickle monkey, low in every way, and yet Raghuvir showed me grace; recalling the Lord's virtues his eyes fill.

prasang.title_en: Hanuman finds a devotee in Lanka
prasang.summary: Searching Lanka by night, Hanuman wonders how a good person could live there, then hears someone wake saying 'Ram, Ram'. Vibhishan fears he has no practice or love worth Ram's notice; Hanuman, joking that no one wants to hear a monkey's name before breakfast, says that Ram showed kindness even to him, and weeps remembering it. The two talk of Ram late into the night and find a rest beyond words.
prasang.lesson: In a hostile place, one friend who shares your faith can be enough.

rcm_3.speaker: Sita
rcm_3.setting: Sita, captive in Lanka, is reached by Hanuman with Ram's ring.
rcm_3.sanskrit: हरिजन जानि प्रीति अति गाढ़ी। सजल नयन पुलकावलि बाढ़ी॥ बूड़त बिरह जलधि हनुमाना। भयहु तात मो कहुँ जलजाना ॥
rcm_3.translation: Knowing him to be the Lord's own, her love deepened; her eyes filled and she thrilled. 'Hanuman, I was drowning in a sea of separation, and you became my ship.'
rcm_3.line: I was drowning in a sea of separation, and you became my ship.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Sita, knowing Hanuman to be the Lord's servant, is overcome with love: I was sinking in the ocean of viraha and you have become my boat.

prasang.title_en: Hanuman reaches Sita
prasang.summary: Sita, captive and threatened by Ravana, has nearly lost hope; only the guard Trijata has been kind. Hanuman drops Ram's ring from a tree, then tells her Ram's whole story. Sita says he has been her ship in a sea of separation; he gives her Ram's message that speaking of pain helps, but there is no one to tell, and asks her to wait a few days more.
prasang.lesson: When someone is near despair, a message that they are remembered can carry them.

rcm_3.speaker: Hanuman
rcm_3.setting: Alone in Ravana's garden, Sita has just cried 'He has forgotten me completely'; Hanuman answers.
rcm_3.sanskrit: मातु कुसल प्रभु अनुज समेता। तव दुख दुखी सुकृपा निकेता॥ जनि जननी मानह जियँ ऊना। तुम्ह ते प्रेमु राम कें दूना ॥
rcm_3.translation: Mother, the Lord and his brother are well, but your sorrow makes him sorrowful. Don't let your heart feel small, mother: Ram's love for you is twice yours.
rcm_3.line: Don't think you've been forgotten. He hurts because you hurt, and his love for you is twice yours.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Hanuman to Sita in Ashok Vatika: the Lord and his brother are well, but he is sad in your sorrow; do not feel small at heart, mother, Ram's love is twice yours.

rcm_3.speaker: Ram (message)
rcm_3.setting: Hanuman delivers Ram's message to Sita across the sea.
rcm_3.sanskrit: सो मनु सदा रहत तोहि पाहीं। जानु प्रीति रसु एतनेहि माहीं॥ प्रभु संदेसु सुनत बैदेही। मगन प्रेम तन सुधि नहिं तेही ॥
rcm_3.translation: And that heart of mine stays with you always. Know that this is the whole of my love. Hearing her Lord's message, Sita was so lost in love she forgot herself.
rcm_3.line: My heart is always with you. That is all you need to know about my love.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Ram's message concludes: that mind of mine dwells ever with you; know the essence of my love in just this. Hearing it, Vaidehi is lost in love and forgets her body.

rcm_3.speaker: Hanuman
rcm_3.setting: Hanuman, having given Ram's message, comforts Sita.
rcm_3.sanskrit: कह कपि हृदयँ धीर धरु माता। सुमिरु राम सेवक सुखदाता॥ उर आनहु रघुपति प्रभुताई। सुनि मम बचन तजहु कदराई ॥
rcm_3.translation: Hanuman said: 'Hold steady in your heart, mother. Remember Ram, who gives joy to his servants. Bring to mind Raghupati's strength; hearing my words, put away your fear.'
rcm_3.line: Hold steady, mother. Remember Ram, and let my words take away your fear.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_3.our_note: Hanuman to Sita after giving Ram's message: hold dhira in your heart, mother, remember Ram the giver of joy to servants, bring his prabhuta to mind and give up faint-heartedness.

rcm_3.speaker: Hanuman
rcm_3.setting: Sita doubts that small monkeys can beat Ravana's army; Hanuman answers.
rcm_3.sanskrit: सुनु माता साखामृग नहिं बल बुद्धि बिसाल। प्रभु प्रताप तें गरुड़हि खाइ परम लघु ब्याल ॥
rcm_3.translation: Listen, mother: monkeys have no great strength or wisdom. But by the Lord's power even a tiny snake can swallow Garuda.
rcm_3.line: We have no great strength of our own. By the Lord's power, the small can do the impossible.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_3.our_note: Hanuman to Sita, who doubts the monkeys: we branch-animals have no great bala or buddhi, but by the Lord's pratap a very small snake may eat Garuda.

rcm_3.speaker: Hanuman
rcm_3.setting: Hanuman, a prisoner, tells Ravana himself that the door is still open.
rcm_3.sanskrit: प्रनतपाल रघुनायक करुना सिंधु खरारि। गएँ सरन प्रभु राखिहैं तव अपराध बिसारि ॥
rcm_3.translation: Raghunayak protects those who bow to him; he is an ocean of compassion. If you go to him for refuge, the Lord will protect you and forget your offence.
rcm_3.line: Even now, go to him for refuge and he will protect you and forget your offence.
rcm_3.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_3.our_note: Hanuman, bound in Ravana's court: Raghunayak is protector of the humble and an ocean of mercy; go to his sharan and the Lord will keep you, forgetting your offence. Ravana refuses.

rcm_3.speaker: Hanuman
rcm_3.setting: Hanuman, bound in Ravana's court, warns him about power that has no root.
rcm_3.sanskrit: राम बिमुख संपति प्रभुताई। जाइ रही पाई बिनु पाई॥ सजल मूल जिन्ह सरितन्ह नाहीं। बरषि गएँ पुनि तबहिं सुखाहीं ॥
rcm_3.translation: For one turned away from Ram, wealth and power slip away even while held, and having them is like not having them. Rivers with no spring at their source dry up as soon as the rains have passed.
rcm_3.line: Wealth with no deep source is a rain-fed river: gone as soon as the rains stop.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Hanuman to Ravana: the wealth and lordship of one averse to Ram go even while they stay, got and yet not got, like rivers without a watered source.

prasang.title_en: Hanuman speaks plainly to Ravana
prasang.summary: Bound and dragged before Ravana, Hanuman feels no shame and tells the most powerful man in the world, calmly, to return Sita: wealth with no deep source dries up like a rain-fed river. Ravana orders his tail set on fire; Hanuman burns Lanka and returns. Back before Ram, he insists none of it was his own greatness.
prasang.lesson: Speak truth to power calmly, and afterwards don't take the credit.

rcm_3.speaker: Sita
rcm_3.setting: Sita gives Hanuman her message for Ram before he leaves Lanka.
rcm_3.sanskrit: कहेहु तात अस मोर प्रनामा। सब प्रकार प्रभु पूरनकामा॥ दीन दयाल बिरिदु संभारी। हरहु नाथ सम संकट भारी ॥
rcm_3.translation: Give him my greeting, friend, and say: Lord, you lack nothing, but kindness to the helpless is your promise. Remember it, and take away my heavy trouble.
rcm_3.line: You are kind to those in trouble. Remember that now, and lift this heavy weight from me.
rcm_3.misuse: A prayer in crisis, not a replacement for practical help.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Sita's message through Hanuman: give my pranam and say, Lord, you are purnakama in every way; remembering your fame as deendayal, take away my great sankat.

rcm_3.speaker: Hanuman
rcm_3.setting: Ram asks how Sita keeps herself alive in captivity.
rcm_3.sanskrit: नाम पाहरू दिवस निसि ध्यान तुम्हार कपाट। लोचन निज पद जंत्रित जाहिं प्रान केहिं बाट ॥
rcm_3.translation: Your name is the watchman day and night; meditation on you is the door; her eyes are fixed on her own feet. By what way could life leave her?
rcm_3.line: Your name guards her day and night; thinking of you is the door. How could life slip away?
rcm_3.misuse: Speaks of how remembrance kept Sita going through captivity; if you are in danger or despair, reach out for help too.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_3.our_note: Asked how Sita preserves her life, Hanuman says: your name is the sentry day and night, dhyana of you the door, her eyes the lock fixed on her feet; by what path can her prana go.

rcm_3.speaker: Ram
rcm_3.setting: Hearing of Sita's suffering, Ram's eyes fill with tears.
rcm_3.sanskrit: सुनि सीता दुख प्रभु सुख अयना। भरि आए जल राजिव नयना॥ बचन कायँ मन मम गति जाही। सपनेहुँ बूझिअ बिपति कि ताही ॥
rcm_3.translation: Hearing of Sita's sorrow, the Lord, home of joy, filled his lotus eyes with tears. 'Can one whose only refuge is me, in word, body and mind, ever meet calamity, even in a dream?'
rcm_3.line: Hearing of her pain, his eyes filled: can one who takes refuge in me ever truly be lost?
rcm_3.misuse: Devotion is not a promise of a particular outcome, and it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_3.our_note: Hearing Sita's sorrow the Lord's lotus eyes fill; he asks, can one whose refuge I am in word, body and mind know vipatti even in a dream. Hanuman's reply in the next verse completes it.

rcm_3.speaker: Hanuman
rcm_3.setting: Ram has asked whether one who relies on him can meet calamity; Hanuman answers.
rcm_3.sanskrit: कह हनुमंत बिपति प्रभु सोई। जब तव सुमिरन भजन न होई॥ केतिक बात प्रभु जातुधान की। रिपुहि जीति आनिबी जानकी ॥
rcm_3.translation: Hanuman said: 'Lord, calamity is only this: when remembering and worshipping you does not happen. What is a demon to the Lord? We will defeat the enemy and bring Janaki back.'
rcm_3.line: Real calamity is only this: the moment we stop remembering you.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_3.our_note: Hanuman: Lord, vipatti is only when your smaran and bhajan are not; what is a demon to you, we will conquer the foe and bring Janaki.

rcm_3.speaker: Hanuman
rcm_3.setting: Hanuman, back from Lanka, when Ram asks how he crossed the ocean and burned the city.
rcm_3.sanskrit: सो सब तव प्रताप रघुराई। नाथ न कछू मोरि प्रभुताई ॥
rcm_3.translation: "All of it was your glory, Lord. None of it was my own greatness."
rcm_3.line: All of it was your strength, not my greatness.
rcm_3.misuse: Humility about success, not denying your own effort.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Asked how he crossed the sea and burned Lanka, Hanuman says it was all Ram's pratap and no prabhutai of his own; the tradition holds this up as the mark of the true servant.

prasang.title_en: Hanuman speaks plainly to Ravana
prasang.summary: Bound and dragged before Ravana, Hanuman feels no shame and tells the most powerful man in the world, calmly, to return Sita: wealth with no deep source dries up like a rain-fed river. Ravana orders his tail set on fire; Hanuman burns Lanka and returns. Back before Ram, he insists none of it was his own greatness.
prasang.lesson: Speak truth to power calmly, and afterwards don't take the credit.

rcm_3.speaker: Hanuman
rcm_3.setting: Ram offers Hanuman anything; Hanuman asks for one thing.
rcm_3.sanskrit: नाथ भगति अति सुखदायनी। देहु कृपा करि अनपायनी॥ सुनि प्रभु परम सरल कपि बानी। एवमस्तु तब कहेउ भवानी ॥
rcm_3.translation: 'Lord, give me by your kindness the devotion that brings great joy and never leaves.' Hearing the monkey's utterly simple words, the Lord said 'so be it', Bhavani.
rcm_3.line: Offered anything, he asked only for a love that never leaves.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_3.our_note: Hanuman to Ram, who has said he cannot repay him: Lord, grant me by your grace the anapayani bhakti that gives great joy. The Lord says evamastu.

prasang.title_en: Ram cannot repay Hanuman
prasang.summary: Back from Lanka, Hanuman tells Ram how Sita survives: his name guards her day and night. Ram, in tears, asks whether one who relies on him can meet calamity; Hanuman answers that the only calamity is forgetting him. Ram says he can never repay Hanuman and cannot even look him in the face; Hanuman falls at his feet and will not get up. Offered anything, he asks only for unwavering devotion, and credits every deed to Ram.
prasang.lesson: Do the work, give away the credit, and ask only to keep loving.

rcm_3.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_3.setting: Ravana's ministers flatter him as Ram's army arrives; the poet comments.
rcm_3.sanskrit: सचिव बैद गुर तीनि जौं प्रिय बोलहिं भय आस राज धर्म तन तीनि कर होइ बेगिहीं नास ॥
rcm_3.translation: When a minister, a doctor and a teacher speak only to please, out of fear or hope of reward, then the kingdom, the body and righteousness are soon destroyed.
rcm_3.line: When advisers, doctors and teachers only say what pleases you, the ruin comes quickly.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Tulsidas on Ravana's flattering ministers: if sachiv, vaidya and guru speak sweetly out of fear or hope, then rule, health and dharma are quickly lost.

prasang.title_en: Mandodari pleads, the ministers flatter
prasang.summary: Mandodari takes Ravana aside and begs him to return Sita before it is too late. He laughs at her fear and goes to court, where his ministers tell him only what pleases him. Tulsidas notes that when advisers, doctors and teachers speak only to please, ruin comes quickly.
prasang.lesson: Beware a circle that only tells you what you want to hear.

rcm_3.speaker: Vibhishan
rcm_3.setting: Vibhishan, Ravana's younger brother, advises him in open court.
rcm_3.sanskrit: चौदह भुवन एक पति होई। भूत द्रोह तिष्टइ नहिं सोई॥ गुन सागर नागर नर जोऊ। अलप लोभ भल कहइ न कोऊ ॥
rcm_3.translation: Even a sole master of the fourteen worlds cannot last if he makes enemies of living beings. A person may be an ocean of virtues and clever too, but if he has even a little greed, no one calls him good.
rcm_3.line: You may be gifted and clever, but even a little greed and people stop calling you good.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Vibhishan's counsel to Ravana in court: the sole lord of fourteen worlds cannot stand if he is hostile to beings; no one speaks well of a virtuous man with a little greed.

prasang.title_en: Vibhishan speaks up and is kicked
prasang.summary: Vibhishan, bowing to his brother, advises him to return Sita: good sense and bad sense live in every heart, and Ravana is feeding the wrong one. Ravana kicks him. Vibhishan still says Ravana is like a father to him, and then he leaves, telling him not to blame him.
prasang.lesson: Say the hard thing with respect; if you are struck for it, you may go.

rcm_3.speaker: Vibhishan
rcm_3.setting: Vibhishan keeps advising Ravana after the wise minister Malyavan is thrown out.
rcm_3.sanskrit: सुमति कुमति सब कें उर रहहीं। नाथ पुरान निगम अस कहहीं॥ जहाँ सुमति तहँ संपति नाना। जहाँ कुमति तहँ बिपति निदाना ॥
rcm_3.translation: Good sense and bad sense live in every heart; so say the scriptures. Where good sense is, many kinds of prosperity follow; where bad sense is, calamity is sure to come.
rcm_3.line: Good sense and bad sense live in every heart. Which you feed decides what follows.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Vibhishan to Ravana: Puranas and Vedas say sumati and kumati dwell in every heart; where sumati is there is wealth of every kind, where kumati, disaster in the end.

prasang.title_en: Vibhishan speaks up and is kicked
prasang.summary: Vibhishan, bowing to his brother, advises him to return Sita: good sense and bad sense live in every heart, and Ravana is feeding the wrong one. Ravana kicks him. Vibhishan still says Ravana is like a father to him, and then he leaves, telling him not to blame him.
prasang.lesson: Say the hard thing with respect; if you are struck for it, you may go.

rcm_3.speaker: Vibhishan
rcm_3.setting: Ravana kicks his brother Vibhishan for urging him to return Sita.
rcm_3.sanskrit: उमा संत कइ इहइ बड़ाई। मंद करत जो करइ भलाई॥ तुम्ह पितु सरिस भलेहिं मोहि मारा। रामु भजें हित नाथ तुम्हारा ॥
rcm_3.translation: (Shiva:) Uma, this is the greatness of the good: they do good even to those who harm them. (Vibhishan:) You are like a father to me; strike me if you will. But your good, brother, lies in turning to Ram.
rcm_3.line: The good still wish you well when you strike them.
rcm_3.misuse: Wishing someone well does not mean staying to be hurt; Vibhishan leaves.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Shiva remarks that the saint's greatness is doing good to one who does him ill; Vibhishan, kicked, says you are as my father, yet your good lies in worshipping Ram. He then leaves Lanka.

prasang.title_en: Vibhishan speaks up and is kicked
prasang.summary: Vibhishan, bowing to his brother, advises him to return Sita: good sense and bad sense live in every heart, and Ravana is feeding the wrong one. Ravana kicks him. Vibhishan still says Ravana is like a father to him, and then he leaves, telling him not to blame him.
prasang.lesson: Say the hard thing with respect; if you are struck for it, you may go.

rcm_3.speaker: Vibhishan
rcm_3.setting: Vibhishan, insulted and kicked, leaves his brother's court.
rcm_3.sanskrit: रामु सत्यसंकल्प प्रभु सभा कालबस तोरि। मैं रघुबीर सरन अब जाउँ देहु जनि खोरि ॥
rcm_3.translation: Ram is the Lord whose resolve is true, and your court is in the grip of doom. I go now to Raghuvir for refuge; don't blame me.
rcm_3.line: I've said what I had to say. I am leaving now; don't blame me.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Kicked by Ravana for honest counsel, Vibhishan declares that Ram's resolve is true and the court is in the grip of kala, and goes to Raghuvir's sharan. The tradition honours the leaving.

prasang.title_en: Vibhishan speaks up and is kicked
prasang.summary: Vibhishan, bowing to his brother, advises him to return Sita: good sense and bad sense live in every heart, and Ravana is feeding the wrong one. Ravana kicks him. Vibhishan still says Ravana is like a father to him, and then he leaves, telling him not to blame him.
prasang.lesson: Say the hard thing with respect; if you are struck for it, you may go.

rcm_3.speaker: Sugriva / Ram
rcm_3.setting: Sugriva suspects Vibhishan is a spy and wants him bound; Ram answers.
rcm_3.sanskrit: भेद हमार लेन सठ आवा। राखिअ बाँधि मोहि अस भावा॥ सखा नीति तुम्ह नीकि बिचारी। मम पन सरनागत भयहारी ॥
rcm_3.translation: 'The wretch has come to learn our secrets; I think we should bind him.' 'Friend, you have weighed policy well. But my vow is to take away the fear of whoever comes for refuge.'
rcm_3.line: You have reasoned well, friend. But my vow is to take away the fear of whoever comes for refuge.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_3.our_note: Sugriva wants Vibhishan bound as a spy; Ram: friend, you have judged niti well, but my pana is to remove the fear of the sharanagat.

prasang.title_en: Vibhishan crosses over: Ram's refuge speech
prasang.summary: Kicked out of Lanka for telling his brother the truth, Vibhishan crosses the sea to Ram, dreaming of his feet. Sugriva wants him bound as a spy; Ram says his vow is to remove the fear of anyone who comes for refuge, and if the visitor were truly wicked he would not have come at all. Ram embraces him, asks how he kept his goodness among the cruel, describes the devotee who ties every thread of love to him, and crowns him king, shyly giving what Ravana got for ten heads.
prasang.lesson: The turning itself is enough to be taken in; your past is not the deciding question.

rcm_3.speaker: Ram
rcm_3.setting: Ravana's brother Vibhishan has come asking for shelter; Sugriva suspects a spy, and Ram answers.
rcm_3.sanskrit: कोटि बिप्र बध लागहिं जाहू। आएँ सरन तजउँ नहिं ताहू॥ सनमुख होइ जीव मोहि जबहीं। जन्म कोटि अघ नासहिं तबहीं ॥
rcm_3.translation: Even someone who carries the sin of killing countless brahmins, if he comes to me for shelter, I will not turn away. The moment a soul turns to face me, the wrongs of countless lives are wiped away.
rcm_3.line: I never turn away anyone who comes to me. The moment you turn toward me, your past is washed away.
rcm_3.misuse: Not a licence to keep doing harm; the turning has to be real.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Ram to Sugriva on receiving Vibhishan: even one guilty of slaying a crore of brahmins I do not abandon if he comes for sharan; when the jiva turns toward me the sins of a crore births perish.

rcm_3.speaker: Ram
rcm_3.setting: Ram explains why he trusts the one who turns up at his door.
rcm_3.sanskrit: पापवंत कर सहज सुभाऊ। भजनु मोर तेहि भाव न काऊ॥ जौं पै दुष्ट हृदय सोइ होई। मोरें सनमुख आव कि सोई ॥
rcm_3.translation: It is the natural way of a sinner never to like worshipping me. If he were truly wicked at heart, would he come before me at all?
rcm_3.line: If they were truly wicked, would they have turned toward me at all?
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_3.our_note: Ram: it is the sinner's nature never to like my bhajan; if he were wicked of heart, would he come before me.

prasang.title_en: Vibhishan crosses over: Ram's refuge speech
prasang.summary: Kicked out of Lanka for telling his brother the truth, Vibhishan crosses the sea to Ram, dreaming of his feet. Sugriva wants him bound as a spy; Ram says his vow is to remove the fear of anyone who comes for refuge, and if the visitor were truly wicked he would not have come at all. Ram embraces him, asks how he kept his goodness among the cruel, describes the devotee who ties every thread of love to him, and crowns him king, shyly giving what Ravana got for ten heads.
prasang.lesson: The turning itself is enough to be taken in; your past is not the deciding question.

rcm_3.speaker: Ram
rcm_3.setting: Ram, when Sugriva suspects Vibhishan is a spy and urges him to be turned away.
rcm_3.sanskrit: निर्मल मन जन सो मोहि पावा। मोहि कपट छल छिद्र न भावा॥ भेद लेन पठवा दससीसा। तबहुँ न कछु भय हानि कपीसा ॥
rcm_3.translation: "A person with a clean mind reaches me; I have no liking for deceit, tricks or fault-finding. Even if Ravana sent him to learn our secrets, there is no fear or loss in it for us, Sugriva."
rcm_3.line: Deceit and tricks win nothing lasting. People with a clean mind are the ones who are trusted.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Ram overrules Sugriva's suspicion of Vibhishan: the man of pure mind attains me, I do not like kapat and chhal; even if Ravana sent him to spy, there is no fear or harm.

prasang.title_en: Vibhishan crosses over
prasang.summary: Vibhishan crosses the sea to Ram. Sugriva suspects a spy; Ram says he never turns away anyone who comes for refuge, and that only a clean heart, without deceit, reaches him. He embraces Vibhishan, asks how he kept his goodness among the wicked, and crowns him king of Lanka before the war has even begun.
prasang.lesson: Leaving a bad place takes courage; a good leader receives people without suspicion first.

rcm_3.speaker: Ram
rcm_3.setting: Sugriva fears Vibhishan is a spy; Ram says it makes no difference.
rcm_3.sanskrit: जग महुँ सखा निसाचर जेते। लछिमनु हनइ निमिष महुँ तेते॥ जौं सभीत आवा सरनाईं। रखिहउँ ताहि प्रान की नाईं ॥
rcm_3.translation: Friend, Lakshman could destroy every demon in the world in a moment. And if he has come to me in fear, seeking shelter, I will keep him as dear as my own life.
rcm_3.line: If someone comes to me afraid, looking for shelter, I will keep them as dear as my own life.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Ram: Lakshman can slay all the world's demons in a moment, so there is nothing to fear; and if he has come frightened for refuge, I will guard him like my own life.

rcm_3.speaker: Vibhishan
rcm_3.setting: Vibhishan, standing before Ram, names who he is and asks for shelter.
rcm_3.sanskrit: श्रवन सुजसु सुनि आयउँ प्रभु भंजन भव भीर। त्राहि त्राहि आरति हरन सरन सुखद रघुबीर ॥
rcm_3.translation: Hearing your good name with my own ears I have come, Lord, breaker of the fear of the world. Save me, save me, remover of distress, Raghubir, whose refuge brings joy.
rcm_3.line: I heard of you and came. Save me, you who take away distress.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_3.our_note: Vibhishan before Ram: hearing your fair fame I have come, Lord who breaks the fear of rebirth; save me, save me, remover of distress, Raghuvir, giver of joy to the surrendered.

prasang.title_en: Vibhishan crosses over: Ram's refuge speech
prasang.summary: Kicked out of Lanka for telling his brother the truth, Vibhishan crosses the sea to Ram, dreaming of his feet. Sugriva wants him bound as a spy; Ram says his vow is to remove the fear of anyone who comes for refuge, and if the visitor were truly wicked he would not have come at all. Ram embraces him, asks how he kept his goodness among the cruel, describes the devotee who ties every thread of love to him, and crowns him king, shyly giving what Ravana got for ten heads.
prasang.lesson: The turning itself is enough to be taken in; your past is not the deciding question.

rcm_3.speaker: Vibhishan
rcm_3.setting: Vibhishan, newly arrived at Ram's camp, on his years in Ravana's palace.
rcm_3.sanskrit: बरु भल बास नरक कर ताता। दुष्ट संग जनि देइ बिधाता॥ अब पद देखि कुसल रघुराया। जौं तुम्ह कीन्हि जानि जन दाया ॥
rcm_3.translation: "Better to live in hell, friend, than to be given the company of the wicked. Now that I have seen your feet, Lord, I am well, since you have shown me kindness, knowing me as your own."
rcm_3.line: Better to live in hell than to be stuck in the company of the cruel.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Vibhishan to Ram: better to dwell in hell, may the Creator never give the company of the wicked; now, having seen your feet, I am well, since you have shown mercy knowing me your own.

prasang.title_en: Vibhishan crosses over
prasang.summary: Vibhishan crosses the sea to Ram. Sugriva suspects a spy; Ram says he never turns away anyone who comes for refuge, and that only a clean heart, without deceit, reaches him. He embraces Vibhishan, asks how he kept his goodness among the wicked, and crowns him king of Lanka before the war has even begun.
prasang.lesson: Leaving a bad place takes courage; a good leader receives people without suspicion first.

rcm_3.speaker: Vibhishan
rcm_3.setting: Vibhishan, newly welcomed by Ram, can hardly believe it.
rcm_3.sanskrit: मैं निसिचर अति अधम सुभाऊ। सुभ आचरनु कीन्ह नहिं काऊ॥ जासु रूप मुनि ध्यान न आवा। तेहिं प्रभु हरषि हृदयँ मोहि लावा ॥
rcm_3.translation: I am a demon, low by nature; I have never done a single good deed. And yet the Lord whose form sages cannot reach even in meditation has gladly held me to his heart.
rcm_3.line: I had never done anything good, and still he was glad to hold me to his heart.
rcm_3.misuse: Vibhishan's self-judgement is harsh; the point is the welcome, not the self-contempt.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Vibhishan: I am a nishachara of very low nature who never did a good act, yet the Lord whose form does not come even into sages' meditation gladly embraced me.

rcm_3.speaker: Ram
rcm_3.setting: Ram tells Vibhishan his own nature.
rcm_3.sanskrit: सुनहु सखा निज कहउँ सुभाऊ। जान भुसुंडि संभु गिरिजाऊ॥ जौं नर होइ चराचर द्रोही। आवै सभय सरन तकि मोही ॥ तजि मद मोह कपट छल नाना। करउँ सद्य तेहि साधु समाना॥ जननी जनक बंधु सुत दारा। तनु धनु भवन सुहृद परिवारा ॥
rcm_3.translation: Listen, friend, I tell you my own nature, as Bhushundi, Shambhu and Girija know it. If a person who has harmed every living thing comes to me afraid, looking for shelter, and gives up pride, delusion, deceit and trickery, I make him like a saint at once. Mother, father, brother, son, wife, body, wealth, home, friends and family:
rcm_3.line: Even one who has harmed everyone, if they come afraid and drop their pride, I make good at once.
rcm_3.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_3.our_note: Ram tells his own nature: if a man hostile to all creation comes frightened to my shelter, leaving mada, moha, kapat and chhal, I make him like a sadhu at once.

prasang.title_en: Vibhishan crosses over: Ram's refuge speech
prasang.summary: Kicked out of Lanka for telling his brother the truth, Vibhishan crosses the sea to Ram, dreaming of his feet. Sugriva wants him bound as a spy; Ram says his vow is to remove the fear of anyone who comes for refuge, and if the visitor were truly wicked he would not have come at all. Ram embraces him, asks how he kept his goodness among the cruel, describes the devotee who ties every thread of love to him, and crowns him king, shyly giving what Ravana got for ten heads.
prasang.lesson: The turning itself is enough to be taken in; your past is not the deciding question.

rcm_3.speaker: Ram
rcm_3.setting: Ram describes the devotee who lives in his heart.
rcm_3.sanskrit: सब कै ममता ताग बटोरी। मम पद मनहि बाँध बरि डोरी॥ समदरसी इच्छा कछु नाहीं। हरष सोक भय नहिं मन माहीं ॥ अस सज्जन मम उर बस कैसें। लोभी हृदयँ बसइ धनु जैसें॥ तुम्ह सारिखे संत प्रिय मोरें। धरउँ देह नहिं आन निहोरें ॥
rcm_3.translation: Gathering the threads of attachment to all of these, he twists them into one cord and ties his mind to my feet. Even-minded, wanting nothing, with no elation, grief or fear in his mind: such a good person lives in my heart as wealth lives in a miser's heart. Saints like you are dear to me; I take a body for no other reason.
rcm_3.line: Gather every thread of love into one cord, and tie your heart to me.
rcm_3.misuse: Not 'give up your family': it is gathering one's loves into a single devotion. Surrender here comes after effort and honest reflection; it is not a reason to stop acting or to stay in harm's way.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_3.our_note: Ram: he who collects the threads of mamata for mother, father, kin, wealth and home, twists them into a cord and ties his mind to my feet, dwells in my heart as wealth in a miser's.

prasang.title_en: Vibhishan crosses over: Ram's refuge speech
prasang.summary: Kicked out of Lanka for telling his brother the truth, Vibhishan crosses the sea to Ram, dreaming of his feet. Sugriva wants him bound as a spy; Ram says his vow is to remove the fear of anyone who comes for refuge, and if the visitor were truly wicked he would not have come at all. Ram embraces him, asks how he kept his goodness among the cruel, describes the devotee who ties every thread of love to him, and crowns him king, shyly giving what Ravana got for ten heads.
prasang.lesson: The turning itself is enough to be taken in; your past is not the deciding question.

rcm_3.speaker: Vibhishan
rcm_3.setting: Vibhishan admits why he first came.
rcm_3.sanskrit: सुनहु देव सचराचर स्वामी। प्रनतपाल उर अंतरजामी॥ उर कछु प्रथम बासना रही। प्रभु पद प्रीति सरित सो बही ॥
rcm_3.translation: Listen, Lord of all that moves and does not move, protector of those who bow, knower of hearts: there was some desire in my heart at first; it has been carried away in the river of love for your feet.
rcm_3.line: I came with my own wants. They were carried away in the river of love.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_3.our_note: Vibhishan: Lord, knower of hearts, there was at first some vasana in my heart; it has flowed away in the river of love for your feet. Ram crowns him all the same.

prasang.title_en: Vibhishan crosses over: Ram's refuge speech
prasang.summary: Kicked out of Lanka for telling his brother the truth, Vibhishan crosses the sea to Ram, dreaming of his feet. Sugriva wants him bound as a spy; Ram says his vow is to remove the fear of anyone who comes for refuge, and if the visitor were truly wicked he would not have come at all. Ram embraces him, asks how he kept his goodness among the cruel, describes the devotee who ties every thread of love to him, and crowns him king, shyly giving what Ravana got for ten heads.
prasang.lesson: The turning itself is enough to be taken in; your past is not the deciding question.

rcm_3.speaker: Vibhishan
rcm_3.setting: At the shore, Ram asks how to cross the ocean, and Vibhishan advises.
rcm_3.sanskrit: कह लंकेस सुनहु रघुनायक। कोटि सिंधु सोषक तव सायक॥ जद्यपि तदपि नीति असि गाई। बिनय करिअ सागर सन जाई ॥
rcm_3.translation: Raghunath, though a single arrow of yours could dry up countless oceans, good policy says: first go and ask the ocean politely.
rcm_3.line: Even when you have the power to force it, ask politely first.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Vibhishan advises Ram to petition the ocean though one arrow could dry it. Whole arc: three days of humble asking, then the bow. Humility first, but not without limit.

prasang.title_en: Three days at the ocean: humble first, firm after
prasang.summary: On Vibhishan's advice, Ram first asks the ocean politely to let his army cross, and waits three days. When nothing changes, he takes up his bow, observing that counsel to the unwilling is like seed on barren soil. The ocean appears, apologises, and shows him how to build a bridge.
prasang.lesson: Always ask humbly first. But don't let humility be taken for weakness.

rcm_3.ref_label: Ramcharitmanas, Sundar Kand (data 5.55 doha; Gita Press 5.57)
rcm_3.speaker: Tulsidas (narrating Ram)
rcm_3.setting: Ram has sat on the shore three days, humbly asking the ocean for a way. The ocean stays silent.
rcm_3.sanskrit: बिनय न मानत जलधि जड़ गए तीनि दिन बीति। बोले राम सकोप तब भय बिनु होइ न प्रीति ॥
rcm_3.translation: Three days passed and the stubborn ocean ignored his humble request. Then Ram spoke in anger: without some fear, there is no regard.
rcm_3.line: Three days of humble asking, ignored. Some people only listen once they see you'll act.
rcm_3.misuse: About a stubborn party who ignores repeated humble requests, not a rule for love or for people close to you. Patience comes first; Ram waited three days and forgave the ocean the moment it came.
rcm_3.verified_with: data tr.hi / tr.en_src
rcm_3.our_note: The ocean, jad, does not heed vinaya for three days; Ram then shows anger as niti requires. The ocean appears, begs pardon, and Ram spares it and takes its counsel.

prasang.title_en: Three days at the ocean: humble first, firm after
prasang.summary: On Vibhishan's advice, Ram first asks the ocean politely to let his army cross, and waits three days. When nothing changes, he takes up his bow, observing that counsel to the unwilling is like seed on barren soil. The ocean appears, apologises, and shows him how to build a bridge.
prasang.lesson: Always ask humbly first. But don't let humility be taken for weakness.

rcm_3.speaker: Ram
rcm_3.setting: After three days of humble requests the ocean still won't let the army cross; Ram finally turns firm.
rcm_3.sanskrit: लछिमन बान सरासन आनू। सोषौं बारिधि बिसिख कृसानु॥ सठ सन बिनय कुटिल सन प्रीति। सहज कृपन सन सुंदर नीति ॥ ममता रत सन ग्यान कहानी। अति लोभी सन बिरति बखानी॥ क्रोधिहि सम कामिहि हरिकथा। ऊसर बीज बएँ फल जथा ॥
rcm_3.translation: "Lakshman, bring my bow and arrows; I will dry up the ocean with fiery shafts. Pleading with the stubborn, friendship with the crooked, fine principles to a born miser, talk of wisdom to someone lost in possessiveness, praise of renunciation to the very greedy, calm to the angry, and holy stories to the lustful: all are like sowing seed in barren soil."
rcm_3.line: Calm advice to an angry person, or detachment to a greedy one, is seed sown in barren soil.
rcm_3.misuse: Firmness after real patience, not permission to bully. The doha 'bhay binu hoi na priti' is deliberately not used.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: After three days of vinaya the ocean does not yield and Ram calls for his bow, listing mismatched efforts as seed on barren land. The ocean then comes in submission and Ram spares it.

prasang.title_en: Three days at the ocean: humble first, firm after
prasang.summary: On Vibhishan's advice, Ram first asks the ocean politely to let his army cross, and waits three days. When nothing changes, he takes up his bow, observing that counsel to the unwilling is like seed on barren soil. The ocean appears, apologises, and shows him how to build a bridge.
prasang.lesson: Always ask humbly first. But don't let humility be taken for weakness.

rcm_3.speaker: Mandodari
rcm_3.setting: Ravana's wife Mandodari pleads with him to give up the war.
rcm_3.sanskrit: नाथ बयरु कीजे ताही सों। बुधि बल सकिअ जीति जाही सों॥ तुम्हहि रघुपतिहि अंतर कैसा। खलु खद्योत दिनकरहि जैसा ॥
rcm_3.translation: "My lord, pick a quarrel only with someone you can defeat with your wits and strength. Between you and Ram there is the difference between a firefly and the sun."
rcm_3.line: Pick your fights only where your wits and strength can actually win.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Mandodari pleads with Ravana: make enemies of one you can defeat by buddhi and bala; between you and Raghupati the gap is that of a glow-worm and the sun.

prasang.title_en: Mandodari and Prahasta warn Ravana again
prasang.summary: Mandodari, hearing the bridge is built, again begs Ravana to pick fights only where he can win, and to step back. Ravana boasts. His son Prahasta tells the court that flatterers are many and honest advisers few, and suggests first sending an envoy. Ravana insults him, and Prahasta leaves saying good advice cannot reach one set on ruin.
prasang.lesson: Some people cannot hear good advice; give it, then stop beating yourself up.

rcm_3.speaker: Prahasta
rcm_3.setting: Prahasta, Ravana's son, leaves after his father rejects his advice and insults him.
rcm_3.sanskrit: हित मत तोहि न लागत कैसें। काल बिबस कहुँ भेषज जैसें॥ संध्या समय जानि दससीसा। भवन चलेउ निरखत भुज बीसा ॥
rcm_3.translation: How is it that sound advice doesn't take with you? Like medicine on one in death's grip. Seeing it was evening, Ravana went to his palace, admiring his twenty arms.
rcm_3.line: Good advice won't take on someone set on ruin, like medicine on the dying.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Prahasta, insulted by Ravana for honest counsel, says good advice suits him as medicine suits one under kala's sway, and leaves. Ravana goes off admiring his arms.

prasang.title_en: Mandodari and Prahasta warn Ravana again
prasang.summary: Mandodari, hearing the bridge is built, again begs Ravana to pick fights only where he can win, and to step back. Ravana boasts. His son Prahasta tells the court that flatterers are many and honest advisers few, and suggests first sending an envoy. Ravana insults him, and Prahasta leaves saying good advice cannot reach one set on ruin.
prasang.lesson: Some people cannot hear good advice; give it, then stop beating yourself up.

rcm_3.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_3.setting: Angad walks alone into Ravana's hostile court as Ram's envoy.
rcm_3.sanskrit: गयउ सभा दरबार तब सुमिरि राम पद कंज। सिंह ठवनि इत उत चितव धीर बीर बल पुंज ॥
rcm_3.translation: Then he went into the court, remembering Ram's lotus feet, looking this way and that with a lion's gait, steady, brave, a mass of strength.
rcm_3.line: He walked into the hostile room remembering Ram, steady as a lion.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_3.our_note: Angad goes into Ravana's sabha remembering Ram's lotus feet, glancing here and there with a lion's stance, dhira, vira and a mass of strength.

rcm_3.speaker: Angad (thinking)
rcm_3.setting: Ram sends Angad to Ravana; Angad sees the honour for what it is.
rcm_3.sanskrit: स्वयंसिद्ध सब काज नाथ मोहि आदरु दियउ। अस बिचारि जुबराज तन पुलकित हरषित हियउ ॥
rcm_3.translation: 'Every task is already accomplished by itself; the Lord has only given me the honour.' Thinking this, the prince's body thrilled and his heart was glad.
rcm_3.line: The work is already done; I've only been given the honour of carrying it.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_3.our_note: Angad reflects: all the Lord's works are svayamsiddha, he has only given me honour; thinking so the prince's body thrills and his heart rejoices.

rcm_3.speaker: Narrator
rcm_3.setting: Angad plants his foot in Ravana's court and dares anyone to move it; no one can.
rcm_3.sanskrit: भूमि न छाँड़त कपि चरन देखत रिपु मद भाग। कोटि बिघ्न ते संत कर मन जिमि नीति न त्याग ॥
rcm_3.translation: The monkey's foot would not leave the ground, and seeing it, the enemy's pride drained away; just as a good person's mind does not abandon what is right, though a million obstacles come.
rcm_3.line: A good mind doesn't leave what is right, though a million obstacles come.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Angad's planted foot cannot be moved by Ravana's warriors and the enemy's pride drains away; Tulsidas likens it to the saint's mind that never forsakes niti.

prasang.title_en: Angad in Ravana's court
prasang.summary: Ram sends Angad as envoy, asking him to speak so the work gets done and it does Ravana good too. In court Ravana insults Angad, his dead father and his lord. Angad bears it, remembering that a lion gains no glory by killing a jackal. At last he plants his foot and dares anyone to move it; no warrior can.
prasang.lesson: Under insult, keep your purpose; a steady mind does not leave what is right.

rcm_3.speaker: Ram
rcm_3.setting: Ram at midnight, holding Lakshman struck down in battle, waiting for Hanuman and the herb.
rcm_3.sanskrit: सकहु न दुखित देखि मोहि काउ। बंधु सदा तव मृदुल सुभाऊ॥ मम हित लागि तजेहु पितु माता। सहेहु बिपिन हिम आतप बाता ॥
rcm_3.translation: Brother, you could never bear to see me sad; your nature was always gentle. For my sake you left mother and father and bore the forest's cold, heat and wind.
rcm_3.line: You could never bear to see me sad. For me you left home and bore every hardship.
rcm_3.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_3.our_note: Ram's lament over Lakshman struck by the shakti, in the manner of a man: you could never see me sad; for me you left father and mother and bore cold, heat and wind.

prasang.title_en: Lakshman falls; Hanuman brings the mountain
prasang.summary: Lakshman is struck down by Meghnad's spear. The physician Sushena names a herb on a far mountain, and Hanuman races there, sees through a demon disguised as a sage, and, not recognising the herb, carries the whole peak. Over Ayodhya Bharat shoots him down by mistake, then revives him and helps him on. At midnight Ram holds Lakshman and grieves aloud for a brother who left everything for him; Hanuman arrives just in time.
prasang.lesson: When someone you love is ill, urgency and hope go together.

rcm_4.speaker: Kumbhakarna
rcm_4.setting: Kumbhakarna, going out to fight for Ravana though he knows him wrong, meets Vibhishan, who has joined Ram.
rcm_4.sanskrit: सुनु भयउ कालबस रावन। सो कि मान अब परम सिखावन॥ धन्य धन्य तैं धन्य विभीषन। भयहु तात निसिचर कुल भूषन ॥
rcm_4.translation: Listen, son: Ravana is in the grip of doom; would he heed good counsel now? Blessed, blessed, blessed are you, Vibhishan; you have become the ornament of our clan.
rcm_4.line: Blessed, blessed are you, brother. You have become the pride of our family.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Kumbhakarna to Vibhishan on the battlefield: Ravana is in death's power and will not heed counsel; thrice blessed are you, who have become the jewel of the nishachara line.

prasang.title_en: Kumbhakarna fights for a brother he knows is wrong
prasang.summary: Woken to fight, Kumbhakarna tells Ravana plainly he was wrong to take Sita and should have consulted him first. Still he goes out to fight for his brother. On the field he meets Vibhishan, who chose Ram, and instead of cursing him, he blesses him as the pride of their family.
prasang.lesson: Siblings can choose differently and still bless each other.

rcm_4.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_4.setting: Ravana, on the eve of battle, lectures his wives on wisdom; the poet remarks.
rcm_4.sanskrit: तिन्हहि ग्यान उपदेसा रावन। आपुन मंद कथा सुभ पावन॥ पर उपदेस कुसल बहुतेरे। जे आचरहिं ते नर न घनेरे ॥
rcm_4.translation: Ravana gave them sermons on knowledge: he himself was wicked, but his talk was pure and fine. Many are skilled at advising others; those who practise it themselves are not many.
rcm_4.line: Many are skilled at advising others. Few live by the advice themselves.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Ravana preaches jnana to his grieving queens while himself in the wrong; Tulsidas remarks that experts in advising others are many, practitioners few.

rcm_4.speaker: Ram
rcm_4.setting: After the war Vibhishan begs Ram to rest in Lanka; Ram wants to hurry home.
rcm_4.sanskrit: तोर कोस गृह मोर सब सत्य बचन सुनु भ्रात। भरत दसा सुमिरत मोहि निमिष कल्प सम जात ॥
rcm_4.translation: Listen, brother: your treasury and home are truly mine. But remembering Bharat's state, each moment feels like an age to me.
rcm_4.line: All you offer is mine too. But thinking of my brother back home, each moment feels like an age.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Ram declines Vibhishan's hospitality after the war: your treasury and house are mine, but remembering Bharat's condition each nimisha passes like a kalpa.

prasang.title_en: Ram hurries home
prasang.summary: After the war, Vibhishan begs Ram to stay a while, bathe and rest in Lanka's palaces. Ram says all of it is his as much as Vibhishan's, but thinking of Bharat waiting at home, each moment feels like an age; if he is late, he may not find his brother alive.
prasang.lesson: When someone at home is waiting, no comfort elsewhere can hold you.

rcm_4.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_4.setting: Vibhishan showers jewels from the sky; the monkeys put them in their mouths; Ram laughs.
rcm_4.sanskrit: मुनि जेहि ध्यान न पावहिं नेति नेति कह बेद। कृपासिंधु सोइ कपिन्ह सन करत अनेक बिनोद ॥
rcm_4.translation: The one whom sages cannot reach in meditation, whom the Vedas call 'not this, not this': that ocean of kindness is joking and playing with monkeys.
rcm_4.line: The one sages cannot reach in meditation is laughing and joking with the monkeys.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_4.our_note: Tulsidas: he whom munis do not attain in dhyana and the Veda describes as neti neti, that ocean of grace makes many jests with the monkeys.

rcm_4.speaker: Shiva
rcm_4.setting: Shiva comments on Ram's play with the monkeys.
rcm_4.sanskrit: उमा जोग जप दान तप नाना मख ब्रत नेम। राम कृपा नहिं करहिं तसि जसि निष्केवल प्रेम ॥
rcm_4.translation: Uma, yoga, chanting, charity, austerity, sacrifices, vows and rules: none of these win Ram's kindness the way pure love alone does.
rcm_4.line: No practice wins his kindness the way plain love does.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_4.our_note: Shiva to Uma: yoga, japa, dana, tapa, the many yajnas, vratas and niyamas do not draw Ram's kripa as nishkeval prema does.

rcm_4.speaker: Ram
rcm_4.setting: The war is over; before flying home, Ram sends his monkey and bear friends back to their homes.
rcm_4.sanskrit: निज निज गृह अब तुम्ह सब जाहू। सुमिरेहु मोहि डरपहु जनि काहू॥ सुनत बचन प्रेमाकुल बानर। जोरि पानि बोले सब सादर ॥
rcm_4.translation: Now go home, each of you. Remember me, and don't be afraid of anyone. Hearing this, the monkeys, overcome with love, joined their hands and spoke respectfully.
rcm_4.line: Go home now. Remember me, and don't be afraid of anyone.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: After the war Ram tells the monkeys and bears: go now each to his home, remember me and fear no one. They are overcome with love.

rcm_4.speaker: Narrator
rcm_4.setting: Bharat, with one day left of Ram's fourteen years, still has no word.
rcm_4.sanskrit: रहेउ एक दिन अवधि अधारा। समुझत मन दुख भयउ अपारा॥ कारन कवन नाथ नहिं आयउ। जानि कुटिल किधौं मोहि बिसरायउ ॥
rcm_4.translation: Only one day of the appointed time, the support of his life, was left. Thinking of it, Bharat's grief was boundless. 'Why hasn't my Lord come? Has he forgotten me, knowing me to be crooked?'
rcm_4.line: One day left, and still no word. Has he forgotten me?
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: One day of the avadhi remains, the prop of Bharat's life; boundless grief rises: why has the Lord not come, has he forgotten me, knowing me false.

prasang.title_en: The last day of waiting
prasang.summary: One day is left of the fourteen years and there is no word. Bharat wonders whether Ram has forgotten him, and his mind starts to sink. Just then Hanuman arrives like a boat and says Ram is coming. Bharat says no gift could repay this news.
prasang.lesson: Waiting is hardest on the last day; hope can arrive just as you go under.

rcm_4.speaker: Narrator
rcm_4.setting: Just as Bharat sinks into despair, Hanuman arrives with news.
rcm_4.sanskrit: राम बिरह सागर महँ भरत मगन मन होत। बिप्र रूप धरि पवनसुत आइ गयउ जनु पोत॥1क॥
rcm_4.translation: Bharat's mind was sinking in the ocean of separation from Ram when the son of the wind arrived in a Brahmin's guise, as if a boat had come.
rcm_4.line: Just as he was going under, help arrived like a boat.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Bharat's mind is sinking in the ocean of Ram viraha when Hanuman, in a brahmin's form, arrives like a ship. Narrative of an event, not a promise that rescue always comes.

prasang.title_en: The last day of waiting
prasang.summary: One day is left of the fourteen years and there is no word. Bharat wonders whether Ram has forgotten him, and his mind starts to sink. Just then Hanuman arrives like a boat and says Ram is coming. Bharat says no gift could repay this news.
prasang.lesson: Waiting is hardest on the last day; hope can arrive just as you go under.

rcm_4.speaker: Bharat
rcm_4.setting: Bharat, hearing from Hanuman that Ram is on his way home.
rcm_4.sanskrit: कपि तव दरस सकल दुख बीते। मिले आजुमोहि राम पिरीते॥ बार बार बूझी कुसलाता। तो कहुँ देउँ काह सुन भ्राता ॥ एहि संदेस सरिस जग माहीं। करि बिचार देखेउँ कछु नाहीं॥ नाहिन तात उरिन मैं तोही। अब प्रभु चरित सुनावहु मोही ॥
rcm_4.translation: Seeing you, all my sorrows are over; today I have met my beloved Ram himself. He asked again and again after everyone's welfare. 'Brother, what can I give you? Nothing in the world equals this news; I have thought it over. I can never repay you. Now tell me about my Lord.'
rcm_4.line: Nothing in the world equals this news. I can never repay you.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Bharat to Hanuman: at the sight of you all my sorrows are gone; I have searched and find nothing in the world equal to this message; I can never be free of this debt.

prasang.title_en: The last day of waiting
prasang.summary: One day is left of the fourteen years and there is no word. Bharat wonders whether Ram has forgotten him, and his mind starts to sink. Just then Hanuman arrives like a boat and says Ram is coming. Bharat says no gift could repay this news.
prasang.lesson: Waiting is hardest on the last day; hope can arrive just as you go under.

rcm_4.speaker: Bharat
rcm_4.setting: After fourteen years, Hanuman brings Bharat the news that Ram is coming; Bharat has one question.
rcm_4.sanskrit: तब हनुमंत नाइ पद माथा। कहे सकल रघुपति गुन गाथा॥ कहु कपि कबहुँ कृपाल गोसाईं। सुमिरहिं मोहि दास की नाईं ॥
rcm_4.translation: Then Hanuman bowed at his feet and told all of Raghupati's virtues. 'Tell me, Hanuman: does the kind master ever remember me, as one remembers a servant?'
rcm_4.line: Tell me: does he ever think of me?
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_4.our_note: Bharat to Hanuman: tell me, does the gracious master ever remember me as his servant. Hanuman's answer is that Bharat is dear to Ram as life.

rcm_4.speaker: Ram
rcm_4.setting: Ram, flying home in the Pushpak, points out Ayodhya to his friends.
rcm_4.sanskrit: जद्यपि सब बैकुंठ बखाना। बेद पुरान बिदित जगु जाना॥ अवधपुरी सम प्रिय नहिं सोऊ। यह प्रसंग जानइ कोउ कोऊ ॥ जन्मभूमि मम पुरी सुहावनि। उत्तर दिसि बह सरजू पावनि॥ जा मज्जन ते बिनहिं प्रयासा। मम समीप नर पावहिं बासा ॥
rcm_4.translation: Though everyone praises Vaikuntha, as the Vedas and Puranas say and the world knows, even that is not as dear to me as Avadhpuri; few know this secret. This lovely city is my birthplace; to its north flows the holy Sarayu, by bathing in which people come to dwell near me without effort.
rcm_4.line: Heaven may be praised by all. It isn't as dear to me as the town where I was born.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: From the Pushpak Ram shows the vanaras Ayodhya: all praise Vaikuntha, yet it is not as dear to me as Avadhpuri, my janmabhumi, north of which flows the Sarayu.

prasang.title_en: Ram comes home
prasang.summary: From the air Ram points out his birthplace, dearer to him than heaven. Bharat falls at his feet; Ram lifts him up and the mothers run to him like cows to their calves at dusk. Ram introduces his friends as those who carried him through the war, and seeing Kaikeyi ashamed, goes to her house first.
prasang.lesson: Homecoming means gratitude to those who carried you and kindness to those ashamed to face you.

rcm_4.speaker: Narrator
rcm_4.setting: Bharat, who blamed himself for fourteen years for his mother's scheme, falls at Ram's feet.
rcm_4.sanskrit: परे भूमि नहिं उठत उठाए। बर करि कृपासिंधु उर लाए॥ स्यामल गात रोम भए ठाढ़े। नव राजीव नयन जल बाढ़े ॥
rcm_4.translation: Bharat lay on the ground and would not get up when they tried to lift him. The ocean of kindness lifted him by force and held him to his heart. Ram's dark body thrilled, and tears flooded his lotus eyes.
rcm_4.line: He lay on the ground and would not rise. So Ram lifted him up and held him to his heart.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Bharat, fallen on the earth, does not rise though raised; the ocean of grace lifts him by force to his breast, his dark body thrilling and his lotus eyes overflowing.

rcm_4.speaker: Bharat
rcm_4.setting: After fourteen years apart, Ram embraces Bharat and asks how he is; Bharat can barely speak.
rcm_4.sanskrit: बूझत कृपानिधि कुसल भरतहि बचन बेगि न आवई॥ सुनु सिवा सो सुख बचन मन ते भिन्न जान जो पावई॥ अब कुसल कौसलनाथ आरत जानि जन दरसन दियो। बूड़त बिरह बारीस कृपानिधान मोहि कर गहि लियो ॥
rcm_4.translation: When the Lord asked Bharat how he was, no words would come. Shiva says: Parvati, that joy is beyond words and thought; only one who has felt it knows. Bharat said: Now I am well, Lord of Kosala. You saw how I suffered and showed yourself to me. I was drowning in the sea of separation, and you took me by the hand.
rcm_4.line: I was drowning in missing you, and you took me by the hand.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Asked his welfare, Bharat cannot speak; then: now I am well, lord of Kosala, you gave darshan knowing your servant distressed and caught my hand as I sank in the ocean of viraha.

rcm_4.speaker: Narrator
rcm_4.setting: Ram returns to Ayodhya after fourteen years; his mothers run to meet him.
rcm_4.sanskrit: जनु धेनु बालक बच्छ तजि गृहँ चरन बन परबस गईं। दिन अंत पुर रुख स्रवत थन हुंकार करि धावत भईं॥ अति प्रेम प्रभु सब मातु भेटीं बचन मृदु बहुबिधि कहे। गइ बिषम बिपति बियोगभव तिन्ह हरष सुख अगनित लहे॥
rcm_4.translation: Like cows that had to leave their young calves at home to graze in the forest, and at day's end run lowing toward the village, milk flowing, so the mothers ran. With great love the Lord met each of them and spoke many gentle words. The hard pain of separation left them, and they found countless joys.
rcm_4.line: Like cows running home at dusk to their calves, the mothers ran to hold their sons again.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: On Ram's return the mothers rush like cows that left young calves at home and run lowing at day's end; he meets each with love, and the calamity born of separation departs.

rcm_4.speaker: Ram
rcm_4.setting: Ram introduces his monkey and bear companions to his teacher on returning home.
rcm_4.sanskrit: ए सब सखा सुनहु मुनि मेरे। भए समर सागर कहँ बेरे॥ मम हित लागि जन्म इन्ह हारे। भरतहु ते मोहि अधिक पिआरे ॥
rcm_4.translation: Listen, sage: these are all my friends. They were my boats across the ocean of battle. For my sake they staked their lives; they are dearer to me than even Bharat.
rcm_4.line: These friends carried me across the battle. For me they staked their lives.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Ram presents the vanaras to Vasishtha: these friends were my ships across the sea of battle, they staked their lives for me, they are dearer to me than Bharat.

prasang.title_en: Ram comes home
prasang.summary: From the air Ram points out his birthplace, dearer to him than heaven. Bharat falls at his feet; Ram lifts him up and the mothers run to him like cows to their calves at dusk. Ram introduces his friends as those who carried him through the war, and seeing Kaikeyi ashamed, goes to her house first.
prasang.lesson: Homecoming means gratitude to those who carried you and kindness to those ashamed to face you.

rcm_4.speaker: Shiva
rcm_4.setting: Back in Ayodhya, Ram notices that Kaikeyi is ashamed to face him.
rcm_4.sanskrit: प्रभु जानी कैकई लजानी। प्रथम तासु गृह गए भवानी॥ ताहि प्रबोधि बहुत सुख दीन्हा। पुनि निज भवन गवन हरि कीन्हा ॥
rcm_4.translation: The Lord saw that Kaikeyi was ashamed, so he went first to her house, Bhavani, comforted her and gave her great ease. Then he went to his own palace.
rcm_4.line: Seeing her shame, he went to her house first and put her at ease.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Shiva tells Parvati: the Lord knew Kaikeyi was ashamed, so he went first to her palace, consoled her and gave her joy, and only then to his own.

prasang.title_en: Ram comes home
prasang.summary: From the air Ram points out his birthplace, dearer to him than heaven. Bharat falls at his feet; Ram lifts him up and the mothers run to him like cows to their calves at dusk. Ram introduces his friends as those who carried him through the war, and seeing Kaikeyi ashamed, goes to her house first.
prasang.lesson: Homecoming means gratitude to those who carried you and kindness to those ashamed to face you.

rcm_4.speaker: Angad
rcm_4.setting: Angad, whose father Bali died, pleads not to be sent home after the war.
rcm_4.sanskrit: असरन सरन बिरदु संभारी। मोहि जनि तजहु भगत हितकारी॥ मोरें तुम्ह प्रभु गुर पितु माता। जाउँ कहाँ तजि पद जलजाता ॥
rcm_4.translation: Remember your vow to shelter the shelterless and don't abandon me, friend of devotees. You are my lord, teacher, father and mother; leaving your feet, where would I go?
rcm_4.line: You are my teacher, my father and mother now. Where would I go?
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Angad, whose father Bali is dead, at the farewell: remembering your vow as refuge of the refugeless, do not abandon me; where shall I go leaving your lotus feet.

prasang.title_en: Ram says goodbye to his friends
prasang.summary: After six happy months, Ram sends his monkey and bear friends home with gifts. Angad, whose father is dead, begs to stay: Ram is his father and mother now. Ram embraces him and sends him on. To the boatman Guha he says: you are a brother to me; keep visiting.
prasang.lesson: Friendships made in hard times deserve to be kept; say so out loud.

rcm_4.speaker: Ram
rcm_4.setting: Ram bids farewell to Guha, the boatmen's chief who helped him into exile.
rcm_4.sanskrit: तुम्ह मम सखा भरत सम भ्राता। सदा रहेहु पुर आवत जाता॥ बचन सुनत उपजा सुख भारी। परेउ चरन भरि लोचन बारी ॥
rcm_4.translation: You are my friend and a brother like Bharat. Keep coming and going to Ayodhya always. Hearing this, he felt great joy and fell at Ram's feet, eyes full of tears.
rcm_4.line: You are my friend, a brother to me. Keep visiting, always.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Ram to Nishad Guha at parting: you are my friend, a brother like Bharat; keep coming to the city always. Guha falls at his feet with tears of joy.

prasang.title_en: Ram says goodbye to his friends
prasang.summary: After six happy months, Ram sends his monkey and bear friends home with gifts. Angad, whose father is dead, begs to stay: Ram is his father and mother now. Ram embraces him and sends him on. To the boatman Guha he says: you are a brother to me; keep visiting.
prasang.lesson: Friendships made in hard times deserve to be kept; say so out loud.

rcm_4.speaker: Ram
rcm_4.setting: Bharat asks Ram to explain the difference between good and bad people.
rcm_4.sanskrit: संत असंतन्हि कै असि करनी। जिमि कुठार चंदन आचरनी॥ काटइ परसु मलय सुनु भाई। निज गुन देइ सुगंध बसाई ॥
rcm_4.translation: The way good and bad people treat each other is like sandalwood and the axe: listen, brother, the axe cuts the sandalwood tree, yet the sandalwood, by its own nature, leaves its fragrance on the axe.
rcm_4.line: The axe cuts the sandalwood, and the sandalwood still leaves its fragrance on the axe.
rcm_4.misuse: Staying kind is not the same as staying within reach of the axe.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Ram on sant and asant: the axe cuts the Malaya tree, which still perfumes it. The next doha completes it: sandal is raised to the gods' heads, the axe is heated and hammered.

prasang.title_en: Ram on good people and difficult people
prasang.summary: Bharat asks Ram to explain the difference between good and malicious people. Ram says the good are like sandalwood that perfumes the axe that cuts it; they feel others' sorrow and joy as their own and never speak harshly. The malicious burn at others' success and feast on gossip. No duty equals doing good to others.
prasang.lesson: Do good, feel others' joy as your own, and refuse the pleasure of gossip.

rcm_4.speaker: Ram
rcm_4.setting: Ram, answering Bharat, describes the marks of a good person.
rcm_4.sanskrit: बिषय अलंपट सील गुनाकर। पर दुख दुख सुख सुख देखे पर॥ सम अभूतरिपु बिमद बिरागी। लोभामरष हरष भय त्यागी ॥
rcm_4.translation: They are not greedy for pleasures; they are mines of good conduct and virtue; others' sorrow makes them sad and others' joy makes them glad. They are even-minded, see no one as an enemy, are free of pride and detached, and have let go of greed, rage, elation and fear.
rcm_4.line: A good person is saddened by others' sorrow and gladdened by others' joy.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Ram to Bharat on the marks of saints: free of craving for sense objects, mines of sheel, sorrowing in others' sorrow and glad in their gladness, even and enemy-less.

prasang.title_en: Ram on good people and difficult people
prasang.summary: Bharat asks Ram to explain the difference between good and malicious people. Ram says the good are like sandalwood that perfumes the axe that cuts it; they feel others' sorrow and joy as their own and never speak harshly. The malicious burn at others' success and feast on gossip. No duty equals doing good to others.
prasang.lesson: Do good, feel others' joy as your own, and refuse the pleasure of gossip.

rcm_4.speaker: Ram
rcm_4.setting: Ram to Bharat, finishing his list of the marks of a good person.
rcm_4.sanskrit: ए सब लच्छन बसहिं जासु उर। जानेहु तात संत संतत फुर॥ सम दम नियम नीति नहिं डोलहिं। परुष बचन कबहूँ नहिं बोलहिं ॥ निंदा अस्तुति उभय सम ममता मम पद कंज। ते सज्जन मम प्रानप्रिय गुन मंदिर सुख पुंज ॥
rcm_4.translation: Know that whoever carries all these qualities in their heart is truly good. They never waver from self-control, discipline and right conduct, and never speak a harsh word. Praise and blame are the same to them, and their love is for my feet: such good people, homes of virtue and joy, are dear to me as life.
rcm_4.line: Never speak a harsh word. Let praise and blame land on you the same way.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Ram concludes the marks of the saint: firm in shama, dama, niyama and niti, never harsh in speech, alike to ninda and stuti, devoted to my feet; such are dear to me as life.

prasang.title_en: Ram on good people and difficult people
prasang.summary: Bharat asks Ram to explain the difference between good and malicious people. Ram says the good are like sandalwood that perfumes the axe that cuts it; they feel others' sorrow and joy as their own and never speak harshly. The malicious burn at others' success and feast on gossip. No duty equals doing good to others.
prasang.lesson: Do good, feel others' joy as your own, and refuse the pleasure of gossip.

rcm_4.speaker: Ram
rcm_4.setting: Ram to Bharat on the nature of the malicious.
rcm_4.sanskrit: खलन्ह हृदयँ अति ताप बिसेषी। जरहिं सदा पर संपति देखी॥ जहँ कहुँ निंदा सुनहिं पराई। हरषहिं मनहुँ परी निधि पाई ॥
rcm_4.translation: The hearts of the wicked burn with a special heat: they are always on fire at the sight of someone else's prosperity. Wherever they hear someone being run down, they are delighted, as if they had stumbled on treasure.
rcm_4.line: Envy burns at another's success and feasts on gossip as if it found treasure.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Ram on the asant: their hearts have a special heat, they burn seeing others' wealth, and where they hear another slandered they rejoice as if they had found treasure on the road.

prasang.title_en: Ram on good people and difficult people
prasang.summary: Bharat asks Ram to explain the difference between good and malicious people. Ram says the good are like sandalwood that perfumes the axe that cuts it; they feel others' sorrow and joy as their own and never speak harshly. The malicious burn at others' success and feast on gossip. No duty equals doing good to others.
prasang.lesson: Do good, feel others' joy as your own, and refuse the pleasure of gossip.

rcm_4.speaker: Ram
rcm_4.setting: Ram sums up his teaching to his brothers in Ayodhya.
rcm_4.sanskrit: पर हित सरिस धर्म नहिं भाई। पर पीड़ा सम नहिं अधमाई॥ निर्नय सकल पुरान बेद कर। कहेउँ तात जानहिं कोबिद नर ॥
rcm_4.translation: There is no duty equal to doing good to others, brother, and no baseness equal to causing others pain. This is the verdict of all the scriptures; the wise know it.
rcm_4.line: No duty equals doing good to others, and nothing is lower than causing others pain.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Ram to his brothers: there is no dharma like par hit and no vileness like par peeda; this is the settled conclusion of all Puranas and Vedas.

prasang.title_en: Ram on good people and difficult people
prasang.summary: Bharat asks Ram to explain the difference between good and malicious people. Ram says the good are like sandalwood that perfumes the axe that cuts it; they feel others' sorrow and joy as their own and never speak harshly. The malicious burn at others' success and feast on gossip. No duty equals doing good to others.
prasang.lesson: Do good, feel others' joy as your own, and refuse the pleasure of gossip.

rcm_4.speaker: Ram
rcm_4.setting: King Ram calls the whole city together and tells them how to treat what he says.
rcm_4.sanskrit: सोइ सेवक प्रियतम मम सोई। मम अनुसासन मानै जोई॥ जौं अनीति कछु भाषौं भाई। तौ मोहि बरजहु भय बिसराई ॥
rcm_4.translation: "The one who follows my teaching is truly my dear servant. But if I say anything unjust, brothers, put aside your fear and stop me."
rcm_4.line: If I say anything wrong, stop me. Don't be afraid.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Ram to the assembled citizens: he who follows my instruction is my dearest servant; yet if I say anything contrary to niti, brothers, forget fear and restrain me.

prasang.title_en: Ram's address to the citizens
prasang.summary: Ram calls his people together and says he speaks without pride of rank: if he says anything wrong, stop him without fear. The way he recommends needs no grand effort, only a simple nature, an honest mind, contentment, and no grudges, no quarrels, no craving and no fear.
prasang.lesson: A good leader invites correction; a good life is simple, honest and free of grudges.

rcm_4.speaker: Ram
rcm_4.setting: Ram, now king, speaks to the people about the human life they have.
rcm_4.sanskrit: फिरत सदा माया कर प्रेरा। काल कर्म सुभाव गुन घेरा॥ कबहुँक करि करुना नर देही। देत ईस बिनु हेतु सनेही ॥ नर तनु भव बारिधि कहुँ बेरो। सन्मुख मरुत अनुग्रह मेरो॥ करनधार सदगुर दृढ़ नावा। दुर्लभ साज सुलभ करि पावा ॥
rcm_4.translation: Driven always by illusion, surrounded by time, karma, nature and the qualities, the soul wanders; then sometimes, out of compassion, God, a friend without a reason, gives it a human body. The human body is a boat for the ocean of becoming, my grace is the favourable wind, a true teacher is the steady helmsman: you have been given, easily, what is hard to get.
rcm_4.line: This life is the boat, my grace the wind behind it, a good teacher at the helm.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_4.our_note: Ram to the citizens: the jiva wanders driven by maya; God, the causeless friend, sometimes gives a human body, a boat for bhavasagar with my grace as fair wind and the sadguru as helmsman.

rcm_4.speaker: Ram
rcm_4.setting: Ram to the citizens, on how simple the path really is.
rcm_4.sanskrit: कहहु भगति पथ कवन प्रयासा। जोग न मख जप तप उपवासा। सरल सुभाव न मन कुटिलाई। जथा लाभ संतोष सदाई ॥
rcm_4.translation: "Tell me, what effort does this path take? No yoga, no sacrifices, no chanting, austerities or fasts. Only a simple nature, a mind without crookedness, and contentment with whatever comes."
rcm_4.line: No grand effort needed: a simple nature, an honest mind, and contentment with what comes.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Ram to the citizens: what labour is there in the path of bhakti; it needs neither yoga nor yajna, japa, tapa or fasting, only a straight nature and constant contentment.

prasang.title_en: Ram's address to the citizens
prasang.summary: Ram calls his people together and says he speaks without pride of rank: if he says anything wrong, stop him without fear. The way he recommends needs no grand effort, only a simple nature, an honest mind, contentment, and no grudges, no quarrels, no craving and no fear.
prasang.lesson: A good leader invites correction; a good life is simple, honest and free of grudges.

rcm_4.speaker: Ram
rcm_4.setting: Ram describes the simple devotee he is won over by.
rcm_4.sanskrit: मोर दास कहाइ नर आसा। करइ तौ कहहु कहा बिस्वासा॥ बहुत कहउँ का कथा बढ़ाई। एहि आचरन बस्य मैं भाई ॥
rcm_4.translation: If someone calls himself my servant and still hangs his hopes on others, tell me, what sort of trust is that? Why say more and lengthen the story: it is by this conduct that I am won, brothers.
rcm_4.line: If you call yourself mine and still hang every hope on others, what kind of trust is that?
