rcm_4.misuse: Not 'never accept help from people'; it is about where the heart's final reliance rests. Surrender here comes after effort and honest reflection; it is not a reason to stop acting or to stay in harm's way.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_4.our_note: Ram to the citizens: if one called my servant hopes in men, tell me, what faith is that. By this conduct I am won.

rcm_4.speaker: Ram
rcm_4.setting: Ram to the citizens, describing the person at peace.
rcm_4.sanskrit: बैर न बिग्रह आस न त्रासा। सुखमय ताहि सदा सब आसा॥ अनारंभ अनिकेत अमानी। अनघ अरोष दच्छ बिग्यानी ॥
rcm_4.translation: "Holding no grudge and picking no quarrel, with neither craving nor fear, every direction is joyful to him. He starts nothing out of craving for results, clings to no house, wants no honour, is free of wrongdoing and anger, skilled and wise."
rcm_4.line: No grudges, no quarrels, no craving, no fear: for such a person every direction is joy.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Ram describes the devotee dear to him: without vair or vigraha, hope or fear, for whom all quarters are full of joy; undertaking nothing for self, homeless in attachment, prideless, sinless, angerless.

prasang.title_en: Ram's address to the citizens
prasang.summary: Ram calls his people together and says he speaks without pride of rank: if he says anything wrong, stop him without fear. The way he recommends needs no grand effort, only a simple nature, an honest mind, contentment, and no grudges, no quarrels, no craving and no fear.
prasang.lesson: A good leader invites correction; a good life is simple, honest and free of grudges.

rcm_4.speaker: Shiva
rcm_4.setting: Shiva, met on the road by the doubt-ridden Garuda, sends him to good company instead of answering.
rcm_4.sanskrit: मिलेहु गरुड़ मारग महँ मोही। कवन भाँति समुझावौं तोही॥ तबहिं होइ सब संसय भंगा। जब बहु काल करिअ सतसंगा ॥
rcm_4.translation: You met me on the road; how can I explain it to you in passing? All doubts end only when one spends a long time in good company.
rcm_4.line: Doubts don't end in a passing conversation. They clear with long time in good company.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Shiva to the doubting Garuda: you met me on the road, how shall I instruct you; doubts break only when one keeps satsang a long while. He sends him to Kakbhushundi.

prasang.title_en: Garuda's doubt
prasang.summary: Garuda, Vishnu's own mount, frees Ram from a serpent-noose in battle and starts to doubt: how can God be bound? He goes to Narada, Brahma and Shiva, who sends him to an old crow, Kakbhushundi, saying doubts clear only with long time in good company. Kakbhushundi tells him no one has escaped delusion, desire, craving or anger; Garuda ends up grateful for the doubt that led him there.
prasang.lesson: Doubt is human; stay long enough in good company and it can lead somewhere better.

rcm_4.speaker: Garuda
rcm_4.setting: Garuda, his doubt resolved, thanks Kakbhushundi.
rcm_4.sanskrit: जो अति आतप ब्याकुल होई। तरु छाया सुख जानइ सोई॥ जौं नहिं होत मोह अति मोही। मिलतेउँ तात कवन बिधि तोही ॥
rcm_4.translation: Only one scorched by the sun knows the comfort of a tree's shade. Friend, had I not been so deeply confused, how would I ever have met you?
rcm_4.line: Only the one scorched by the sun knows the shade. Without my doubt, I'd never have found you.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Garuda to Kakbhushundi after his doubt is cured: only he who is tormented by heat knows the joy of shade; had I not fallen into deep moha, how would I have met you.

prasang.title_en: Garuda's doubt
prasang.summary: Garuda, Vishnu's own mount, frees Ram from a serpent-noose in battle and starts to doubt: how can God be bound? He goes to Narada, Brahma and Shiva, who sends him to an old crow, Kakbhushundi, saying doubts clear only with long time in good company. Kakbhushundi tells him no one has escaped delusion, desire, craving or anger; Garuda ends up grateful for the doubt that led him there.
prasang.lesson: Doubt is human; stay long enough in good company and it can lead somewhere better.

rcm_4.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm_4.setting: Kakbhushundi tells the ashamed Garuda that his confusion is nothing unusual.
rcm_4.sanskrit: मोह न अंध कीन्ह केहि केही। को जग काम नचाव नजेही॥ तृस्नाँ केहि न कीन्ह बौराहा। केहि कर हृदय क्रोध नहिं दाहा ॥
rcm_4.translation: Whom has delusion not blinded? Who in the world has desire not made to dance? Whom has craving not maddened? Whose heart has anger not burned?
rcm_4.line: Who hasn't been blinded, made to dance by desire, maddened by craving, burned by anger?
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Kakbhushundi consoles the ashamed Garuda: whom has moha not blinded, whom has kama not made dance, whom has trishna not maddened, whose heart has krodha not burned.

prasang.title_en: Garuda's doubt
prasang.summary: Garuda, Vishnu's own mount, frees Ram from a serpent-noose in battle and starts to doubt: how can God be bound? He goes to Narada, Brahma and Shiva, who sends him to an old crow, Kakbhushundi, saying doubts clear only with long time in good company. Kakbhushundi tells him no one has escaped delusion, desire, craving or anger; Garuda ends up grateful for the doubt that led him there.
prasang.lesson: Doubt is human; stay long enough in good company and it can lead somewhere better.

rcm_4.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm_4.setting: The crow-sage Kakbhushundi consoles Garuda, ashamed of his own confusion: no one is immune.
rcm_4.sanskrit: मच्छर काहि कलंक न लावा। काहि न सोक समीर डोलावा॥ चिंता साँपिनि को नहिं खाया। को जग जाहि न ब्यापी माया ॥
rcm_4.translation: Whom has envy not stained? Whom has the wind of grief not shaken? Whom has the snake of worry not bitten? Who in the world has not been caught by illusion?
rcm_4.line: Whom has the snake of worry not bitten? You are not the only one.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Continuing: whom has matsar not stained, whom has the wind of shoka not shaken, whom has the she-serpent chinta not bitten, whom has maya not pervaded.

prasang.title_en: Garuda's doubt
prasang.summary: Garuda, Vishnu's own mount, frees Ram from a serpent-noose in battle and starts to doubt: how can God be bound? He goes to Narada, Brahma and Shiva, who sends him to an old crow, Kakbhushundi, saying doubts clear only with long time in good company. Kakbhushundi tells him no one has escaped delusion, desire, craving or anger; Garuda ends up grateful for the doubt that led him there.
prasang.lesson: Doubt is human; stay long enough in good company and it can lead somewhere better.

rcm_4.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm_4.setting: Kakbhushundi, explaining to Garuda how people misjudge what they see.
rcm_4.sanskrit: नयन दोष जा कहँ जब होई। पीत बरन ससि कहुँ कह सोई॥ जब जेहि दिसि भ्रम होई खगेसा। सो कह पच्छिम उयउ दिनेसा ॥ नौकारूढ़ चलत जग देखा। अचल मोह बस आपुहि लेखा॥ बालक भ्रमहिं न भ्रमहिं गृहादी। कहहिं परस्पर मिथ्याबादी ॥
rcm_4.translation: When someone's eyes are diseased, he calls the moon yellow; when someone loses his bearings, he says the sun rose in the west. A man on a moving boat sees the world moving and, deluded, thinks himself still. Children spin round, not the houses, yet they call each other liars.
rcm_4.line: Diseased eyes see a yellow moon. From a moving boat, the shore seems to move.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Kakbhushundi: those who attribute delusion to Ram are themselves deluded, like the jaundiced eye that calls the moon yellow or the boat passenger who sees the world moving.

prasang.title_en: Garuda's doubt
prasang.summary: Garuda, Vishnu's own mount, frees Ram from a serpent-noose in battle and starts to doubt: how can God be bound? He goes to Narada, Brahma and Shiva, who sends him to an old crow, Kakbhushundi, saying doubts clear only with long time in good company. Kakbhushundi tells him no one has escaped delusion, desire, craving or anger; Garuda ends up grateful for the doubt that led him there.
prasang.lesson: Doubt is human; stay long enough in good company and it can lead somewhere better.

rcm_4.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm_4.setting: Kakbhushundi, beginning his own story, on why pride is taken from us.
rcm_4.sanskrit: नहु राम कर सहज सुभाऊ। जन अभिमान न राखहिं काऊ॥ संसृत मूल सूलप्रद नाना। सकल सोक दायक अभिमाना ॥
rcm_4.translation: Hear Ram's natural way: he never lets pride stay in his devotee, for pride is the root of the cycle of birth and death, the giver of many pains and of every sorrow.
rcm_4.line: Pride is the root of countless pains and every sorrow.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Kakbhushundi: it is Ram's nature never to leave abhiman in his servant, for abhiman is the root of samsara, giving many pains and all grief.

prasang.title_en: Kakbhushundi and the child Ram
prasang.summary: Kakbhushundi used to visit Ayodhya to watch Ram as a child. Once he doubted that a toddler chasing a crow could be God; Ram reached for him across every world, and he saw universes inside the child's mouth. Humbled, he was offered every power and chose devotion, since comforts without it are a feast without salt. Ram explains that pride is lanced from those he loves, as a mother lances a child's boil.
prasang.lesson: Pride is taken from us painfully, for our good; what remains is what matters.

rcm_4.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm_4.setting: Kakbhushundi, on why being humbled can be a kindness.
rcm_4.sanskrit: ताते करहिं कृपानिधि दूरी। सेवक पर ममता अति भूरी॥ जिमि सिसु तन ब्रन होई गोसाईं। मातु चिराव कठिन की नाईं ॥ जदपि प्रथम दुख पावइ रोवइ बाल अधीर। ब्याधि नास हित जननी गनति न सो सिसु पीर॥ 74 क॥
rcm_4.translation: So the merciful one removes it, for he loves his servant deeply. When a boil forms on a child's body, the mother has it lanced as if she were hard-hearted. Though the child suffers at first and cries out, the mother, to cure the illness, pays no heed to that pain.
rcm_4.line: A mother has the boil lanced though the child cries. Some humbling is like that.
rcm_4.misuse: Not every pain is for your good; don't use this to excuse harm done to anyone.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Kakbhushundi: pride is the root of samsara's pains, so the merciful Lord removes it from his servant, as a mother has the boil cut though the child weeps.

prasang.title_en: Kakbhushundi and the child Ram
prasang.summary: Kakbhushundi used to visit Ayodhya to watch Ram as a child. Once he doubted that a toddler chasing a crow could be God; Ram reached for him across every world, and he saw universes inside the child's mouth. Humbled, he was offered every power and chose devotion, since comforts without it are a feast without salt. Ram explains that pride is lanced from those he loves, as a mother lances a child's boil.
prasang.lesson: Pride is taken from us painfully, for our good; what remains is what matters.

rcm_4.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm_4.setting: Offered every power and pleasure by the child Ram, young Kakbhushundi thinks before choosing.
rcm_4.sanskrit: भगति हीन गुन सब सुख ऐसे। लवन बिना बहु बिंजन जैसे॥ भजन हीन सुख कवने काजा। अस बिचारि बोलेउँ खगराजा ॥
rcm_4.translation: Without devotion, all virtues and pleasures are like many dishes without salt. What use is happiness without devotion? Thinking so, I spoke.
rcm_4.line: Every comfort without devotion is like a feast without salt.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Kakbhushundi, offered siddhis, jnana and moksha by the child Ram, reflects that all virtues and joys without bhakti are like dishes without salt, and asks for bhakti alone.

prasang.title_en: Kakbhushundi and the child Ram
prasang.summary: Kakbhushundi used to visit Ayodhya to watch Ram as a child. Once he doubted that a toddler chasing a crow could be God; Ram reached for him across every world, and he saw universes inside the child's mouth. Humbled, he was offered every power and chose devotion, since comforts without it are a feast without salt. Ram explains that pride is lanced from those he loves, as a mother lances a child's boil.
prasang.lesson: Pride is taken from us painfully, for our good; what remains is what matters.

rcm_4.speaker: Ram
rcm_4.setting: Ram continues: what makes someone dear to him is not status.
rcm_4.sanskrit: भगति हीन बिरंचि किन होई। सब जीवहु सम प्रिय मोहि सोई॥ भगतिवंत अति नीचउ प्रानी। मोहि प्रानप्रिय असि मम बानी ॥
rcm_4.translation: Even Brahma, without devotion, is dear to me only as any being is. A devoted creature, however lowly, is dear to me as life: this is my word.
rcm_4.line: Without love, even the creator is just another being. With love, the lowliest is dear as life.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_4.our_note: Ram to Kakbhushundi: be he Brahma, one without bhakti is dear to me like all beings; a creature with bhakti, though very low, is dear to me as life. This is my word.

prasang.title_en: The child Ram and the crow
prasang.summary: The crow-sage Kakbhushundi, after being humbled by the child Ram's play, receives his boon. Ram tells him devotees are always dear to him, that status counts for nothing without love, and gives the parable of a father with many gifted sons whose dearest son is the one who simply loves him, though skilled at nothing. Then the Lord goes back to being a hungry baby and cries until his mother runs to him.
prasang.lesson: You are loved for loving, not for being impressive.

rcm_4.speaker: Ram
rcm_4.setting: Ram explains to Kakbhushundi how he loves all beings, using a father's love as the picture.
rcm_4.sanskrit: एक पिता के बिपुल कुमारा। होहिं पृथक गुन सील अचारा॥ कोउ पंडित कोउ तापस ग्याता। कोउ धनवंत सूर कोउ दाता ॥ कोउ सर्बग्य धर्मरत कोई। सब पर पितहि प्रीति सम होई॥ कोउ पितु भगत बचन मन कर्मा। सपनेहुँ जान न दूसर धर्मा ॥
rcm_4.translation: One father has many sons, each different in gifts, nature and conduct: one a scholar, one an ascetic, one wise, one rich, one brave, one generous; one all-knowing, one devoted to duty. The father's love is the same for all; but if one is devoted to the father in mind, word and deed, knowing no other duty even in dreams...
rcm_4.line: One parent, many children, each different in gifts and nature, and the love for all is the same.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Ram to Kakbhushundi: a father's love is equal for all his sons, but the son devoted to him alone is dear as life; so all beings are mine, and the devotee is dearest.

prasang.title_en: Kakbhushundi and the child Ram
prasang.summary: Kakbhushundi used to visit Ayodhya to watch Ram as a child. Once he doubted that a toddler chasing a crow could be God; Ram reached for him across every world, and he saw universes inside the child's mouth. Humbled, he was offered every power and chose devotion, since comforts without it are a feast without salt. Ram explains that pride is lanced from those he loves, as a mother lances a child's boil.
prasang.lesson: Pride is taken from us painfully, for our good; what remains is what matters.

rcm_4.speaker: Ram
rcm_4.setting: Ram's parable of a father with many sons.
rcm_4.sanskrit: कोउ सर्बग्य धर्मरत कोई। सब पर पितहि प्रीति सम होई॥ कोउ पितु भगत बचन मन कर्मा। सपनेहुँ जान न दूसर धर्मा ॥ सो सुत प्रिय पितु प्रान समाना। जद्यपि सो सब भाँति अयाना॥ एहि बिधि जीव चराचर जेते। त्रिजग देव नर असुर समेते ॥
rcm_4.translation: One is all-knowing, one devoted to duty; the father loves them all equally. But one son is devoted to his father in word, mind and deed, and in his dreams knows no other duty: that son is dear to his father as life, though he is unskilled in every way. In this same way are all beings, moving and unmoving, gods, humans and demons.
rcm_4.line: The child who simply loves the father is dear to him as life, though skilled at nothing.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_4.our_note: Ram's parable completed: the son devoted to the father in word, mind and deed, who knows no other dharma, is dear as life though ignorant in every way; so with all beings.

prasang.title_en: The child Ram and the crow
prasang.summary: The crow-sage Kakbhushundi, after being humbled by the child Ram's play, receives his boon. Ram tells him devotees are always dear to him, that status counts for nothing without love, and gives the parable of a father with many gifted sons whose dearest son is the one who simply loves him, though skilled at nothing. Then the Lord goes back to being a hungry baby and cries until his mother runs to him.
prasang.lesson: You are loved for loving, not for being impressive.

rcm_4.speaker: Ram
rcm_4.setting: Ram ends his teaching to Kakbhushundi.
rcm_4.sanskrit: पुरुष नपुंसक नारि वा जीव चराचर कोइ। सर्ब भाव भज कपट तजि मोहि परम प्रिय सोइ ॥
rcm_4.translation: Man, woman or of any gender, any being that moves or does not move: whoever worships me with all their heart, giving up deceit, is supremely dear to me.
rcm_4.line: Man, woman, any gender, any being: whoever loves me without deceit is supremely dear to me.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_4.our_note: Ram: purusha, napunsaka or nari, any moving or unmoving being who worships me with all his being, leaving guile, is most dear to me.

prasang.title_en: The child Ram and the crow
prasang.summary: The crow-sage Kakbhushundi, after being humbled by the child Ram's play, receives his boon. Ram tells him devotees are always dear to him, that status counts for nothing without love, and gives the parable of a father with many gifted sons whose dearest son is the one who simply loves him, though skilled at nothing. Then the Lord goes back to being a hungry baby and cries until his mother runs to him.
prasang.lesson: You are loved for loving, not for being impressive.

rcm_4.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm_4.setting: Having taught the crow, the child Ram goes back to being a baby and cries for his mother.
rcm_4.sanskrit: देखि मातु आतुर उठि धाई। कहि मृदु बचन लिए उर लाई॥ गोद राखि कराव पय पाना। रघुपति चरित ललित कर गाना ॥
rcm_4.translation: Seeing him, the mother rose anxiously and ran, spoke softly to him and held him to her heart. She kept him in her lap and fed him, singing of Raghupati's lovely deeds.
rcm_4.line: The Lord of all cried for his mother, and she ran and held him close.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_4.our_note: Kakbhushundi: seeing the child cry, the mother rose in haste and ran, spoke softly and clasped him to her breast, kept him in her lap and gave him milk, singing Raghupati's deeds.

prasang.title_en: The child Ram and the crow
prasang.summary: The crow-sage Kakbhushundi, after being humbled by the child Ram's play, receives his boon. Ram tells him devotees are always dear to him, that status counts for nothing without love, and gives the parable of a father with many gifted sons whose dearest son is the one who simply loves him, though skilled at nothing. Then the Lord goes back to being a hungry baby and cries until his mother runs to him.
prasang.lesson: You are loved for loving, not for being impressive.

rcm_4.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm_4.setting: Kakbhushundi, summing up what he learned, on how love grows.
rcm_4.sanskrit: जानें बिनु न होइ परतीती। बिनु परतीति होइ नहिं प्रीती॥ प्रीति बिना नहिं भगति दिढ़ाई। जिमि खगपति जल कै चिकनाई ॥
rcm_4.translation: Without knowing his greatness, no trust forms; without trust, no love; and without love, devotion is not firm, just as, king of birds, oil does not stay on water.
rcm_4.line: Without knowing, there is no trust. Without trust, there is no love.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Kakbhushundi: without knowing the Lord's greatness there is no pratiti, without pratiti no priti, and without priti bhakti is not firm, like oiliness on water.

prasang.title_en: Kakbhushundi and the child Ram
prasang.summary: Kakbhushundi used to visit Ayodhya to watch Ram as a child. Once he doubted that a toddler chasing a crow could be God; Ram reached for him across every world, and he saw universes inside the child's mouth. Humbled, he was offered every power and chose devotion, since comforts without it are a feast without salt. Ram explains that pride is lanced from those he loves, as a mother lances a child's boil.
prasang.lesson: Pride is taken from us painfully, for our good; what remains is what matters.

rcm_4.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm_4.setting: Kakbhushundi to Garuda on what actually brings rest.
rcm_4.sanskrit: कोउ बिश्राम कि पाव तात सहज संतोष बिनु। चलै कि जल बिनु नाव कोटि जतन पचि पचि मरिअ ॥
rcm_4.translation: Can anyone find rest without natural contentment, friend? Can a boat move without water, though you strain and wear yourself out with a million efforts?
rcm_4.line: No one finds rest without contentment, any more than a boat moves without water.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Kakbhushundi: can anyone find vishram without sahaj santosh; can a boat move without water though one die straining with a crore of efforts.

prasang.title_en: Kakbhushundi and the child Ram
prasang.summary: Kakbhushundi used to visit Ayodhya to watch Ram as a child. Once he doubted that a toddler chasing a crow could be God; Ram reached for him across every world, and he saw universes inside the child's mouth. Humbled, he was offered every power and chose devotion, since comforts without it are a feast without salt. Ram explains that pride is lanced from those he loves, as a mother lances a child's boil.
prasang.lesson: Pride is taken from us painfully, for our good; what remains is what matters.

rcm_4.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm_4.setting: Kakbhushundi, describing a degraded age, on what teachers and parents pass on.
rcm_4.sanskrit: हरइ सिष्य धन सोक न हरई। सो गुर घोर नरक महुँ परई॥ मातु पिता बालकन्हि बोलावहिं। उदर भरै सोइ धर्म सिखावहिं ॥
rcm_4.translation: The teacher who takes his disciple's money but not his sorrow falls into a terrible hell. Parents call their children and teach them only the dharma that fills the belly.
rcm_4.line: Parents call their children and teach them only what fills the stomach.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: From the description of Kali Yuga: the guru who robs the disciple's wealth and not his sorrow falls into hell; mothers and fathers teach children the dharma of filling the stomach.

rcm_4.speaker: Kakbhushundi's teacher
rcm_4.setting: The gentle teacher whose proud student refused even to rise for him pleads with Shiva to lift the student's curse.
rcm_4.sanskrit: तव माया बस जीव जड़ संतत फिरइ भुलान। तेहि पर क्रोध न करिअ प्रभु कृपासिंधु भगवान ॥
rcm_4.translation: This ignorant soul, in the grip of your maya, wanders constantly astray. Ocean of mercy, Lord, do not be angry with him.
rcm_4.line: He is confused and lost. Don't be angry with him.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: The guru whom Kakbhushundi slighted begs Shiva to lift the curse: the jiva, deluded by your maya, ever strays; do not be angry with him, ocean of mercy.

prasang.title_en: The student who would not stand for his teacher
prasang.summary: In an earlier life Kakbhushundi was a proud, wealthy, sharp-tongued young man whose gentle teacher kept trying to guide him. One day in the temple he refused even to rise when the teacher entered. The teacher said nothing, but a curse fell on the student; the teacher at once prayed for him, asking that he not be punished in anger. Lives later, the one thorn Kakbhushundi still carries is the memory of that teacher's gentleness.
prasang.lesson: Respect those who teach you; and forgive like the teacher who prayed for his rude student.

rcm_4.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm_4.setting: Kakbhushundi, many lives later, on the one memory that still stings.
rcm_4.sanskrit: त्रिजग देव नर जोइ तनु धरउँ। तहँ तहँ राम भजन अनुसरऊँ॥ एक सूल मोहि बिसर न काऊ। गुर कर कोमल सील सुभाऊ ॥
rcm_4.translation: Whatever body I took, animal, god or human, I kept up my devotion to Ram. Yet one thorn never left me: I never forgot my teacher's gentle, kindly nature.
rcm_4.line: One thorn never left me: how gentle the teacher I insulted had been.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Kakbhushundi to Garuda: in every body I kept up Ram bhajan, yet one shool I never forgot, my guru's tender and gentle nature.

prasang.title_en: The student who would not stand for his teacher
prasang.summary: In an earlier life Kakbhushundi was a proud, wealthy, sharp-tongued young man whose gentle teacher kept trying to guide him. One day in the temple he refused even to rise when the teacher entered. The teacher said nothing, but a curse fell on the student; the teacher at once prayed for him, asking that he not be punished in anger. Lives later, the one thorn Kakbhushundi still carries is the memory of that teacher's gentleness.
prasang.lesson: Respect those who teach you; and forgive like the teacher who prayed for his rude student.

rcm_4.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm_4.setting: Kakbhushundi recalls arguing endlessly with the sage Lomash until the sage lost his temper.
rcm_4.sanskrit: सुनु प्रभु बहुत अवग्या किएँ। उपज क्रोध ग्यानिन्ह के हिएँ॥ अति संघरषन जौं कर कोई। अनल प्रगट चंदन ते होई ॥
rcm_4.translation: Lord, listen: even a wise man's heart grows angry when he is slighted again and again. If someone rubs sandalwood too hard, even it will burst into flame.
rcm_4.line: Rub even sandalwood too hard, and it bursts into flame.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Kakbhushundi, who kept contradicting the sage Lomash, owns that the fault was his: much disrespect raises anger even in a jnani's heart, as friction draws fire from chandan.

prasang.title_en: Arguing with Lomash
prasang.summary: As a young seeker Kakbhushundi went to the sage Lomash, who taught the formless God; Kakbhushundi kept arguing for his own view until the sage, provoked again and again, lost his temper and cursed him to become a crow. Kakbhushundi took it without fear or self-pity, and the sage, regretting his anger, called him back and taught him the Ramcharitmanas.
prasang.lesson: Even calm people burn when pushed too far; take correction without bitterness.

rcm_4.speaker: Shiva
rcm_4.setting: Shiva, as the cursed Kakbhushundi flies off without bitterness.
rcm_4.sanskrit: उमा जे राम चरन रत बिगत काम मद क्रोध। निज प्रभुमय देखहिं जगत केहि सन करहिं बिरोध ॥
rcm_4.translation: Uma, those devoted to Ram's feet, free of desire, pride and anger, see the whole world filled with their Lord; with whom would they quarrel?
rcm_4.line: When you see the divine in everyone, who is left to quarrel with?
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Shiva to Uma as Kakbhushundi accepts Lomash's curse calmly: those who love Ram's feet and are rid of kama, mada and krodha see the world as their Lord; with whom would they quarrel.

prasang.title_en: Arguing with Lomash
prasang.summary: As a young seeker Kakbhushundi went to the sage Lomash, who taught the formless God; Kakbhushundi kept arguing for his own view until the sage, provoked again and again, lost his temper and cursed him to become a crow. Kakbhushundi took it without fear or self-pity, and the sage, regretting his anger, called him back and taught him the Ramcharitmanas.
prasang.lesson: Even calm people burn when pushed too far; take correction without bitterness.

rcm_4.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm_4.setting: Kakbhushundi compares knowledge to a lamp that can blow out, and devotion to a jewel.
rcm_4.sanskrit: कहेउँ ग्यान सिद्धांत बुझाई। सुनहु भगति मनि कै प्रभुताई॥ राम भगति चिंतामनि सुंदर। बसइ गरुड़ जाके उर अंतर ॥ परम प्रकास रूप दिन राती। नहिं कछु चहिअ दिआ घृत बाती॥ मोह दरिद्र निकट नहिं आवा। लोभ बात नहिं ताहि बुझावा ॥
rcm_4.translation: I have explained the principle of knowledge; now hear the power of the jewel of devotion. Devotion to Ram is a beautiful wish-granting gem, Garuda: in whose heart it lives, it is supreme light day and night, needing no lamp, ghee or wick. The poverty of delusion does not come near, and the wind of greed cannot blow it out.
rcm_4.line: Devotion is a jewel that shines day and night; it needs no lamp, no oil, no wick.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_4.our_note: Kakbhushundi contrasts the lamp of jnana, hard to light and easily blown out, with the chintamani of Ram bhakti, which shines of itself.

rcm_4.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm_4.setting: Kakbhushundi on how devotion reaches people.
rcm_4.sanskrit: राम सिंधु घन सज्जन धीरा। चंदन तरु हरि संत समीरा॥ सब कर फल हरि भगति सुहाई। सो बिनु संत न काहूँ पाई ॥
rcm_4.translation: Ram is the ocean, and the steady good are the clouds; Hari is the sandal tree, and the saints are the breeze. The fruit of everything is beautiful devotion to Hari, and no one has found it without the good.
rcm_4.line: The ocean gives rain only through clouds; grace reaches us through good people.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_4.our_note: Kakbhushundi: Ram is the sea and steady saints the clouds, Hari the sandal tree and saints the breeze; the fruit of all is Hari bhakti, and none has got it without a saint.

rcm_4.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm_4.setting: Kakbhushundi, on what people do with a rare human life.
rcm_4.sanskrit: सो तनु धरि हरि भजहिं न जे नर। होहिं बिषय रत मंद मंद तर॥ काँच किरिच बदलें ते लेहीं। कर ते डारि परस मनि देहीं ॥
rcm_4.translation: Those who gain this body and still do not worship Hari, sunk in the lowest of pleasures, throw away the philosopher's stone from their hand and take shards of glass in exchange.
rcm_4.line: We throw away the philosopher's stone and take shards of glass in exchange.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Kakbhushundi: men who get this body and do not worship Hari, lost in base pleasures, drop the paras mani from their hand and take bits of glass.

prasang.title_en: Garuda's seven questions
prasang.summary: Garuda asks seven questions: the rarest body, the greatest sorrow and joy, the nature of good and wicked people, the highest virtue and the worst wrong, and the diseases of the mind. Kakbhushundi answers: no sorrow like want, no joy like meeting good people; non-harm is highest and slander worst; delusion is the root disease, with lust, greed, anger, envy and ego as its symptoms.
prasang.lesson: Know your mind's diseases by name: confusion, anger, greed, envy, ego.

rcm_4.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm_4.setting: Kakbhushundi answers Garuda's questions: what is the greatest sorrow, and the greatest joy?
rcm_4.sanskrit: नहिं दरिद्र सम दुख जग माहीं। संत मिलन सम सुख जग नाहीं॥ पर उपकार बचन मन काया। संत सहज सुभाउ खगराया ॥
rcm_4.translation: There is no sorrow in the world like poverty, and no joy like meeting good people. To do good to others in word, thought and deed is the natural way of the good.
rcm_4.line: No sorrow like want, no joy like meeting good people.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Kakbhushundi answers Garuda: no dukh in the world equals daridrya, no sukh equals sant milan; doing good to others in word, mind and body is the saint's nature.

prasang.title_en: Garuda's seven questions
prasang.summary: Garuda asks seven questions: the rarest body, the greatest sorrow and joy, the nature of good and wicked people, the highest virtue and the worst wrong, and the diseases of the mind. Kakbhushundi answers: no sorrow like want, no joy like meeting good people; non-harm is highest and slander worst; delusion is the root disease, with lust, greed, anger, envy and ego as its symptoms.
prasang.lesson: Know your mind's diseases by name: confusion, anger, greed, envy, ego.

rcm_4.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm_4.setting: Kakbhushundi answers Garuda's questions: what is the highest virtue, and the gravest wrong?
rcm_4.sanskrit: संत उदय संतत सुखकारी। बिस्व सुखद जिमि इंदु तमारी॥ परम धर्म श्रुति बिदित अहिंसा। पर निंदा सम अघ न गरीसा ॥
rcm_4.translation: The rise of the good always brings joy, as moon and sun bring joy to the whole world. The Vedas hold non-harm as the highest duty, and there is no wrong as heavy as slandering others.
rcm_4.line: Non-harm is the highest duty. No wrong weighs as much as slandering others.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: Kakbhushundi's answers to Garuda: ahimsa is the supreme dharma known to the Veda, and there is no sin weightier than par ninda.

prasang.title_en: Garuda's seven questions
prasang.summary: Garuda asks seven questions: the rarest body, the greatest sorrow and joy, the nature of good and wicked people, the highest virtue and the worst wrong, and the diseases of the mind. Kakbhushundi answers: no sorrow like want, no joy like meeting good people; non-harm is highest and slander worst; delusion is the root disease, with lust, greed, anger, envy and ego as its symptoms.
prasang.lesson: Know your mind's diseases by name: confusion, anger, greed, envy, ego.

rcm_4.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm_4.setting: Garuda's last question is about the diseases of the mind; Kakbhushundi answers.
rcm_4.sanskrit: मोह सकल ब्याधिन्ह कर मूला। तिन्ह ते पुनि उपजहिं बहु सूला॥ काम बात कफ लोभ अपारा। क्रोध पित्त नित छाती जारा ॥
rcm_4.translation: Delusion is the root of all diseases, and from it spring many pains. Desire is the wind, greed the endless phlegm, and anger the bile that keeps the chest burning.
rcm_4.line: Confusion is the root illness. Anger is the bile that keeps your chest burning.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: The manas rog passage: moha is the root of all disease; kama is vata, lobha kapha, krodha pitta. The cure given later is devotion to Ram under the sadguru as physician.

prasang.title_en: Garuda's seven questions
prasang.summary: Garuda asks seven questions: the rarest body, the greatest sorrow and joy, the nature of good and wicked people, the highest virtue and the worst wrong, and the diseases of the mind. Kakbhushundi answers: no sorrow like want, no joy like meeting good people; non-harm is highest and slander worst; delusion is the root disease, with lust, greed, anger, envy and ego as its symptoms.
prasang.lesson: Know your mind's diseases by name: confusion, anger, greed, envy, ego.

rcm_4.speaker: Kakbhushundi
rcm_4.setting: Kakbhushundi continues listing the diseases of the mind.
rcm_4.sanskrit: ममता दादु कंडु इरषाई। हरष बिषाद गरह बहुताई॥ पर सुख देखि जरनि सोइ छई। कुष्ट दुष्टता मन कुटिलई ॥
rcm_4.translation: Possessiveness is ringworm and envy is the itch; the swings of elation and dejection are throat ailments. The burning you feel at another's happiness is consumption, and malice and a crooked mind are leprosy.
rcm_4.line: Envy is an itch. Burning at another's happiness is a wasting disease of the mind.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
rcm_4.our_note: The manas rog list continues: mamata is ringworm, irsha the itch, harsha and vishada throat disease, burning at another's happiness is consumption, wickedness and crookedness leprosy.

prasang.title_en: Garuda's seven questions
prasang.summary: Garuda asks seven questions: the rarest body, the greatest sorrow and joy, the nature of good and wicked people, the highest virtue and the worst wrong, and the diseases of the mind. Kakbhushundi answers: no sorrow like want, no joy like meeting good people; non-harm is highest and slander worst; delusion is the root disease, with lust, greed, anger, envy and ego as its symptoms.
prasang.lesson: Know your mind's diseases by name: confusion, anger, greed, envy, ego.

rcm_4.speaker: Shiva
rcm_4.setting: Shiva comments on Garuda's meeting with Kakbhushundi.
rcm_4.sanskrit: गिरिजा संत समागम सम न लाभ कछु आन। बिनु हरि कृपा न होइ सो गावहिं बेद पुरान ॥
rcm_4.translation: Girija, there is no gain like the company of saints; and it does not happen without Hari's grace, sing the Vedas and Puranas.
rcm_4.line: No gain is like good company, and good company itself is a grace.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_4.our_note: Shiva to Girija: no gain equals sant samagam, and without Hari's kripa it does not occur; so sing Veda and Purana.

rcm_4.speaker: Shiva / Tulsidas
rcm_4.setting: The Manas ends with its simplest teaching.
rcm_4.sanskrit: एहिं कलिकाल न साधन दूजा। जोग जग्य जप तप ब्रत पूजा॥ रामहि सुमिरिअ गाइअ रामहि। संतत सुनिअ राम गुन ग्रामहि ॥
rcm_4.translation: In this age of Kali there is no other means, no yoga, sacrifice, chanting, austerity, vow or ritual worship: remember Ram, sing Ram, and always listen to the qualities of Ram.
rcm_4.line: Remember Ram, sing Ram, keep listening to what is good in him.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_4.our_note: The Manas concludes: in Kali there is no second sadhana, not yoga, yajna, japa, tapa, vrata or puja; remember Ram, sing Ram, hear ever the host of Ram's virtues.

rcm_4.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_4.setting: The closing prayer of the Ramcharitmanas.
rcm_4.sanskrit: मो सम दीन न दीन हित तुम्ह समान रघुबीर। अस बिचारि रघुबंस मनि हरहु बिषम भव भीर ॥
rcm_4.translation: There is no one as poor as I am, and no friend of the poor like you, Raghubir. Thinking this over, jewel of the Raghus, take away the heavy fear of the world.
rcm_4.line: No one is as poor as me, and no one befriends the poor like you. Take this fear away.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_4.our_note: Tulsidas's closing prayer: there is none so deen as I and none so kind to the deen as you, Raghuvir; considering this, jewel of the Raghus, take away the grievous fear of rebirth.

rcm_4.speaker: Tulsidas
rcm_4.setting: The very last doha of the Ramcharitmanas.
rcm_4.sanskrit: कामिहि नारि पिआरि जिमि लोभिहि प्रिय जिमि दाम। तिमि रघुनाथ निरंतर प्रिय लागहु मोहि राम ॥
rcm_4.translation: As a woman is dear to a man full of desire, and as money is dear to a greedy man, so, Raghunath, may you be dear to me always, Ram.
rcm_4.line: As money is dear to the greedy, may you be that dear to me, always.
rcm_4.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
rcm_4.our_note: The final doha: as woman is dear to the kami and wealth to the lobhi, so may Raghunath be ever dear to me. Tulsidas borrows the two strongest cravings to measure the love he asks for.

sur_1.speaker: Krishna (message to Yashoda)
sur_1.setting: Krishna, now a prince in the city of Mathura, sends word home to his foster mother.
sur_1.sanskrit: यद्यपि मथुरा बिभव बहुत है तुम बिनु कछु न सुहाय। सूरदास ब्रजबासी लोगनि भेंटत हृदय जुड़ाय॥
sur_1.translation: "Though Mathura has great splendour, nothing pleases me without you." Surdas says: meeting the people of Braj, his heart grows cool and calm.
sur_1.line: "The city has every splendour, but nothing pleases me without you." Even Krishna was homesick.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) or Shukla 1926 glosses (Bhramargeet) + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: Krishna's message home to Yashoda and Braj: success in the city does not replace home. Human in wording.

sur_1.speaker: a gopi (Bhramargeet)
sur_1.setting: In the Bhramargeet, a gopi tells Uddhava she cannot stop remembering Krishna.
sur_1.sanskrit: सूरदास मोहि निमिष न बिसरत मोहन सूरति सोवत जागत॥
sur_1.translation: Surdas says: I cannot forget Mohan's face for a moment, sleeping or waking.
sur_1.line: I can't forget his face for a moment, asleep or awake.
sur_1.verified_with: Shukla 1926 glosses + own reading
sur_1.our_note: A gopi to Uddhava in the Bhramargit: no teaching of formless knowledge can displace the remembered face. Human in wording; the beloved is Krishna.

sur_1.speaker: Radha (Bhramargeet)
sur_1.setting: Radha's message to Krishna in Mathura.
sur_1.sanskrit: बारक जाइयो मिलि माधौ। को जानै कब छूटि जायगो स्वाँस, रहै जिय साधौ॥
sur_1.translation: Come and meet me just once, Madhav. Who knows when the breath may leave; let the heart's wish not remain.
sur_1.line: Come and see me once, Madhav. Who knows how long there is. Don't leave the wish unfulfilled.
sur_1.verified_with: Shukla 1926 glosses + own reading
sur_1.our_note: Radha's message from Braj: longing sharpened by the shortness of life. Human in wording; the beloved is Krishna.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: The opening pada of Surdas's songs, sung by a poet who was himself blind.
sur_1.sanskrit: चरन-कमल बंदों हरि-राइ। जाकी कृपा पंगु गिरि लंघे, अंधे कों सब कछु दरसाइ ॥ बहिरौ सुने, गूँग पुनि बोले, रंक चले सिर छत्र धराइ | सूरदास स्वामी करुनामय, बार बार बंदों तिहि पाइ ॥
sur_1.translation: I bow to the lotus feet of Hari, by whose grace the lame cross mountains and the blind see everything; the deaf hear, the mute speak again, and the pauper walks with a royal canopy over his head. Surdas says: my master is full of compassion; again and again I bow at his feet.
sur_1.line: By grace the lame cross mountains and the blind see.
sur_1.misuse: Not a medical promise; a hope that limits are not the last word.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) or Shukla 1926 glosses (Bhramargeet) + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: Surdas's mangalacharana: the Lord's compassion overturns every limit; the blind poet bows again and again.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas on whose side God stands.
sur_1.sanskrit: नाथ अनाथनि ही के संगी। दीनदयाल, परम करुनामय, जन-हित हरि बहु-रंगी ॥
sur_1.translation: The Lord is the companion of exactly those who have no one: kind to the lowly, supremely compassionate, Hari who takes many forms for the good of his people.
sur_1.line: The Lord is the companion of exactly those who have no one.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) or Shukla 1926 glosses (Bhramargeet) + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: Hari as dina-dayal: he sides with the anatha, the one without a protector.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas sings of Hari as the friend who shows up in hard times.
sur_1.sanskrit: हरि सो मीत न देख्यौ कोई । विपति-काल सुमिरत, तिहिं औसर आनि तिरीछो होई ॥
sur_1.translation: I have never seen a friend like Hari. Remember him in a time of trouble, and at that very moment he comes and stands between you and it.
sur_1.line: I've never seen a friend like Hari. Remember him in trouble, and he comes and stands beside you.
sur_1.misuse: A friend who stands with you, not a guarantee that the trouble disappears.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: Hari as the friend in vipatti who shields the one who remembers him.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas on how Govind receives every kind of love; the pada goes on to Shabari's berries and Vidura's banana peels.
sur_1.sanskrit: गोबिंद प्रीति सबनि की मानत | जिहि जिहि भाइ करत जन सेवा, अंतर की गति जानत ॥
sur_1.translation: Govind accepts everyone's love. In whatever spirit his people serve him, he knows the movement of the heart within.
sur_1.line: Govind accepts everyone's love, in whatever way they serve. He knows what is really in the heart.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: The Lord looks to bhava, not form; the pada cites Shabari and Vidura as examples.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas recalls Krishna washing guests' feet at Yudhishthira's royal sacrifice.
sur_1.sanskrit: जाको चरनोदक सिव सिर धरि, तीनि लोक हितकारी । सोइ प्रभु पांडु-सुतनि के कारन निज कर चरन पखारी ॥
sur_1.translation: He, the water of whose feet Shiva bears on his head and which blesses the three worlds — that Lord, for the sake of the sons of Pandu, washed feet with his own hands.
sur_1.line: The Lord whose feet the whole world honours washed others' feet with his own hands.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: Krishna's humility at Yudhishthira's Rajasuya: greatness shown in service to his devotees.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas on who truly feels a person's pain.
sur_1.sanskrit: और न काहुहि जन की पीर। जब जब दीन दुखी भयो, तब तब कृपा करी बलबीर॥
sur_1.translation: No one else feels the pain of his people. Whenever the lowly were in sorrow, every time, Balbir showed them kindness.
sur_1.line: Every time someone was hurting, kindness came. No one else feels your pain like that.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) or Shukla 1926 glosses (Bhramargeet) + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: The Lord alone truly feels the devotee's pain and has always responded.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas on trusting the Lord's promise.
sur_1.sanskrit: प्रभु तेरो बचन भरोसों साँचों। पोषन भरन विसंभर साहब,
sur_1.translation: Lord, trust in your word is true: the master who sustains the whole universe feeds and holds us.
sur_1.line: Lord, your word is worth trusting. The one who holds up the whole world holds you too.
sur_1.misuse: Trust is not a reason to stop earning or planning; Surdas's next words scold fretting, which the card leaves out.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: Trust in Vishvambhara as provider; the pada goes on to chide needless fretting.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas on being held by Krishna.
sur_1.sanskrit: जाकों मनमोहन अंग करे। ताकौ केस खसे नहिं सिर ते, जो जग बैर परे ॥
sur_1.translation: The one whom Manmohan takes into his embrace — not a hair falls from his head, even if the whole world turns hostile.
sur_1.line: When Krishna holds you close, not a hair on your head is harmed, even if the world turns against you.
sur_1.misuse: Poetic assurance of inner safety, not a guarantee against harm; seek real protection from real threats.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: Assurance of the Lord's protection of his own; a devotee's confidence, not a guarantee against harm.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas speaks to his own mind.
sur_1.sanskrit: रे मन, गोबिंद के है रहिये। … दुख, सुख, कीरति, भाग आपने आइ परे सो गहिये।
sur_1.translation: O mind, stay Govind's. … Sorrow, joy, fame, fortune — whatever falls to you, take it as it comes.
sur_1.line: Mind, stay Govind's. Sorrow, joy, fame, fortune: take whatever comes your way.
sur_1.misuse: Accepting what comes is not accepting mistreatment; it is not chasing or dreading outcomes.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: Self-address to the mind: belong to the Lord and take what comes as his.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas on running a household.
sur_1.sanskrit: नंदनंदन करि घर कौ ठाकुर, आपुन है रह चेरो ॥
sur_1.translation: Make Nandnandan the master of the house, and live in it yourself as his servant.
sur_1.line: Make Krishna the master of your house, and live there as his helper.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: Householder bhakti: the home is the Lord's and one runs it as his steward.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas, looking back on hard times, almost misses them for how close God felt.
sur_1.sanskrit: अब वे बिपदा हू न रहीं। मनसा करि सुमिरत हे जब-जब, मिलते तब-तबहीं ॥ अपने दीन दास के हित लगि, फिरते सँग-सँगहीं । लेते राखि पलक गोलक ज्यों, संतत तिन सबहीं ॥
sur_1.translation: Now even those troubles are gone. Back then, whenever I remembered you in my heart, you met me right then. For the good of your poor servant you walked along beside me, and kept me through all of it as the eyelid keeps the eye.
sur_1.line: In the hardest days he walked beside me and kept me as the eyelid keeps the eye.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) or Shukla 1926 glosses (Bhramargeet) + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: Surdas almost misses his hardships, because in them remembrance was constant and the Lord near.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas teaches the mind to love Madhav, using the chatak bird, which drinks only rain.
sur_1.sanskrit: चातक चितवन पारि । घन-आसा सब दुख सहै, (पै) अनत न जाँचे बारि ॥
sur_1.translation: The chatak, gazing up, bears every hardship in hope of the rain cloud, yet asks no other water.
sur_1.line: The chatak bears every hardship waiting for the rain cloud, and asks no other water.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: The chatak as the image of ananya bhakti, single-minded love that will take nothing else.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas on the shelter of the name.
sur_1.sanskrit: बड़ी है राम नाम की ओट | सरन गएँ प्रभु काढ़ि देत नहिं, करत कृपा के कोट ।
sur_1.translation: Great is the shelter of the name. When you come for refuge, the Lord never turns you out; he builds you forts of kindness.
sur_1.line: The name is a great shelter. Whoever comes to him is never turned away; he builds walls of kindness.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: Nama as refuge; the Lord builds 'forts of grace' around the sharanagata.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas on singing to Gopal.
sur_1.sanskrit: जो सुख होत गुपालहि गाए । सो सुख होत न जप-तप कीन्हें, कोटिक तीरथ न्हाएं ॥
sur_1.translation: The joy that comes from singing of Gopal does not come from chanting or austerity, or bathing at ten million holy places.
sur_1.line: The joy of singing to Gopal doesn't come from rituals or a million pilgrimages.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: Kirtan placed above ritual effort in Sur's bhakti.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas, who owned nothing, on his real wealth.
sur_1.sanskrit: हमारे निर्धन के धन राम । चोर न लेत, घटत नहिं कबहूँ, आवत गाढ़े काम ॥
sur_1.translation: Ram is the wealth of us who have nothing. No thief takes it, it never runs low, and it comes through in hard times.
sur_1.line: Ram is the wealth of those with nothing: no thief takes it, it never runs out.
sur_1.misuse: Inner wealth, not a financial plan: keep paying the bills and asking for help.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: Rama-nama as the one secure wealth.

sur_1.ref_label: Sursagar vinay pada (Sur Vinay Patrika 167, opening)
sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas asks not to be measured.
sur_1.sanskrit: प्रभु, मेरे गुन-अवगुन न बिचारों।
sur_1.translation: Lord, do not weigh my good points and my faults.
sur_1.line: Lord, do not weigh my good points against my faults. Just keep me.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) or Shukla 1926 glosses (Bhramargeet) + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: A plea of dainya: the devotee asks to be taken without being measured.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas remembers what the Lord has already done for him.
sur_1.sanskrit: तुम प्रभु, मोसों बहुत करी | नर-देही दीनी सुमिरन को, मो पापी ते कछु न सरी ॥ गरभ-बास अति त्रास, अधोमुख, तहाँ न मेरी सुधि बिसरी।
sur_1.translation: Lord, you have done so much for me: you gave me a human body for remembering you, though I, a sinner, achieved nothing with it. In the terror of the womb, head down, even there you did not forget me.
sur_1.line: You did so much for me. Even in the dark of the womb, you did not forget me.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: Confession joined to gratitude: the human birth was given for remembrance, and the Lord's care came first.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: At the end of a long confession, Surdas names what makes the Lord great.
sur_1.sanskrit: सुकृती सुचि सेवक जन काहि न जिय भावै। प्रभु की प्रभुता यहै जु दीन सरन पावे॥
sur_1.translation: Who wouldn't love a virtuous, pure servant? The Lord's greatness is this: that the lowly find shelter.
sur_1.line: Anyone would love a perfect servant. The Lord's greatness is that the lowly find shelter with him.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: The close of a long confession: God's lordship is shown in sheltering the unworthy.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas asks for steadiness in love.
sur_1.sanskrit: सोइ कछु कीजे दीन-दयाल ! जातें जन छन चरन न छाँड़े, करुना-सागर, भक्त-रसाल
sur_1.translation: Do whatever it takes, kind to the lowly, so that your servant never lets go of your feet even for a moment, ocean of compassion, delight of devotees.
sur_1.line: Do whatever it takes so that I never let go of your feet, not even for a moment.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: Prayer for unbroken devotion; steadiness itself is asked as a gift.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas on how a mother treats her child.
sur_1.sanskrit: अपुने को को न आदर देइ ? ज्यों बालक अपराध कोटि करे, मातु न माने तेइ ॥
sur_1.translation: Who does not honour their own? A child may do ten million wrongs, and the mother does not count them.
sur_1.line: Who doesn't honour their own? A child may do a million wrongs; a mother doesn't keep count.
sur_1.misuse: About God's forgiveness, not a reason to excuse harm done to real people.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: The Lord's forgiveness of his own, by the likeness of a mother. It speaks of God's regard, not of excusing harm between people.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas on where his strength lies.
sur_1.sanskrit: तुम्हरी नाम तजि प्रभु जगदीसर, सु तो कहो मेरे और कहा बल ?
sur_1.translation: Leaving your name aside, Lord of the world, tell me, what other strength do I have?
sur_1.line: Apart from your name, Lord, tell me: what other strength do I have?
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: The devotee's whole strength is the name.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas asks to be kept in shelter.
sur_1.sanskrit: अब मोहि सरन राखिये नाथ ! कृपा करी जो गुरुजन पठए, बह्यो जात गह्यो हाथ ॥
sur_1.translation: Now keep me in your shelter, Lord. By your grace the elders were sent; as I was being swept away, they caught my hand.
sur_1.line: Keep me in your shelter now. I was being swept away, and your grace sent people who caught my hand.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: Grace is seen in the guides who arrived in time; the devotee asks to remain sheltered.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas on living through ups and downs.
sur_1.sanskrit: जैसे राखहु तैसे रहौं। जानत हौ दुख-सुख सब जन के, मुख करि कहा कहौं ॥ कबहुँक भोजन लहाों कृपानिधि, कबहुँक भूख सहोँ। कवहुँक चढ़ों तुरंग, महा गज, कबहुँक भार बहों ॥
sur_1.translation: However you keep me, so I will live. You know all the joys and sorrows of your people; why should I say them aloud? Sometimes I get food, kind one, sometimes I go hungry; sometimes I ride a horse or a great elephant, sometimes I carry loads myself.
sur_1.line: Some days a feast, some days hunger; some days riding high, some days carrying loads. You already know.
sur_1.misuse: Acceptance is not resignation to mistreatment.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) or Shukla 1926 glosses (Bhramargeet) + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: Acceptance of ups and downs as the Lord's keeping; he already knows.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas, with no one else to tell.
sur_1.sanskrit: कौन सुने यह बात हमारी | समरथ ओर न देखों तुम विनु, कासों विथा कहों बनवारी ॥
sur_1.translation: Who will hear this matter of mine? I see no one capable but you. To whom shall I tell my pain, Banwari?
sur_1.line: Who will listen? I see no one else who can help. Who do I tell my pain to, Krishna?
sur_1.misuse: Telling God is good; telling a person too is also good.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: The devotee has no other hearer; the plea is itself the turning to God.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas on belonging.
sur_1.sanskrit: मेरी तो गति-पति तुम, अनतहिं दुख पाऊँ। हों कहाइ तेरों, अब कोन कौ कहाऊँ ॥
sur_1.translation: You are my way and my keeper; anywhere else I find only sorrow. Called yours, whose else could I be called now?
sur_1.line: You are my way and my keeper. I'm known as yours; whose else could I be?
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: Ananya sharanagati: belonging exclusively to the Lord.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas on belonging that does not depend on being good.
sur_1.sanskrit: जौ हम भले बुरे तो तेरे। तुम्हें हमारी लाज-बड़ाई, बिनती सुनि प्रभु मेरे ॥
sur_1.translation: Good or bad, we are yours. Our shame and our honour are yours to carry. Hear my plea, my Lord.
sur_1.line: Good or bad, we are still yours.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) or Shukla 1926 glosses (Bhramargeet) + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: Belonging to the Lord does not depend on being good; the devotee's honour is the Lord's own concern.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas describes the Lord he trusts.
sur_1.sanskrit: ऐसे प्रभु अनाथ के स्वामी | दीनदयाल, प्रेम-परिंपूरन, सब घट अंतरजामी ॥
sur_1.translation: Such is the Lord, master of those who have no one: kind to the lowly, brimming with love, knowing every heart from within.
sur_1.line: He is the protector of those who have no one: kind, full of love, knowing every heart.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: The Lord as anatha-natha and antaryami.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas on the Lord's readiness.
sur_1.sanskrit: कबहूँ तुम नाहिन गहरु कियो | सदा सुभाव-सुलभ सुमिरन-बस, भक्तनि अमर दियौ ॥
sur_1.translation: You have never once delayed. By nature easy to reach and won over by remembrance, you have always given your devotees what is undying.
sur_1.line: You never once delayed. You are easy to reach, and remembering you is enough to win you.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: The Lord is sulabha and sumirana-vasha, won by remembrance.

sur_1.ref_label: Sursagar vinay pada (Sur Vinay Patrika 256, opening)
sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas opens a list of rescues (Gajendra, Draupadi, Parikshit).
sur_1.sanskrit: तुम हरि, सॉकरे के साथी ।
sur_1.translation: Hari, you are the companion of those in a tight spot.
sur_1.line: When you are cornered, you are not alone. He is the companion of tight places.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) or Shukla 1926 glosses (Bhramargeet) + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: Opens Sur's list of rescues: Gajendra, Draupadi, Parikshit.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas on what pleases the Lord.
sur_1.sanskrit: सरबस प्रभु रीझि देत तुलसी के पाता॥
sur_1.translation: Pleased by a single tulsi leaf, the Lord gives everything.
sur_1.line: Pleased by a single tulsi leaf, the Lord gives everything.
sur_1.misuse: About the worth of small sincere offerings, not a transaction for material gain.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: The Lord values the smallest sincere offering; compare Gita 9.26.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas asks to be remembered.
sur_1.sanskrit: मेरी सुधि लीजो हो, ब्रजराज । और नहीं जग मैं कोउ मेरो, तुमहि सुधारन काज़ ॥
sur_1.translation: Remember me, Lord of Braj. I have no one else in the world to set me right but you.
sur_1.line: Remember me, Lord of Braj. There's no one else to set my life right.
sur_1.misuse: A prayer from a lonely place, not advice to cut off from people.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: A plea from loneliness: only the Lord can mend him.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: The famous bhajan "Prabhu mere avgun chit na dharo".
sur_1.sanskrit: हमारे प्रभु, औगुन चित न धरो । समदरसी है नाम तुम्हारा, सोई पार करौ॥ इक लोहा पूजा में राखत, इक घर बधिक परो। सो दुबिधा पारस नहिं जानत, कंचन करत खरो॥
sur_1.translation: My Lord, do not hold my faults in your mind. Your name is "the one who sees all alike"; live up to it and carry me across. One piece of iron is kept in the shrine for worship, another lies in a butcher's house; the touchstone knows no such difference, and turns both into pure gold.
sur_1.line: The touchstone turns any iron to gold, the shrine's or the butcher's.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) or Shukla 1926 glosses (Bhramargeet) + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: The famous pada: the Lord is samadarshi, and like the paras he does not ask where the iron has been.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas on why to serve the Lord of the Yadus.
sur_1.sanskrit: संपति बिपति, बिपति ते संपति, देह कौ यहै सुभाइ ॥ तरुवर फूले, फरे, पतझरे, अपने कालहि पाइ।
sur_1.translation: Fortune into trouble, trouble into fortune — that is the nature of the body's life. Trees flower, fruit and shed their leaves, each in its season.
sur_1.line: Good times turn hard and hard times turn good. Trees flower, fruit and shed, each in its season.
sur_1.misuse: Surrender comes after doing your part and reflecting (Gita 18.63), not instead of it.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: Sur uses the turning of fortune as the reason to serve the Lord, who alone is constant. The quoted lines stand without the devotional frame.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas on remembering in good times.
sur_1.sanskrit: सबे दिन एके-से नहि जात। सुमिरन-भजन कियौ करि हरि कौ,जब लों तन-कुसलात॥
sur_1.translation: Not all days pass the same. Keep remembering and singing of Hari while the body is well.
sur_1.line: Not every day will be like this one. Remember Hari while you're well.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: Do bhajan in health; the pada warns that fortune and strength do not last.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas on the way of one who has tasted Hari.
sur_1.sanskrit: कोमल बचन, दीनता सब सौं, सदा अनंदित रहिये ।
sur_1.translation: Gentle words, humility with everyone, and always remain joyful.
sur_1.line: Speak gently, be humble with everyone, and stay joyful.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: The conduct of one who has tasted Hari-rasa. The line stands as plain conduct.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas on how the Lord provides.
sur_1.sanskrit: जो प्रभु के सरनागत आवे। ताकों प्रभु क्यों करि बिसरावे ॥ मातु-उदर में रस पहुँचावत। बहुरि रुधिर तें छीर बनावत ॥
sur_1.translation: How could the Lord forget one who has come to him for refuge? He sent nourishment to the child in the mother's womb, then turned blood into milk.
sur_1.line: How could he forget someone who comes to him? He fed you in the womb, then turned blood into milk.
sur_1.misuse: Trust alongside work and planning; the pada's earlier lines about not caring for food or family are left out.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: Providence argued from the care already received before one could ask.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: One of Surdas's best-known padas.
sur_1.sanskrit: मेरो मन अनत कहाँ सुख पावे । जैसे उड़ि जहाज को पच्छी, फिरि जहाज पर आये ॥
sur_1.translation: Where else will my mind find happiness? Like the bird on a ship at sea that flies off and comes back to the ship again.
sur_1.line: Where else will my heart find rest? Like a bird on a ship at sea, it flies off and returns.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: Sur's best-known pada: the mind wanders and has only one resting place, the Lord.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas on what devotion is to him.
sur_1.sanskrit: तुम्हारी भक्ति हमारे प्रान । छूटि गए केसे जन जीवत, ज्यों पानी बिनु पान ॥
sur_1.translation: Devotion to you is my very breath. If it were gone, how would your servant live? Like a leaf without water.
sur_1.line: Loving you is my breath. Without it I'd wither, like a leaf with no water.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: Bhakti as the devotee's very life.

sur_1.speaker: Surdas
sur_1.setting: Surdas on a mind given to Nandlal.
sur_1.sanskrit: जैसे सरिता मिले सिंधु को, बहुरि प्रवाह न आवे (हो)। ऐसे सूर कमल-लोचन तें, चित नहिं अनत डुलावै (हो) ॥
sur_1.translation: As a river that meets the sea never flows back again, so Sur's mind, given to the lotus-eyed one, does not wander elsewhere.
sur_1.line: Like a river that has reached the sea and never flows back, my heart doesn't wander from him.
sur_1.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
sur_1.our_note: The settled mind of ananya bhakti.

sur_1.speaker: The sages
sur_1.setting: Told to meditate on his form, the sages admit their minds will not stay still.
sur_1.sanskrit: प्रभो! तथोपदेष्टव्यं वातवच्चपलं मन: यथा निगृह्य शक्ष्यामस्त्वां स्मर्तुं चिरशान्तये ॥
sur_1.translation: Lord, now teach us how to restrain this mind, restless as the wind, so that we can remember you for lasting peace.
sur_1.line: My mind is restless as the wind. Teach me to steady it, to remember you and be at peace.
sur_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (OCR noise checked); data tr.hi only; own English
sur_1.our_note: The sages' request to Surya; it echoes Arjuna's complaint about the mind in Gita 6.34.

prasang.title_en: Overwhelmed sages ask the Sun for a gentle form, and learn devotion
prasang.summary: The sages ask Surya to show his cosmic form; seeing it, they lose their peace and take refuge, asking for his gentle form again. Surya tells them to fix their minds on him; they admit their minds are restless as wind, and he teaches that devotion is simply the love we feel for friends and family turned toward God.
prasang.lesson: When the vastness is too much, love is a door small enough to walk through.

sur_1.speaker: Surya
sur_1.setting: Surya defines devotion by pointing to loves people already know.
sur_1.sanskrit: स्त्रीमित्रादिषु सः प्रेमा श्रद्धा स जनकादिषु । मय्येव साधकानां स भक्तिरित्यभिधीयते ॥
sur_1.translation: The love one has for a spouse and friends, the reverent trust one has for parents: when seekers turn that toward me, it is called devotion.
sur_1.line: The love you feel for friends, the trust you feel for parents: turned toward God, that is devotion.
sur_1.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (OCR noise checked); data tr.hi only; own English
sur_1.our_note: Bhakti defined through loves already known.

prasang.title_en: Overwhelmed sages ask the Sun for a gentle form, and learn devotion
prasang.summary: The sages ask Surya to show his cosmic form; seeing it, they lose their peace and take refuge, asking for his gentle form again. Surya tells them to fix their minds on him; they admit their minds are restless as wind, and he teaches that devotion is simply the love we feel for friends and family turned toward God.
prasang.lesson: When the vastness is too much, love is a door small enough to walk through.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas on the one thing that makes him safe.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: जैसो तैसो रावरो केवल कोसलपाल। तौ तुलसी को है भलो तिहूँ लोक तिहुँ काल॥
tulsi_1.translation: Lord of Kosala, whatever I am, I am yours alone; and so Tulsi is well in all three worlds and all three times.
tulsi_1.line: Whatever I am, I am yours. So I am well, now and always.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only) + own reading
tulsi_1.our_note: Dohavali: such as I am, I am yours only, lord of Kosala; so who fares as well as Tulsi in the three worlds and three times.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas on the one good thing he has.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: है तुलसी कें एक गुन अवगुन निधि कहैं लोग। भलो भरोसो रावरो राम रीझिले जोग॥
tulsi_1.translation: People call Tulsi a treasury of faults, but he has one virtue: a good trust in you, Ram, which is fit to please you.
tulsi_1.line: People call me a heap of faults. I have one virtue: I trust you.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_1.our_note: Dohavali: Tulsi has one guna though people call him a treasury of avagunas, a good reliance on you, Ram, who are fit to be pleased by it.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas on belonging without conditions.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: रामहि डरु करू राम सों ममता प्रीति प्रतीति। तुलसी निरुपधि राम को भएँ हारेहूँ जीति॥
tulsi_1.translation: Hold Ram in awe; give Ram your closeness, love and trust. Tulsi says: once you belong to Ram without conditions, even losing is winning.
tulsi_1.line: When you belong without conditions, even losing is a kind of winning.
tulsi_1.misuse: Surrender comes after doing your part and reflecting (Gita 18.63), not instead of it.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only) + own reading
tulsi_1.our_note: Dohavali: fear Ram, and have mamata, priti and pratiti toward Ram; Tulsi, on becoming Ram's without reserve there is victory even in defeat.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas's advice to himself when weighed down.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: तुलसी राम कृपालु सों कहि सुनाउ गुन दोष। होय दूबरी दीनता परम पीन संतोष॥
tulsi_1.translation: Tulsi, tell the kind Ram all of it, your good points and your faults. Your misery will grow thin and your contentment will grow full.
tulsi_1.line: Tell the kind one everything, good and bad. The heaviness thins; peace grows.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only) + own reading
tulsi_1.our_note: Dohavali: Tulsi, tell gracious Ram your gunas and doshas; deenata will grow lean and santosha very plump.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas on finding no helpers.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: बाधक सब सब के भए साधक भए न कोइ। तुलसी राम कृपालु तें भलो होइ सो होइ॥
tulsi_1.translation: Everyone became an obstacle to everyone; no one became a helper. Tulsi says: whatever good comes will come from the kind Ram.
tulsi_1.line: When no one around you helps, good can still come from somewhere kinder.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only) + own reading
tulsi_1.our_note: Dohavali: all have become hindrances to all, none a helper; Tulsi, whatever good is to be will be from kripalu Ram.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas on being protected without knowing it.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: खेलत बालक ब्याल सँग मेलत पावक हाथ। तुलसी सिसु पितु मातु ज्यो राखत सिय रघुनाथ॥
tulsi_1.translation: A child plays with a snake and reaches for the fire; as a father and mother keep that child safe, Tulsi says, so Sita and Ram keep us.
tulsi_1.line: As parents pull a child back from the fire, you are kept safe more often than you know.
tulsi_1.misuse: Not a promise that nothing bad happens; a reminder of care.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only) + own reading
tulsi_1.our_note: Dohavali: the child plays with a serpent and puts its hand in fire; Tulsi, as father and mother guard the infant, so do Sita and Raghunath. Same picture as Manas 3.39.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas on his own life, once a beggar boy.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: घर घर मागे टूक पुनि भूपति पूजे पाय। जे तुलसी तब राम बिनु ते अब राम सहाय॥
tulsi_1.translation: I begged for scraps from house to house; later kings bowed at my feet. The Tulsi who was then without Ram now has Ram's help.
tulsi_1.line: He once begged for scraps door to door. Where you are now is not where you end.
tulsi_1.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only) + own reading
tulsi_1.our_note: Dohavali: he begged crusts from house to house, and then kings worshipped his feet; Tulsi who was then without Ram now has Ram for helper.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas recalls the feet that freed Ahalya from her curse.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: सिला साप मोचन चरन सुमिरहु तुलसीदास । तजहु सोच संकट मिटिहिं पूजहि मनकी आस॥
tulsi_1.translation: Tulsidas, remember the feet that freed the woman turned to stone from her curse. Let your worry go: the trouble will pass and the heart's hope will be met.
tulsi_1.line: Let the worry go. The trouble will pass; the heart's hope can still be met.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only) + own reading
tulsi_1.our_note: Dohavali: Tulsidas, remember the feet that released the stone from its curse; leave soch, sankat will vanish and the mind's hope be fulfilled.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: A doha on what love for Ram produces.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: सूधे मन सूधे बचन सूधी सब करतूति। तुलसी सूधी सकल बिधि रघुबर प्रेम प्रसूति॥
tulsi_1.translation: A straight mind, straight words, straight deeds in everything: Tulsi says, all this straightness is born of love for Raghubar.
tulsi_1.line: A straight heart, straight words, straight deeds: that is what love for God gives birth to.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_1.our_note: Dohavali: a straight mind, straight speech and all conduct straight; Tulsi, straightness of every kind is the offspring of love for Raghuvar.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: A doha on home and renunciation.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: घर कोन्हें घर जात है घर छाँड़े घर जाइ। तुलसी घर बन बीचहीं राम प्रेम पुर छाइ॥
tulsi_1.translation: Making a home, the true home is lost; leaving home, home is lost too. Tulsi says: between home and forest, settle in the city of Ram's love.
tulsi_1.line: Clinging to home loses it, fleeing home loses it too. Live in between, in the city of love.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_1.our_note: Dohavali: making a house the house is lost, leaving the house the house is lost; Tulsi, midway between home and forest, settle the city of Ram prem.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: A chataka doha: hope that does not depend on being answered.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: जौ घन बरषे समय सिर जौँ भरि जनम उदास। तुलसी या चित चातकहि तऊ तिहारी आस॥
tulsi_1.translation: Whether the cloud rains on time, or stays indifferent my whole life, Tulsi says: this chataka heart still hopes in you.
tulsi_1.line: Whether you answer on time or stay silent my whole life, my heart still hopes in you.
tulsi_1.misuse: About trust in God through unanswered seasons; not a reason to stay where a person ignores your needs.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_1.our_note: Dohavali: whether the cloud rain in time or be cold for a lifetime, Tulsi, this chataka mind still hopes in you.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: The opening of Tulsidas's famous chataka (rain-bird) dohas.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: एक भरोसो एक बल एक आस बिस्वास । एक राम घन स्याम हित चातक तुलसीदास॥
tulsi_1.translation: One trust, one strength, one hope and faith: for the chataka Tulsidas, the one dark cloud, Ram, is his friend.
tulsi_1.line: One trust, one strength, one hope: like the rain-bird waiting for its one cloud.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_1.our_note: Dohavali, the chataka dohas: one reliance, one strength, one hope and trust; for the chataka Tulsidas the one friend is Ram, the dark cloud. Ananyata.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: A doha on betrayal.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: जासु भरोसें सोइऐे राखि गोद में सीस। तुलसी तासु कुचाल तें रखवारो जगदीस॥
tulsi_1.translation: When the one you trusted enough to sleep with your head in their lap turns on you, Tulsi says, the Lord of the world is your guardian.
tulsi_1.line: When the person you trusted most turns on you, the Lord of the world still guards you.
tulsi_1.misuse: Comfort after betrayal; it does not replace getting real-world help or protection.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_1.our_note: Dohavali: from the ill-dealing of him on whose trust one sleeps with head in his lap, Tulsi, the protector is Jagdish alone.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Under the heading "God protects everyone".
tulsi_1.sanskrit: भागें भल ओड़ेहुँ भलो भलो न घालें घाउ। तुलसी सब के सीस पर रखवारो रघुराउ॥
tulsi_1.translation: Better to step away, better to shield yourself; better not to strike a wound. Tulsi says: over everyone's head stands Raghurao, the guardian.
tulsi_1.line: Over every head, including yours, there is a guardian.
