tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only) + own reading
tulsi_1.our_note: Dohavali: fleeing is good, taking cover is good, dealing a wound is not good; Tulsi, on the head of all the keeper is Raghurau.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: A doha on Hanuman's devotion.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: साहब तें सेवक बड़ो जो निज धरम सुजान। राम बाँधि उतरे उदधि लाँघि गए हनुमान॥
tulsi_1.translation: The servant who knows his own duty is greater than the master: Ram had to build a bridge to cross the ocean; Hanuman simply leapt across.
tulsi_1.line: Ram had to build a bridge to cross the sea. Hanuman, out of love, simply leapt.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_1.our_note: Dohavali: greater than the master is the servant who knows his own dharma; Ram crossed the ocean by binding it, Hanuman went leaping.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas (narrating)
tulsi_1.setting: After Ram leaves for the forest, his mother Kausalya keeps his childhood things.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: जननी निरखति बान-धनुहियाँ। बार-बार उर नैननि लावति प्रभुजूकी ललित पनहियाँ॥ कबहुँ प्रथम ज्यों जाइ जगावति कहि प्रिय बचन सँवारे। उठहु तात! बलि मातु बदनपर, अनुज-सखा सब द्वारे॥
tulsi_1.translation: The mother gazes at his little bow and arrows. Again and again she presses the Lord's small, lovely shoes to her heart and eyes. Sometimes, as before, she goes to wake him with tender words: "Get up, my child, your mother adores your face; your brothers and friends are all at the door."
tulsi_1.line: She held his little shoes to her heart, and some mornings still went to wake him.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in the same scan (meaning only) + own reading
tulsi_1.our_note: Gitavali, Ayodhya: the mother gazes at his toy bow and arrows, lays his little sandals again and again on heart and eyes, and at times goes as before to wake him: rise, child, your brothers and friends are at the door.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas, after Vibhishan's refuge, on who is welcome.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: गये राम सरन सबकौ भलो। गनी-गरीब, बड़ो-छोटो, बुध-मूढु, हीनबल-अतिबलो॥ १ ॥ पंगु-अंध, निरगुनी-निसंबल, जो न लहै जाचे जलो। सो निबह्यो नीके, जो जनमि जग राम-राजमारग चलो॥
tulsi_1.translation: Whoever goes to Ram for refuge is well: rich or poor, great or small, wise or foolish, weak or very strong. The lame, the blind, those without virtue or provision, who do not get water even when they ask: whoever was born in the world and walked Ram's royal road was looked after well.
tulsi_1.line: Rich or poor, wise or foolish, weak or strong: whoever goes to him for refuge is held.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_1.our_note: Gitavali: going to Ram's refuge is good for all, wealthy and poor, great and small, wise and dull, weak and mighty; the lame, the blind, the meritless and unprovided all fared well on Ram's highway.

tulsi_1.speaker: Vibhishan
tulsi_1.setting: Vibhishan explains why he does not list his troubles.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: जानत प्रभु दुख-सुख दासनिको, तातें कहि न सुनायो। करि करुना भरि नयन बिलोकहु, तब जानौं अपनायो॥
tulsi_1.translation: The Lord knows the joys and sorrows of his servants, so I have not told mine. Look at me with eyes full of kindness; then I'll know you have made me your own.
tulsi_1.line: You know my sorrows, so I won't list them. Just look at me kindly, and I'll know I'm yours.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_1.our_note: Gitavali, Vibhishan: the Lord knows his servants' dukh and sukh, so I have not told mine; look on me with eyes filled with compassion, then I shall know you have made me your own.

prasang.title_en: Vibhishan crosses over: Ram's refuge speech
prasang.summary: Kicked out of Lanka for telling his brother the truth, Vibhishan crosses the sea to Ram, dreaming of his feet. Sugriva wants him bound as a spy; Ram says his vow is to remove the fear of anyone who comes for refuge, and if the visitor were truly wicked he would not have come at all. Ram embraces him, asks how he kept his goodness among the cruel, describes the devotee who ties every thread of love to him, and crowns him king, shyly giving what Ravana got for ten heads.
prasang.lesson: The turning itself is enough to be taken in; your past is not the deciding question.

tulsi_1.speaker: Ram
tulsi_1.setting: Ram tells his friends his natural way with those who come to him.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: सब बिधि हीन-दीन, अति जड़मति जाको कतहुँ न ठाउँ। आयो सरन भजौं, न तजौँ तिहि, यह जानत रिपिराठ॥ … पुनि पुनि भुजा उठाइ कहत हौं, सकल सभा पतिआउ। नहि कोऊ प्रिय मोहि दास सम, कपट-प्रीति बहि जाउ॥
tulsi_1.translation: Lacking in every way, poor, very slow-witted, with no place anywhere: if such a one comes for refuge, I care for him and never abandon him; the great sages know this. Again and again I raise my arm and say it, let the whole assembly believe me: no one is as dear to me as my servant; let false love be swept away.
tulsi_1.line: Whoever comes with nothing and nowhere to go, I take in and never abandon. I say it, arm raised.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_1.our_note: Gitavali, Ram: one deprived in every way, wretched, very dull, with no place anywhere, if he comes for sharan I cherish and do not leave; again and again raising my arm I say, none is dear to me as my servant.

prasang.title_en: Vibhishan crosses over: Ram's refuge speech
prasang.summary: Kicked out of Lanka for telling his brother the truth, Vibhishan crosses the sea to Ram, dreaming of his feet. Sugriva wants him bound as a spy; Ram says his vow is to remove the fear of anyone who comes for refuge, and if the visitor were truly wicked he would not have come at all. Ram embraces him, asks how he kept his goodness among the cruel, describes the devotee who ties every thread of love to him, and crowns him king, shyly giving what Ravana got for ten heads.
prasang.lesson: The turning itself is enough to be taken in; your past is not the deciding question.

tulsi_1.speaker: Ram
tulsi_1.setting: Lakshman lies struck down; Ram, exhausted, speaks to Sugriva.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: मेरो सब पुरुषारथ थाको। बिपति बँटावन बंधु-बाहु बिनु करौं भरोसो काको॥ … गिरि, कानन जैहें साखा-मृग, हौं पुनि अनुज-सँघाती। ह्वैहै कहा बिभीषनकी गति रही सोच भरि छाती॥
tulsi_1.translation: All my strength is spent. Without my brother's arm to share my trouble, whom can I rely on? The monkeys will go back to their hills and forests, and I will go with my brother; but my chest is full of one worry: what will become of Vibhishan?
tulsi_1.line: All my strength is spent. And still my chest is full of worry for the one who came to me.
tulsi_1.misuse: Devotion is not a promise of a specific outcome, and it doesn't replace medical, legal or emotional help.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_1.our_note: Gitavali: my whole purushartha is exhausted; without a brother's arm to share calamity, on whom shall I rely; the monkeys will return to the hills and I shall follow my brother, but my breast is full of care for Vibhishan's fate.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas describes Hanuman's nature.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: कुलिस-कठोरतनु जोरपै रोर रन, करुना-कलित मन धारमिक धीरको॥ दुर्जजको कालसो कराल पाल सज्जनको, सुमरि हरनहार तुलसीकी पीरको। सीय-सुखदायक दुलारो रघुनायको, सेवक सहायक है साहसी समीरको॥
tulsi_1.translation: A body hard as a thunderbolt, a roar in battle, yet a mind full of compassion, righteous and steady. Terrible to the wicked, protector of the good: remembering him takes away Tulsi's pain. Giver of joy to Sita, darling of Raghunayak, the brave son of the wind is the helper of servants.
tulsi_1.line: A body like iron, a heart full of compassion. Remembering him eases my pain.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_1.our_note: Hanuman Bahuk: body hard as vajra, a roar in battle, a mind adorned with karuna, righteous and steady; death to the wicked, guardian of the good; remembered, he removes Tulsi's pain.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas on those who keep Hanuman's call in their heart.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: बालक-ज्यों पालिहें कृपालु मुनि सिद्ध ताको, जाके हिये हुलसति हाँक हनुमानकी॥
tulsi_1.translation: The kind sages and perfected ones will care for him like a child, in whose heart Hanuman's war-cry rings with joy.
tulsi_1.line: Whoever keeps that brave call in their heart will be cared for like a child.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha in the same scan (meaning only) + own reading
tulsi_1.our_note: Hanuman Bahuk: gracious munis and siddhas will rear like a child him in whose heart Hanuman's shout exults.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas on what Hanuman's name does to fear.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: संकट सोच सबै तुलसी लिये नाम फटै मकरीके-से जाले।
tulsi_1.translation: Tulsi says: all troubles and worries tear apart like spider webs when your name is taken.
tulsi_1.line: Troubles and worries tear like cobwebs when you call on the one you trust.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha in the same scan (meaning only) + own reading
tulsi_1.our_note: Hanuman Bahuk: Tulsi says all sankat and soch burst like a spider's web on taking your name.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas on what Hanuman is to him.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: रामके गुलामनिको कामतरु रामदूत, मोसे दीन दूबरेको तकिया तिहारिये॥
tulsi_1.translation: Messenger of Ram, wishing tree for Ram's servants: for a poor, weak one like me, you are the pillow I lean on.
tulsi_1.line: For someone as weak as me, you are the pillow I lean on.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_1.our_note: Hanuman Bahuk: Ram's envoy, wishing tree to Ram's slaves, for one deen and weak like me the bolster is yours alone.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas remembers his begging childhood.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: टूकनिको घर-घर डोलत कंगाल बोलि, बाल ज्यों कृपाल नतपाल पालि पोसो है। कोन्ही है संभार सार अंजनीकुमार बीर, आपनो बिसारिं न मेरेहू भरोसो है॥
tulsi_1.translation: A beggar going house to house for scraps: the kind protector of those who bow called me and raised me like his own child. Brave son of Anjani, you took care of me; do not forget your own, I trust in you too.
tulsi_1.line: I went door to door for scraps. You called me and raised me like your own child.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_1.our_note: Hanuman Bahuk: a pauper roaming house to house for morsels, the gracious guardian called and reared me like a child; brave son of Anjani, you took charge; do not forget your own, my trust is in you.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas in severe pain in his arm.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: औषध अनेक जंंत्र-मंत्र-टोटकादि किये, बदि भये देवता मनाये अधिकाति है॥ … चेरो तेरो तुलसी तू मेरो कह्यो रामदूत, ढील तेरी बीर मोहि पीरतें पिराति है॥
tulsi_1.translation: I tried many medicines, charms and remedies, prayed to the gods; it only got worse. Tulsi is your servant; you said 'you are mine', messenger of Ram. Your delay hurts me more than the pain.
tulsi_1.line: I've tried every medicine; it keeps getting worse. Your delay hurts more than the pain.
tulsi_1.misuse: An honest prayer in illness, not advice to stop treatment. Devotion is not a promise of a particular outcome, and it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_1.our_note: Hanuman Bahuk: I did many medicines, yantras, mantras and charms, entreated the gods, and it only increases; Tulsi is your slave and you called him yours; your slackness, hero, pains me more than the pain.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas, ill, asks Hanuman for one gentle gesture.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: तुलसीके माथेपर हाथ फेरो कीसनाथ, देखिये न दास दुखी तोसे कनिगरके॥
tulsi_1.translation: Lord of the monkeys, stroke Tulsi's head with your hand. With a protector like you, let your servant not be seen in pain.
tulsi_1.line: Put your hand on my head. Let me not be left alone in this pain.
tulsi_1.misuse: Prayer is company in pain, not a substitute for medical care.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha in the same scan (meaning only) + own reading
tulsi_1.our_note: Hanuman Bahuk: lord of monkeys, pass your hand over Tulsi's head; with a guardian like you, do not look on while your servant suffers.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas, old and in agony from a painful arm, prays to Hanuman.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: अंबु तू हौं अंबुचर, अंब तू हौं डिंभ, सो न, बूझिये बिलंब अवलंब मेरे तेरिये। बालक बिकल जानि पाहि प्रेम पहिचानि, तुलसीकी बाह पर लामीलूम फेरिये॥
tulsi_1.translation: You are the water and I the fish; you are the mother and I the baby. So do not delay, for you are my only support. Knowing the child is in distress, protect him; recognise the love, and stroke Tulsi's aching arm with your long tail.
tulsi_1.line: You are the water and I the fish; you the mother, I the child. Stroke the place that hurts.
tulsi_1.misuse: Prayer is company in pain, not a substitute for medical care.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha in the same scan (meaning only) + own reading
tulsi_1.our_note: Hanuman Bahuk: you are water and I the water creature, you mother and I the child; do not delay, my support is you alone; knowing the child distressed, protect him and pass your long tail over Tulsi's arm.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas admits the wrong turns of his life.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: खोटे-खोटे आचरन आचरत अपनायो, अंजनीकुमार सोध्यो रामपानि पाक हौं।
tulsi_1.translation: Even while I did bad things, you took me as your own; son of Anjani, you cleansed me and made me fit for Ram's hand.
tulsi_1.line: Even while I was doing wrong, you took me as your own and made me fit for Ram.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_1.our_note: Hanuman Bahuk: though I practised base conduct you made me your own; son of Anjani, you purified me and I became fit for Ram's hand.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas on how Ram treats his people's faults.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: अपराध अगाध भएँ जनते, अपने उर आनत नाहिन जू।
tulsi_1.translation: Even when his people commit faults beyond measure, he does not take them into his heart.
tulsi_1.line: Even when we fail beyond measure, he does not hold it in his heart.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_1.our_note: Kavitavali: though his servant's offences be fathomless, he does not bring them into his heart. Same proposition as Manas 1.27, 'rahati na prabhu chit chuk kiye ki'.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas on Ram's way with the hurting.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: आरत, दीन, अनाथनको रघुनाथु करैं निज हाथकी छाहें॥
tulsi_1.translation: For the hurting, the poor and those with no one, Raghunath makes shade with his own hand.
tulsi_1.line: For the hurting and the alone, he makes shade with his own hand.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_1.our_note: Kavitavali: for the arta, the deen and the anath, Raghunath makes the shade of his own hand.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas names everything Ram is to him.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: रामु हैं मातु, पिता, गुरु, बंधु, औ संगी, सखा, सुतु, स्वामि, सनेही। रामको सौंह, भरोसो है रामको, राम रंँग्यो, रुचि राच्यो न केही॥
tulsi_1.translation: Ram is my mother, father, teacher, brother, companion, friend, son, master and beloved. I swear by Ram, my trust is in Ram; I am coloured by Ram, and my heart is taken by no one else.
tulsi_1.line: Ram is my mother, father, teacher, brother, friend, child and beloved. My trust is in him.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_1.our_note: Kavitavali: Ram is mother, father, guru, brother, companion, friend, son, master and lover; by Ram's oath, my reliance is on Ram; dyed in Ram, my liking delights in none else.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas on what life is for, in his own view.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: मति रामहि सों, गति रामहि सों, रति रामसों, रामहि को बलु है। सबकी न कहै, तुलसीके मतें इतनो जग जीवनको फलु है॥
tulsi_1.translation: My mind is with Ram, my goal is with Ram, my love is for Ram, Ram is my strength. I don't speak for everyone; in Tulsi's view, this much is the fruit of living in the world.
tulsi_1.line: I don't speak for everyone. For me, this is the fruit of a life: my heart with Ram.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_1.our_note: Kavitavali: understanding in Ram, refuge in Ram, love for Ram, strength from Ram; I do not speak for all, in Tulsi's opinion this much is the fruit of life in the world.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas recalls Prahlad, unharmed by poison, fire and elephants.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: नेकु बिषादु नहीं प्रहलादहि कारन केहरिके बल हो रे। कौनकी त्रास करै तुलसी जो पै राखिहै राम, तौ मारिहै को रे॥
tulsi_1.translation: Prahlad felt not the least despair, because of the strength of the man-lion. Whom should Tulsi fear? If Ram protects, who can kill?
tulsi_1.line: If Ram is protecting, whom should I fear?
tulsi_1.misuse: Devotion is not a promise of a particular outcome, and it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_1.our_note: Kavitavali: Prahlad had not the least vishada, by the strength of the lion; whom shall Tulsi dread, if Ram will keep, who will kill.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas imagines being lost in a wilderness of dangers.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: संकट कोटि जहाँ 'तुलसी', सुत, मातु, पिता, हित, बंधु न नेरे॥ राखिहैँ रामु कृपालु तहाँ, हनुमानु-से सेवक हैं जेहि केरे। नाक, रसातल, भूतलमें रघुनायकु एकु सहायकु मेरे॥
tulsi_1.translation: Where there are a million dangers, Tulsi, and no son, mother, father, friend or kin is near, kind Ram will protect you there, he who has a servant like Hanuman. In heaven, the underworld or on earth, Raghunayak is my one helper.
tulsi_1.line: Where a million dangers surround you and no family is near, he is still there, with Hanuman.
tulsi_1.misuse: Devotion is not a promise of a particular outcome, and it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_1.our_note: Kavitavali: where there are a crore of dangers and neither son, mother, father, friend nor kin is near, gracious Ram, who has servants like Hanuman, will keep you; Raghunayak alone is my helper.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas imagines the hour when no friend or family can come along.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: जहाँ हित स्वामि, न संग सखा, बनिता, सुत, बंधु, न बापु, न मैया। काय-गिरा-मनके जनके अपराध सबै छलु छाडि छमैया॥ तुलसी! तेहि काल कृपाल बिना दूजो कौन है दारुन दुःख दमैया॥ जहाँ सब संकट, दुर्घट सोचु, तहाँ मेरो साहेबु राखे रमैया॥
tulsi_1.translation: Where there is no kind master, no friend beside you, no wife, son, brother, father or mother, there is one who forgives every fault of body, word and mind, without holding back. Tulsi, at that time who but the kind one can calm the terrible pain? Where everything is crisis and the worry seems impossible, there my master Ram keeps me.
tulsi_1.line: Where everything is crisis and the worry seems impossible, there I am still kept.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in the same scan + Wikisource 1933 edition text and arth
tulsi_1.our_note: Kavitavali: where there is no kind master, no companion, wife, son, brother, father or mother, who but the gracious one quells the dreadful pain; where all is sankat, there my lord Ram keeps me. Read of the hour of death.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas on his own childhood: abandoned at birth, he grew up begging.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: मातु-पिताँ जग जाइ तज्यो बिधिहूँ न लिखी कछु भाल भलाई। नीच, निरादरभाजन, कादर, कूकर-टूकन लागि ललाई॥ रामु-सुभाउ सुन्यो तुलसीं प्रभुसों कह्यो बारक पेटु खलाई। स्वारथको परमारथको रघुनाथु सो साहेबु, खोरि न लाई॥
tulsi_1.translation: My mother and father brought me into the world and left me; fate wrote nothing good on my forehead. Lowly, scorned, timid, I hungered like a dog for scraps. Then Tulsi heard of Ram's nature and, just once, showed the Lord his empty stomach. Such a master is Raghunath that he held nothing back, in this world or the next.
tulsi_1.line: Abandoned as a child, he poured out his hunger just once, and was held.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in the same scan + Wikisource 1933 edition text and arth
tulsi_1.our_note: Kavitavali, Uttarakand: mother and father bore and abandoned me, fate wrote no good on my brow; low, scorned, cowardly, craving a dog's morsels. Hearing Ram's nature, Tulsi once showed his belly, and Raghunath proved master for both worlds.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas describes his own life before grace.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: उँचो मनु, ऊँची रुचि, भागु नीचो निपट ही, लोकरीति-लायक न, लंगर लबारु है। स्वारथु अगमु, परमारथकी कहा चली, पेटकी कठिन जगु जीवको जबारु है॥ चाकरी न आकरी, न खेती, न बनिज-भीरख, जानत न कूर कछु किसब कबारु है। तुलसीकी बाजी राखी रामहीकें नाम,
tulsi_1.translation: A high mind, high tastes, and very low luck; no good at worldly ways, a stubborn talker. Selfish gain was out of reach, never mind higher goals; the belly's demands are hard on every living being. No job, no mine, no farm, no trade, no begging; the fool knows no craft or skill. Tulsi's game was saved by Ram's name alone.
tulsi_1.line: High hopes, low luck, no job, no trade, no skill. The name of Ram saved my game.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_1.our_note: Kavitavali: mind high, tastes high, luck wholly low; unfit for worldly custom; no service, no mine, no farming, no trade or alms, the dolt knows no craft; Tulsi's wager was kept by Ram's name.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas remembers a childhood of hunger, wandering door to door.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: जायो कुल मंगन, बधावनो बजायो, सुनि भयो परितापु पापु जननी-जनकको। बारेतें ललात-बिललात द्वार-द्वार दीन, जानत हो चारि फल चारि ही चनकको॥ तुलसी सो साहेब समर्थको सुसेवकु है, सुनत सिहात सोचु बिधिहू गनकको। नामु राम! रावरो सयानो किधौं बावरो, जो करत गिरीतें गरु तृनतें तनकको॥
tulsi_1.translation: Born into a family of beggars, my birth brought my parents only grief. From childhood I wandered door to door, wailing with want, thinking four grains of chickpea were the four great goals of life. Now that same Tulsi is the trusted servant of a mighty master, and even the stars' accountant is amazed. Ram, is your name clever or mad, that it makes one lighter than a straw heavier than a mountain?
tulsi_1.line: He once thought four chickpeas were everything. Grace made someone lighter than straw weigh more than a mountain.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in the same scan + Wikisource 1933 edition text and arth
tulsi_1.our_note: Kavitavali: born in a begging line, my birth was pain to mother and father; from infancy wretched at every door, knowing four grams as the four fruits; that Tulsi is now the good servant of an able lord. Is your name wise or mad, Ram.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Prahlad, his father's sword raised over him.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: काढ़ि कृपान, कृपा न कहूँ, पितु काल कराल बिलोकि न भागे। “राम कहाँ ?' “सब ठाउँ हें', 'खंभमें ?' ' हा' सुनि हाँक नृकेहरि जागे॥
tulsi_1.translation: Sword drawn, no mercy anywhere, the boy did not run on seeing his terrible father. 'Where is Ram?' 'Everywhere.' 'In this pillar?' 'Yes.' Hearing that cry, the man-lion awoke.
tulsi_1.line: 'Where is your God?' 'Everywhere.' 'In this pillar?' 'Yes.'
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_1.our_note: Kavitavali: sword drawn and no mercy anywhere, he did not flee seeing his father terrible as death. Where is Ram? Everywhere. In the pillar? Yes. At that shout Narasimha awoke.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas on where Ram can be found.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: आरतपाल कृपाल जो रामु जेहीं सुमिरे तेहिको तहँ ठाढ़े।
tulsi_1.translation: Kind Ram, protector of the hurting: wherever anyone remembers him, there he stands.
tulsi_1.line: Wherever anyone remembers him, there he stands.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_1.our_note: Kavitavali: gracious Ram, guardian of the arta, stands there for whoever remembers him, wherever that is.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas on how Ram responds to his name.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: अंतरजामिहुतें बड़े बाहेरजामि हैं राम, जे नाम लियेतें। धावत धेनु पेन्हाइ लवाई ज्यों बालक-बोलनि कान कियेतें॥
tulsi_1.translation: Greater than the Ram who dwells within is the Ram outside, who comes when his name is called: he runs the way a cow runs, milk flowing, when she hears her calf's cry.
tulsi_1.line: Call his name and he comes running, like a cow who hears her calf cry.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_1.our_note: Kavitavali: greater than the antaryami is the Ram outside who comes on the taking of his name, running like a new-calved cow at the sound of her calf.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas, in a pada to Hanuman.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: सुमिरत संकट-सोच-व्रिमोचन, मूरति मोद-निधानकी॥ … तुलसी कपिकी कृपा-बिलोकनि, खानि सकल कल्यानकी॥
tulsi_1.translation: Remembering him frees one from trouble and worry; his form is a treasury of joy. Tulsi says: the monkey's kind glance is a mine of every blessing.
tulsi_1.line: Remember him and worry loosens. His kind glance is a mine of blessings.
tulsi_1.misuse: Devotion is not a promise of a particular outcome, and it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_1.our_note: Vinay Patrika hymn to Hanuman: remembered, he frees from sankat and soch, an image that is a treasury of delight; the monkey's gracious look is a mine of all welfare.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas asks Hanuman to forgive what he said in distress.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: अति आरत, अति स्वारथी, अति दीन-दुखारी। इनको बिलगु न मानिये, बोलहिं न बिचारी॥ … नाकहि आये नाथसों, साँसति भय भारी। कहि आयो, कीबी छमा, निज ओर निहारी॥
tulsi_1.translation: The very distressed, the very needy, the very poor and hurting: do not take offence at them; they speak without thinking. I had reached my limit, Lord; the suffering and fear were heavy. I said what I said; forgive me, looking at it from your side.
tulsi_1.line: Don't hold it against the hurting; they speak without thinking. Forgive me, looking from your side.
tulsi_1.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_1.our_note: Tulsidas to Hanuman: the very distressed, the very needy, the very wretched, do not mind them, they speak unthinking; I was at my limit, Lord, and said it; forgive, looking to your own nature.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas, after complaining harshly to Hanuman.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: कटु कहिये गाढे परे, सुनि समुझि सुसाई। करहिं अनभलेउ को भलो, आपनी भलाई॥
tulsi_1.translation: In hard straits one says bitter things; a good master hears, understands, and out of his own goodness does good even to the one who wronged him.
tulsi_1.line: In hard times we say bitter things. A good master understands and does good anyway.
tulsi_1.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_1.our_note: Tulsidas: hard pressed, one says bitter things; the good master hears and understands, and by his own goodness does good even to the ill-doer.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas urges his own mind to remember the name.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: सुमिरु सनेहसों तू नाम रामरायको। संबल निसंबलको, सखा असहायको॥ १॥ भाग है अभागेहूको, गुन गुनहीनको। गाहक गरीबको, दयालु दानि दीनको॥ २॥ कुल अकुलीनको, सुन्यो है बेद साखि है। पाँगुरेको हाथ-पाँय, आँधरेको आँखि है॥३॥ माय-बाप भूखेको, अधार निराधारको।
tulsi_1.translation: Remember with love the name of King Ram: provision for the one with none, friend of the helpless; the fortune of the unfortunate, the merit of the meritless, a buyer for the poor, the kind giver to the needy; family for the one without family, the Veda bears witness; hands and feet for the lame, eyes for the blind; mother and father for the hungry, a support for the one with no support.
tulsi_1.line: Friend of the helpless, luck of the unlucky, mother and father to the hungry: remember that name.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_1.our_note: Tulsidas to his mind: remember with love the name of King Ram, provision of the unprovided, friend of the helpless, fortune of the luckless, lineage of the low-born, limbs of the lame, eyes of the blind, mother and father of the hungry.

tulsi_1.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_1.setting: Tulsidas, looking back at his failings, on why he was not abandoned.
tulsi_1.sanskrit: मेरो भलो कियो राम आपनी भलाई। हौं तो साई-द्रोही पै सेवक-हित साई॥ पाथ माथे चढ़े तृन तुलसी ज्यों नीचो। बोरत न बारि ताहि जानि आपु सींचो॥
tulsi_1.translation: Ram did me good out of his own goodness. I have wronged my master, yet my master is good to his servant. Tulsi is as low as a blade of grass floating on the water; the water does not drown it, knowing it was the water that made it grow.
tulsi_1.line: Water does not drown the grass it once watered. The one who raised you will not let you sink.
tulsi_1.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
tulsi_1.our_note: Tulsidas: Ram did me good by his own goodness; I am a traitor to my master, yet he is good to his servant. Water does not sink the straw riding on its head, knowing it watered it.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas remembers how Ram first took him in.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: बूझ्यौ ज्यौ ही, कह्यो, मैं हूँ चेरो ह्वैहौ रावरो जू मेरो कोऊ कहूँ नाहि, चरन गहत हों। मींजो गुरु पीठ, अपनाइ गहि बाँह, बोलि सेबक-सुखद, सदा बिरद बहत हाौं॥
tulsi_2.translation: The moment he asked, I said: 'I will be your servant; I have no one anywhere,' and I held his feet. Like a teacher he patted my back, took me by the arm and made me his own, and called me; ever the one who gives joy to servants, he carries that name.
tulsi_2.line: I said: I have no one anywhere. He patted my back, took my arm, and made me his own.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas recalls his acceptance: as soon as asked I said I will be your slave, I have no one anywhere, and I hold your feet; he stroked my back like a guru, took my arm and owned me.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas ends a petition asking for only one thing.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: तू गरीबको निवाज, हौं गरीब तेरो। बारक कहिये कृपालु! तुलसिदास मेरो॥
tulsi_2.translation: You are the one who lifts up the poor, and I am your poor one. Kind one, say it just once: "Tulsidas is mine."
tulsi_2.line: You lift up the poor, and I am yours. Just say it once: "You are mine."
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: you are garib nivaj and I am your garib; gracious one, say once, Tulsidas is mine.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas, in his book of petitions to Ram, lists every bond between them.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: तू दयालु, दीन हौं, तू दानि, हौं भिखारी । हौं प्रसिद्ध पातकी, तू पाप-पुंज-हारी॥ नाथ तू अनाथको, अनाथ कौन मोसो। मो समान आरत नहिं, आरतिहर तोसो॥ ब्रह्म तू, हौं जीव, तू है ठाकुर, हौं चेरो। तात-मात, गुरु-सखा, तू सब बिधि हितु मेरो॥ तोहिं मोहिं नाते अनेक, मानियै जो भावै। ज्यों त्यों तुलसी कृपालु! चरन-सरन पावै॥
tulsi_2.translation: You are kind and I am in need; you give and I am a beggar. I am a known wrongdoer and you lift heaps of wrong. Lord, you shelter those who have no one, and who has less than I do? No one hurts as I do, and no one heals hurt as you do. You are the infinite, I a small life; you the master, I the servant. Father and mother, teacher and friend: you wish me well in every way. There are many bonds between us; take whichever one pleases you. Only let Tulsi, somehow, find shelter at your feet.
tulsi_2.line: Father, mother, teacher, friend: you are mine in every way. Choose any bond, only keep me close.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: you are compassionate and I wretched, you giver and I beggar, I a famed sinner and you destroyer of sin's heap, you Brahman and I jiva, you master and I slave, father, mother, guru, friend; take whichever tie pleases you.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: One of the best-known bhajans of the Vinay Patrika.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: जाउँ कहाँ तजि चरन तुम्हारे। काको नाम पतित-पावन जग, केहि अति दीन पियारे॥
tulsi_2.translation: Where would I go, leaving your feet? Whose name in the world is "the one who lifts the fallen"? To whom are the lowliest so very dear?
tulsi_2.line: Where would I go but to you? Who else holds the fallen so dear?
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: where shall I go leaving your feet; whose name in the world is patit pavan, to whom are the very deen dear.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas thanks God, then asks for one more thing.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: हरि! तुम बहुत अनुग्रह कीन्हों। साधन-धाम विबुध दुरलभ तनु, मोहि कृपा करि दीन्हों॥ … तुलसिदास येहि जीव मोह-रजु, जेहि बाँध्यो सोइ छोरै॥
tulsi_2.translation: Hari, you have been very kind: out of grace you gave me this body, home of every practice, which even the gods find hard to get. Tulsidas says: the rope of delusion that binds this soul, only the one who tied it can untie.
tulsi_2.line: The one who tied this knot is the one who can untie it.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: Hari, you showed great favour, giving me this body, abode of sadhana, rare even for gods; the rope of moha that binds this jiva only he who bound can loose.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas's prayer for steady love.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: यह बिनती रघुबीर गुसाई। और आस-बिस्वास-भरोसो, हरो जीव-जड़ताई॥ … कुटिल करम लै जाहि मोहि जहँ जहँ अपनी बरिआई। तहँँ तहँ जनि छिन छोह छाँड़ियो, कमठ-अंडकी नाई॥
tulsi_2.translation: This is my prayer, Raghubir, master: take away every other hope, trust and reliance, and the dullness of this soul. Wherever my crooked karma drags me by force, there do not leave off your care even for a moment, as the tortoise keeps watch over its eggs.
tulsi_2.line: Wherever my mistakes drag me, don't stop watching over me, as the tortoise watches her eggs.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: this is my petition, Raghuvir: take away other hope, trust and reliance and the jiva's dullness; wherever crooked karma forcibly carries me, do not for an instant leave off your affection, like the tortoise with her eggs.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas, after years he feels were lost, resolves to begin again.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: अबलों नसानी, अब न नसैहौं। राम-कृपा भव-निसा सिरानी, जागे फिरि न डसैहौं॥
tulsi_2.translation: Till now it has been wasted; from now it will not be. By Ram's grace the long night is over. Now that I am awake, I will not spread the bed of sleep again.
tulsi_2.line: What is lost is lost, but the night is over. Awake now, I begin again.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas's vow: till now it was ruined, now I will not ruin it; by Ram's kripa the night of worldliness has ended, and having woken I will not spread the bedding again.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas complains that greed, anger and pride have broken into his heart.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: मम हृदय भवन प्रभु तोरा।तहँ बसे आइ बहु चोरा॥ … कह तुलसिदास सुनु रामा।लूटहिं तसकर तव धामा॥ ८॥ चिंता यह मोहिं अपारा। अपजस नहिं होइ तुम्हारा॥
tulsi_2.translation: My heart is your house, Lord, and many thieves have come and settled in it. Tulsidas says: listen, Ram, thieves are looting your home; my great worry is only that it will give you a bad name.
tulsi_2.line: My heart is your house, and thieves have moved in. Come and see to your own home.
tulsi_2.misuse: Surrender comes after doing your part and reflecting (Gita 18.63), not instead of it.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: my heart is your dwelling, Lord, and many thieves have come to live there, robbing your abode; my endless care is only that no ill fame come to you.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas longs for Ram's hand on his head.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: कबहुँ सो कर-सरोज रघुनायक ! धरिहौ नाथ सीस मेरे। जेहि कर अभय किये जन आरत, बारक बिबस नाम टेरे॥ … सीतल सुखद छाँह जेहि करकी, मेटति पाप, ताप, माया। निसि-बासर तेहि कर सरोजकी, चाहत तुलसिदास छाया॥
tulsi_2.translation: Will you ever place that lotus hand on my head, Raghunayak, the hand that made the distressed fearless when they once called your name helplessly? The cool, comforting shade of that hand removes wrongdoing, pain and illusion; day and night Tulsidas longs for the shade of that lotus hand.
tulsi_2.line: Will you ever rest that hand on my head? Day and night I long for its shade.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: when, Raghunayak, will you lay on my head that lotus hand which made the afflicted fearless when they once called your name; night and day Tulsidas desires its cool shade.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas on what hostility can and cannot do to one who is held.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: जो पै कृपा रघुपति कृपालुकी, बैर औरके कहा सरै। होइ न बाँको बार भगतको, जो कोउ कोटि उपाय करे॥
tulsi_2.translation: If the kind Raghupati's grace is with you, what can anyone's enmity achieve? Not a hair of the devotee is bent, though someone tries a million schemes.
tulsi_2.line: When grace is with you, others' ill will cannot even bend a hair.
tulsi_2.misuse: Not a promise that harm never happens; a reassurance to steady fear.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: if the grace of gracious Raghupati is there, what can another's enmity accomplish; not a hair of the bhakta is bent though one try a crore of devices.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas reminds Ram of everyone he has sheltered.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: सो धौ को जो नाम-लाज तें, नहिं राख्यो रघुबीर। कारुनीक बिनु कारन ही हरि हरी सकल भव-भीर॥
tulsi_2.translation: Who is there that Raghubir did not keep safe, for the honour of his name? The compassionate one, for no reason at all, takes away the whole crowd of fears.
tulsi_2.line: The compassionate one needs no reason to take your fears away.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: who is there whom Raghuvir did not keep for his name's honour; the compassionate Hari, causelessly, took away the whole press of worldly fear.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas explains why he both worries and doesn't.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: रामभद्र! मोहिं आपनो सोच है अरु नाहीं। जीव सकल संतापके भाजन जग माहीं॥ १॥ नातो बड़े समर्थ सों इक ओर किधौं हूँ तोको मोसे अति घने मोको एकै तूँ॥
tulsi_2.translation: Ramabhadra, I worry about myself, and I don't. Every soul in the world is a vessel of suffering. On one side is my bond with the great and mighty one, and on the other, I: you have many like me, but I have only you.
tulsi_2.line: I worry about myself, and I don't. You have many like me; I have only you.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: Ramabhadra, I have care for myself and have not; all jivas in the world are vessels of affliction; you have very many like me, I have only you.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas finds, almost playfully, a reason for hope in his own failings.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: मैं हरि पतित-पावन सुने। मैं पतित तुम पतित-पावन दोउ बानक बने॥
tulsi_2.translation: Hari, I have heard you are the one who lifts the fallen. I am fallen and you lift the fallen: the two of us are a perfect match.
tulsi_2.line: I have fallen, and you lift the fallen. We are a perfect match.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas with a devotee's boldness: I have heard Hari is patit pavan; I am patit and you patit pavan, so both our parts are made.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: A famous bhajan on a love that asks nothing in return.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: ऐसो को उदार जग माहीं। बिनु सेवा जो द्रवै दीनपर राम सरिस कोउ नाहीं॥
tulsi_2.translation: Who in the world is so generous? There is none like Ram, who melts for the suffering without any service done.
tulsi_2.line: Who else melts for the hurting without asking anything first?
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: who in the world is so udar; there is none like Ram, who is moved toward the deen without seva.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas on what makes Ram's court different.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: रघुबर! रावरि यहै बड़ाई। निदरि गनी आदर गरीबपर, करत कृपा अधिकाई॥ … यहि दरबार दीनको आदर, रीति सदा चलि आई
tulsi_2.translation: Raghubar, this is your greatness: passing over the rich, you honour the poor and show them more kindness. In this court the poor are respected; that has always been the custom here.
tulsi_2.line: In his court the rich are passed over and the poor are honoured. It has always been so.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: Raghuvar, this is your glory: slighting the wealthy you honour the poor and show them greater grace; in this darbar the deen are respected, the custom from of old.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas opens a list of those Ram embraced: Ahalya, Guha, Jatayu, Shabari.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: ऐसे राम-दीन हितकारी । अतिकोमल करुनानिधान बिनु कारन पर-उपकारी॥
tulsi_2.translation: Such is Ram, the well-wisher of the lowly: utterly tender, a treasury of compassion, doing good to others without any reason.
tulsi_2.line: Utterly tender, full of compassion, doing good without needing a reason.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas opens the list of Ahalya, Guha, Jatayu and Shabari: such is Ram, benefactor of the deen, very tender, treasury of karuna, helper of others without cause.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas admits devotion is hard to live.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: रघुपति-भगति करत कठिनाई । कहत सुगम करनी अपार जानै सोइ जेहि बनि आई॥
tulsi_2.translation: Devotion to Raghupati is hard to practise. It is easy to talk about, but the doing is endless; only the one in whom it has taken root knows.
tulsi_2.line: Devotion is easy to talk about and hard to live. Only those who live it know.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: the bhakti of Raghupati is hard in the doing; easy to tell, its practice is boundless, and he alone knows it to whom it has come.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas describes the life he hopes Ram's grace will one day give him.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: कबहुँक हौं यहि रहनि रहौंगो। श्रीरघुनाथ-कृपालु-कृपातें संत-सुभाव गहौंगो॥ ९॥ जथालाभसंतोष सदा, काहू सों कछु न चहांगो। पर-हित-निरत निरंतर, मन क्रम बचन नेम निबहौंगो॥ … परुष बचन अति दुसह श्रवन सुनि तेहि पावक न दहांगो। बिगत मान, सम सीतल मन, पर-गुन नहिं दोष कहाँगो॥ ३॥ परिहरि देह-जनित चिंता, दुख-सुख समबुद्धि सहोंगो।
tulsi_2.translation: Will I ever live like this? By the grace of kind Raghunath, will I take on the nature of a saint: always content with what comes, wanting nothing from anyone, always devoted to others' good, keeping my vow in mind, deed and word; hearing very harsh words and not burning in that fire; free of pride, even and cool of mind, speaking of others' virtues and not their faults; letting go of the body's worries, bearing joy and sorrow with an even mind?
tulsi_2.line: Will I ever live like this: content, kind, cool when insulted, speaking of others' good, not their faults?
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: will I ever live in this way, by Raghunath's grace taking on a saint's nature: content with what is gained, intent on others' good, unburnt by harsh speech, prideless, cool, bearing dukh and sukh alike.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas's vow of love.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: जो तुम त्यागों राम हौं तौ नहिं त्यागो । परिहरि पाँय काहि अनुरागों॥ … हौं तो कुजाचक, स्वामी सुदाता । हौं कुपूत, तुम हितु पितु-माता॥
tulsi_2.translation: Even if you leave me, Ram, I will not leave you; leaving your feet, whom would I love? I am a poor beggar and you the good giver; I am a bad son, and you my loving father and mother.
tulsi_2.line: Even if you leave me, Ram, I won't leave you. You are my father and mother.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: if you forsake me, Ram, I will not forsake you; leaving your feet whom shall I love; I am a bad beggar and you the good giver, I a bad son and you my well-wishing father and mother.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas, feeling he has no one to tell, speaks to Ram.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: कहाँ जाउँ, कासों कहौं, कौन सुने दीनकी। त्रिभुवन तुही गति सब अंगहीनकी॥ जग जगदीस घर धरनि घनेरे हैं। निराधारके अधार गुनगन तेरे हैं॥
tulsi_2.translation: Where do I go, whom do I tell, who will listen to someone so low? In all three worlds you alone are the way for the one who has lost every support. The world is full of would-be lords in every house, but your goodness is the support of those who have none.
tulsi_2.line: Where do I go, whom do I tell? You are the support of those who have none.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: where shall I go, whom tell, who hears the lowly; in the three worlds you alone are the refuge of the helpless; lords are many in the world, but your virtues are the support of the supportless.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas compares himself to Sugriva, hiding from Bali.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: केहू भाँति कृपासिंधु मेरी ओर हेरिये। मोको और ठौर न, सुटेक एक तेरिये॥ … करम-कपीस बालि-बली, त्रास-त्रस्यो हौं। चाहत अनाथ-नाथ! तेरी बाह बस्यो हौं॥
tulsi_2.translation: Somehow, ocean of kindness, look my way; I have no other place, my one firm support is you. Like Sugriva terrified of mighty Bali, I am terrified of my karma; lord of the helpless, I want to live in the shelter of your arm.
tulsi_2.line: Like Sugriva hiding from Bali, I'm afraid. Somehow, look my way; let me live under your arm.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: somehow, ocean of grace, look toward me, I have no other place; karma is the monkey-king Bali and I am terrified; lord of the lordless, I want to dwell under your arm.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas, out of ideas, leaves it to Ram.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: बाप! बलि जाउँ, आप करिये उपाउ सो। तेरे ही निहारे परै हारेहू सुदाउ सो॥४॥ तेरे ही सुझाये सूझै असुझ सुझाउ सो। तेरे ही बुझाये बूझै अबुझ बुझाउ सो॥
tulsi_2.translation: Father, I give myself to you: you find the way. By your glance alone a losing throw becomes a winning one; by your showing, what cannot be seen is seen; by your explaining, what cannot be understood is understood.
tulsi_2.line: By your glance a losing throw turns into a winning one.
tulsi_2.misuse: Devotion is not a promise of a particular outcome, and it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: father, I am your sacrifice, you devise the means; at your mere glance a lost throw falls well; by your showing the unseeable is seen, by your teaching the unknowable known.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas on how Ram's love levels everyone.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: राम! प्रीतिकी रीति आप नीके जनियत है। बड़ेकी बड़ाई, छोटेकी छोटाई दूरि करै, ऐसी बिरुदावली, बलि, बेद मनियत है॥
tulsi_2.translation: Ram, you know the ways of love well. The Vedas praise you as the one who takes away the bigness of the big and the smallness of the small.
tulsi_2.line: Love takes away the bigness of the big and the smallness of the small.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: Ram, you know well the manner of love; the Veda honours your fame as one who removes the bigness of the big and the littleness of the little.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas on what finally cools a heart on fire.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: राम-नामके जपे जाइ जियकी जरनि।
tulsi_2.translation: By repeating Ram's name, the burning of the heart goes away.
tulsi_2.line: Say his name, and slowly the burning in the heart eases.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
tulsi_2.our_note: Vinay Patrika refrain: by japa of Ram nam the jarani of the heart departs.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: A walking song: the road of life as a long, hard journey.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: राम कहत चलु, राम कहत चलु, राम कहत चलु भाई रे। नाहिं तौ भव-बेगारि महँ परिहै, छुटत अति कठिनाई रे॥ … मारग अगम, संग नहिं संबल, नाउँ गाउँकर भूला रे। तुलसिदास भव त्रास हरहु अब, होहु राम अनुकूला रे॥
tulsi_2.translation: Walk on saying Ram, walk on saying Ram, walk on saying Ram, brother; otherwise you'll be caught in the forced labour of the world, and getting free is very hard. The road is hard, there are no provisions with me, I've forgotten the name of my village. Tulsidas says: take away the fear of the world now, be kind to me, Ram.
tulsi_2.line: The road is hard and I've lost my way. Walk on, saying Ram.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas's marching song: go on saying Ram, brother, else you fall into the forced labour of rebirth; the path is impassable, no provision with me, the village's name forgotten; Ram, be favourable now.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas questions a life lived only for oneself.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: लाभ कहा मानुष-तनु पाये। काय-बचन-मन सपनेहुँ कबहुँक घटत न काज पराये॥
tulsi_2.translation: What is gained by getting a human body, if in body, word and mind, not even in a dream, one ever helps with someone else's work?
tulsi_2.line: What is a human life for, if we never help with someone else's load?
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: what gain in having the human body if, by body, speech or mind, even in dream, one is never of use in another's work.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas explains why he keeps bringing his troubles to Ram.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: जो पै दूसरो कोउ होइ। तौ हौं बारहि बार प्रभु कत दुख सुनावौं रोइ॥ … आपसे कहुँ सौंपिये मोहि जो पै अतिहि घिनात। दासतुलसी और बिधि क्यों चरन परिहरि जात॥
tulsi_2.translation: If there were anyone else, why would I keep coming back, Lord, to cry my troubles to you? If you find me too distasteful, then hand me over to someone like yourself. How else could Tulsidas leave your feet?
tulsi_2.line: If there were anyone else, why would I keep coming to you in tears?
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: were there any other, why would I tell you my sorrows weeping again and again; if you loathe me, hand me to one like yourself; how else can Tulsidas leave your feet.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas, in a long dry season, waits.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: नाथ ! कृपाहीको पंथ चितवत दीन हौं दिनराति। होइ धौं केहि काल दीनदयालु ! जानि न जाति॥
tulsi_2.translation: Lord, day and night this poor one watches the road your kindness will come by. Kind to the lowly, when will it be? I cannot tell.
tulsi_2.line: Day and night I watch the road for your kindness. I do not know when, but I wait.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: Lord, wretched, I watch day and night only the path of your grace; at what time it may be, compassionate one, cannot be known.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas on his own trust, without judging anyone else's.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: भरोसो जाहि दूसरो सो करो। मोको तो रामको नाम कलपतरु कलि कल्यान फरो॥ … प्रीति-प्रतीति जहाँ जाकी, तहँ ताको काज सरो। मेरे तो माय-बाप दोउ आखर, हौं सिसु-अरनि अरो॥
tulsi_2.translation: Let whoever trusts something else trust it; for me, Ram's name is the wishing tree that bears good fruit in this age. Where a person's love and trust lie, there their work gets done. For me, those two syllables are mother and father, and I am a stubborn child who has dug in his heels.
tulsi_2.line: Where your love and trust are, your work gets done. For me those two syllables are mother and father.
tulsi_2.misuse: Surrender comes after doing your part and reflecting (Gita 18.63), not instead of it.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: let him who has another reliance keep it; for me Ram's name is the kalpataru fruiting welfare in Kali; where one's love and trust are, there one's work succeeds; those two letters are my mother and father.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas remembers his years as a begging orphan.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: नाम राम रावरोई हित मेरे। स्वारथ-परमारथ साथिन्ह सों भुज उठाइ कहाँ टेरे॥ … फिरयौ ललात बिनु नाम उदर लगि, दुखउ दुखित मोहि हेरे। नाम-प्रसाद लहत रसाल-फल अब हौं बबुर बहेरे॥
tulsi_2.translation: Ram, your name alone is my well-wisher; I say it to all my companions in this life and the next, arms raised. Without the name I wandered, longing for something to fill my belly; even sorrow felt sorry when it looked at me. By the grace of the name, I who was a thorny babul now get mangoes.
tulsi_2.line: I wandered hungry; even sorrow pitied me. By the grace of the name, I now bear sweet fruit.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: your name alone, Ram, is my friend; without it I roamed craving for my belly, and grief itself grieved to see me; by the name's grace I, a babul and bahera, now get mango fruit.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas on whose bread he has lived on.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: गरैगी जीह जो कहौं औरको हौं। जानकी-जीवन! जनम-जनम जग ज्यायो तिहारेहि कौरको हों॥ … तुलसिदास सीतल नित यहि बल, बड़े ठेकाने ठौरको हौं॥
tulsi_2.translation: My tongue would rot if I called myself anyone else's. Life of Janaki, birth after birth in this world I have lived on your morsel. Tulsidas is always at peace on this strength: I belong to a great place.
tulsi_2.line: I am always at peace on this strength: I belong somewhere great.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: my tongue would rot if I called myself another's; life of Janaki, birth after birth I have lived on your morsel; Tulsidas is ever cool in this strength, I am of a great abode.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas on why he brings his sorrow only to Ram.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: दीनबन्धु दूसरो कहँ पावों ? को तुम बिनु पर-पीर पाइ है? केहि दीनता सुनावों॥
tulsi_2.translation: Where would I find another friend of the lowly? Who but you feels another's pain? To whom else would I tell my sorrow?
tulsi_2.line: Who else feels another's pain as their own? To whom else would I tell mine?
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: where shall I find another deenbandhu; who but you feels another's pain; to whom shall I tell my wretchedness.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas on who is truly good in Ram's eyes.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: सोइ सुकृती, सुचि साँचो जाहि राम! तुम रीझे। गनिका, गीध, बधिक हरिपुर गये, लै कासी प्रयाग कब सीझे॥ … तुलसी सहज सनेह राम बस, और सबै जलकी चिकनाई॥
tulsi_2.translation: He alone is virtuous, pure and true with whom you, Ram, are pleased. The courtesan, the vulture and the hunter went to Hari's abode; when were they ever made perfect by Kashi or Prayag? Tulsi says: Ram is won by natural love; everything else is like oil on water.
tulsi_2.line: Ram is won by plain, natural love. Everything else just floats on top.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: he is the doer of good, pure and true with whom you, Ram, are pleased; ganika, gidh and vyadh went to Hari's city, when did they perfect themselves at Kashi or Prayag; Ram is won by sahaj sneh.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Frightened by hard times, Tulsidas asks Ram to say the words he needs to hear.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: रीति सुनि रावरी प्रतीति-प्रीति रावरे सों, डरत हौं देखि कलिकालको कहरु। कहेही बनैगी कै कहाये, बलि जाउँ, राम, “तुलसी ! तू मेरो, हारि हिये न हहरु'॥
tulsi_2.translation: Having heard your ways, my trust and love are in you, yet I am afraid, seeing the cruelty of these times. It will only be well if you say it, or have it said, Ram: "Tulsi, you are mine. Do not lose heart, do not tremble."
tulsi_2.line: "You are mine. Do not lose heart, do not tremble."
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: hearing your ways my trust and love are in you, yet I fear seeing Kali's havoc; it will be well only if you say or have it said, Ram: Tulsi, you are mine, do not lose heart or tremble.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas asks to be kept as he always has been.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: राम ! राखिये सरन, राखि आये सब दिन। बिदित त्रिलोक तिहुँ काल न दयालु दूजो, आरत-प्रनत-पाल को है प्रभु बिन॥
tulsi_2.translation: Ram, keep me in your shelter, as you have kept me every day till now. All three worlds know there has never been another so kind. Who but you protects the hurting who bow before him?
tulsi_2.line: Keep me now, as you have kept me every day until now.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: Ram, keep me in your sharan as you have kept me all my days; the three worlds know there is no second so kind, no protector of the afflicted but you.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas, orphaned as a child, on who his family became.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: राम ! रावरो नाम मेरो मातु-पितु है। सुजन-सनेही, गुरु-साहिब, सखा-सुहृद, राम-नाम प्रेम-पन अबिचल बितु है॥
tulsi_2.translation: Ram, your name is my mother and father, my kin and dear ones, my teacher and master, my companion and true friend. My steady love for your name is my unshakeable wealth.
tulsi_2.line: Your name is my mother and father, my teacher, my friend, my family.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: Ram, your name is my mother and father, my kinsman and loved one, guru and lord, comrade and friend; my vow of love to Ram nam is unmoving wealth.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas on what makes Ram different from every other protector.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: दीनबंधु ! दूरि किये दीनको न दूसरी सरन। आपको भले हैं सब, आपनेको कोऊ कहूँ, सबको भलो है राम! रावरो चरन॥
tulsi_2.translation: Friend of the poor, if you push the poor away they have no other refuge. Everyone is good to their own people, and someone somewhere is good to their own; but your feet, Ram, are good to everyone.
tulsi_2.line: Everyone is good to their own. Your feet, Ram, are good to everyone.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: friend of the poor, if you put the poor away they have no second refuge; all are good to themselves, some to their own; your feet, Ram, are good to all.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas, after trying and failing to set himself right.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: मेरी न बने बनाये मेरे कोटि कलप लौं राम! रावरे बनाये बने पल पाउ मैं।
tulsi_2.translation: What I try to make of myself would not come right in millions of ages; Ram, what you make comes right in a quarter of a moment.
tulsi_2.line: What I could not fix in ages, grace can mend in a moment.
tulsi_2.misuse: Not a reason to stop trying; a release from the belief that everything rests on you.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: what I make does not come right in a crore of kalpas; made by you, Ram, it is done in a quarter of an instant.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas admits that trying harder seems to push him further away.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: ज्यों ज्यों निकट भयो चहं कृपालु ! त्यों त्यों दूरि परयो हौं। तुम चहुँ जुग रस एक राम ! हौं हूँ राबरो, जदपि अघ अवगुननि भरो हौं॥
tulsi_2.translation: The more I try to come near, kind one, the further away I fall. You are the same in all four ages, Ram; and I too am yours, though I am full of wrongs and faults.
tulsi_2.line: The more I try to come close, the further I fall. Still, I am yours.
tulsi_2.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: the nearer I wish to come, gracious one, the farther I fall; you, Ram, are of one flavour in all four ages, and I am yours though filled with sin and fault.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas lies down at Ram's door like a stubborn child.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: पन करि हौं हठि आजुतें रामद्वार परयो हौं। “तू मेरो' यह बिन कहे उठिहाँ न जनमभरि, प्रभुकी सौंकरि निरयो हौं॥
tulsi_2.translation: I have made a vow: from today I lie stubbornly at Ram's door. I will not get up my whole life until you say 'you are mine'; I swear by the Lord, I have lain down here.
tulsi_2.line: I've lain down at your door. I won't get up until you say: you are mine.
tulsi_2.misuse: Surrender comes after doing your part and reflecting (Gita 18.63), not instead of it.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: making a vow, from today I lie obstinately at Ram's door; until you say 'you are mine' I will not rise my life long; I swear by the Lord.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas describes how he will know he has been accepted.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: तुम अपनायो तब जानिहौं, जब मन फिरि परिहै। जेहि सुभाव बिषयनि लग्यो, तेहि सहज नाथ सौं नेह छाडि छल करिंहै॥ … प्रभु-गुन सुनि मन हरषिहै, नीर नयननि ढरिहै। तुलसिदास भयो रामको बिस्वास, प्रेम लखि आनँद उमगि उर भरिहै॥
tulsi_2.translation: I'll know you have made me your own when my mind turns around: when, with the same ease with which it clung to pleasures, it loves the Lord without deceit. Hearing the Lord's qualities the mind will rejoice, tears will flow from the eyes; Tulsidas will trust Ram, and seeing that love, joy will well up and fill the heart.
tulsi_2.line: I'll know you've accepted me when my heart turns toward you as easily as it once turned away.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: I shall know you have made me yours when my mind turns back, when with the nature by which it stuck to sense objects it loves the Lord without guile, rejoicing and weeping at his virtues.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas asks to be seen, faults and all.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: कबहुँ कृपा करि रघुबीर! मोहू चितैहो। भलो-बुरो जन आपनो, जिय जानि दयानिधि ! अवगुन अमित बितैहो॥
tulsi_2.translation: Raghubir, will you ever kindly look my way too? Treasury of mercy, knowing in your heart that good or bad I am your own, will you let my countless faults go?
tulsi_2.line: Good or bad, I am still your own. Look my way, and let my faults go.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: Raghuvir, will you ever in grace look at me too; knowing your servant, good or bad, as your own, treasury of mercy, will you let my endless faults pass.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas asks not to be given up on.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: जैसो हौं तैसो राम रावरो जन, जनि परिहरिये। कृपासिंधु, कोसलधनी! सरनागत-पालक, ढरनि आपनी ढरिये॥ अपराधी तउ आपनो, तुलसी न बिसरिये। टूटियो बाँह गरे परै, फूटेहु बिलोचन पीर होत हित करिये॥
tulsi_2.translation: Ram, whatever I am, I am your servant; do not cast me off. Ocean of mercy, lord of Kosala, protector of those who come for shelter, keep to your own nature. Even at fault, I am your own; do not forget Tulsi. A broken arm still hangs at your neck, and an injured eye still aches as your own and is tended with care.
tulsi_2.line: A broken arm is still held close in a sling.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: such as I am, Ram, I am your servant, do not forsake me; though guilty, I am yours; the arm though broken hangs at the neck, the eye though hurt aches as one's own and is cared for.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas on whom he can turn to.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: तुम तजि हौं कासों कहां, और को हितु मेरे ? दीनबंधु ! सेवक, सखा, आरत, अनाथपर सहज छोह केहि केरे॥
tulsi_2.translation: Leaving you, whom would I tell? Who else wishes me well? Friend of the lowly, who else has a natural tenderness for the servant, the friend, the suffering and the one with no one?
tulsi_2.line: Who else has such natural tenderness for the hurting and the alone?
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: leaving you, to whom shall I speak, who else is my friend; deenbandhu, who else has natural affection for servant, friend, the afflicted and the orphan.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas, weak in body and spirit, looks for a place to rest.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: जाउँ कहाँ, ठौर है कहाँ देव! दुखित-दीनको ? को कृपालु स्वामी-सारिखो, राखै सरनागत सब अँग बल-बिहीनको ॥
tulsi_2.translation: Where do I go? Where is there a place for the hurting and poor, Lord? Who is as kind as my master, who keeps the one who comes for shelter even when every limb has lost its strength?
tulsi_2.line: When every limb has lost its strength, there is still a place where you are kept.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: where shall I go, where is a place for the dukhit and deen; who is a master so gracious that he keeps the refugee bereft of strength in every limb.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas remembers begging and being ignored, and what the saints told him.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: द्वार द्वार दीनता कही, काढ़ि रद, परि पाहूँ। हैं दयालु दुनी दस दिसा, दुख-दोष-दलन-छम, कियो न सँभाषन काहूँ॥ … दुखित देखि संतन कह्यो, सोचै जनि मन माँहू। तोसे पसु-पाँवर-पातकी परिहरे न सरन गये, रघुबर ओर बिनाहूँ॥ ३॥ तुलसी तिहारो भये भयो सुखी प्रीति-प्रतीति बिनाहू। नामकी महिमा, सील नाथको, मेरो भलो बिलोकि अब तें सकुचाहुँ, सिहाहूँ॥
tulsi_2.translation: Door to door I told my need, teeth bared, falling at feet; there are kind people in all ten directions, able to end sorrow and fault, and not one spoke to me. Seeing my sorrow, the saints said: 'Don't worry in your heart. The Lord of Raghus has not cast off even beasts, low ones and sinners like you once they took refuge, even without any other side.' Tulsi became yours and was happy, even without love or trust. The glory of the name, the Lord's gentleness: seeing my good fortune now, I am both shy and amazed.
tulsi_2.line: Door to door, no one spoke to me. Then good people said: don't worry; he turns no one away.
tulsi_2.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: door to door I told my wretchedness, falling at feet; none of the compassionate spoke to me. Seeing me suffer the saints said do not grieve, Raghuvar has not abandoned even beasts and sinners who went for refuge.

tulsi_2.speaker: Tulsidas
tulsi_2.setting: Tulsidas on what happens once someone takes shelter in the name.
tulsi_2.sanskrit: कैसेउ पाँवर पातकी, जेहि लई नामकी ओट। गाँठी बाँध्यो दाम तो, परख्यो न फेरि खर-खोट॥
tulsi_2.translation: However low or sinful a person, once they took the shelter of the name, he tied them into his cloth like a coin and never again tested whether it was true or false.
tulsi_2.line: Once you take his shelter, he ties you in his cloth like a coin and never tests you again.
tulsi_2.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.
tulsi_2.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
tulsi_2.our_note: Tulsidas: however vile a sinner, whoever took the shelter of the name, Ram tied him in his knot like money and never again assayed him true or false.

up_1.speaker: Seer
up_1.setting: Advice on keeping up practice.
up_1.sanskrit: यथापकृष्टं शैवालं क्षणमात्रं न तिष्ठति । आवृणोति तथा माया प्राज्ञं वापि पराङ्मुखम् ॥
up_1.translation: As moss pushed aside does not stay away even a moment, so illusion covers again even a wise person who turns away.
up_1.line: Push moss aside and it closes back at once. So confusion returns to the wise who look away.
up_1.verified_with: data tr.hi
up_1.our_note: Heedlessness toward the self lets ignorance cover even the learned again, as parted moss closes over water. The same verse stands in the Vivekachudamani on pramada.

up_1.speaker: Seer
up_1.setting: One of a series of marks of a person free while living.
up_1.sanskrit: साधुभिः पूज्यमानेऽस्मिन्पीड्यमानेऽपि दुर्जनैः । समभावो भवेद्यस्य स जीवन्मुक्त इष्यते ॥
up_1.translation: Whether honoured by the good or harassed by the wicked, one who stays the same is called free while living.
up_1.line: Praised by the good or harassed by the cruel, the free person stays the same.
up_1.misuse: Staying even does not mean staying in a harmful situation.
up_1.verified_with: data tr.hi
up_1.our_note: One of the marks of the jivanmukta: evenness whether worshipped by the good or afflicted by the wicked.

up_1.speaker: Seer
up_1.setting: On past actions already in motion.
up_1.sanskrit: ज्ञानोदयात्पुरारब्धं कर्म ज्ञानान्न नश्यति । अदत्त्वा स्वफलं लक्ष्यमुद्दिश्योत्सृष्टबाणवत् ॥ व्याघ्रबुद्ध्या विनिर्मुक्तो बाणः पश्चात्तु गोमतौ । न तिष्ठति भिनत्त्येव लक्ष्यं वेगेन निर्भरम् ॥
up_1.translation: Action that began before knowledge dawned is not destroyed by knowledge without yielding its fruit, like an arrow released at its target. An arrow loosed at what looked like a tiger does not stop when you see it is a cow; it flies on and strikes the target with force.
up_1.line: An arrow already shot does not stop because you changed your mind. Past actions run their course.
up_1.misuse: Facing consequences is not punishment for being bad; it is how actions work.
up_1.verified_with: data tr.hi
up_1.our_note: Prarabdha, action that has begun to bear fruit, continues for the knower until spent, as an arrow shot at a supposed tiger still strikes when the target is seen to be a cow.

up_1.speaker: Seer
up_1.setting: The third birth: the parent's passing.
up_1.sanskrit: सोऽस्यायमात्मा पुण्येभ्यः कर्मभ्यः प्रतिधीयते । अथास्यायामितर आत्मा कृतकृत्यो वयोगतः प्रैति । स इतः प्रयन्नेव पुनर्जायते तदस्य तृतीयं जन्म ॥
up_1.translation: This self of his, the child, is put in his place to carry on good works. Then his other self, the parent, having done what was to be done and grown old, departs; departing from here, he is born again. That is his third birth.
up_1.line: The child takes up the good work; the parent, duties done and years full, departs and is born again.
up_1.verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 1, Ait. Ar. II.5
up_1.our_note: The son is set in the father's place to perform meritorious works; the father, his duties done and advanced in age, departs and is reborn. That is his third birth.

prasang.title_en: The three births of a person
prasang.summary: The Aitareya describes three births: conception and pregnancy, when the mother nourishes the child and must herself be nourished; birth and upbringing, when caring for the child is caring for oneself; and death, when the parent, duties done, departs and the child carries on.
prasang.lesson: Care for the one who carries and raises the child; raising children continues your life.

up_1.speaker: Seer
up_1.setting: A prayer chanted at the start of a Vedic hymn.
up_1.sanskrit: अथातः पवमानानामेवाभ्यारोहः । स वै खलु प्रस्तोता साम प्रस्तौति । स यत्र प्रस्तुयात् तदेतानि जपेदसतो मा सद् गमय तमसो मा ज्योतिर्गमय मृत्योर्माऽमृतं गमयेति ।
up_1.translation: Now the chanting of the purifying verses. When the priest begins the hymn, one should recite: From the unreal lead me to the real. From darkness lead me to light. From death lead me to immortality.
up_1.line: Lead me from the unreal to the real, from darkness to light, from death to the deathless.
up_1.verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Brih. I.3.28
up_1.our_note: The unreal and darkness both mean death, that is, natural ignorant thought and action; the real and light mean immortality, one's divine nature. The third line sums up the first two. A japa for the chanter.

up_1.speaker: Seer
up_1.setting: The creation story: the first being, alone.
up_1.sanskrit: सोऽबिभेत् तस्मादेकाकी बिभेति । स हायमीक्षां चक्रे यन्मदन्यन्नास्ति कस्मान्नु बिभेमीति । तत एवास्य भयं वीयाय । कस्माद्ध्यभेष्यत् द्वितीयाद्वै भयं भवति ॥
up_1.translation: He was afraid; that is why one who is alone is afraid. Then he thought: 'Since there is nothing but me, what am I afraid of?' At that his fear left him. What was there to fear? Fear arises only from a second.
up_1.line: Alone, he was afraid. Then he asked: since there is nothing but me, what am I afraid of?
up_1.verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Brih. I.4.2
up_1.our_note: Viraj feared as we do, from ignorance; fear left him through the knowledge that there is no second, since fear arises only from another.

prasang.title_en: The first being: fear, loneliness and dharma
prasang.summary: In this creation story the first being, alone, feels fear, then realises there is no one else to fear. He feels no joy alone and longs for a companion, splitting into husband and wife. Finally dharma is created, the truth by which even the weak can stand up to the strong.
prasang.lesson: Fear and loneliness are human; truth gives even the weak a footing.

up_1.speaker: Seer (quoting Yajnavalkya)
up_1.setting: The first being, alone, longs for another.
up_1.sanskrit: स वै नैव रेमे तस्मादेकाकी न रमते । स द्वितीयमैच्छत् स हैतावानास यथा स्त्रीपुमाꣳसौ सम्परिष्वक्तौ । स इममेवाऽऽत्मानं द्वेधाऽपातयत् । ततः पतिश्च पत्नी चाभवताम् । तस्मादिदमर्धबृगलमिव स्व इति ह स्माऽऽह याज्ञवल्क्यस्तस्मादयमाकाशः स्त्रिया पूर्यत एव । ताꣳ समभवत् ततो मनुष्या अजायन्त ॥
up_1.translation: He found no delight; that is why one who is alone finds no delight. He longed for a second. He became as large as a man and woman embracing, and split himself in two; from that came husband and wife. So, said Yajnavalkya, each of us is like a half. That is why this space is filled by a wife.
up_1.line: Alone, he found no joy and longed for another. So, said Yajnavalkya, each of us is like a half.
up_1.verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Brih. I.4.3
